entries.name: Beast Court of Ten Thousand Mountains
entries.summary: The spirit beast realm of the Vast Wilds Continent, ruled from a forest of stone pillars by four beast kings.
entries.lore: The White Ape King and the Storm Roc have both reached Deity Transformation and taken human form; the Golden Python and the Old Tortoise are close behind. Humans who enter without leave are prey. Beast tamers are hunted on sight, and their tamed beasts are 'freed' and eaten. The Court still trades with Apricot Grove Valley, because even beasts get sick.
entries.truth: The Ape King and the Roc are a breath away from civil war over who leads the Court when the tide peaks. The prince the Beast-Butcher Gate killed was the son of the Court's dowager queen, a Void Refinement beast who went into seclusion before the Ape and the Roc were crowned. She has woken, and she remembers.

ties.why: The Butchers cross the strait to cut cores from our young; we send hunters after every raiding party.
The herders chain our children for mounts; we kill the tamers and free the beasts.
Our emissaries walk the valley's streets for pills the strait can't make, under the one protection the valley gives.
We offered the thunder-wolf king a seat at the lowest table if his packs clear the loggers from the groves.

top.note: the dowager queen, newly woken; two beast kings at Deity Transformation

entries.name: Azure Wave Palace
entries.summary: The court of the sea clans, deep in the Shoreless Sea. Every ship on the outer ocean sails by its leave.
entries.lore: The Sea Sovereign is an old jiao, a flood dragon at Deity Transformation, who means to pass a tribulation and become a true dragon before the tide turns. Its court holds shark-folk generals, turtle sages and things from the deep trenches that nobody names. Humans who pay toll sail safely. Humans who fish the sea clans' young are hunted down in their own ports.
entries.truth: To become a true dragon the Sovereign needs a dragon pearl from the Age of the Ascent. One sits in a vault on the Floating Peak Continent. The Sovereign is a Body Integration flood dragon; the pearl is his last step to true dragon. Two dragon elders at Void Refinement guard the Palace.

ties.why: Our factor's pavilion at the Sea Gate takes the toll on every voyage and reports on every convoy.
The weavers give us the coast's convoys, harbors and secrets, and we leave their cove alone.
One of our court's jiao raises its young in a cave on this coast, and we will come ashore for any that is taken.
We let Held Pearl dive the shoals for a tenth of the catch and a third left whole, and our wardens count every buoy.
The eastern kingdoms pay our toll in sea silver and thunderwood, grudgingly and never in full.
Our factor's pavilion on the First Sun quay seals every ship that leaves, and takes the Palace's share.
We watch the Tidal Realm's cave mouth and take a share of all that comes out.
The Thunder Cliffs coast pays us toll for every boat that fishes past the reefs.
Our factor keeps an office on the Stilled Waves quay, and no ship for the outer ocean sails without his seal.
Surf Rocks pays us a tenth of its catch, and our toll ships keep dying on its reefs, which the storms get blamed for.

entries.name: Vast Wilds Continent
entries.summary: Jungle, miasma marsh and stone forests ruled by spirit beasts. Gu clans, half-bloods and the oldest living thing in the world.
entries.lore: Humans hold only the northern coast of the Vast Wilds Continent, across the Jade Strait from the Morning Star Continent. The rest belongs to the Beast Court of Ten Thousand Mountains and its four kings. In the poison valleys, the Jar-Mother Clans raise Gu that can kill a Core Formation elder from a mile away. In the far south the Evergreen Deep grows around the Root Mother, and its herbs are the oldest in the world: an alchemist's dream, and usually their grave.
entries.truth: Most beasts of the Age of the Ascent never died. They slept through the Dim Age in the deep mountains, and the tide is waking them one by one.

entries.name: Realm of a Hundred Battles
entries.summary: The Court's proving ground, a shard world that opens every ten years for young beasts below Core Formation. Humans may enter too, as the prey.
entries.lore: Every tenth year the gate at the foot of the Court's oldest pillar opens for thirty days. Young beasts below Core Formation go in to fight for rank, and those who come out with the most kills receive titles, territory and a place at court. By the Court's oldest rule the gate refuses no one, so humans may enter as well; few do, because inside every beast hunts them first. Survivors bring out Hundred-Battle Grass, which grows only where blood has soaked the ground and is the base of Slaughter Dao pills.
entries.truth: The next opening is in four years, and both kings mean to fill it with their own clans' young. Whoever wins the most titles will own the next generation of the Court's lords.

entries.name: Brindled Ridges
entries.summary: Tiger country beyond the Thornwall, held for the White Ape King by the Brindled Lord. The tigers have gone quiet this year, and the frontier is reading that as weakness.
entries.lore: The Brindled Lord is a Core Formation tiger who has eaten, by his own count, four thousand humans; he keeps their teeth in a gourd and lets envoys hear it rattle. His sons and daughters hold the ridges as hunting ranges, and no human crosses them without a tooth-token bought from him, usually through the [[Bridgehead Town]] middlemen. This spring he answered the Ape King's summons and his grown cubs pulled back from the wall. Poachers have since taken more tiger cores in four months than in the ten years before, mostly from yearlings left behind.
entries.truth: The Brindled Lord is old and his core is cracking. The slaughter he is waiting for is meant to feed him enough human blood and qi to mend it.

entries.name: Running-Thunder River
entries.summary: A short, violent river that falls off the west face of the range into the Shoreless Sea. In storm season its floods roar louder than the thunder.
entries.lore: It drops nine thousand zhang in about forty-five thousand li through gorges so narrow the sky is a thread. Floods come down it in walls after every storm, carrying boulders and drowned takin to the sea. Storm-iron washes out of the gorges into its gravel bars, and panners risk the floods for it. The mouth is a fan of boulders where nothing can anchor, which is one reason the west coast has no ports.

entries.name: Grotto of Hidden Souls
entries.summary: A ghost fief in the sea caves, ruled by a judge who fled the Court of No Light with a stolen page of its register. The dead who do not want to be judged come here.
entries.lore: Judge Gao Ming sat in the lower courts of the [[Court of No Light]] for nine hundred years before he walked out with page 41,307 of the death register under his robe. Whoever holds a soul's page commands it, and that page holds three thousand souls: his army, his servants and his treasury. Runaway ghosts cross the strait in Ghost Month and ask for asylum, and he grants it for a price paid in memories, which he sells to the [[Gate of Beast Craft]]. The Court's bounty judges come every few years. None have gone back.
entries.truth: The page dates from the Severance. One of its three thousand names is an Upper Realm envoy, and Gao Ming has never dared to call that one.

entries.name: Ridge of Long Calls
entries.summary: The gibbon clans' towers north of the Court. Their dawn songs carry the Court's decrees across a hundred li of karst, and everything else they hear goes to the Ape King.
entries.lore: Gibbons are the Court's heralds: each dawn the clans sing the day's decrees from tower to tower, and by noon every beast within a thousand li knows them. They are also its ears. The Gibbon Mother, a Core Formation singer, can hear a whisper at ten li and repeat it in the speaker's voice. Young gibbons train as couriers and interpreters, and a few who learned human speech work for the [[House of Translated Tongues]] in Shared Roost City. Their towers grow Moon-Ear Fungus, a Qi Condensation tonic that sharpens hearing.
entries.truth: The Gibbon Mother has started editing the dawn songs. Small changes: a decree delayed, a name dropped. She is deciding the war's opening moves before either king does.

entries.name: Pond of Toad Song
entries.summary: A domain of spirit toads whose night chorus can stop a heart. They rule the eastern marsh and take their tolls from catchers in live insects.
entries.lore: The toad clans sing all night from ten thousand ponds, and the song carries a Death Dao rhythm that makes sleepers' hearts skip; locals sleep with wax in their ears. The Toad Elder, a Core Formation toad the size of a house, sits on a mud island and grants catching rights to Gu raisers in exchange for live insects and silence about his ponds. Toad venom from the clans is the base of half the Jar-Mothers' paralytics. The toads serve neither the Ape nor the Roc; they belong to the marsh, and want to keep it that way.
entries.truth: The Toad Elder knows what lies under the [[Exhaling Pool]] and that it is waking. He is its descendant.

entries.name: City Under the Silt
entries.summary: An Ascent Age city buried under eighty zhang of delta mud. The Old Tortoise kills anyone who digs, which has only convinced everyone it is worth digging.
entries.lore: Dike workers strike jade roofs when the channels shift, and three times in the last century someone has sunk a shaft. Each time the river rose overnight and filled the shaft, and the diggers were found in the paddies with their limbs neatly folded. At the spring flood the city's outline shows from the air: streets, a harbor, a great ferry hall facing north. Treasure hunters still come with water-repelling talismans, and the alligators watch them work.
entries.truth: Under the mud the city is dry, sealed and lit. Its sect left a hall of Ladder-building records that the Tortoise has never let anyone read, not even the [[Armillary Pavilion]].

entries.name: Red Rift
entries.summary: A rift of volcanoes splitting the southwest corner from the rest of the Vast Wilds Continent, a finger's width a year. The Golden Python coils in its heat, and smiths come for its fire and metal.
entries.lore: The [[Flame Spine Ridge]] marks the rift: a chain of craters and lava lakes, black glass plains and sulfur springs that never cool. The land beyond it is slowly pulling away, and every century the rift floor drops another zhang. The Golden Python, youngest of the four kings, has made the rift his country. He eats ore, and his scales are gold. He plays the Ape King and the Storm Roc against each other and sells his vote to neither. His half-blood children at the [[Molten Gold Hold]] are the best artifact refiners on the continent.
entries.truth: The Python is waiting for the Fire Rat of the [[Fire Rat Warren]] to wake fully, so he can eat it and break through to Deity Transformation before the war. Then he will choose a side, or replace both kings.

entries.name: Sky-Hanging Falls
entries.summary: Where the Untamed River drops off the edge of the karst plateau in a curtain of water nine li wide. The roar can be felt in the chest a hundred li away.
entries.lore: The falls drop three hundred zhang into the [[Catfish Deep]], and their spray stands above them as a permanent cloud lit by rainbows. Water Dao cultivators meditate on the ledges behind the curtain, where the water's weight makes every breath a trial. A ledge path behind the falls leads to caves where Ascent Age cultivators carved their insights into the rock; the carvings shift with the river's flow, and reading them takes years. Rafts going downstream are portaged around the falls on an elephant road.

entries.name: Eagle Crags
entries.summary: The sea eagle lord's domain on the karst sea-towers, held for the Storm Roc. His eagles watch the strait, tax the corpse ships and drown the ones that do not pay.
entries.lore: The White Sea Eagle is a Core Formation vassal of the Roc with a forty-zhang wingspan and a temper to match. His clan nests on the tallest towers of the [[Forest of Sea Pillars]], and from there every ship nearing the coast is visible. Corpse ships pay a tithe of one carcass in ten; ships that try to slip past at night are lifted from the water and dropped. Fishing villages pay in fish and are left alone. His eyries are full of eggshell, gold and the bones of tamers who tried to steal eaglets.
entries.truth: His eldest eaglet was stolen four years ago by a [[Gate of One Heart]] tamer and is now a bonded bird in the Morning Star Continent. He knows the tamer's name, and he is waiting for her to come back for another.

entries.name: Plain of Low Songs
entries.summary: The elephant clans' home range on the river's flood plain, ruled by the Eldest Matriarch. Elephants talk in songs too low to hear, and the ground carries them for a thousand li.
entries.lore: Nine clans of spirit elephants graze the flood plain, each led by its grandmothers and all ruled by the Eldest Matriarch, a Nascent Soul elephant who remembers her grandmother remembering the Dim Age. They do not hunt, they do not serve, and they cannot be stopped: a herd on the march levels jungle like a flood. Few of them speak human words, so the council deals with outsiders through the [[House of Translated Tongues]] interpreters. Calves learn the Earth Dao by standing in the river until they feel the bed move.
entries.truth: The Matriarch's songs carry under the whole continent. She has heard the [[Scale-Armor Mountain]] breathing for ten years, and she has been teaching the clans an old migration route that leads away from it.

entries.name: Forest of Cauldrons
entries.summary: A clearing filled with the cauldrons of dead alchemists, ten thousand bronze and jade furnaces overgrown by vines. Some still hold the pill they were making.
entries.lore: Alchemists who reach the forest's richest grounds often try to refine on the spot, before the herbs lose potency, and their cauldrons are what is left when the forest objects. Generations of them stand in rows under the vines, some cracked, some still sealed. Appraisers come for the cauldrons, which include Ascent Age furnaces worth a sect's treasury; scavengers come for the pills, which are sometimes perfect and sometimes the reason the alchemist died. The vines here are the forest's most vicious, and they seem to like the bronze.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Dark Crossing
entries.summary: A human kingdom of corpse traders that salts beast carcasses for the Long Dusk Continent's puppet makers. In the Kingdom of the Dark Crossing your grandmother's body is part of your inheritance.
entries.lore: The Sang family has ruled for four centuries from a smokehouse palace, and its wealth is counted in barrels of salted carcass. Hunters bring in dead spirit beasts; the Kingdom of the Dark Crossing's guilds gut, salt and stitch them, and ships carry them across the strait to buyers from the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]]. A Core Formation beast's body is worth a village. Children learn to stitch hide before they can write. The kingdom's own dead are sold too, by law, and families bid on their elders at the funeral auction. Rooted children are apprenticed to puppet makers.
entries.truth: The Kingdom of the Dark Crossing's salt pans sit on a Low-grade yin vein, which is why its carcasses never rot. The vein is swelling with the tide, and the kingdom's children have started to be born cold.

entries.name: Forest of Peaks
entries.summary: The karst heart of the Vast Wilds Continent: ten thousand stone towers rising from the jungle, and among them the forest of pillars where the Beast Court's four kings sit.
entries.lore: The towers stand so close that the jungle floor between them sees sun for an hour a day; rivers run beneath, and sinkholes open without warning. At the center stands the [[Beast Court of Ten Thousand Mountains]] where the White Ape King holds the inner pillars and the Storm Roc's perch is empty more nights than not. Envoys, hostages and the [[Apricot Grove Valley]] physicians wait on the [[Physicians' Terrace]] for audiences. Humans without a seal of passage are prey. Two of the Court's Nascent Soul lords are away serving a term with the [[Seal Watch]].
entries.truth: Not all of the ten thousand pillars are stone. A few dozen are Ascent Age beasts that slept so long the karst grew over them, and in the last ten years three have cracked. The oldest of the three is a Body Integration ape, and the White Ape King is its descendant.

top.note: an Ascent beast in a cracked pillar; the White Ape King and the Storm Roc at Deity Transformation

entries.name: Kingdom of Burned Registers
entries.summary: A kingdom founded by families who fled the Jing registry with their spirit-rooted children and burned their papers on the beach. Nobody here is written down.
entries.lore: Three hundred years ago nine families crossed the island chain with children the Jing testers would have taken. The Ash Council of their descendants still rules, and the founding law still holds: no census, no registers, no written names. Mothers test their own children for spirit roots in secret, and a rooted child learns early to hide when Jing registrars come asking. That makes the Kingdom of Burned Registers the best hunting ground for talent outside the empire: the [[Clear Heaven Sword Sect]] and the [[Apricot Grove Valley]] scouts pay families quietly, and so does the [[Night Banquet Sect]].
entries.truth: One of the nine founding families never fled anything. It was planted by the Jing registry office, and it has sent a list of rooted children to the [[Jing Capital]] every ten years since.

entries.name: Hidden-Flow River
entries.summary: A river that sinks into the karst under the Beast Court and rises again in the Evergreen Deep, cold and clear, then winds under the Root Mother's canopy to the southern sea.
entries.lore: For its first twenty thousand li the river runs underground through the bat caverns of the [[Caverns of the Hidden River]]. It surfaces at the Weeping Spring on the forest's northern edge already cold, clear and full of blind white fish. Expeditions follow its banks because the river's own plants are drowsy. Downstream it passes under the [[Mother's Shade]], where nobody follows it, and reaches the outer sea through a bay where the water stays fresh a hundred li out. Spirit lotus grows in its slow stretches.

entries.name: Hatching Sands
entries.summary: Black-sand beaches where sea clan turtles come ashore to lay their eggs, guarded by the Azure Wave Palace's turtle sages. It is the sea clans' only holding on the Vast Wilds Continent.
entries.lore: Each year in the eighth month the sea turtles come ashore by the thousand, and the sands are closed to everything that walks or flies. Turtle sages of the [[Azure Wave Palace]] hold the beaches by an understanding with the Court older than any human kingdom: the sea clans own the sand, the beasts own the rest. Eggs from these sands are a Foundation-grade longevity tonic, and egg thieves are hunted into their home ports, as the sea clans hunt all who take their young. The Old Tortoise is said to be the sages' distant cousin.
entries.truth: The sages keep a second nest deep under the sand: eggs of the Sea Sovereign's own line, hidden where no one in the sea would think to look.

entries.name: Floating Market
entries.summary: A market of lashed-together rafts that drifts down the Untamed River every dry season, run by half-bloods and river folk. It sells salt to elephants and cores to anyone.
entries.lore: Three hundred rafts make up the market, and it moves twenty li a day from the falls toward the delta, stopping wherever buyers wait on the banks. Salt, iron, cloth and wine go to the beasts; cores, hides, herbs and ivory go to the coast. Half-blood raft clans run it under a council of captains, and every king's tollkeeper takes a cut on the way. Expeditions bound for the Evergreen Deep buy guides, rope and antidotes here, and its raft inns are the cheapest place to learn the river.
entries.truth: The council sells the Court's patrol schedules to the [[Tusk-Saw Gang]] and the Gang's ivory to the [[Night Banquet Sect]] buyers in the delta. Half the captains do not know what is under their own decks.

entries.name: High Pastures
entries.summary: Alpine meadows between the peaks where the golden takin herds graze. The takin are the Roc's vassals and pay him in calves; their bull lord is tired of paying.
entries.lore: Takin are shaggy golden giants, half goat and half ox, and the spirit herds of these meadows grow to the size of houses. They are peaceful until they are not, and a stampede can flatten a forest. The Old Bull, a Core Formation takin, rules the herds and has always paid the Roc a calf in ten. This year the Roc demanded a calf in five to feed his falcons through a war. The herds' cloud-wool is the warmest cloth on the Vast Wilds Continent, and their meadows grow Snowcap Gentian, a Foundation herb found nowhere lower.
entries.truth: The Old Bull has sent his eldest daughter to the White Ape King's court as a guest. If war comes, the herds will stampede through the Roc's supply camps on the first night.

entries.name: Sea of Roots
entries.summary: The primeval forest of the Vast Wilds Continent's far south, grown around the Root Mother. Its herbs are the oldest in the world, its plants fight back, and its soil is full of alchemists.
entries.lore: The forest floor here is roots, not earth, layered so deep that the ground is springy for a hundred li. At its heart the [[Evergreen Deep]] grows around the Root Mother, whose canopy covers a kingdom. Walking trees hold court in the west, ginseng children hide in the southern valleys, and a strangler fig has swallowed an Ascent Age city whole. Expeditions set out from the [[Town of Last Letters]] with the [[Rope-Holders' Guild]] guides and come back with roots worth a career, or not at all. Nothing here obeys the Beast Court; beasts are prey too.
entries.truth: The forest's plants are not separate. Every root in the Sea of Roots is joined to the Root Mother's, and whatever one tree feels, she can feel if she bothers to.

top.note: the Root Mother; the world only guesses

entries.name: Tortoise Market
entries.summary: A market town on the river where humans, half-bloods and beasts trade under the Tortoise's truce. Nobody kills on the water here, and everybody cheats on land.
entries.lore: The market sits on a hundred moored barges and the mud island they are tied to. River porpoises bring smoked fish and freshwater pearls, farmers bring rice and salt, and beasts in human form come to buy wine and silk with cores taken from other beasts. A killing on the water is punished by the alligators; on the island it is merely fined. The best shell-readers of the [[Hall of Tortoise Omens]] keep stalls here, and their prices rise with the river.

entries.name: Kingdom of Bone Ramparts
entries.summary: A poacher-lords' kingdom walled with the skulls of the beasts it hunts. It sells cores to anyone and pays for them every spring in blood.
entries.lore: The Ran family started as a poaching crew and became a dynasty when their patriarch reached Foundation on a tiger's core. The capital's walls are beast skulls packed with lime, and every Ran child kills a spirit beast at twelve or is sent to the salt pans. Cores go out through the [[Bridgehead Town]] to the [[Apricot Grove Valley]] buyers and the [[Night Banquet Sect]] brokers. Every spring the beasts come for revenge, the Bone Spring, and the kingdom hires every sword it can find for the forty days it lasts. This year the beasts did not come, and the Ran are celebrating.
entries.truth: Patriarch Ran Gui has been stuck at late Foundation for forty years and will try for Core Formation this winter on a pill brewed with blood of the waking the [[Thousand-Legs Ridge]] centipede, bought from the [[Jarless Gang]]. If he fails, his three sons will kill each other for the seat.

entries.name: Court of Ancient Trees
entries.summary: A moot of walking trees in the western forest: old spirit trees that uproot themselves to gather once a century and hold grudges for much longer.
entries.lore: A tree that wakes slowly grows a mind, and a mind grows a grudge. Two hundred walking trees make up the Court, from camphors and banyans to an ironwood that remembers the Dim Age. They move a few li a day, and when they hold a moot the forest falls silent for a month. They punish fire and axes with death, and every woodcutters' camp on the forest's edge has a story about a tree that was not there the night before. They will answer questions about the forest's past in exchange for burying something that was once alive at their roots.

entries.name: Forest of Sea Pillars
entries.summary: Thousands of karst towers marching out of the jungle and into the sea, some a thousand zhang high. Eagles own the tops, smugglers own the caves, and the sea owns the rest.
entries.lore: The towers begin as stone forest inland and walk out into the strait, where the tide has hollowed them into arches, sea caves and drowned halls. Fog sits between them most mornings. Ships navigate by tower names chalked on the rock, and getting them wrong is the commonest way to die here after the eagles. Cliff swiftlets nest by the million in the caves, and their spirit nests, gathered on ropes, are a favorite Foundation tonic.

entries.name: Kingdom of Ripe Grain
entries.summary: A human rice kingdom west of the bay that feeds Shared Roost City and will not let a half-blood sleep inside its walls. Its crown prince has started wearing gloves.
entries.lore: The Wen kings have ruled these paddies for six hundred years with a Foundation household guard and one rule: sell to Shared Roost City, never let Shared Roost City in. Half-bloods may enter the markets by day and must be outside the walls by dusk, and a mixed birth is left at Shared Roost City's gate. Rooted children are sold to Morning Star sect recruiters at the spring fair, and the kingdom's rice is the cheapest on the north coast. Crown Prince Wen Lu is sixteen, beloved, and has lately taken to wearing gloves in summer.
entries.truth: The queen's lover was a python lord in human form. She has bought a blood-lock talisman from the [[Blood-Lock Gang]] to hide the prince's scales, and the slavers now own the kingdom's future.

entries.name: Red Thread Clan
entries.summary: The Jar-Mother clan that raises thread Gu, which bind hearts, wills and oaths. Morning Star nobles buy loyalty from them by the strand.
entries.lore: Thread Gu are hair-fine red worms that live in the blood. Two raised in the same jar always seek each other, and whoever carries one can never truly turn against whoever carries its twin. The clan sells them as marriage threads, loyalty threads for bodyguards and oath threads for contracts no court could enforce. Every girl of the clan is given her own thread at birth and never told who carries the twin. The clan mother is Core Formation and the most diplomatic of the Jar-Mothers, which is to say the most patient.
entries.truth: The loyalty threads the clan sold to the [[Protectorate of the Quelled Wilds]]'s officers have twins, and the twins are not with the Protector-General. They are in a jar in this valley.

entries.name: Gate-Waiting Town
entries.summary: The shanty town outside Shared Roost City's walls where newly arrived half-bloods wait for the blood test. Some wait a month; some wait for the slavers.
entries.lore: Shared Roost City tests forty applicants a day, and the line is four thousand long. Arrivals live in reed huts on the mudflats, sell what they brought, and learn quickly who is a recruiter, who is a slaver and who is both. The [[Hall of Woken Blood]] runs a soup kitchen that doubles as a scouting post, and a place in the queue sells for a low-grade spirit stone per day saved. Humans and beasts in a hurry pass the town's toll gate straight to the city markets; half-bloods with no money do not.
entries.truth: Places in the queue are sold by a clerk of Shared Roost City's own council, who also sells the [[Blood-Lock Gang]] a list of who has no one to miss them.

entries.name: Yellow Marsh
entries.summary: A miasma marsh on the southeast coast where the yellow fog never lifts. Venomous creatures breed here by the million, and the Jar-Mothers' catchers come for them.
entries.lore: The marsh runs from the foot of the valleys to the southeast cape, and the fog over it is yellow, warm and sweet-smelling, which is how it kills: slowly and pleasantly, over a few days. Toads, cobras and leeches the size of dogs thrive in it, and catchers from the [[Venom-Catchers' Camp]] harvest them for Gu jars. Expeditions bound for the Evergreen Deep's eastern edge cross it on the half-sunk the [[Jade Road]]. Walking mangroves are spreading out of the south, and the toads say the marsh is breathing harder every year.
entries.truth: The king cobra of the [[King-Cobra Mere]] has been selling the Golden Python's venom tithe to the Jar-Mothers, the Python's oldest enemies. The Python has noticed.

entries.name: Spring-Returning Clan
entries.summary: The Jar-Mother clan that raises healing Gu and sells antidotes to the Apricot Grove Valley. The other clans call them the Apricot Grove Valley's lapdogs, and the Apricot Grove Valley wants their jars.
entries.lore: A healing Gu lives in a wound and eats rot; a good one closes a sword cut overnight and draws poison out of the blood in an hour. The clan raises dozens of kinds, makes an antidote for every venom in the valleys, and sells them to the [[Apricot Grove Valley]] by the cartload for salt, iron and Morning Star silver. That trade keeps the whole confederation rich, and the clan mother speaks for the valleys at the [[Physicians' Terrace]]. The other clans resent their comfort. The Apricot Grove Valley's buyers have been asking, more and more often, to see how the jars are made.
entries.truth: The Apricot Grove Valley has already bribed a clan daughter to carry out a breeding pair. When the theft is discovered, the Apricot Grove Valley will deny everything and the clan will take the blame.

entries.name: Ash-Feather Cliffs
entries.summary: Basalt cliffs above the rift where a vulture lord circles in the ash plumes. He is the Storm Roc's vassal in the Python's country, and everyone knows what he is for.
entries.lore: The Ash Vulture is a Core Formation carrion lord who nests on the rift's northern lip, where the plumes keep the cliffs warm and the eruptions keep him supplied with the dead. Officially he collects the Roc's tithe from the southern birds; unofficially he watches the Python, and takes no trouble to hide it. Vulture feathers from the ash plumes are fireproof and in demand at the [[Molten Gold Hold]]. The vultures will guide travelers through the rift for a price, and will wait politely if the travelers die.
entries.truth: He spies on the Python for the Roc and on the Roc for the Python. Both kings pay him, and he is saving the money for the day neither of them is king.

entries.name: Soul-Lantern Cliff
entries.summary: A headland where Ghost Month's drifting lights come ashore from the strait. For thirty nights a year the cliff is crowded with the dead, and the living who go there come back changed.
entries.lore: In the seventh month lights rise from the strait and drift east, and most of them fetch up on this headland: the souls of the drowned, the lost and the runaways. They crowd the cliff path and whisper what they want. Ghost Way cultivators come to bargain with them, priests come to guide them, and the [[Grotto of Hidden Souls]] sends recruiters. Anyone who sleeps on the cliff in Ghost Month wakes with a stranger's memories, and some wake as the stranger.

entries.name: Bay of Mixed Waters
entries.summary: The brackish bay around Shared Roost City, the half-blood free city: stilt holds, pearl flats, slavers' coves and the only transfer array on the Vast Wilds Continent.
entries.lore: Fresh water from the interior meets the Shattered Sea here, and so do the continent's outcasts. [[Shared Roost City]] sits at the head of the bay, admitting half-bloods after a blood test and trading with anyone who keeps its peace; its array links to [[Ten Thousand Sails]] and the [[Pale City]], so every expedition into Vast Wilds passes through. Around it lie the half-blood holds, a human rice kingdom that feeds the city and despises it, and the coves where slavers wait for new arrivals. This year the Ape King has demanded that Shared Roost City hand over the Roc's children.
entries.truth: Shared Roost City's first lord was the Old Tortoise's half-human son. The Tortoise has never acknowledged him and has never let any beast harm the city; that, not its usefulness, is why it still stands.

entries.name: Fire Rat Warren
entries.summary: Burrows in a lava field where an Ascent Age fire rat is waking. Its fur cannot burn, and every smith and king on the continent wants it.
entries.lore: The burrows are tunnels through cooling lava, too hot to enter without a fire-warding talisman. Thousands of fire rats live in them, spirit rodents whose fur is woven into cloth that is cleaned by burning, and in the deepest chamber sleeps their ancestor, a rat the size of an ox that was old in the Ascent Age. It has been waking for six years, gnawing the Python's ore veins in its sleep. Its shed fur sells for a mid-grade spirit stone a strand. The Golden Python has forbidden anyone to hunt it, and everyone understands why.

entries.name: River Porpoise Clan
entries.summary: Spirit porpoises who serve the Old Tortoise as messengers and pilots up and down the Untamed River. They smile at everyone and drown poachers with great courtesy.
entries.lore: The porpoises carry the Tortoise's word from the delta to the falls in a month and know every channel, sandbar and drowned village on the river. Travelers who pay their toll in salted fish are guided past the whirlpools; those who do not find the whirlpools by themselves. The clan teaches river beasts the Water Dao and keeps the old river laws: no nets across the full channel, no killing at the fords in the elephants' season. Their leader, the Grey Smile, is Core Formation and speaks perfect human.

entries.name: Shark-Gate Hold
entries.summary: A stilt hold of shark-blooded half-bloods over the bay's tide flats. They pilot ships through the reefs, dive for pearls, and pay the sea clans for the right to exist.
entries.lore: Their fathers or grandmothers were shark-folk of the [[Azure Wave Palace]], and the blood shows in grey skin, black eyes and a second row of teeth. At three, every child is lowered into the bay at slack tide; those who breathe the water are raised as divers, and those who choke are raised as pilots. The Tide Mother, a Foundation diver of 190, rules from the gate-house and sends a tithe of black pearls out to sea each year. No hold pilot, no safe anchorage: ships that refuse a pilot tend to find the reef.
entries.truth: The tithe is not tribute. The Tide Mother reports to the Azure Wave Palace on every ship, cargo and passenger that uses the Shared Roost City array harbor.

entries.name: Shell Mound
entries.summary: The Old Tortoise's island in the middle of the delta, a hill of black stone that the river folk swear is his shell. His court of turtles, salamanders and porpoises waits around it.
entries.lore: Nobody has seen the Tortoise move in living memory. Petitioners row to the landing, kneel on the Answer Stone and burn their question into a turtle plastron; if the Tortoise is listening, the cracks answer, and his giant salamanders read them aloud in voices like crying children. Answers cost rice, salt or silence. His court keeps the delta's peace: no killing on the water between the spring floods and the harvest, by human or beast.
entries.truth: The Tortoise was the mount of an Ascent Age sect master who climbed the Heaven Ladder and promised to come back down it. He lies beneath the mound, which is the old ferry landing of the [[City Under the Silt]], keeping the place for her.

entries.name: Temple of the Forsworn Fang
entries.summary: A mountain temple of beasts who have taken vows: tigers who eat grass, eagles who fast, apes who chant. Both kings mock it, and both have sent envoys to it this year.
entries.lore: Nine hundred years ago a tiger heard a wandering monk of the [[Thousand Lamps Temple]] preach on a mountain road, ate him, and spent the rest of its life in remorse. The temple it founded takes any beast that stops killing. Monks learn sutra breathing, a way to cultivate without devouring, and the vajra body; a few half-bloods and runaway tamed beasts shelter there too. The abbot, a Core Formation tiger with no fangs, offers to mediate between the Ape and the Roc. The White Ape King's mother took her vows here.
entries.truth: The Ape King's mother is still alive in the temple's back hall, and she is the only creature he obeys. The Roc knows, and has been thinking about what to do with the knowledge.

entries.name: Whale Grave
entries.summary: The skeleton of an Ascent Age sea beast stranded on the shore, its ribs as tall as pagodas. Its marrow still leaks qi, and its corpse-gas still kills.
entries.lore: Something vast washed up here before the Dim Age, and its bones have lain half-sunk in the black sand ever since. Bone-cutters work its ribs for refining material, each piece worth a fortune, and die of the grey corpse-gas that seeps from the marrow when it is cut. The sea clans claim the creature was an ancestor and demand its return; the Grey Strand Lord charges both the cutters and the sea clans for access. Something nests in the skull, and the cutters keep away from the skull.
entries.truth: Its soul never left. Too old and slow to notice it has no body, it has begun to dream with the tide, and the cutters' nightmares are its dreams.

entries.name: Realm of Startling Thunder
entries.summary: A shard gate on a lightning-scarred summit that opens only after a hundred strikes in a single storm, usually once every three years. It admits only Qi Condensation.
entries.lore: Nine black stone pillars stand on the summit and drink lightning in the storm season; when a hundred bolts have struck in one storm, a door of white light stays open for three days. A Foundation aura snaps it shut, so only Qi Condensation cultivators and young beasts get in. Inside is a shard of endless storm over glass plains, with pools of liquid lightning that temper meridians for the Lightning Dao and thunder-struck wood that refiners buy by the inch. The [[Thunder Falcon Clan]] send their fledglings, and kill any human they find inside.

entries.name: Thornwall
entries.summary: Blood-fed spirit thorn planted across every valley mouth of the frontier, forty thousand li from end to end. Beasts that push through it bleed for days.
entries.lore: The thorns stand five zhang high, grow a hand a day in the rains, and carry a slow venom that keeps beast wounds open. The wall has nine gates, each held by one polity and taxed by all of them. Gaps open wherever a waking beast leans on it, and the [[Thorn-Planting Gate]] pays 50 low-grade spirit stones to whoever reports a breach first. This year, for the first time, humans are cutting the gaps themselves to get out faster.

entries.name: Golden Coil Lair
entries.summary: The Golden Python's lair, a lava cave beneath the rift's largest crater where the king sleeps coiled around a lake of molten ore. His court is serpents and his treasury is himself.
entries.lore: The Python eats ore and sheds gold: his scales are true metal, and each one he sheds is a Core Formation cultivator's fortune. His lair is a domain of hot caverns where serpent vassals wait in coils for audience and his half-blood children run his business. He receives envoys from both kings and makes them wait for days in the heat. Visitors who leave with a shed scale have usually traded something they will regret. He is clever, patient and vain, and he hates the Jar-Mothers more than he hates humans.

ties.why: The Python's grandson crossed the strait and made the Soul-Lost Stone Forest his hunting ground.

entries.name: Nine Furnaces Mountain
entries.summary: The great volcano of the rift, with nine craters that erupt in turn. Refiners prize its fires, and its ash grows the hottest peppers in the world.
entries.lore: Each of the nine craters burns at a different heat, and refiners name their fires after them: First Furnace for softening bronze, Ninth for melting spirit iron. Smiths of the [[Molten Gold Hold]] lease forge ledges on the rim, and independent refiners pay the Python's serpents for a night's access. One crater or another erupts every few months, and the Fire Dao is easy to sense on the rim. Cinder Pepper, a spirit plant of the ash slopes, is a Qi Condensation fire tonic and a dare.

entries.name: Giant Lizard Strand
entries.summary: A coastal domain of giant monitor lizards whose lord sells smugglers safe passage and sells the Court a quiet coast. He has learned to like human money.
entries.lore: The Grey Strand Lord is a Core Formation monitor lizard thirty zhang long whose bite rots flesh within the hour. He holds the beaches and coves of the central east coast in the Ape King's name and keeps them quiet by taking a cut of everything: a tithe of each smuggler's cargo, passage fees from pirates, a share of the [[Moonless Market]]'s takings. He is the only beast lord on Vast Wilds who keeps a counting-house, run by a half-blood clerk who keeps two sets of books.
entries.truth: Some of the cargo he lets through is Court beasts taken alive, young lords' heirs sold for the Night Banquet's tables. Two missing gibbon heralds went this way, and the Gibbon Mother is asking questions.

entries.name: Tusk-Saw Gang
entries.summary: Human poachers who hunt the oldest elephants for ivory and cores. They poison waterholes, saw tusks from the living and sell everything to the Night Banquet.
entries.lore: The gang is sixty killers out of the Morning Star Continent's southern marshes, led by a Core Formation woman called Sister Hook who once worked the [[Night Banquet Sect]] kitchens. They hunt in the dry season, when the herds are thirsty, poisoning waterholes with Gu from the [[Jarless Gang]] and sawing tusks from the paralyzed. An old matriarch's core sells for more than a kingdom's yearly revenue. Every beast on the river wants them dead, and they move through the jungle on maps nobody can explain.
entries.truth: Sister Hook's buyer is the Night Banquet, but her real employer is Protector-General Yao of the [[Protectorate of the Quelled Wilds]], who wants elephant cores to raise Core Formation officers for a throne.

entries.name: Helm-Crest Cliffs
entries.summary: Sea cliffs where the hornbill clans nest, red-casqued birds who serve the Storm Roc and watch the coast. Their casques are the most valuable carving material in the east.
entries.lore: A hornbill mother walls herself into a cliff hole with mud to raise her young while the father feeds her through a slit, and the clan guards its sealed nests fiercely. Their lord, the Red Helm, is a Core Formation hornbill who reports every ship and smuggler to the Roc's falcons. Their solid red casques carve like jade and hold a Fire Dao charge; one sells for a mid-grade spirit stone in [[Ten Thousand Sails]], and poachers raid the cliffs every year. The hornbills drop the poachers from a great height.
entries.truth: Two of the sealed nests hold no eggs. The Red Helm is hiding a pair of the [[Gate of One Heart]] children there for a debt he owes their mother, and the Roc would kill him for it.

entries.name: Thunder Falcon Clan
entries.summary: The Storm Roc's hunters and messengers, falcons that ride lightning and hunt beast tamers across the whole continent. Their patrols have doubled this year.
entries.lore: A thunder falcon can cross the Vast Wilds Continent in five months and strikes at the speed of the bolt it rides. The clan carries the Roc's messages, guards the passes of the [[Sheer Spine Range]] and enforces the Court's oldest law: the tamer dies, the tamed beast is freed and eaten. Young beasts of any clan may learn the falcons' Lightning and Wind Dao techniques in exchange for a term of service. They hate the [[Gate of One Heart]] above all things. This year they are drilling in formation, which falcons have never needed against humans.
entries.truth: The falcons' Core Formation chief keeps a pet of his own: a human girl he raised from a captive, who reads him the tamers' intercepted letters.

entries.name: Thunder-Feather Hold
entries.summary: A cliff hold of half-bloods sired by the Storm Roc in human form over eight centuries. Their father has suddenly remembered them, and so has the White Ape King.
entries.lore: Roc-blooded children are born with grey down along the spine and hear storms a day before they come; the strongest can call a spark from dry air. For eight hundred years the Roc ignored them. This year his envoys brought feathers of rank, Lightning Dao manuals and an invitation to fly west. Six of the hold's elders have died since, poisoned or pushed from the cliffs, and all of [[Shared Roost City]] knows the Ape King's agents did it. The Grey Plume, the Core Formation eldest, has not yet answered his father.
entries.truth: The Grey Plume means to answer neither king. He is negotiating with the [[Protectorate of the Quelled Wilds]] for Jing protection, which would bring imperial soldiers into the bay.

entries.name: Kingdom of Lotus Isles
entries.summary: The largest human kingdom of the delta, eleven hundred years under the Tortoise's peace. Its children swim before they walk, never eat turtle, and fear the tribute-takers.
entries.lore: The founder of the Lu dynasty made the first tribute pact on the Answer Stone, and every Lu king since has kept it. Each autumn at the Tribute Steps the king pours the first tenth of the harvest into the river with his own hands. Spirit-rooted children go to the [[Shell Mound]] as shell pages for ten years; most come home able to read cracks and unwilling to say what else they learned. The kingdom's Foundation generals have never fought a war, and the court is quietly terrified of what the Ape King's envoy said in spring.
entries.truth: The envoy offered to end the tribute forever if the king tells the Ape where the Tortoise's body really lies. The king's younger brother knows. He was a shell page.

entries.name: Hunting Park
entries.summary: The gate of an Ascent Age hunting preserve, a shard world stocked with beasts that have not changed in seventy thousand years. Opens every 12 years; Foundation and below only.
entries.lore: The gate is a ring of nine carved stags on a hilltop beyond the Thornwall. Every twelfth spring it opens for forty days; a Core Formation aura cracks it, so crews are Foundation and below. Inside run the preserve's descendants: horned deer with ancient bloodlines, striped boar that eat iron, birds that never learned to fear people. Their cores are small and pure, and tamers would kill for a hatchling. The next opening is in two years, and the [[Kingdom of Bone Ramparts]], the [[Core-Takers' Society]] and the [[Brindled Ridges]] tigers all mean to hold the hill.
entries.truth: The preserve's first beasts came down the Heaven Ladder as a gift from the Upper Realm. Their bloodlines are Upper Realm bloodlines, and the Beast Court would go to war to keep humans from learning it.

entries.name: Scale-Armor Mountain
entries.summary: A mountain of overlapping grey plates that rises and falls a finger's width with every breath. It is an Ascent Age pangolin, asleep since the Dim Age, and it is waking up.
entries.lore: Prospectors call it the Breathing Mountain. Its slopes are scales the size of fields, and the caves at its base are tunnels that run for ten thousand li under the range, each ending at a spirit vein bitten off clean. The tremors of the [[Sheer Spine Range]] come from here, and they have grown stronger every year of the High Tide. The Storm Roc forbids anyone, beast or human, to go near it. Prospectors go anyway, because the tunnels are lined with vein ends worth more than a mine.
entries.truth: It eats spirit veins. The Storm Roc has been dropping spirit stones down its tunnels for thirty years, hoping a grateful ancient will fight the Ape. Nobody has asked what it will eat when it wakes and the stones run out. The ancient under the plates reached Body Integration in the Age of the Ascent, which is why it eats veins and not stones.

entries.name: Realm of Flowing Flame
entries.summary: A shard gate inside a dormant crater beside the Ninth Furnace that opens when its shard swings close, every fifteen years for twelve days. Core Formation and below may enter, if they can bear the heat.
entries.lore: When the shard nears, the cold crater fills with flowing light instead of lava, and a stair of obsidian appears. Inside is a world of fire rivers and floating islands of ore, where the Fire Dao comes easily and Flame-Heart Iron, a top refining material, can be dug from the islands. Fire spirits guard the richest veins. A Nascent Soul aura shatters the stair. The Python claims the gate and sells passes for five mid-grade spirit stones; the smiths of the [[Molten Gold Hold]] go in free.

entries.name: Bone-Burial Caves
entries.summary: Karst caves full of Ascent Age beast bones, where the Kingdom of the Dark Crossing's diggers quarry relics for the bone market. The bones are too big for anything alive today.
entries.lore: Something drove the great beasts of the Ascent Age into these caves to die, or dragged them here. Thighbones as long as boats lie in the lower galleries, glazed with seventy thousand years of dripstone. Appraisers grade them by the qi left in the marrow, and a single tooth can be refined into a Foundation-grade weapon. The Beast Court forbids the trade and sends patrols, so diggers work in the dark with shuttered lamps and listen for wings.
entries.truth: Not all the bones in the deepest gallery belong to dead beasts. Some of the sleepers there are only very thin, and the tide is waking them.

entries.name: Untamed River
entries.summary: The greatest river of the Vast Wilds Continent: it gathers a thousand karst springs, drops off the plateau at the Sky-Hanging Falls and spreads into a delta of nine hundred channels at the North Cape.
entries.lore: In the rains it is two hundred li wide in the middle reach and carries whole islands of floating jungle out to sea. Its water is tea-brown and warm, and it belongs to the beasts: porpoises, catfish and alligators enforce the Old Tortoise's river laws from the falls to the sea, and the elephants cross at the ford every dry season. Humans travel it on the [[Floating Market]] rafts or not at all. River pearls, drowned Ascent Age bronze and spirit lotus seed are its treasures.

entries.name: Drowned Garden
entries.summary: The gate of an Ascent Age herb garden drowned under the marsh. It surfaces only when a great drought drains the eastern meres, about once in twenty-seven years, and admits Foundation and below.
entries.lore: When the meres dry out, a ring of jade garden walls appears in the mud with a moon gate at its center. For the eleven days before the rains return, cultivators below Core Formation can step through into a terraced garden where Ascent Age herbs have run wild for seventy thousand years: thousand-year lingzhi, Snake-Tongue Grass, spirit rice that ripens in a day. The garden's walking herbs fight back. The last opening was twenty-five years ago, the meres are already low, and the Jar-Mothers have sworn the gate is theirs.

entries.name: Mother's Shade
entries.summary: The ground beneath the Root Mother's canopy, a kingdom-wide shade where it is always dusk. Those who cut nothing sometimes walk out; those who cut anything never do.
entries.lore: The canopy is so dense that rain takes an hour to reach the ground. Under it the air is cool and still, and the roots underfoot are warm as skin. Herbs grow here that grow nowhere else: Root Mother sap, which adds a decade to a mortal's life with each drop, and Ladder Moss, which glows faintly and has no known use. Guides will lead clients to the edge of the shade and not one step further. Expeditions that went in with saws and fire were found years later, as part of the bark.

entries.name: Catfish Deep
entries.summary: The plunge pool below the Sky-Hanging Falls, a lake three hundred zhang deep ruled by a catfish lord who owes the Old Tortoise his life and repays it in drowned poachers.
entries.lore: The Whiskered Lord is a Core Formation catfish as long as a war junk, blind, and able to taste a drop of blood anywhere in the lake. He serves the Old Tortoise and keeps the river below the falls free of anything that does not pay. Fishermen of the [[Floating Market]] pay him in salt to work his shallows. Divers who go after the lake bed, where the falls have dropped ten thousand years of upstream wrecks, rarely come up; those who do bring cold-iron anchors, Ascent Age bronze and the occasional sealed jar.

entries.name: Warm Creek Valley
entries.summary: A hot-spring valley on the range's eastern flank where a clan of white macaques bathes, gossips and spies for the White Ape King inside the Roc's own mountains.
entries.lore: The springs come up at blood heat from deep under the range, and the macaques have soaked in them for longer than the Roc has had a nest. They are the Ape King's distant kin and do not hide it. Their matriarch, a Core Formation macaque with a taste for human tea, lets travelers soak for a price and listens to everything said in the water. Sulfur crystals from the springs sell to alchemists, and the water itself mends damaged meridians if you can bear the heat.
entries.truth: The matriarch reports to both kings. The Roc knows and feeds her lies; the Ape knows the Roc knows, and reads the lies for what they reveal.

entries.name: Coiled Serpent Clan
entries.summary: The Golden Python's serpent vassals: pythons, vipers and kraits who carry his messages, guard his ore and collect his tithe in venom and metal across the south.
entries.lore: Every snake clan from the rift to the Yellow Marsh owes the Python tithe, and the Coiled Serpents collect it. They teach young serpents the Metal Dao of scales and the patience of the ambush, and they recruit by eating rivals who will not join. Their envoys are the most polite beasts at court. They guard the ore veins the Python feeds on and kill prospectors efficiently. Lately they have been patrolling the [[Fire Rat Warren]] burrows, less to keep anyone out than to keep something in.

entries.name: Roc's Nest Peak
entries.summary: The Storm Roc's eyrie on the highest peak of the west, wrapped in a storm that has not stopped in nine hundred years. His heir rules the domain while he sits at court.
entries.lore: The nest is a bowl of fused lightning-glass a li across on the summit, reached only by flight or by a stair cut by prisoners who did not survive the cutting. Vassal clans bring tribute to the lower terraces: takin calves, eagle down, ore and, in bad years, their own weakest young. The Roc's heir, a Nascent Soul roc who has not yet shown a human form in public, judges disputes there. Storm-tempered feathers shed around the nest are the finest Lightning Dao material on the Vast Wilds Continent, and gathering one is a death sentence.
entries.truth: Under the glass floor the Roc keeps what he means to burn in his Void Refinement tribulation at the tide's peak: nine thousand years of hoarded lightning-wood. The heir has counted it.

entries.name: Rope-Holders' Guild
entries.summary: The guild of forest guides who rope every client to themselves before entering the Evergreen. Cut the rope and the guide leaves you; keep it and you might live.
entries.lore: Guides learn which plants are awake, which are listening and which are hungry, and keep clients alive with three rules: never use a blade on anything green, never sleep on bare roots, never pick what has not fallen. Most deaths in the forest are clients who broke a rule. The guild charges a third of the harvest, sells maps it swears are accurate, and trains apprentices for ten years before they may lead. Half its guides are half-bloods with a plant-sense nobody can explain.
entries.truth: The plant-sense is a seed. Guides swallow one from the forest at their initiation, and after twenty years the oldest stop needing to eat.

entries.name: Thousand-Legs Ridge
entries.summary: A segmented ridge on the valleys' southern edge that the Jar-Mothers say is an Ascent Age centipede, asleep. Since last spring its legs have been moving.
entries.lore: From the air the ridge is plainly a body: three hundred armored segments, two antennae of black rock and a thousand rib-like spurs down each side. Last spring a segment split and something red showed inside, and since then the spurs have shifted a few zhang each month. The [[Scent-Seeking Clan]] has netted the ridge with sentry Gu and wants to jar the creature before it wakes; the [[Jarless Gang]] wants its eggs. A shed segment plate sells to refiners as Foundation-grade armor.

entries.name: Sheer Spine Range
entries.summary: The granite spine of the western Vast Wilds Continent, running north to south for eighty thousand li. Its peaks catch every storm off the Shoreless Sea.
entries.lore: The highest peaks stand above the weather and keep their ice through the jungle summer. Passes are few: the Falcon Gate in the north and the Steaming Pass by the [[Warm Creek Valley]] are the only routes a mortal could survive, and both are watched by the [[Thunder Falcon Clan]]. Lightning-struck spirit pines on the upper slopes yield thunder-wood, and the scree below the cliffs is rich in storm-iron. The range has been shaking since the tide began to rise.

entries.name: Bridgehead Town
entries.summary: The port where the Jade Strait island chain comes ashore. Walkers from Morning Star arrive with nothing, poachers leave with cores, and every price is chalked on the harbor wall.
entries.lore: At low tide the last island of the chain is a three-day wade from the harbor, and the [[Jade Strait]] walkers arrive half-drowned and broke. The harbor wall carries this month's prices: a Foundation-grade tiger core fetches 180 low-grade spirit stones here and three times that in the [[Jing Capital]]. The [[Apricot Grove Valley]] runs a buying hall for herbs and beast gall, the [[Core-Takers' Society]] hires crews in the Salt Lane, and the protectorate keeps a customs hall nobody pays. Fights are common. Killings are fined by the weight of the corpse.
entries.truth: The harbor master is a half-blood who reports every arrival to the [[House of Translated Tongues]] in Shared Roost City, which sells the list to the Beast Court.

entries.name: Core-Takers' Society
entries.summary: The poachers' guild of the frontier: crews, maps, buyers and burial money. It teaches the trade of taking cores from beasts that would rather keep them.
entries.lore: Anyone with a blade and ten low-grade spirit stones can join a crew. Members learn tracking, scent-masking with river mud, snare formations and the core cut: how to open a beast and lift its core before the qi bleeds out. Seniors appraise cores by color and heat. The Society pays a widow's share if a crew dies inside its maps, which is why everyone buys the maps. It hates beast tamers, who waste good cores on leashes, and it wants one thing badly: a Nascent Soul core, worth more than the Society itself.
entries.truth: The Society's best maps come from a gibbon courier of the [[Ridge of Long Calls]] who sells the Court's patrol routes. The Ape King knows, and uses the leak to choose which poachers die.

entries.name: Vine-Wound City
entries.summary: An Ascent Age city swallowed by a strangler fig the size of a kingdom. The fig rules the ruins as its domain, and it eats whatever sleeps beneath it.
entries.lore: The fig began as a seed on a palace roof and spent forty thousand years strangling the city around it; now towers, walls and streets stand inside its hollow trunks like bones inside a body. Ruin hunters come for Ascent Age artifacts, formation plates and libraries still dry in their vine-wrapped halls. The fig is a Core Formation spirit plant with no mind anyone has found, only appetite. It moves its roots at night, and campers wake a li from where they lay down, or do not wake.
entries.truth: The fig has a mind. It learned to read in the city's libraries, and it decides which hunters to let out by what they took.

entries.name: Molten Gold Hold
entries.summary: A fortified forge town of python-blooded half-bloods, the Golden Python's children, who refine artifacts with volcanic fire and their father's shed scales.
entries.lore: The Python has sired half-blood children for two thousand years and keeps the useful ones here. They have golden eyes, cool skin and a tolerance for heat that lets them work lava-fed forges bare-handed. They make blades of storm-iron and beast bone, armor of centipede plate, and gold-scale talismans that turn aside poison. Apprentices are taken from their own children and, for a steep fee, from outside. Their Forgemaster is Core Formation and answers only to their father, who takes half of everything.
entries.truth: The Forgemaster is forging war gear for the Roc's falcons and the Ape's rhinos at the same time, on her father's orders, and sabotaging one side's order. She has not been told which.

entries.name: Ginseng Child Valley
entries.summary: Southern valleys where ginseng roots old enough to grow legs live in hiding. Every alchemist on the continent wants one, and the ginseng children know it.
entries.lore: A ginseng root that lives a thousand years wakes, grows arms, legs and the face of a fat child, and runs at the first footstep. A thousand-year root is the heart of a Foundation pill; a ten-thousand-year root makes Core Formation pills by the furnace. The valley's children hide among ordinary ginseng and steal travelers' salt. Their elder, Grandfather Root, is ten thousand years old, Core Formation, and has not run in a century. Hunters still use the old method: a red thread tied to a leaf, and patience.
entries.truth: Grandfather Root has a bargain with the [[Rope-Holders' Guild]]: one ginseng child a year, chosen by him, in exchange for the guild keeping other hunters out. He picks the troublemakers.

entries.name: Market of Tested Medicines
entries.summary: The one market in the valleys open to outsiders, on stilts above the miasma line. Every seller must drink from their own wares in front of the buyer.
entries.lore: The rule is older than the clans' memory: a seller who will not taste their own medicine has no place in the market. Antidotes, healing Gu, curses with a guaranteed hour of death, miasma masks and Gu-proof talismans are all on the stalls, and buyers must show a Jar-Mother's token at the ladder or be turned back. A miasma mask lasts a day and costs a low-grade spirit stone; a good antidote for valley fever costs five. Outsiders who stay past dark should check their food for small movements.

entries.name: Gate of Beast Craft
entries.summary: A demonic puppet sect that builds war puppets from beast corpses. Its founder was thrown out of the Thousand Puppet Gate for being too ambitious.
entries.lore: Master Qiu Yan learned corpse refining in the Long Dusk Continent and came east with one idea: an immortal's corpse is rare, but a beast's is everywhere. The Gate's puppets are refined spirit beasts, tigers and eagles and once an elephant, that fight at their old realm and obey a bone flute. Disciples learn puppetry, corpse preservation and refining; recruits come from the [[Kingdom of the Dark Crossing]]'s stitching guilds. The Beast Court calls them robbers of its dead and pays a bounty on every disciple's head. The [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] would also like Qiu Yan back, in pieces.
entries.truth: Qiu Yan wants an Ascent Age beast to puppet, and he has chosen one: the pangolin of the [[Scale-Armor Mountain]]. He does not plan to wait for it to die.

entries.name: Realm of Twin Blood
entries.summary: A shard gate on the bay's tide flats, uncovered at the lowest tide every seven years. It admits only those who carry two bloods: half-bloods get in, everyone else burns.
entries.lore: The gate is a ring of white coral on the flats. At the seventh-year neap it drains dry for nine days, and anyone of mixed blood below Core Formation can walk through; pure humans and pure beasts who try are burned to the bone at the threshold. Inside is a shard where land and sea were never separated, and on its reefs grow Twin-Blood Fruit, which wake a bloodline by a full stage. The [[Hall of Woken Blood]] escorts its disciples in, the [[Blood-Lock Gang]] waits for them to come out, and the next low tide is next autumn.
entries.truth: The shard was a nursery for Ascent Age half-bloods. Its last keeper is still inside, and she asks every visitor which of their two bloods they would give up.

entries.name: Blood-Lock Gang
entries.summary: Slavers who work the coves around the bay, catching half-bloods for Morning Star nobles, beast-fighting pits and the Night Banquet's tables.
entries.lore: Their trade rests on one technique: a blood-lock talisman pressed into the skin that seals a half-blood's beast blood and leaves them as weak as a mortal. They hunt new arrivals in the [[Gate-Waiting Town]] before Shared Roost City admits them, sell shark-blooded divers to pearl lords and roc-blooded girls to collectors, and sell the rest to the [[Night Banquet Sect]] by the dozen. Their boss, a Core Formation woman called Aunt Lan, never sets foot inside Shared Roost City; she does not need to. Locks can be broken, but the breaking usually kills.
entries.truth: Aunt Lan is a half-blood herself and wears her own lock, a looser one that hides her blood but not her cultivation. Breaking it would make her stronger than anyone in the gang, and would show them what she is.

entries.name: Iron Rhino Ridge
entries.summary: The White Ape King's war camp on the Court's western edge, ruled by an armored rhino general who has waited three hundred years for a war worth fighting.
entries.lore: General Iron Horn is a Nascent Soul rhino of the Earth Dao whose hide turns flying swords, and his domain is a parade ground of trampled karst facing the [[Sheer Spine Range]]. Rhino, boar and bear clans drill there by the thousand, and this year the Ape King's eastern marchers are camped on its slopes. The camp eats a forest a month and buys its salt and iron through the [[Floating Market]] traders. Iron Horn has been urging the Ape King to strike before the Roc's ancient wakes.
entries.truth: If the Ape King hesitates again, Iron Horn will start the war himself with a raid on the [[High Pastures]], and let the kings argue about it afterward.

entries.name: Iron Fair
entries.summary: A fair town on the rift's northern rim where the Molten Gold Hold smiths sell weapons and refiners buy fire, ore and scale. Beasts in human form shop here for armor.
entries.lore: The Iron Fair has no walls; the rift's heat is its wall. Its stalls sell storm-iron blades, centipede-plate armor, fire-rat cloth and furnace time by the hour, and its buyers are half-bloods, Gu clan traders, smugglers who sail round the south cape and beasts who have only just learned to wear clothes. A Foundation-grade blade costs 400 low-grade spirit stones, a third more than in the Morning Star Continent and a third better. The Python's serpents tax every sale.

entries.name: Gate of One Heart
entries.summary: The outlaw school of beast tamers, hidden in the sea caves of the east coast. The Court kills its members on sight, and it keeps recruiting.
entries.lore: The Gate teaches the heart-bond, a contract in which a tamer and a beast share a sliver of each other's soul and feel each other's pain. Members call it partnership, not slavery; the Court says a bonded beast is no longer a beast and has it eaten. Disciples learn beast raising, feeding, bond seals and beast speech, and children who can hear beasts are recruited from the coast's fishing villages. They smuggle bonded beasts out to the Thousand Isles and the Morning Star Continent and want the Court to recognize the bond. The [[Thunder Falcon Clan]] hunts them.
entries.truth: The Gate's founder bonded a beast who is now a Nascent Soul lord at court. He has argued the tamers' case for two hundred years without ever saying why.

entries.name: Sea-Swallowing Caves
entries.summary: Sea caves that drink the tide and roar it back out. Behind the roaring mouths lie dry galleries where the outlaw tamers live and train.
entries.lore: Twice a day the tide rushes into the cave mouths and is spat back as spray a hundred zhang high, and the noise covers anything that happens inside. Past the flooded mouths, stairs cut by Ascent Age hands climb into dry galleries lit by glowworm colonies. The [[Gate of One Heart]] keep their beasts here, and the galleries smell of fish, fur and the salve tamers use on bond scars. Getting in means timing the tide to the breath; getting it wrong breaks bones.

entries.name: Pushed Frontier
entries.summary: The Vast Wilds Continent's human frontier, where the Jade Strait island chain comes ashore: two walled kingdoms and a Jing protectorate pushing into beast country one valley at a time.
entries.lore: Humans hold a strip of hills between the sea and the [[Thornwall]]; everything past the thorns belongs to the beasts. For two centuries the line barely moved. Then the White Ape King called his marcher lords west to face the Storm Roc, and the hills beyond the wall went quiet. Now poachers, herb diggers and loggers pour through every gap, core prices in the [[Bridgehead Town]] have halved, and the three human polities are racing to plant flags. Old frontier hands say the beasts are not gone, only counting.
entries.truth: The withdrawal is a feint aimed at the Storm Roc as much as at the humans. The tigers of the [[Brindled Ridges]] are lying up in the hills, and the Ape King has promised them every human head they take before the rains.

ties.why: The chain comes ashore at Bridgehead Town, bringing broke walkers from the Border Wilds and sending cores back.

entries.name: Alligator-Drum Clan
entries.summary: The alligators who collect the Old Tortoise's tribute and eat those who do not pay. Their bellowing carries a hundred li and sounds like war drums.
entries.lore: The clan numbers some three hundred spirit alligators, from Qi Condensation hatchlings to the Core Formation Drum-Mother, whose hide is like lacquered iron and whose grudges run a century deep. They patrol the channels, count the rice that goes into the river, and take payment in flesh from villages that short the tribute. They do not eat children, a rule the Tortoise imposed and they resent. Their shed scutes make the best drum-heads and shield faces in the delta, and the Drum-Mother sells them herself.
entries.truth: The Drum-Mother wants to be a king. She has been talking to the Storm Roc's envoy, who has promised her the delta when the Tortoise finally dies.

entries.name: Exhaling Pool
entries.summary: A pool at the marsh's heart that breathes out yellow fog every nine days. Those who stand at its edge on the ninth day come home smiling and die within the month.
entries.lore: The pool is a li across, perfectly round and warm. Every ninth day it heaves and exhales a wall of yellow fog that rolls out over the marsh, and every ninth night it draws a little air back in. Catchers time their work by it. Rare creatures gather at its edge, and so do rare herbs: the Yellow-Breath Lotus grows nowhere else and is the heart of a Core Formation pill of the Life Dao. The [[Pond of Toad Song]] toads guard it and will not say why.
entries.truth: It is a mouth. An Ascent Age toad as large as the marsh lies asleep under the mud, and the High Tide is quickening its breath: once every nine days now, once every eight next year.

entries.name: King-Cobra Mere
entries.summary: A reed mere ruled by a king cobra, vassal of the Golden Python. She collects the Python's venom tithe from every serpent in the marsh, and lately has been delivering it elsewhere.
entries.lore: The Hooded Queen is a Core Formation king cobra who eats other snakes and rules those of the marsh's western mere. Her domain is reeds, black water and the hum of insects, and she gathers the Python's tithe in sealed jade gourds of venom from every serpent clan in the marsh. Snake catchers pay her for licenses, and Gu raisers pay more. Her own venom stops a Foundation cultivator's heart in ten breaths, and her shed skins make the best poison-proof gloves on the Vast Wilds Continent.

entries.name: Ladder-Watch Cape
entries.summary: The tip of the North Cape, where the Broken Ladder is plainest to see. Pilgrims come for the Ladder-Watch, when the Stump hums and the cape's stones hum back.
entries.lore: A tower of Ascent Age jade stands on the cape, older than any kingdom, with a ferry stair that goes down into the sea and does not come up. When the Mirror is overhead the [[Ladder Stump]] hums, and the tower answers with a note that makes teeth ache for a hundred li. Pilgrims from three continents gather for it every year. Cultivators of the Space Dao meditate on the stair, and a few each decade see something in the water that changes their path.
entries.truth: The stair led to a ferry that crossed to the central continent. Its moorings still answer a ferry token, though nobody knows what would come to the stair if one were shown.

entries.name: Pit of Ten Thousand Bones
entries.summary: A karst sinkhole near the Court where beast tamers and their beasts are thrown together, alive. The bats clean the bones, and the pit is still not full.
entries.lore: The sinkhole is three hundred zhang deep with sheer walls and a lake of bone at the bottom. The Court's sentence for beast taming is the same for tamer and beast: both go down. Beasts that survive the fall are offered a bargain, kill the tamer and climb out on the bat lord's rope, and few refuse. At the top of the rope the Court eats them anyway. The pit's resentment qi is so thick that Death Dao cultivators pay the bats to be lowered in for a night. The walls are scratched with names in every script on the continent.
entries.truth: A tamer and her serpent survived the fall forty years ago, refused the bargain, and still live in a cave halfway down, fed by the bats. The bat lord thinks it is funny.

entries.name: Jar-Heaven Realm
entries.summary: A shard world the first Jar-Mother used as a jar. Every thirty-three years its gate opens for nine days to any realm, and what comes out is the strongest Gu in the world.
entries.lore: The gate is a bronze lid set in a cliff and sealed with the clans' blood. Inside, a world of venomous creatures has been fighting for nine thousand years, each generation eating the last, and the survivors are monstrous. Every thirty-three years the clans lift the lid and send in their best daughters to catch what they can; a Gu brought out of the Jar Heaven is worth a clan's ransom. Outsiders may buy a place for a mid-grade spirit stone and a blood oath. Most of those who go in are eaten.
entries.truth: The eldest Jar-Mother's great Gu came out of this jar as its last survivor. The shard has been breeding a successor ever since, and at the next opening it will be ready.

entries.name: Fertile Wilds
entries.summary: The Untamed River's delta and the North Cape: endless rice paddies farmed by human kingdoms under the Old Tortoise's peace, which costs a tenth of every harvest.
entries.lore: The [[Untamed River]] splits into nine hundred channels here before it reaches the Shattered Sea, and the land between them is the largest open farmland on the Vast Wilds Continent. It belongs to the Old Tortoise, one of the Court's four kings, who has not attended court in sixty years; he sends a carved shell with his vote. Humans farm by his leave: every autumn a tenth of the rice goes into the river, and the alligators of the [[Alligator-Drum Clan]] collect from those who forget. Both the Ape King and the Storm Roc have sent envoys this year. The Tortoise is said to be asleep.
entries.truth: He is awake. Every ten years an [[Armillary Pavilion]] astronomer comes to the [[Shell Mound]] with one question about how the Heaven Ladder was built, and he answers it, because he wants the Ladder rebuilt more than anyone alive.

entries.name: Jarless Gang
entries.summary: Men cast out of the matriarchal Gu clans who raise their Gu without jars, inside their own bodies. They sell cheap curses and do not care to whom.
entries.lore: Among the Jar-Mothers only women may keep a jar, and men who raise Gu are exiled. The exiles found that a body can serve as a jar: feed the Gu your blood, let them fight inside you, and become the jar's last survivor. The Jarless are gaunt, fearless and short-lived, and their curses cost a tenth of a clan curse. They sell to poachers, slavers and anyone else the clans refuse. Recruits are exiles, runaways and anyone willing to swallow a centipede. They want a Gu that can eat a Core Formation, and a jar to bring down on the clans.
entries.truth: Their leader has bred a Gu inside himself from the eggs of the [[Thousand-Legs Ridge]] centipede. It is growing faster than he is.

entries.name: Moonless Market
entries.summary: A smugglers' market on a hidden beach that opens only on moonless nights, when the Night Banquet's ships come in. Cores, Gu, hatchlings and people change hands by lantern.
entries.lore: On the night of each new moon, while the [[Night Banquet Sect]] holds its banquets across the sea, its ships are here instead, along with pirates from the [[Thousand Isles]] and smugglers out of Shared Roost City. Buyers bring spirit stones; sellers bring cores, beast gall, Gu, stolen eggs and the occasional captive. The Grey Strand Lord's lizards keep order and take a tenth. Prices run a third below Shared Roost City's, and there is no blood test, no law and no refund. By dawn the beach is empty and the tide has taken the footprints.

entries.name: Elephant Ford
entries.summary: The middle course of the Untamed River through flooded jungle, where the elephant clans cross on their long migration and answer to no king.
entries.lore: The [[Untamed River]] is two hundred li wide here in the rains, and the jungle stands in water half the year. The elephant clans own the middle reach by a custom older than the Court: each dry season they cross at the ford on their way to the Evergreen Deep and back, and the crossing is the nearest thing the Vast Wilds Continent has to a festival. Both kings have courted the Eldest Matriarch for a year. Poachers have learned that elephant cores are the largest of any land beast, and the [[Tusk-Saw Gang]] has started hunting the old ones.
entries.truth: The Eldest Matriarch has already chosen. She will side with whichever king hands her the [[Tusk-Saw Gang]], every last one of them, alive.

entries.name: Elephant Barrow
entries.summary: The valley where elephants go to die. It holds the bones and cores of every matriarch for forty thousand years, and the herds will hunt anyone who loots it to the end of the world.
entries.lore: Old elephants walk here alone when they feel death coming, and lie down among their grandmothers. The valley is a field of ivory and grey bone, and in each great skull lies a core the herds will not touch. A single matriarch's core would found a sect.
