The herds keep no guard and need none: every looter in living memory has been tracked down, once across the strait into the Morning Star Continent, and trampled with their families. Death Dao cultivators come to meditate on the bones and leave with nothing, which is allowed.
entries.truth: The [[Tusk-Saw Gang]] has found a way in without leaving a scent, using Gu bought from the [[Jarless Gang]]. They took three cores last year, and the herds still do not know.

entries.name: Hall of Woken Blood
entries.summary: The half-blood sect of Shared Roost City, which reads bloodlines and teaches half-bloods to wake the beast in their veins without losing the human.
entries.lore: Applicants bleed into a basin of spirit water and the Hall reads the colors: shark, roc, tiger, python and stranger things. Disciples learn body tempering, bloodline breathing and partial beast forms, and the best learn to fight a realm above their own for the length of one breath. The Hall takes every half-blood child who reaches [[Shared Roost City]] and asks nothing about where they came from. It hates the [[Blood-Lock Gang]] above everything and wants a method of full awakening that does not end, as it always has so far, in madness.
entries.truth: The Hall's founder achieved full awakening and did go mad. He is chained under the Hall, and the elders draw his blood to make their awakening pills.

entries.name: Heart-Vein Spring
entries.summary: A spring of milk-white water among the inner pillars where the Court's great vein breaks the surface. Only kings bathe in it, and anyone else is killed for looking.
entries.lore: Beneath the Court runs the richest spirit vein on the Vast Wilds Continent, Top-grade at its heart, and this is the only place it surfaces. The water is so dense with qi that a mortal who drinks a cupful bursts. The kings who attend bathe here before every council, and young beasts dream of it. As the tide rises the spring has grown from a pool to a lake, and the Court's lesser lords have started asking who it belongs to. Geomancers who have seen the Court from above say the pillars stand around the spring like a formation, and a true map of them sells for more than any herb.
entries.truth: Whoever leads the Court when the tide peaks will have the whole vein for a tribulation. That is what the Ape and the Roc are really fighting over: one of them will try for Void Refinement on it, and the vein cannot feed two.

entries.name: Blood Slope
entries.summary: The battlefield of the Thornwall War, forty-one years ago, where the resentment of ten thousand dead men and beasts has never settled. Ghost cultivators come to harvest; many stay.
entries.lore: The Thornwall War began, like every frontier war, on the [[Jade Strait]] islands; it ended here after nine days of fighting over a breached gate. Neither side buried its dead. The slope is grey grass over bone, and at dusk the dead finish the fight: men in rusted armor and beasts without skins. Resentment qi pools in the hollows thick enough to bottle, and Ghost Way cultivators pay well for it. Anything that sleeps on the slope wakes wearing someone else's wounds.
entries.truth: The island quarrel that started the war was staged by a [[Night Banquet Sect]] agent who killed a tiger cub and left a Jing spear in it. The Night Banquet bought the captives afterward.

entries.name: Snow Ape Clan
entries.summary: The White Ape King's own clan, white-furred apes who hold the Court's inner pillars and fight with the Fist Dao. Most of the Court's guards and all of its executioners are theirs.
entries.lore: Snow apes are born grey and whiten as they grow strong; a pure white ape is at least Core Formation. The clan teaches the Fist Dao and stone-climbing body arts, and its young train by breaking karst pillars bare-handed. The King's sons and grandsons lead it, two of them Nascent Soul. They hold the inner pillars, guard the [[Heart-Vein Spring]] and carry out the Court's sentences. They despise the Roc's falcons as noisy and are itching to prove it.
entries.truth: The King's eldest son is a half-blood, born to a human woman, and has bleached his fur for three hundred years. The Roc's spies are close to finding out.

entries.name: Scent-Seeking Clan
entries.summary: The Jar-Mother clan of hunters and avengers, whose scent Gu remember anyone who harms the valleys. They are why that warning is not a figure of speech.
entries.lore: A scent Gu is a beetle no bigger than a grain of rice that is fed a drop of someone's sweat and never forgets it; released, it will cross a continent to find them. The clan seeds the valley paths with sentry Gu that take the scent of every passer-by, and when a valley is harmed, they wake them all. They also sell the service: bring them something a person touched, and the clan will find that person anywhere. They have sealed the [[Thousand-Legs Ridge]] with Gu nets and mean to jar what sleeps there.
entries.truth: Last spring the [[Brindled Ridges]] tigers paid the clan to mark every poacher who took a cub's core. The marks wake when the rains come.

entries.name: Kingdom That Gazes at the Ladder
entries.summary: A small kingdom on the North Cape, the nearest land on the Vast Wilds Continent to the Broken Ladder. Its kings claim descent from Ascent Age ferrymen and send divers into the Shattered Sea.
entries.lore: On clear nights the [[Ladder Stump]] stands on the northern horizon as a black line across the Mirror, and the Kingdom That Gazes at the Ladder was built to watch it. Its priests keep the Ladder Calendar, read the Stump's hum as omens and sell those omens to merchants. Its divers, the best on the north coast, sail into the [[Shattered Sea]] for Ascent Age salvage and come back with jade, bronze and fewer crew. Children must hold their breath for a slow count of four hundred before they are allowed on a boat. A good haul makes a family rich; the Shattered Sea's scavenger sects make sure most hauls are not good.
entries.truth: The royal line really does descend from Ascent Age ferrymen, and the king's crown is a ferry token of the Heaven Ladder. Nobody alive knows what it opens.

entries.name: Flame Spine Ridge
entries.summary: The volcanic chain of the Red Rift: sixty thousand li of craters, lava lakes and black glass running from the Thunder-Shaken Ridges toward the Evergreen Deep.
entries.lore: Seen from the air the chain is a red seam across the southwest, smoking in a dozen places at once. North of it the land is old karst and granite; south of it the ground is young, cracked and sinking a zhang a century. Lava tubes run under the whole chain, and the ore veins they expose feed the Golden Python and the smiths alike. Sulfur, obsidian and fire crystal are mined along its flanks, and an eruption buries a mining camp every few years.

entries.name: Salt-and-Smoke Port
entries.summary: The Kingdom of the Dark Crossing's corpse port: smokehouses, salt pans and ship sheds that can be smelled fifty li downwind. The strait crossing to Long Dusk starts here.
entries.lore: Ships leave for Long Dusk every eight days with barrels of salted carcass and the occasional passenger who wants to visit the dead; a berth costs 20 low-grade spirit stones and a signed promise not to die aboard. The bone market sells Ascent Age beast bones dug from the [[Bone-Burial Caves]] caves, appraised by men with burned fingertips. Ghost Month closes the port for thirty days, and in that month the harbor lamps are turned to face the land.

entries.name: Herb-Bed Realm
entries.summary: A shard gate in a sunken glade that opens every forty years for thirty days and admits only Qi Condensation. Inside are Ascent Age herb beds that someone is still tending.
entries.lore: The gate is a doorway of living willow that leafs out only in its opening year; a Foundation aura withers it. Inside is a shard of terraced herb beds under two suns, weeded and watered, with no gardener in sight. Visitors who take only what they need come out with Ascent Age seeds that sell for a fortune in the [[Town of Last Letters]]; greedy ones come out with nothing and a gardener's mark on the palm. The next opening is in nine years, and sects across the Morning Star Continent are already training children for it.
entries.truth: The gardeners are descendants of Severance survivors, cut off for sixty-six thousand years. They are blind, they are kind, and they are running out of seed.

entries.name: Caverns of the Hidden River
entries.summary: The cave domain beneath the Court, where bat lords rule the underground rivers and keep the Court's prisons. Everything that disappears in the Forest of Peaks passes through here.
entries.lore: Under the pillars the karst is hollow for twenty thousand li: galleries, lakes and rivers running in the dark that surface far to the south as the [[Hidden-Flow River]]. The bat clans own all of it. Their lord, a Core Formation bat of the Death Dao, keeps the Court's prisoners, its executioners and its secrets. Guano from the deep halls is the richest spirit fertilizer on the continent, and the clans sell it carefully through half-blood middlemen. Blind white fish from the cave lakes cure night blindness and cause nightmares.
entries.truth: The bat lord rents cells to both kings. The Roc's three captured spies and the Ape's two sit in neighboring cells, and the bat lord has been letting them talk.

entries.name: Hidden Coves
entries.summary: The Vast Wilds Continent's east coast, a broken shore of jungle cliffs and sea caves facing the Thousand Isles. Smugglers, outlaw tamers and the sea clans' nesting beaches share it uneasily.
entries.lore: No human holds this coast, but plenty of humans work it. Pirate junks from the [[Thousand Isles]] and black-sailed ships from the [[Night Banquet Sect]]'s marshes slip into the coves on moonless nights to buy cores, Gu and stolen hatchlings at the [[Moonless Market]]. The giant lizard lord of the [[Giant Lizard Strand]] takes a cut and keeps the Court from looking. Sea turtles come ashore at the [[Hatching Sands]] under the sea clans' protection, the hornbills of the cliffs watch everything for the Storm Roc, and the outlaw tamers hide in the caves.
entries.truth: The Night Banquet's captains are sounding the coves for a deep harbor. The Banquet Master wants a foothold on Vast Wilds before anyone in Morning Star thinks of it.

entries.name: Town of Last Letters
entries.summary: The expedition town on the Evergreen's northern edge, where alchemists hire guides, buy rope and write the letter they hope nobody will need to send.
entries.lore: Every expedition member leaves a sealed letter at the Letter House before entering the forest. Letters unclaimed after a year go home with the dead traveler's effects, at the town's expense, which it recovers by auctioning the effects. Inns, guide halls, a pill shop that buys raw herbs at a third of Shared Roost City's price and an antidote stall line one muddy street. The half-blood guides who run the town pay the Court a salt tithe for the right to exist. The [[Apricot Grove Valley]] keeps an agent here with a standing order for Root Mother sap.
entries.truth: The Letter House reads every letter. Any that mention where a herb was found are copied and sold to the [[Rope-Holders' Guild]].

entries.name: Physicians' Terrace
entries.summary: A walled terrace on a karst tower at the Court's edge where the Apricot Grove Valley's beast physicians practice, envoys wait for audiences and human hostages live out their lives.
entries.lore: The [[Apricot Grove Valley]] leases the terrace from the Court and staffs it with a Nascent Soul elder and forty physicians who treat everything from a sick gibbon to a king's old wound, for fees paid in herbs only the Court can reach. Envoys from Shared Roost City, the Jar-Mothers and the human kingdoms wait here, sometimes for years. Seven human princes live here as hostages for their kingdoms' good behavior; the oldest arrived fifty years ago. Inside the walls a human is safe. One step outside without a seal, they are prey.
entries.truth: The Apricot Grove Valley elder treats the White Ape King's old wound in secret, and on the Valley Master's orders has been making it slowly worse. The Apricot Grove Valley would like a long war.

entries.name: House of Translated Tongues
entries.summary: Half-blood interpreters and brokers in Shared Roost City who speak to beasts and humans in their own tongues, and sell every conversation twice.
entries.lore: Most beasts below Nascent Soul cannot take human form or shape human words, so nearly every deal between the races needs a go-between. The House trains half-bloods with good ears in beast speech, carries letters to the Court, negotiates passage, ransoms captives and writes contracts for both sides. Its interpreters travel under both kings' seals. A Qi Condensation interpreter earns more than a Foundation guard, and a good one can get a human out of the [[Forest of Peaks]] alive.
entries.truth: The House is the Beast Court's ear in Shared Roost City. Its master reports to the [[Ridge of Long Calls]] gibbons, and its archive of contracts is the best map of human ambition on the Vast Wilds Continent.

entries.name: Jade Road
entries.summary: An Ascent Age causeway of green jade slabs that crosses the Yellow Marsh toward the Evergreen Deep. Half of it has sunk, and the half that has not is the only safe path.
entries.lore: The causeway runs straight as a sword for eight thousand li on jade pilings carved with cranes, and the miasma will not settle on it: the stone repels it to a hand's height. Expeditions walk it in single file and pray it holds; where slabs have sunk, they wade. The toads charge a toll at the Crane Gate halfway across. Appraisers argue about who built it, and why it points straight at the Root Mother.
entries.truth: It is the last stretch of the road that carried the Root Mother's seed from the foot of the Heaven Ladder to where she now stands. The jade still remembers the weight.

entries.name: Moon-Tide Realm
entries.summary: A shard gate in a tidal cave that opens at the spring tide of the eighth month every third year. Qi Condensation and Foundation may enter; anything stronger is spat back out.
entries.lore: When the year's highest tide floods the cave, the water inside turns silver and becomes a door, and it stays open for six days. Inside is a shard of shallow seas and moon-pale islands where oysters the size of houses grow Moon Pearls, a Foundation treasure for the Water and Ice Daos, and amphibious beasts that have never seen a human. The [[Gate of One Heart]] takes apprentices in to find their first companions. The sea clans say the realm is theirs and have started posting guards at the cave.

entries.name: Lingering Glow Coast
entries.summary: The Vast Wilds Continent's northwest coast, facing the Long Dusk Continent's endless dusk across the strait: drowned karst towers, corpse ships and a horizon that is never quite dark or light.
entries.lore: From these cliffs the western sky is always the color of a dying fire; it is the Long Dusk Continent's twilight, across the water. The coast trades with it. The [[Kingdom of the Dark Crossing]] salts beast carcasses and ships them to the corpse refiners of the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]], and the towers of the [[Forest of Sea Pillars]] hide coves for every kind of smuggler. The Storm Roc's sea eagles hold the towers and sink corpse ships when they feel like it. In Ghost Month the strait fills with drifting lights, and the dead who cannot find the Pale City come ashore here instead.
entries.truth: The corpse ships do not come back empty. For twenty years the Storm Roc has been buying the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] puppets through the Kingdom of the Dark Crossing and hiding them in the sea caves: an army that does not need to be fed.

entries.name: Clouded Leopard Forest
entries.summary: A canopy domain of clouded leopards, the Ape King's hunters in the high jungle. They take the Ape's toll from river traders and the heads of poachers who skip it.
entries.lore: The leopards live in the canopy and almost never touch the ground. Their lady, a Core Formation leopard called Smoke, rules from a hollow strangler fig and can cross her domain without moving a leaf. The domain is the Ape King's tollgate on the river: rafts of the [[Floating Market]] pay at the Leopard Steps, and poachers caught without a token are hung from the canopy by their ankles for the gibbons to report. Leopard-claw orchids grow on her trees and fetch a mid-grade spirit stone apiece in Shared Roost City.
entries.truth: Smoke takes a second toll for herself and lets the [[Tusk-Saw Gang]] pass through her canopy for a share of the ivory. If the Eldest Matriarch learns this, there will be no more leopards on the river.

entries.name: Miasma Valleys
entries.summary: Deep limestone gorges choked with yellow-green miasma, home of the Jar-Mother clans. Every creature here is venomous, and the people are worse.
entries.lore: The gorges cut a thousand zhang into the plateau's eastern edge, and miasma pours out of their floors like smoke from a kiln. In them live the [[Jar-Mother Clans]] in stilt villages hung above the miasma line, raising Gu in sealed jars. The Beast Court leaves the valleys alone, and so does everyone else who has heard the stories. Outsiders come for antidotes, curses and healing Gu through the [[Market of Tested Medicines]], the one market that will sell to them. This year two clans are feuding over a waking Ascent Age centipede.
entries.truth: The eldest Jar-Mother's great Gu ate the Golden Python's elder brother when he led the Court's last march into the valleys, seven hundred years ago. The Python has not forgotten, and he wants a Court strong enough to burn the gorges.

entries.name: Miasma Eye
entries.summary: The vent at the bottom of the deepest gorge, where the valleys' miasma rises from the earth. It is thick enough to move on its own and eats anything that goes down without a Jar-Mother's blessing.
entries.lore: Miasma pours out of a crack in the gorge floor like water from a spring, yellow-green and warm. Within a li of the vent it is thick enough to hold up a dropped stone, and things live in it that live nowhere else: transparent moths, bone-white toads, Gu that were never put in any jar. The Jar-Mothers lower their daughters on ropes to collect wild Gu at its edge, and those who come back are made clan mothers. Death Dao cultivators pay dearly for a night on the rim.
entries.truth: The miasma is alive: one colony of Gu older than the clans. The first Jar-Mother's first jar was a bowl dipped into it.

entries.name: Hall of Tortoise Omens
entries.summary: Diviners trained as shell pages at the Old Tortoise's court, who read the cracks in burned plastrons. Their omens are right often enough to be expensive.
entries.lore: Founded by former shell pages who wanted to be paid for what they had learned, the Hall teaches plastron divination, flood-and-star calendars and the Karma of questions: every question asked changes the answer a little. Novices spend their first year cleaning plastrons and their second learning which questions not to ask. Caravans buy route omens, kingdoms buy war omens, and in the last two years both beast kings have bought omens about each other. The Hall wants to learn the question the Tortoise has been asking the cracks for sixty thousand years.
entries.truth: The Tortoise's question is always the same: is she coming back? The cracks have always said yes.

entries.name: Thunder-Shaken Ridges
entries.summary: The high granite ranges of the western Vast Wilds Continent, the Storm Roc's country: peaks above the clouds, storms every afternoon and tremors no storm explains.
entries.lore: The [[Sheer Spine Range]] catches every storm that blows in off the Shoreless Sea, and lightning strikes its peaks more often than rain falls in the lowlands. The Storm Roc's eyrie crowns the range, though the Roc himself sits at court and leaves it to his heir; lately he flies home more nights than not. His thunder falcons have doubled their patrols, the takin herds have been told to fatten for an army, and the ridges have begun to shake. Herders blame thunder. Old beasts look toward the [[Scale-Armor Mountain]] and say nothing.
entries.truth: The Roc's heir has been meeting the Ape King's envoys in secret. He would rather inherit a peaceful Court than his father's war, and he is prepared to arrange for his father not to come home.

entries.name: Protectorate of the Quelled Wilds
entries.summary: The Great Jing Dynasty's toehold in the Vast Wilds Continent: a fortress protectorate at the strait landing, garrisoned by conscripts and ruled by an exiled prince who needs a victory.
entries.lore: Protector-General Yao, a great-grandson of the Ancestor Emperor and a Core Formation spear cultivator, lost a succession duel in the [[Jing Capital]] and was sent here to be forgotten. He commands 3,000 conscript cultivators, most of them Qi Condensation, who serve twelve years and are buried here more often than not. Children are registered at birth exactly as in the Morning Star Continent, and a spirit root means the barracks at nine. Yao's open plan is to carry a beast lord's head home; his standing order is to return every runaway from the [[Kingdom of Burned Registers]] in chains.
entries.truth: Yao has guessed that the Ancestor Emperor is eating the capital's veins. He is not trying to go home. He is building a throne here for the day the [[Jing Capital]] starves.

entries.name: Thorn-Planting Gate
entries.summary: The formation masters and spirit farmers who planted the Thornwall and keep it fed. Their beast-repelling talismans are sold on every frontier in the world.
entries.lore: The Gate's founder planted the first stretch of the [[Thornwall]] with blood-fed spirit thorn 180 years ago, and the three human polities have paid the Gate to extend and tend it ever since. Disciples learn spirit farming, thorn formations and talisman making; the entry test is to keep a blood-thorn cutting alive for a month on your own blood. Their Tiger-Bane talismans sell for two low-grade spirit stones in the [[Bridgehead Town]] and twenty in [[Ten Thousand Sails]]. They loathe the [[Core-Takers' Society]], whose crews hack gaps in the wall to save a day's walk, and they want one cutting of the Root Mother's line from the [[Mother's Shade]] to make it unbreakable.
entries.truth: The Thornwall's roots have reached a Mid-grade vein under the hills and are drinking it. In fifty years the frontier's fields will fail, and the Gate's elders have decided not to mention it.

entries.name: Venom-Catchers' Camp
entries.summary: A stilt camp on the marsh's edge where Gu apprentices and hired catchers trap venomous creatures for the Jar-Mothers' jars. Pay is good and funerals are frequent.
entries.lore: Catchers go out at dawn in miasma masks with bamboo tongs and clay pots and come back at dusk with toads, centipedes, scorpions and snakes, or do not come back. The [[Spring-Returning Clan]] runs the camp, pays by the creature and sells antidotes on credit. A live gold-banded centipede is worth a low-grade spirit stone, a Foundation-grade snake a hundred. Half-bloods, runaways and Qi Condensation cultivators too poor for a sect come here to earn, and a few earn enough to leave. Outsiders are welcome as long as they owe the camp money.

entries.name: Walking Wood
entries.summary: A forest of spirit mangroves that walk on their stilt roots, a few dozen li a year, toward the sea. Where they pass, the marsh becomes forest, and anything in the way becomes soil.
entries.lore: The mangroves came north out of the Evergreen Deep three thousand years ago and have been walking ever since, a slow green tide across the marsh. Their roots strangle what they step on, and their fallen leaves poison everything but crabs. The grove is ruled by the Eldest Root, a Core Formation mangrove that speaks by creaking. Its bark yields a red dye and a Wood Dao tonic, and cutters who take it from fallen limbs are tolerated. Cutters who take an axe to a living tree are planted.
entries.truth: The grove is not wandering. It is walking away from the [[Exhaling Pool]], because trees feel the ground better than beasts do.

entries.name: Long Dusk Continent
entries.summary: A continent in endless twilight under the Fallen Ladder. Ghost courts, corpse refiners and the richest graves in the world.
entries.lore: When the Heaven Ladder broke, its upper span came down across the Long Dusk Continent: two hundred thousand li of immortal jade lying on the land. Its shadow never lifts. The dead of the Severance never left either, and the Court of No Light rules them from the Pale City with laws, registers and judges. The Thousand Puppet Gate mines the Fallen Ladder's tombs for immortal corpses. The living farm the sunlit coasts and pay the dead for the privilege.
entries.truth: Some of the 'dead' in the Pale City came through from the Nether Shard and were never citizens of Severed Heaven at all.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Dark Walkers
entries.summary: A living kingdom of foresters in the northern Grey Forest who never light lamps outdoors, because light draws the dusk moths, and who see in the grey better than any ghost.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of the Dark Walkers walk in near darkness from birth; their eyes are large and pale, and they read by the glow of orchid sap. A council of village elders rules and pays tribute to both ghost fiefs. Children learn the forest by touch and smell, and the first lesson is to stand still when the moths come. Grey timber, orchid sap and moth silk are the kingdom's wealth, sold at the Lampless Market. The Shadow-Refining Sect recruits here every Ghost Month and takes the children who can see a soul outside its body.

entries.name: White Bone Plain
entries.summary: The plain south of the Ladder where the falling span killed the old Long Dusk Continent: bones in every furrow, the Court's oldest dead, and the busiest fields of the corpse trade.
entries.lore: When the span fell, the blast crossed this plain faster than sound, and sixty-six thousand years have not buried what it killed. The soil is half bone. The Court claims every skeleton as the property of a registered soul; the Puppet Gate says a soul that has moved on leaves its bones to whoever digs. Licensed gatherers with Court seals and unlicensed crews with Gate puppets work the same fields, and the bone war kills a few hundred a year. Every Ghost Month the plain's dead stand up and march north through the Heart-Piercing Gallery to be counted.
entries.truth: Some skeletons never stand in Ghost Month: their souls went to the Nether Shard and never came back. Lately the Court has registered returnees under those same names, and nobody has checked the bones.

entries.name: Realm of Broad Daylight
entries.summary: A secret realm on the Dawn Shore whose shard world has a whole day of full sun. Its gate opens every twelve years and admits only those below Foundation Establishment.
entries.lore: The gate is a ring of standing stones that fills with sunlight for nine days when the shard passes close; it cracks under any aura above Qi Condensation. Inside lies a sunlit valley of the old central continent: grass, bees, fruit trees and a twelve-hour day, the only full day most Long Dusk children will ever see. Sun-loving herbs grow wild, and dawn lotus seeds from there sell for a fortune. Some children come back weeping, and a few refuse to come back at all. The next opening is in the autumn of 3,128.
entries.truth: The shard's sun is not a sun. It is a lamp the Ascent Age left burning, and it is running down: each opening, the day inside is a few breaths shorter.

entries.name: Sun-Embracing Sect
entries.summary: The strongest orthodox sect of the rice coast, whose disciples hoard sunlight in their bodies and fight best at noon. It holds the lower springs of the new yang vein.
entries.lore: The Sun-Embracing Sect disciples sit in the coast's three hours of sun every day and store it in their meridians, a slow body-refining art that leaves them warm to the touch and hard for ghosts to grip. The sect teaches Fire Dao, medicine for grave cold, and the farming of sun-loving herbs on mirror-lit terraces. It recruits at the harvest fairs: children hold a sun-salt crystal, and those who make it glow are taken. It despises the Shadow-Refining Sect, owes the Court nothing, and pays the Year Tithe anyway.
entries.truth: The founder bought the sect's first lease by selling the Court a list of rebel cultivators. The Court still has the list, in his handwriting.

entries.name: Water-Parting Realm
entries.summary: A secret realm whose gate lies in the drowned capital's palace, under thirty zhang of water. It opens every fifteen years and admits only those below Core Formation.
entries.lore: When the shard passes close, a bubble of dry air forms around the gate for thirty days, and anyone who can reach it through the water can walk in; a Core Formation aura bursts the bubble. Inside is a dry, sunlit land of terraced fields and a walled town whose people speak an old form of the Long Dusk tongue and trade grain and lamp oil for news. Sects send Foundation disciples to trade and to search the hills for Ascent Age herb gardens. The next opening is in the summer of 3,130.
entries.truth: The townsfolk descend from old Long Dusk people who fled into the shard the day the span fell. Their elders keep a record of that day, including what the Pale Sovereign was doing on the Ladder.

entries.name: Prefecture of the Broken Army
entries.summary: A ghost fief of soldiers killed by the falling span: an army that still stands in formation over its own bones and treats the bone trade as grave robbery.
entries.lore: When the span fell, an army of the old Long Dusk Continent was drilling on this plain. It died in its ranks, and its ghosts never broke formation. Their general holds the fief from the Court and runs it like a camp: the living are quartermasters' families who keep the army's rolls, and children learn the drill and the names of the dead. Diggers who enter without the general's leave are met by soldiers who stand up out of the ground. In the bone war he sides with the Court, but he has refused its orders twice.

entries.name: Fading Glow Sword School
entries.summary: The sword school of the evening coast, whose Sword and Fire arts draw on the last light of the day, and whose disciples hold the coast against the spring beasts for a fee.
entries.lore: Fading Glow swords are tempered at sunset and the school's techniques are strongest in the last hour of light, so it duels, hunts and trains at dusk. It teaches Sword Dao, Fire Dao and some medicine. It recruits at the evening markets with a test: hold a blade still while the sun goes down, and those whose blade catches the last light are taken. It hates corpse refiners on principle and kills Gate agents on sight, which pleases the Court and costs the coast, which pays its fee in grain.

entries.name: Long Lantern Road
entries.summary: The road between the Pale City and the Court's terraces, lined with ten thousand cold lanterns. On it you are a guest; off it, without a pass, you are fair game.
entries.lore: Lamp-Keepers from the Kingdom of the Lamp-Keepers walk its length once a year to rekindle each lantern. The hungry dead of the plain gather just beyond the light and watch travelers, and the Court allows them anyone who steps off the stones without a pass. Petitioners walk it on foot to show humility before the Court; the rich hire living porters so their own feet never touch it. Every thousand li there is a pilgrims' inn staffed by ghosts who charge in ash notes.

entries.name: Sunken Vales
entries.summary: Valleys south of the Ladder's foot that sank when the span fell and filled with sea: drowned towns, water ghosts, a floating market of memories, and outlaw dead hiding from the registers.
entries.lore: The impact dropped this land a hundred zhang and the Shattered Sea ran in along every valley. Towns of old Long Dusk stand under brackish water, their roofs a hazard to boats. Stilt villages fish silver eels and dive for relics by day; at night the drowned of the Sea Bell Prefecture come up to trade. The Night Tide Market floats on rafts in the largest vale, where ghosts sell memories outside the Pale City's tax. Unregistered dead hide in the deep towns, and the Court's hunters come looking every Ghost Month.
entries.truth: The vales are still sinking, a finger's breadth a year, always toward the span. Something under the Ladder's south face is drawing the land down, and the Sea-Swallowing Mouth grows wider every decade.

entries.name: Kingdom of Morning Radiance
entries.summary: The rebel kingdom of the Dawn Shore, which stopped paying the Year Tithe forty years ago and has kept the dead out since with towers full of stored morning light.
entries.lore: The Lu dynasty rules with the Sun-Reflecting Gate as patron and garrison. Every child takes a turn polishing mirrors at dawn and learns the tower drills for Ghost Month. Most have never seen a tax ghost and think the old stories are jokes; their grandparents remember. Refugees from tithe-paying lands crowd its towns, betting the towers will hold, and its ships carry mirrors and dawn jars to anyone who means to defy the Court. Its port, the Port of the Broken Silhouette, is its window on the world and the source of most of its money.
entries.truth: The stored light is weaker every year as the dusk deepens. The Sun-Reflecting Gate's engineers have calculated that this Ghost Month or the next, the towers will go dark before midnight.

entries.name: Lamp-Bearers' Society
entries.summary: The tomb raiders' guild of the Long Dusk Continent. It sells lamps, maps and rescue pledges, buys finds at a fixed discount, and assigns the crews the Marquis licenses to the Ladder's lower halls.
entries.lore: Members carry a brass lamp stamped with their rank and swear one oath: never put out a partner's lamp. The Society keeps its hall in the Kingdom of Broken Doors and posts along the whole span, buys finds at seven tenths of auction price, and sends rescue crews into the halls for a fee paid in advance. Appraisers, formation breakers and geomancers learn the trade here. Its founder, a Nascent Soul raider, came out of the deep halls blind and has not left the hall since. It pays the Court's licenses and sells bodies to the Gate, and both hate it.
entries.truth: The founder carried an Upper Realm token fragment out of the deep halls. Doors open for him that open for nobody else, and the Society's best finds come from halls only he can enter.

entries.name: Red Spring Valley
entries.summary: A valley where a yang spirit vein broke the surface nine years ago, the only one in the Long Dusk Continent: hot red springs, fire herbs, and three sects fighting over the lease.
entries.lore: The vein is mid-grade and still rising, and its springs run hot enough to cook rice. Fire herbs nobody had seen in the Long Dusk Continent for ages sprouted in the first year, and fire-rooted cultivators stuck for decades broke through within months of sitting in the steam. The Sun-Embracing Sect holds the lower springs, two smaller sects hold the upper slopes, and nobody holds the middle, where the duels happen. Ghosts will not come within ten li, and the coast's rich have started building summer houses.
entries.truth: Yin and yang veins draw each other up. The Shadow-Refining Sect's elders know that a yang vein this close to their own means that, within a century, one will swallow the other.

entries.name: Heart-Piercing Gallery
entries.summary: A gallery running straight through the Fallen Ladder from the bone plain to the Pale Plain, the only safe crossing of the span in the middle of the continent.
entries.lore: It is seven thousand li long and wide enough for an army, a crossing hall from the days when the Ladder stood. The Court holds both ends and charges the living a year for the passage; the dead pass free. Every Ghost Month the dead of the bone plain march through it to be counted in the Pale City, and nobody living uses it that month. Side halls branch off into the span's interior, and raiders pay the gate wardens to look away.

entries.name: First Light Cliff
entries.summary: A headland on the Dawn Shore where the first sunlight in Long Dusk lands each morning, and the only place outside a secret realm where the dawn lotus grows.
entries.lore: For a few breaths after sunrise the cliff top is fully lit and the dawn lotus opens: a spirit herb that blooms only in direct sun and dies if it is shaded. Alchemists use its petals in Foundation Establishment pills for fire-rooted cultivators, and one bloom sells for a mid-grade spirit stone in the Pale City. The Sun-Reflecting Gate holds the cliff and lets pickers in for a third of the harvest. Pilgrims come from every coast to stand in the first light once in their lives.

entries.name: Light-Hoarders' Guild
entries.summary: The guild of salt masters and light merchants that controls the sun-salt trade, sets its price, and decides which smugglers live long enough to retire.
entries.lore: The guild grades every crystal, keeps the warehouses where sun-salt is stored in black jars, and lends against stored light the way banks lend against spirit stones. It trains formation masters to build light-storage arrays and alchemists to refine sun-salt into yang pills, and it recruits from salt-raking families. Officially it sells only to the coasts; in fact it runs the smuggling routes into the ghost lands and pays the Prefecture of the Shaded Sands to look away. Its rival is the Sun-Reflecting Gate, whose mirrors make sun-salt less necessary.
entries.truth: The guild holds forty years of sun-salt in a vault under Bright Salt Port. It has one buyer for all of it, an agent of the Pale Sovereign offering a price nobody in the guild can explain.

entries.name: Eastern Diggings
entries.summary: The Puppet Gate's concession on the Ladder's south face near the coast, where puppet crews cut new breaches for immortal bodies and pay nobody for them.
entries.lore: A Core Formation deacon of the Gate runs the diggings with five hundred laboring puppets and a few hundred living debtors who signed their bodies over. Debtors who die are refined on site and go back to work. Lesser bodies are sold to coastal refiners; the best are shipped west to the Gate. The Marquis of the Prefecture of the Barred Stair raids the diggings every season, and the deacon has stopped reporting losses so his masters will not replace him. Debtors' children work the sorting sheds and are written into their parents' contracts.
entries.truth: The deacon broke into a hall nobody had opened since the Severance and told the Gate it was empty. It was not, and he is waiting to hear what the thing inside will pay him.

entries.name: Puppet-Duel Terrace
entries.summary: A jade arena below the Gate's cliff where puppets fight for wagers and buyers watch to choose. Its champion, a nameless sword puppet, has not lost in two hundred years.
entries.lore: Fights are held every ten days; anyone may enter a puppet for a fee, and the Gate takes a tenth of every wager. The champion is a sword puppet refined from an Ascent Age body at Core Formation, and it fights better than any puppet should: it feints, it adapts, and once it refused to kill a beaten opponent. The Gate's master calls it the finest work of his life and has refused every offer for it.
entries.truth: The champion is not empty. Its body's owner never left it, and he has spent two hundred years relearning the world from inside. He is deciding when to stop pretending.

entries.name: Port of the Broken Silhouette
entries.summary: The Dawn Shore's port on the Shattered Sea, named for the Stump's black outline against the Mirror on clear nights, and the rebel kingdom's link to the outside world.
entries.lore: Scavenger ships from the Shattered Sea islands moor here to sell Ascent Age salvage, storm-silk and rift-glass, and to buy dawn jars, which keep sea ghosts off a deck at night. The harbor master is a Foundation cultivator of the Sun-Reflecting Gate. Every ship from the Court's lands is searched for levy ghosts hidden in the cargo, and every few years one is found. On the nights the Stump hums, the whole town goes down to the water to listen.

entries.name: Beast-Crossing Shoals
entries.summary: Sandbars on the Evening Sun coast where spirit beasts from Vast Wilds come ashore each spring after swimming the strait: starving, exhausted, and worth a fortune.
entries.lore: At the spring low tides the strait narrows and sandbars run out from both coasts. Spirit beasts work their way down the Sleeping Beast's island chain over a season, swim the last gap and drag themselves ashore here: sea leopards, horned boars, river serpents and, every few years, something at Core Formation. Exhausted beasts are the easiest to tame, and tamers from across Long Dusk camp on the dunes with nets and meat; the rest come for the cores. Locals call the first night of the crossing the Feast, and nobody is sure who is meant to be eating.

entries.name: Towers of Returning Light
entries.summary: The chain of mirror towers along the Dawn Shore that catch the first hour of morning and pour it back out at night. They are the only reason the rebel kingdom still stands.
entries.lore: One hundred and eight towers stand along the hills, each a bronze mirror on a stone column, linked by arrays that pass stored light down the line. At dusk the mirrors turn inland and lay a thin gold light along the border, and ghosts will not cross it. Each tower is kept by a Sun-Reflecting Gate disciple and a family of mortal polishers paid in sun-salt. Two towers have failed in forty years; the villages behind them are empty.

entries.name: Realm of the Flying Hall
entries.summary: A hall of the Ladder flung into orbit when the head burst, now circling Severed Heaven as a shard world. Its gate opens in the jade scree every twenty-seven years, for Foundation cultivators and below.
entries.lore: The gate opens for eighty-one days and cracks under any aura above Foundation Establishment. Inside is an intact stretch of the Ladder's interior: stairs going up into nothing, furnished halls, and tombs whose bodies the Gate would kill for. The Gate and the Court both send teams of young disciples, and every opening turns into a battle. The last one closed with forty dead and a hall of Ascent Age refining furnaces still unlooted. The next opening is due in 3,129.

entries.name: Sealed Bone Works
entries.summary: A bone concession licensed by the Court to the Tan family, who dig only bones whose souls the registers say have moved on, and sell them under the Court's seal.
entries.lore: Every skull the Tans lift is checked against a register extract and stamped; unsealed bones are reburied. Licensed bone sells for twice the wild price, because buyers know the Court will not come after it. The Tans rule their diggers' villages as lords, and children learn to read register numbers and stack skulls by them before they learn their own letters. Bone-jade, the bones of cultivators that kept their qi, goes to formation masters, and bone ash to talisman makers. Gate crews raid the stacks every year.
entries.truth: The Tans' register extracts come from a clerk who forges them. Half the bones they sell as moved on belong to souls still living in the Pale City, and two of them have filed complaints.

entries.name: Kingdom on Stilts
entries.summary: A kingdom of stilt villages and divers in the Sunken Vales, who fish silver eels, dive for relics in drowned towns by day, and never touch the water after dark.
entries.lore: A family of master divers rules from a palace on stilts above the drowned capital, and the throne goes to whoever dives deepest at the coronation. Children swim before they walk and dive for relics at eight. The kingdom pays the Court its tithe and the drowned their dues, and sells relics at the Night Tide Market and in Hollow Jade Port. Its divers hire out to anyone who wants something raised. Spirit-rooted children are taken by a Water Dao sect from the Shattered Sea, which pays their families in pearls.

entries.name: Kingdom of Light Salt
entries.summary: The sun-salt kingdom of the south coast, whose flats grow the crystals that store daylight, and whose people are the only sunburnt folk in the Long Dusk Continent.
entries.lore: A council of salt masters rules, each holding a stretch of the flats, and their port is Bright Salt Port at the mouth of the Jade Sand River. Children rake salt from the age of six and are brown and freckled, which inland people find shocking. The kingdom pays the Year Tithe and sells sun-salt openly only on the coasts, because the Court bans it in its fiefs; most of its wealth comes from not asking where the smugglers go. The Azure Wave Palace takes its toll in salt at the harbor mouth.

entries.name: Bone Fair
entries.summary: The market town of the bone plain, where bone-jade, grave goods and bodies are bought and sold, and the Bone-Sorters' Guild weighs every load.
entries.lore: Wagons of bone come in from the pits every morning and are sorted by grade: plain bone for glue and fertilizer, bone ash for talisman ink, bone-jade for formation bases, and bodies that kept their flesh for refiners. Court-sealed and wild bone are sold in separate halls, and fights between the two are common. Alchemists come for marrow-moss, a yin herb that grows only in bone, and appraisers buy grave goods by the sack. The town walls are skulls set in lime, and each one has a register number.

entries.name: Sea Bell Prefecture
entries.summary: The ghost fief of the drowned: the dead of the towns that sank when the span fell, who live under the water of the Sunken Vales and ring a temple bell at every turn of the tide.
entries.lore: Their lord was the abbot of a temple that went under with its bell, and he rules from the drowned bell tower, still in his robes. The drowned come up at night to trade and to collect their dues from the stilt villages: fish, lamp oil, and the names of everyone who has died since. They resent the Court's tax ghosts as much as the living do and pay the Court late. A child who falls into the water after dark belongs to the fief, unless the family pays to get it back.

entries.name: River Lamp Temple
entries.summary: A Buddhist ferry mission from the Myriad Sands Continent, a daughter house of the Thousand Lamps Temple, that sends lantern boats down the Soul-Sending River to carry souls toward rebirth, beyond the Court's reach.
entries.lore: Monks crossed the strait four thousand years ago to guide the Long Dusk Continent's lost dead. Each Ghost Month they launch lantern boats down the Soul-Sending River, and a soul that boards one is carried out to sea and past the Nether Shard's pull. The Court licenses them to ferry only strays it has not registered, so grieving families pay the temple to get their dead aboard before the registrars arrive. The monks train in vajra body, Karma Dao and medicine, and treat the grey cold of the pass brush for free. The abbot, a Nascent Soul, came from the Thousand Lamps Temple's lamp hall.
entries.truth: The temple ferries registered souls too and burns the receipts; two judges in the Pale City take a cut in years. The abbot sends every soul's account to the Thousand Lamps Temple, which is mapping how the registers work.

entries.name: Dusk Harbor
entries.summary: The port of the evening coast on the strait to the Vast Wilds Continent, where grey timber and corpse candles go out and beast cores, herbs and half-bloods come in.
entries.lore: The port opens at the first gold light and closes at full dusk; ships that arrive after dark lie offshore until the next evening. Traders from Shared Roost City keep a hall here, and half-bloods unwelcome on the Vast Wilds Continent's coast find work as guards and tamers. Beast cores sell cheaper here than anywhere else in the Long Dusk Continent. Each spring the harbor chain is raised against beasts swimming in, and the town keeps a bounty board for anything that gets past it.

entries.name: Terrace of Returned Souls
entries.summary: A terrace against the Ladder's north face where the barrier to the Nether Shard is thinnest. Every Ghost Month souls come through it claiming to be the Long Dusk Continent's long-lost dead.
entries.lore: The Court calls them returnees: souls pulled to the Nether Shard ages ago who find their way home when it passes close. Each Ghost Month a few hundred walk out of the dark at the foot of the span, are judged on the terrace and, if their names are in the old registers, enrolled. The rest of the year the air is so cold that breath freezes into small white flowers, which alchemists buy for yin pills. Raiders who camp there wake with someone else's dreams.
entries.truth: Most returnees were never Severed Heaven's dead. Something on the far side learned the names in the old registers, and every Ghost Month it sends more.

top.note: a judge sits here in Ghost Month

entries.name: Grey Spine Ridge
entries.summary: A low range running down the grey forest from the rice coast toward the Ladder's head, splitting the rivers that run north to the strait from those that run west to the outer sea.
entries.lore: Its slopes are bare grey stone above the trees, the only high ground in the Grey Forest, and on clear days its summits catch a few minutes of sun. Hermits of every Way keep caves along it. Grey wolves den on the west face, and their pelts sell in the Evening Sun for cloaks that hide body heat from ghosts. The old road from the rice coast to the Ladder's head follows the crest, colder than the forest road but safer.

entries.name: Grey Forest
entries.summary: The pale forest north of the Ladder's head, grown on yin instead of light: ash-bark trees, ghost-lamp orchids, high-grade yin veins and the Ghost Way sects that drink from them.
entries.lore: The Grey Forest's trees grow grey and leafless, and their sap glows faintly, so the forest is never fully dark and never bright. Ghost-lamp orchids and shade ginseng grow wild. Dusk moths swarm to any flame, so locals walk without lamps and trade by touch. The Shadow-Refining Sect holds the yin vein at the Dim Spring and grows fastest in Ghost Month. Two ghost fiefs share the forest and quarrel over every border tree. In the west the trees end at fog cliffs on the Shoreless Sea, where the Azure Wave Palace's shark patrols take toll from the few boats that fish there.
entries.truth: The grey is spreading north toward the rice coast at about a li a year, and faster since the tide began to rise. The coast kingdoms have noticed their harvests shrinking. Nobody has noticed why.

entries.name: Mausoleum-Guard Prefecture
entries.summary: The Court's march-fief on the north face of the Ladder's head, garrisoned by tomb wardens who guard the bodies of the Court's subjects from the Puppet Gate.
entries.lore: Its dead were the Ladder's tomb wardens before the fall and never left the post. They patrol the halls from inside, through passages the Gate has never mapped, and burn any digging crew they find. Their living subjects are scouts and guides who know every gorge; children run messages between watch posts and learn to tell a Gate puppet by its walk. The Court pays bounties here in years: five for a Gate disciple's head, fifty for a puppet's control talisman.

entries.name: Bone-Sorters' Guild
entries.summary: The guild that grades, weighs and sells the bone plain's bones. It holds Court licenses, sells to the Puppet Gate, and sets the price of bone-jade for half of the Long Dusk Continent.
entries.lore: Every licensed load crosses a guild scale and gets a grade; unlicensed loads get one too, for a bigger fee. The guild trains appraisers who can tell a cultivator's bone from a mortal's by touch and read its old realm from the marrow, and it recruits the orphans of the pits. It keeps the peace in the Bone Fair, and its masters sit on both sides of the bone war: the guild pays the Court's licenses and the Gate's protection, and both know it.

entries.name: Kingdom of Borrowed Years
entries.summary: A rice kingdom where the poor mortgage years of their lives to the rich, and the Court notarizes every loan for a fee paid in years.
entries.lore: A year-broker will pay a farmer three sacks of rice for a year off the end of his life and sell it to a landlord who wants to live to see a grandson married. The transfer is drawn up at a Court notary's shrine and sealed with a brush on both palms. Debts pass to children: a child whose parents sold forward wears a red thread at the wrist. Landlord families live to a hundred and twenty as mortals; their tenants rarely pass fifty. The River Lamp Temple preaches against the trade and runs the only free clinic, and the brokers pay thugs to burn it every few years.
entries.truth: The Court's notaries keep one year in ten from every transfer. The biggest landlord in the Kingdom of Borrowed Years is the Court.

entries.name: Kingdom of Gold Foil
entries.summary: A paper-making kingdom on the rice coast that prints the ash notes ghost markets spend, and pays its tribute to the Court in paper instead of years.
entries.lore: Grey reed from the marshes is pulped, pressed and stamped with gold foil and the Court's seal; burned at a shrine, an ash note arrives in the ghost markets as money. The Zhi family's mills employ most of the kingdom, and children fold notes from the age of five. Because its paper keeps the economy of the dead running, the kingdom pays no Year Tithe, and the whole coast envies it. Spirit-rooted children go to the Vermilion Brush Academy to learn seal-carving. Forging the seal is the one crime the Court punishes in person.
entries.truth: The Zhi family has been printing extra notes for twenty years and burning them at a hidden shrine. Prices in the ghost markets are rising, and the Court's auditors have started asking why.

entries.name: Vault of Silence
entries.summary: A sealed vault beside the Court's terraces where its Bureau of Quiet keeps memories it has bought, confiscated, or cut out of its own subjects.
entries.lore: Memories the Court rules dangerous end here: deaths too painful to keep, secrets of the living, and every memory of the Outer Demon War the Bureau can buy. Ghosts who hold such memories are paid in years to give them up, and those who refuse are judged. The vault is warded so that divine sense comes back empty and anyone who steps inside forgets why they came. A Nascent Soul judge keeps the key. Thieves who try for it are found wandering the Long Lantern Road, smiling, without their names.
entries.truth: The Bureau is not mourning the war. Some of those memories hold the Nameless Sealer's name, and the Sovereign means to own every copy of it.

entries.name: Crystal Strand
entries.summary: The Long Dusk Continent's south coast on the Shoreless Sea: salt flats that grow sun-salt, the only light ghosts fear, and fishing kingdoms that pay the sea clans in fish and the dead in years.
entries.lore: Sun-salt forms on the Crystal Strand flats where the dusk is thinnest: crystals that soak up daylight and give it back for months. A finger of good sun-salt keeps a hut safe from the hungry dead all winter and buys a week's food anywhere under the Ladder. The Court bans it in its fiefs, so it travels by smuggler. The salt kingdoms pay two masters: years to the Court, and fish and salt to the Azure Wave Palace's shark-folk at every harbor. The Jade Sand River comes down from the bone plain, and panners work its mouth at low tide.
entries.truth: The dusk is creeping. The flats yield less sun-salt every decade as the Ladder's shadow lengthens with the tide, and in a few centuries the Long Dusk Continent will have no light it can store.

entries.name: Kingdom of Golden Tangerines
entries.summary: An orchard kingdom in the evening hills whose dusk tangerines, a spirit fruit that ripens only in the late gold sun, are sold to alchemists on three continents.
entries.lore: The orchards face southwest to catch every minute of evening light, and the kingdom keeps its calendar by the sun's last hour. A mortal dynasty reigns, guided by a family of spirit farmers who tend the oldest trees. Children pick from the age of six and learn to tell ripe fruit by its glow at dusk. A dusk tangerine restores a Qi Condensation cultivator's qi in moments, and the Apricot Grove Valley's buyers take most of the crop. The kingdom pays the Year Tithe like any other; a tangerine is the one bribe a tax ghost refuses, because it cannot taste it.

entries.name: Prefecture of the Old Towers
entries.summary: A ghost fief west of the Pale City held by the dead nobility of the old Long Dusk Continent, who were kings before the Ladder fell and still expect to be bowed to.
entries.lore: Its lord was king of a realm the span crushed, and his court of ghosts still keeps the old ranks, robes and feuds. The living who farm his fields under light arrays are serfs: children grow up under cold lanterns, learn the bow owed to each rank of the dead, and carry a register tablet from birth. Spirit-rooted serf children are sold to the Vermilion Brush Academy for a fee per head. The old nobility despise the Court's newer dead and lose every lawsuit against them.
entries.truth: The old king remembers what the old Long Dusk Continent was doing on the Ladder the day it fell, and why the Sovereign forbade anyone to say. He is selling the memory a sliver at a time at the Night Tide Market.

entries.name: Hollow Jade Port
entries.summary: A port cut into a fallen chunk of the Ladder on the inner coast, where Shattered Sea scavenger sects trade relics and salvage for the Long Dusk Continent's grave goods.
entries.lore: A piece of the span the size of a city broke off in the fall and landed hollow side down on the shore. The port is cut into its halls, and ships sail into a harbor chamber through a cracked doorway. Scavenger sects from the Shattered Sea sell drowned Ascent Age relics here and buy lamps, sun-salt and corpse candles for their dives. Storms off the Sea come twice a month, and the jade walls are the only roof on the coast that never leaks. Anything can be sold; the Lamp-Bearers take a cut of whatever came out of the Ladder.

entries.name: Prefecture of Dead Wood
entries.summary: A ghost fief in the heart of the grey forest, ruled by the ghost of a spirit tree that died when the Ladder's shadow fell and still hates the light that left it.
entries.lore: The Lord of Dead Wood was a spirit tree of the Ascent Age, and its ghost runs through the roots of the whole fief, so in a sense the forest is its body. Its living subjects are charcoal burners and orchid farmers who ask its leave before every cut and burn nothing brighter than a coal. Children learn to speak to trees before they speak to strangers. Lamps are forbidden, and travelers carrying fire are led in circles until they put it out. The fief pays the Court in yin herbs and quarrels with the Prefecture of Sleeping Fog over every border tree.

entries.name: Withered Reed Marsh
entries.summary: The coastal marsh of grey reed that feeds the paper mills of the Kingdom of Gold Foil, home to reed cats, bog wraiths and the cheapest herbs on the coast.
entries.lore: Grey reed grows taller than a man and rattles without wind. Cutters work it in gangs and sing as they go, so the bog wraiths know where they are and leave them alone. Shade herbs grow under the reeds: grave moss, cold ginseng and white bitterroot, cheap and plentiful, the first ingredients of every Qi Condensation alchemist on the coast. Reed cats, small spirit beasts whose grey fur drinks light, are trapped here and sold as night guards. Nobody cuts reed in Ghost Month.

entries.name: Prefecture of the Barred Stair
entries.summary: The Court's ghost fief on the Ladder's north face at the coast, whose Marquis licenses every sanctioned breach and charges raiders a year of lifespan a head.
entries.lore: The Marquis was a stair-warden of the Ladder when it stood, and he still treats it as his post. Every licensed crew gets a bronze stair-token and pays a year from each member; unlicensed crews found inside are judged on the spot. His living subjects are porters and lamp-sellers whose children haul supplies to the breaches and learn early which crews come back. He hates the Puppet Gate's diggings on the south face, and his patrols and its puppets meet in the lower halls more often than either side admits.
entries.truth: The Marquis was on duty the day the Ladder was cut, and he saw what was climbing it. He has guarded stairs ever since, and he will not let anyone go up.

entries.name: Shadow-Refining Sect
entries.summary: A Ghost Way sect of living cultivators on the yin vein at the Dim Spring, who refine their own shadows into a second soul and leave their bodies to cultivate.
entries.lore: Disciples learn to step out of the body and sit as a shade in the yin vein, where Ghost Way cultivation runs three times faster, and faster still in Ghost Month. The sect teaches Death Dao, soul arts, yin pills and ghost taming, and recruits children born in the seventh month, whose shadows it calls thin. The danger is the body: a disciple out too long comes back to find it cold, or occupied. The Vermilion Brush Academy has registered dozens of them as dead while they were out, and the sect has killed two of its clerks over it.
entries.truth: The sect's Nascent Soul ancestor has not been back in his body for eleven years. The thing that answers for him at sect councils has learned his voice, but not his handwriting.

entries.name: Fields That Keep the Day
entries.summary: The great sun-salt flats of the south coast, where shallow pans of seawater catch what little sun Long Dusk gets and grow it into crystals of stored light.
entries.lore: The pans run for thousands of li along the coast, each walled with clay and worked by a raking family. Sun-salt grows slowly, a finger's length in a good year, and only in pans that see at least two hours of sun a day. Reed cats and light-eating moths are trapped around the pans. The hungry dead will not walk on the flats, so outlaws and runaways sleep there, which the salt masters allow as long as they rake.

entries.name: Realm of Falling Clouds
entries.summary: A secret realm on an Evening Sun headland that opens at sunset every ten years. Inside, the sun is always setting, and only Qi Condensation cultivators can enter.
entries.lore: The gate is a crack in a sea cliff that glows red when the shard passes close. It stays open for twenty-one evenings, and an aura above Qi Condensation shatters the light and shuts it. Inside lies a land of cloud seas and red stone where the sun hangs on the horizon and never sets. Evening dew gathered from its grass is a prized ingredient in Foundation Establishment pills, and cloud cranes nest on its cliffs. The Fading Glow Sword School holds the headland and sells places. The next opening is due in 3,133.

entries.name: Brine Corpse Pit
entries.summary: A corpse concession in brackish shallows where the drowned of the old Long Dusk Continent were pickled in brine, and come out whole enough to refine.
entries.lore: Bodies that sank into the brine pools when the vales flooded never rotted; the salt kept them. A corpse-refining family licensed by the Puppet Gate dredges them up, and brine corpses are prized for water puppets that work below the surface. The dredge crews are mostly debtors and children from the stilt villages. The Sea Bell Prefecture claims every body as one of its subjects and drowns a dredge crew every few months; the family answers by hiring Shadow-Refining disciples to stand watch.

entries.name: Prefecture of the Dark Riders
entries.summary: The Court's cavalry fief north of its terraces: dead soldiers on ghost horses, the striking arm of the Court's undeclared war on the Puppet Gate.
entries.lore: Five thousand dead riders and their general, who has served the Court since the Dim Age, are quartered here between campaigns. The fief's living families breed and break the ghost horses, said to be born to living mares on nights when the Nether Shard is near. Children ride before they walk and learn never to step on a ghost horse's shadow. Every season the riders go south through the Ladder to burn Gate digging crews, and every family has a son in the stables or a grave on the bone plain. Beast tamers come from three continents to buy foals and are rarely sold one.
entries.truth: The foals are not born of living mares. They come through under the Ladder in Ghost Month already grown, and the breeders were told what to say.

entries.name: Bright Salt Port
entries.summary: The salt port at the mouth of the Jade Sand River, glittering at night with stored light, where sun-salt is graded, sold and smuggled.
entries.lore: Every roof is tiled with low-grade sun-salt, so the town glows faintly all night and the hungry dead circle it without coming in. Salt is graded on the quays into finger, palm and heart crystals, the last holding a whole season of sun. River panners sell jade sand and relics in the lower market. The Azure Wave Palace's toll-takers sit at the harbor mouth, and the Light-Hoarders' Guild sets the price. Smugglers sail from the back of the harbor every night with salt bound for the ghost lands.

entries.name: Bone-Grinding Flats
entries.summary: A stretch of the bone plain where the wind grinds bone to dust and raises storms that strip flesh. Nothing living crosses it without shelter or a Court escort.
entries.lore: The flats have no soil, only bone ground as fine as flour. When the wind rises, the dust storms scour a man to the skeleton in an hour and the skeleton to dust in a day. The dead walk through the storms untouched, which is why the Court's patrols use the flats as a road. Bone wolves hunt the edges. Talisman makers pay well for the dust, the finest bone ash there is, and gatherers work the flats in calm hours with one eye on the sky.

entries.name: Evening Sun
entries.summary: The southeast coast across the strait from the Vast Wilds Continent: two gold hours of evening sun, terraced orchards, and a frontier where spirit beasts come over from the Vast Wilds every spring.
entries.lore: The Evening Sun gets its sun late and times everything to it: markets, weddings, duels, executions. Its kingdoms pay the Year Tithe and earn it back across the strait, selling grey timber and corpse candles east and buying beast cores and Vast Wilds herbs. Every spring beasts that spent the winter working down the island chain come ashore at the Beast-Crossing Shoals, starving from the journey. The Court protects the living from the dead, not from the living, so the coast pays the Fading Glow Sword School instead, and resents both bills.
entries.truth: The beasts that cross the strait are not hunting. They are fleeing something waking in the mountains of the western Vast Wilds Continent, and every spring there are more of them.

entries.name: Year Gate
entries.summary: The checkpoint town on the road from the rice coast to the Pale City, where living travelers buy passes into the land of the dead and pay in years of lifespan.
entries.lore: At the Pass Office a month's pass costs one year of lifespan and a resident's pass ten; a clerk draws the years out through a brush on your palm. Foundation cultivators and above pay double, because their years are richer. The town is full of year-brokers who will pay your pass for a lien on a child, inns that rent beds by the hour, and healers who treat the grey cold the brush leaves behind. The Heavenly Scale Pavilion keeps a counting house here and, to the Court's annoyance, will not change years into stones.
entries.truth: The pass ledger weighs a traveler's remaining lifespan, so the clerks always know who is about to die. They sell the list to the Puppet Gate, whose buyers are waiting at the funeral.

entries.name: Kingdom of Broken Doors
entries.summary: A raider kingdom south of the Ladder's foot, walled with looted jade door-slabs, where every family lives off the halls and most children are sent in.
entries.lore: The Gou family rules by selling maps: the house geomancer, a Foundation cultivator, reads the span's cracks like veins and charges a tenth of the take for each route. Children go in at twelve as lamp-boys, carrying light for crews; light draws what lives in the halls, so lamp-boys die first and are paid best. Survive three trips and you are a raider. The kingdom pays no tithe, sells bodies to the Puppet Gate, buys protection from the Lamp-Bearers' Society, and hangs anyone caught robbing a crew's camp.
entries.truth: The Gou geomancer's maps are good because her grandmother is still inside the Ladder, as a ghost, and sends them out. The Court would very much like to know how.

entries.name: Thousand-Stair Breach
entries.summary: The great breach in the Ladder's north face near the coast: a stair of a thousand steps down into the lower halls, which takes most crews who use it.
entries.lore: The steps are all different heights, and a lamp shows only the next nine. Below lie the lower halls: stripped, collapsed, and guarded by Ascent Age formations that still kill by the old rules. Stair-ghosts stand on certain steps and ask a question; a wrong answer costs a year, a right one buys a secret. A Prefecture of the Barred Stair license is required, and Lamp-Bearers' rescue crews wait at the top. Ghost Month closes the breach, because what comes up the stairs then does not need a license.
entries.truth: The stair-ghosts are not the Long Dusk Continent's dead and are not in any register. They were Upper Realm wardens of the Ladder, and they are still waiting to be relieved.

entries.name: Drowned Jade Palace
entries.summary: The drowned capital of the old Long Dusk Continent's greatest kingdom, its towers standing in thirty zhang of water, where some halls are still dry inside working Ascent Age arrays.
entries.lore: At low tide the tips of the towers break the surface. Divers have mapped and stripped the upper floors; the lower halls are sealed by formations that still keep the water out, and breaking one floods everything inside, including the diver. Formation masters come to study arrays that have held back the sea for sixty-six thousand years without a single spirit stone of upkeep. The Sea Bell Prefecture's drowned live in the flooded parts and charge divers for the right to enter.

entries.name: Sea-Entering Cliff
entries.summary: The cliff where the Fallen Ladder slides off the land into the Shattered Sea, a white jade wall seven thousand li wide going down under the waves.
entries.lore: At low tide you can walk down the span's outer face into the water for a hundred li before the light fails. Shattered Sea storms break against it in plumes visible from Hollow Jade Port. Divers take jade-shell oysters from its flanks, whose pearls hold a sliver of immortal qi, and the Marquis of the Prefecture of the Barred Stair fines anyone who dives past his marker buoys. On calm nights the span hums under the water, as the Stump does when the Mirror is overhead.
entries.truth: The pearls are not jade. They form around flakes of an Upper Realm alloy the span sheds, and an Armillary Pavilion agent in Hollow Jade Port buys every one he can find.

entries.name: Shark-Head Fort
entries.summary: A fort on a headland over the Kingdom of the Evening Tide's harbor where the Azure Wave Palace's shark-folk collectors come ashore for their toll: the one place in Long Dusk where the sea clans hold land.
entries.lore: Humans built the fort; shark-folk took it six hundred years ago in a toll dispute, and the fisher-kings now pay rent on their own harbor. A shark-folk captain at Core Formation holds it with a garrison of thirty. Every boat that fishes the outer coast stops here to pay in fish, salt or pearls. The fort also buys drowned sailors' gear, sun-salt, and news of anything that floats past. Humans may enter the outer yard only, and only by day.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Lamp-Keepers
entries.summary: A living kingdom inside the land of the dead, whose hereditary lamplighters kindle the Court's cold lanterns once a year, because no ghost can strike a flame.
entries.lore: A mortal dynasty has ruled here since the Dim Age by one contract: its people light the Court's lanterns and the Court lets them live. The king is called the First Lamp. Children learn the lantern routes at six and light their first cold lamp at twelve; each kindling chills the hand and costs a little life, and master lamplighters rarely see fifty. In return the kingdom pays no Year Tithe and its dead are judged gently. Ghost Way sects prize its spirit-rooted children, whose bodies already half live in yin.
entries.truth: The Court can make its own fire now. Its artificers learned to strike cold flame a century ago, and the contract is renewed each year only because the Sovereign has not yet decided to end it.

entries.name: Soul-Sending River
entries.summary: The river of the rice coast, rising at the edge of the grey forest and flowing north to the strait. In Ghost Month it carries the River Lamp Temple's lantern boats out to sea.
entries.lore: Its upper course runs grey and cold out of the forest; its lower course waters the rice terraces of the Kingdom of Borrowed Years and the Kingdom of the Open Ford. In Ghost Month the river is lit end to end with lantern boats, and fishermen stay ashore, because the dead are using the water. The Court's river wardens snag any boat they think carries a registered soul, so the monks send decoys first. Silver carp in its pools feed on the yin it carries and are prized for cooling pills.

entries.name: Pale Plain
entries.summary: The ash-white heartland of the dead under the Ladder's north face, where the Court of No Light and the Pale City register, judge and tax every soul in the Long Dusk Continent.
entries.lore: It is always the last minute of dusk on the Pale Plain. The [[Court of No Light]] rules from the [[Pale City]] and holds court on terraces fourteen thousand li to the northeast, joined to the city by the Long Lantern Road. Every death under the Ladder is entered in the registers, judged, and sent to a fief, a post, a punishment, or out with the tide in Ghost Month. The living enter through the Year Gate and pay in years. Nothing grows here outside light arrays but ash-grass and ghost-lamp orchids, so grain arrives by array and caravan at three times the coastal price. The Court's undeclared war on the Puppet Gate is planned here.
entries.truth: Ghosts that run short of years fade into the hungry dead. The Court pays its officials in years from the tithe and the passes, and the Sovereign keeps every judge a few decades from empty. Loyalty here is a ration.

top.note: the Pale Sovereign; her judges below

entries.name: Ladder's Foot
entries.summary: The coast where the Fallen Ladder comes out of the Shattered Sea: the darkest shore in the Long Dusk Continent and the busiest, because the Ladder's lower halls are the easiest to break into.
entries.lore: The span comes ashore here as a white wall seven thousand li wide, and both sides of it are breaches, rubble fields and raider camps. The lower halls were stripped a thousand years ago; crews now go deep, where stairs still turn and Ascent Age formations still kill. The Marquis of the Prefecture of the Barred Stair charges a year of lifespan a head at every licensed breach, the Puppet Gate digs on the south face without asking, and scavenger sects sail in from the Shattered Sea to buy whatever comes out. A good lamp is worth more than the raider carrying it.
entries.truth: The span runs on under the sea for nine thousand li. Divers who reached its end found it smooth as a mirror: cut, not broken. On the Sovereign's orders the Court drowns any diver who says so.

entries.name: Ladder's Head
entries.summary: The head of the Fallen Ladder, where the top of the span burst on impact: the richest tombs in the world, halls that open only to Upper Realm tokens, and its deadliest formations.
entries.lore: The top of the Ladder held the arrival halls of the Upper Realm, and the immortals buried there were the highest who ever died in Severed Heaven. The halls are sealed by formations that still answer to Upper Realm tokens, and broken token fragments sell for fortunes in the Town of Hanging Threads. Raiders who force a door without one are found standing in place with their eyes open. The Gate and the Court both claim the Head. Rumor says one hall still holds someone alive.
entries.truth: An Upper Realm envoy sealed himself into the highest hall when he saw the Ladder was going to be cut. He is alive, he knows why it was cut, and the Gate's master is three fragments short of a token. Cut off from the Mirror's qi, his cultivation has sunk to Body Integration, and he is still among the strongest on the continent after the Pale Sovereign.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Open Ford
entries.summary: A merchant kingdom on the strait to Myriad Sands that holds the ferry monopoly and the port of the Sand-Watching Mouth, where the Long Dusk Continent's grave goods meet the Myriad Sands Continent's caravans.
entries.lore: A council of nine merchant houses rules, and the presidency goes each year to the house that paid the most tithe. The kingdom collects the whole coast's Year Tithe for the Court and keeps a fee for the service. Children of the houses learn three languages and the price of everything; children of the docks learn to swim the harbor and to spot a smuggled soul in a cargo jar. Myriad Sands monks, caravan masters and the Heavenly Scale Pavilion agents crowd its inns. Collecting the tithe makes it rich, envied and closely watched.

entries.name: Bronze Corpse Stockade
entries.summary: The stockade of the Xun clan, corpse refiners older than the Puppet Gate, who were absorbed by it three centuries ago and have been plotting ever since.
entries.lore: The Xun refine bodies by bathing them in molten bronze and grave salt until the skin rings like a bell; a bronze corpse cannot fight above its old realm, but almost nothing can cut it. The clan rules its villages as hereditary lords and pays the Gate a third of every body it refines. Its children grow up among the corpses and are taught that the Gate stole their craft. The Xun sell bronze guards to coastal kingdoms and caravans.
entries.truth: The Xun patriarch has a deal with the Court: when the Court finally moves on the Gate, the Xun will open its back door, and the concessions will be theirs.

entries.name: Sea-Swallowing Mouth
entries.summary: A breach in the Ladder's south face where the water of the Sunken Vales pours into the span in an endless whirlpool. Raiders ride it into halls no one else can reach.
entries.lore: The water roars down into the Ladder's interior and comes out somewhere nobody has found. Raiders who ride the current in, wrapped in water-parting talismans, reach flooded halls untouched since the fall; perhaps one crew in five comes back, usually rich. Drowned ghosts circle in the whirlpool and grab at swimmers. The Sea Bell Prefecture claims anything that comes out. The Lamp-Bearers will not sell a rescue pledge here at any price.

entries.name: Society of the Struck-Off
entries.summary: An underground of ghosts who erased themselves from the Court's registers and hide in the deepest drowned towns, outside its law and its tax.
entries.lore: A ghost struck from the registers has no fief, no salary of years and no protection, but also no judge.
