The Society forges erasures, smuggles souls out of the Pale City in memory jars, and sells passes that look real. It recruits unregistered dead and pays them in stolen years. The Court's hunters raid the drowned towns every Ghost Month, so the Society moves house every year. Living Ghost Way cultivators who want to die outside the Court's reach pay it handsomely in advance.
entries.truth: The Struck-Off can tell a true Severed Heaven ghost from a Nether-born one by its cold. They keep a list of officials in the Pale City who are the second kind. Nobody believes outlaws.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Evening Tide
entries.summary: A fishing kingdom of the southwest coast that pays toll to the Azure Wave Palace's shark-folk in fish and to the Court in years, and fears the first more.
entries.lore: Fleets go out on the evening tide and come back at dawn, and the catch is split three ways: the family, the shark-folk who come ashore at the Shark-Head Fort for their share, and the market. A fisher-king rules by the harbor's consent. Children learn the sea clans' hand-speech before they can write, because a misread gesture to a shark-folk collector ends in blood. Half-bloods with fins are born here more often than anywhere in the Long Dusk Continent, and are quietly drowned or quietly loved.

entries.name: Ten Thousand Moth Caves
entries.summary: Caves in the western grey forest where dusk moths breed: swarms that eat light and anyone carrying it. Their queens are the best-paid catch in the Long Dusk Continent for a beast tamer.
entries.lore: Dusk moths are hand-sized spirit beasts that drink light; a swarm strips a lamp, then the lamp-bearer's warmth, then the lamp-bearer. The caves hold millions, and the queens grow as big as carts and reach Core Formation. A tamed queen hides its owner's camp from anything that hunts by sight, so the Court and the Puppet Gate both pay for them. Tamers go in dark and naked, painted with orchid sap. Most come out. Few come out with a queen.

entries.name: Sand-Watching Mouth
entries.summary: The port at the mouth of the Soul-Sending River where ships leave on the five-month crossing to the Myriad Sands Continent, and where the coast's Year Tithe is counted before it goes to the Court.
entries.lore: Sailors say the haze on a north wind is dust from the Myriad Sands Continent's sands, five months away. Ships leave daily with rice, ash notes, corpse candles and pilgrims, and come back with salt, dates, monks and caravan goods bound for the Pale City. In the Tithe House by the harbor the coast's years are counted and sealed into ghost-jade jars under the Kingdom of the Open Ford guards and a Court clerk. Every Ghost Month the River Lamp Temple's lantern boats pass out of the river mouth while the whole town watches from the quay.

entries.name: Warm Jade Pit
entries.summary: The Puppet Gate's main concession on the south face of the Ladder's head, where immortal bodies are dug out of the deepest tombs. In the trade such bodies are called warm jade.
entries.lore: Shafts run into the span's flank for hundreds of li. A Gate elder rules the concession like a kingdom: puppet crews dig, living debtors sort, and refiners grade each body by its old realm. The debtors' children are string-children who knot puppet threads before they can read, and the best of them are taken into the Gate. Court tomb wardens raid the shafts from inside the Ladder, so deep crews dig with a puppet guard. One Core Formation body sells for more than a small kingdom's harvest.

entries.name: Lampless Market
entries.summary: The trading town of the Dark Walkers, kept in total darkness so as not to draw the moths, where buyers and sellers deal by touch and smell.
entries.lore: Nothing in the town is lit. Stalls are marked by knotted cords, prices are tapped on the back of the hand, and coins are weighed by ear. Grey timber, moth silk, orchid sap, shade herbs and moth-queen eggs sell here cheaper than anywhere else, and appraisers who can judge by touch make a good living. Outsiders are led in by a paid guide who holds their wrist. A thief caught by the town's blind wardens is walked into the forest carrying a lit lamp.

entries.name: Prefecture of Sleeping Fog
entries.summary: A ghost fief of drowned sailors on the fog cliffs of the western coast, whose lord gathers the souls of everyone the Shoreless Sea takes off the Long Dusk Continent's outer shore.
entries.lore: Fog rolls in from the Shoreless Sea every evening and does not lift until noon. The drowned of the outer coast rise in it and climb the cliffs to their lord, an admiral of old Long Dusk who went down with his fleet. His living subjects are cliff fishermen who lower their boats on ropes and pay the Azure Wave Palace's shark patrols in fish and the Court in years. Children climb before they walk and learn never to answer a voice in the fog. The fief's dead still drill like a navy and will pilot a ship through fog for an ash note.
entries.truth: The fleet did not sink by accident. It was carrying refugees out of Long Dusk the day the Ladder fell, and the sea clans turned it back. The admiral remembers which clans.

entries.name: Strait-Gate Kingdom
entries.summary: The frontier kingdom facing the Vast Wilds Continent across the strait, walled against the beasts that come over each spring and rich on the trade that crosses in summer.
entries.lore: A Foundation cultivator family rules from a fortress above Dusk Harbor, and every adult serves a season a year in the beast watch. Children learn to read the strait's tides and the signs of a beast coming ashore, and they count their age in springs survived. The kingdom pays the Year Tithe and the Fading Glow Sword School's fee, and complains that only one of them protects it. Beast cores, Vast Wilds herbs and half-blood sellswords pass through its customs, and its beast tamers are the best in the Long Dusk Continent.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Former Kings
entries.summary: A coastal kingdom whose dead kings never leave the throne room: eight royal ghosts sit in council beside the living king, and outvote him.
entries.lore: A Ghost Way bargain struck by the dynasty's founder keeps each king's ghost at court after death, registered with the Court as an adviser. The living king is the least important voice in the hall. Policy is old-fashioned, and the kingdom has kept the same borders, laws and grudges for nine reigns. Children learn the kings' names in order and the etiquette of speaking to a dead elder; princes hurry to die well. The kingdom pays its tithe in full and keeps a tutor from the Vermilion Brush Academy at court.
entries.truth: The founder's bargain paid the Court with the royal bodies. The Court sold every one of them to the Puppet Gate, and two dead kings now stand guard at the Gate's door.

entries.name: Dawn Shore
entries.summary: The northeast coast facing the Shattered Sea, where the first hour of every morning comes in bright over the water. Its strongest kingdom has stopped paying the dead.
entries.lore: For an hour after sunrise the Dawn Shore is the brightest land in the Long Dusk Continent; then the Ladder's dusk rolls back over it. On clear nights the Stump stands black against the Mirror across the water. Forty years ago the Kingdom of Morning Radiance stopped paying the Year Tithe, trusting the Sun-Reflecting Gate's mirror towers to hold back the dead with stored morning light, and they have held through forty Ghost Months. The Kingdom of Added Years down the coast still pays and sells the Court every rebel name it can find. The Court's levy ghosts wait in the hills at the Year-Levy Prefecture for the towers to fail.
entries.truth: The Court lets the rebels stand. The Pale Sovereign is quietly testing whether stored light can stop the things that come through under the Ladder in Ghost Month, and her own judges are not told why.

entries.name: Footrest Heaven
entries.summary: A small shard world that was once a rest stop for climbers of the Ladder. Its gate, a narrow door in the north face, opens every nineteen years and admits only Qi Condensation cultivators.
entries.lore: The door opens for forty-nine days and cracks if anyone above Qi Condensation steps through. Inside lies an Ascent Age inn and garden under a sky that is always noon: spirit tea bushes sixty-six thousand years old, wells of sweet qi water, and the bones of climbers who chose to stay. Sects pay raider families to send their best youngsters through, and the last opening made four Foundation cultivators within a year. The next opening is due in the spring of 3,131.
entries.truth: The innkeeper is still there, a climber who refused to go up. He trades with every party and keeps a ledger of who climbed and when. The last entry is dated the day the Ladder was cut.

entries.name: Sunset Glow River
entries.summary: A river that rises at the edge of the bone plain and runs southeast through the orchard hills to the strait, catching the evening sun along its whole length.
entries.lore: Its water runs red-gold at sunset, and the orchard kingdoms irrigate from it through canals that follow the light. Bone silt from its upper course makes the soil rich. Barges carry dusk tangerines and grey timber down to the coast. In spring, beasts that came ashore follow the river inland, and the orchards post a watch at every ford.

entries.name: Town of Hanging Threads
entries.summary: The Puppet Gate's market town below its cliff, where puppets are sold to buyers from every continent and the streets are strung with drying corpse thread.
entries.lore: Buyers come from the Myriad Sands Continent, the Morning Star Continent and the Shattered Sea for guards, laborers and war puppets. A Qi Condensation body refined to obey costs about as much as a good horse; higher realms go to auction. Corpse candles, puppet thread and refining flames fill the side streets. The Court never enters, so it is the one town in Long Dusk where nobody pays in years. Raiders sell their finds here at a third of their worth and leave quickly, because the Gate's buyers prefer them dead.

entries.name: Salt Cave Realm
entries.summary: A secret realm reached through a sea cave on the south coast at the lowest tide. It opens every nine years and admits cultivators below Core Formation.
entries.lore: When the shard passes close and the spring tide runs out, the back wall of a sea cave turns to mist for fifteen days; a Core Formation aura turns it solid again, trapping anyone inside. Beyond lies a shard world of salt caverns lit by veins of sun-salt that have grown there for ages, with crystals the size of houses. Heart crystals, salt worms and an ancient light-storage array draw the Light-Hoarders' Guild and the Sun-Reflecting Gate, who fight at every opening. The next opening is this winter, in 3,127.

entries.name: Night Tide Market
entries.summary: A floating market on rafts in the largest of the Sunken Vales, open only at night, where ghosts sell memories by the ounce outside the Pale City's tax.
entries.lore: Rafts are lashed together into streets each night and cut loose at dawn. Ghosts sell memories in sealed jars: a dead alchemist's hand at the furnace, a sword master's last duel, a lover's face. Swallow one and it becomes yours, in dreams at first. A good technique memory sells for more than the manual would, because it comes with the feel. The living pay in spirit stones, ghosts in ash notes. Three hundred years ago the Court burned the market for selling memories of the Outer Demon War; it was back within a month.
entries.truth: One memory sold here that year held the Nameless Sealer's name. The Court burned the market to destroy it and missed the jar, which still changes hands, buyer to buyer, unopened.

entries.name: Wild Bone Pit
entries.summary: An unlicensed bone pit west of the Bone Fair, run by corpse refiners allied with the Puppet Gate, where bones are dug without asking whose they were.
entries.lore: Its master is a Core Formation corpse refiner who pays the Gate for protection and the Court nothing. Hired crews dig open pits a li wide and sell everything: skulls, bone-jade, grave goods, and now and then a body that kept its flesh. Crew children grow up in the pits and are paid by the skull. The Court's dark riders burn the place every few years, and the pits are dug again within a season. The cheapest bone-jade in Long Dusk comes from here, and so do most of the plain's restless dead.

entries.name: Shadow Wall
entries.summary: A stretch of the Ladder's south face where the shadows of people killed by the falling span are burned into the jade, thousands of them, caught mid-step.
entries.lore: When the span struck, a flash of light burned their outlines into the jade behind them: farmers, soldiers, children, a woman holding up her hands. Diviners come to read the shadows, which shift slightly in Ghost Month, and the Court forbids anyone to scratch them. Appraisers say the jade there is different, that it remembers. On the first night of Ghost Month the plain's dead gather in front of the wall and stand in their own shapes.
entries.truth: One shadow is not of anyone killed in the fall. It shows a figure walking away from the span, and it is still moving, a hand's breadth a century, toward the Pale City.

entries.name: Sun-Reflecting Gate
entries.summary: An orthodox refining sect of the Dawn Shore that builds sun mirrors and dawn jars to store light. It is the backbone of the rebel kingdom's defiance.
entries.lore: The Gate teaches artifact refining and formations built around light: bronze mirrors polished with sun-salt, jars that trap the first hour of morning, arrays that throw stored light across a valley. It recruits children with metal or fire roots from every coastal kingdom and pays well for anyone who can grind a true mirror. Its towers guard the Kingdom of Morning Radiance for a fee in grain and conscripts. It wants to sell towers to every coast in the Long Dusk Continent, and the Court has said that any kingdom that buys one will be judged.
entries.truth: The Gate's master has sold the tower design to a buyer he believes comes from the Evening Sun. The buyer works for the Pale Sovereign.

entries.name: Prefecture of the Shaded Sands
entries.summary: A ghost fief in the dunes behind the salt flats, where the dusk returns. Its lord taxes the salt trade he cannot touch and hires the living to hunt smugglers.
entries.lore: The lord was a salt merchant in life and is a salt inspector in death. Sun-salt burns ghosts, so he employs living wardens to search caravans for it. His fief is a sea of grey dunes and empty caravanserais, and his living subjects are guides and wardens whose children learn to smell sun-salt through a sealed jar. Smugglers pay him a toll to look away and pay his wardens a second toll to make sure. He sends the Court a full count every year and keeps a second ledger for himself.

entries.name: Kingdom of Added Years
entries.summary: The loyal kingdom down the coast from the rebels. The Court rewards its faithful tithe by giving years back to the royal family, so its kings live to two hundred and its commoners die at forty.
entries.lore: The Pan family has ruled for nine reigns, each king older than the last. The Year Tithe is taken from every commoner at sixteen and again at thirty, and the Court returns a tenth of it to the throne. Children are raised to revere age: grey hair is a mark of rank, and the court is full of mortal elders who should have died a century ago. Informers who name rebels in the Kingdom of Morning Radiance are paid in years. Spirit-rooted children go to the Vermilion Brush Academy as tribute; nobody asks to go to the Sun-Reflecting Gate.
entries.truth: The old king died thirty years ago. His ghost still wears his body with the Court's leave, and the years given back to the royal family have been feeding it.

entries.name: Dim Spring
entries.summary: The high-grade yin vein of the grey forest: a black spring in a hollow of white trees, where Ghost Way cultivators sit out of their bodies and grow fastest in Ghost Month.
entries.lore: The water is so cold it burns, and it flows uphill for a few li before it sinks. Shade ginseng and black orchids grow on its banks and fetch high prices in the Pale City. The Shadow-Refining Sect holds the spring and charges outsiders three hundred mid-grade spirit stones a month to sit beside it. In Ghost Month the hollow fills with ghosts from all over the forest, and the sect posts guards to stop them drinking it dry.
entries.truth: The Dim Spring is not a vein. It is a seep from the Nether Shard that runs under the forest from the Ladder's head, and it has grown stronger every year of the tide.

entries.name: Afterglow
entries.summary: The Long Dusk Continent's north coast across the strait from the Myriad Sands Continent: three grey hours of sun a day, enough for rice. Its kingdoms are the dead's most obedient tributaries and the richest of the living.
entries.lore: Afterglow feeds the Long Dusk Continent: rice, dried fish, and grey reed for the mills that print the ash notes every ghost market spends. Its kingdoms pay the Year Tithe on time and get polite tax ghosts in return. Ships make the five-month crossing from the Sand-Watching Mouth to the Myriad Sands Continent's sands, and in Ghost Month the River Lamp Temple sends lantern boats down the Soul-Sending River carrying souls the Court has not registered. Nine years ago a yang vein broke the surface at the Red Spring Valley, the only one in the Long Dusk Continent, and the Sun-Embracing Sect and two rivals are still fighting over the lease.
entries.truth: The coast's Year Tithe is counted at the Sand-Watching Mouth before it goes to the Court, and for a century the count has come up a few thousand years short. Someone on the strait is skimming lifespan and selling it to the Myriad Sands Continent.

entries.name: Jade Sand River
entries.summary: The river that rises under the Ladder's south face and flows south across the bone plain to the sea, carrying jade sand and small relics washed out of the span's halls.
entries.lore: Its source is a spring welling from a crack in the span, and its water is cold and faintly bitter. Panners work every bend for jade sand, which refiners use to polish artifacts, and now and then for a ring, a bead or a sliver of an Upper Realm token. The river cuts through the bone plain, and its banks are layered with skulls. At its mouth in the Crystal Strand the panners pay the salt kingdoms a tenth of their finds.

entries.name: Jade Scree
entries.summary: The shattered southwest where the Ladder's head came down: ridges of broken jade, the richest tombs in the world, and the Thousand Puppet Gate mining them under the Court's nose.
entries.lore: When the span fell, its head struck hardest and burst; for twenty thousand li the land is jade scree, gorges and half-buried halls. The [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] holds a cliff of fused jade above its concessions on the south face. The Court's tomb wardens at the Mausoleum-Guard Prefecture hold the north face and ambush Gate convoys in the gorges. Raiders come here for the best tombs and often end up as stock. Puppets, corpse candles and refining flames are cheaper here than anywhere in the world; so are lives.
entries.truth: The Gate can only refine bodies up to Core Formation reliably. Its few Nascent Soul puppets are its war chest, and the Court knows where each one stands, because one of them reports to a judge in the Pale City.

entries.name: Year-Levy Prefecture
entries.summary: A ghost fief in the hills behind the Dawn Shore, home of the Court's levy ghosts, whose Collector has waited forty years for permission to punish the rebel kingdom.
entries.lore: The Collector was a tax official in life and has been one for nine thousand years since. His fief is a hill country of half-empty villages where his clerks keep a ledger of every year owed on the coast, compounding. His living subjects are charcoal burners and herb-pickers who pay in full and on time, because they can see the ledger hall from their doors. Each Ghost Month his levy ghosts march to the edge of the tower light and stop. His patience is famous, and so is the debt: the ledger says the Kingdom of Morning Radiance owes one hundred and twelve thousand years.

entries.name: Broken Jade Gorge
entries.summary: The gorge through the jade scree that carries the Puppet Gate's convoys from its concessions to the coast, and the Court's favorite place to ambush them.
entries.lore: The gorge walls are broken jade that rings when struck, so every convoy is heard long before it arrives. The Mausoleum-Guard Prefecture's tomb wardens wait in the cracks, and the Gate answers with war puppets and corpse candles that burn ghosts. The dead of both sides are left where they fall, and scavenger crews strip each battlefield within a day. Caravan guards are paid triple. The Gate has tried three times to cut another road and lost the crews each time.

entries.name: Vermilion Brush Academy
entries.summary: A Ghost Way academy of living scribes west of the Pale City who write the Court's registers in yin ink, and are promised posts in its bureaucracy after they die.
entries.lore: The Academy trains the Court's living hands: registrars, pass clerks and talisman writers. Students cultivate yin through calligraphy and learn to write a soul's name so that it stays written. Graduates serve the Court alive and, if they die in good standing, take office as ghosts: a career that does not end is the Academy's real recruiting pitch. It tests children with a blank register page and keeps those whose ink does not fade. It hates the Shadow-Refining Sect, whose out-of-body cultivators keep turning up in its ledgers as dead.
entries.truth: The dean has found register entries in a hand no living clerk writes, enrolling returnees nobody judged. He has told no one. He is afraid he knows whose hand it is.

entries.name: Demon-Sealing Glacier
entries.summary: A glacier in the far north of the Black Frost Continent where an outer demon army was frozen mid-charge in the Outer Demon War.
entries.lore: From the Seal Watch's northern fortress you can see them: a hundred thousand shapes in blue ice, a hundred li deep, still facing south.
entries.truth: The Eternal Night Palace has been thawing demons out one at a time to learn how they cultivate. One escaped forty years ago. The host faces south because it came from the north, up the [[Ice Stair]]. Its general would stand at Body Integration in our reckoning.

entries.name: Age of the Ascent
entries.summary: The last High Tide. The ancients built the Heaven Ladder and walked up it to the Upper Realm.
entries.lore: When the world swung close to the Mirror, qi ran so thick that Tribulation Transcenders appeared every few centuries. The great sects of that age raised the Heaven Ladder from the central continent toward the Mirror, and for thirty thousand years ascension was a road, not a miracle. Seeds, beasts and treasures came down it; the best of each generation went up. Almost nothing survives except ruins, sealed cave abodes and the Ladder Stump.
entries.truth: Traffic on the Ladder ran both ways, and not everything that came down was friendly. Several of today's 'ancient' bloodlines descend from Upper Realm envoys who stayed.

entries.name: The Dim Age
entries.summary: The Ebb. Qi thinned, Foundation Establishment became a legend, and mortal empires ruled.
entries.lore: As the world drifted from the Mirror, qi thinned for forty thousand years. At the bottom of the ebb a Core Formation cultivator was a living god. Lineages broke and libraries rotted. The Demonic Way spread, because taking qi from others was the only way left to climb; the Buddhist Way rose on the Myriad Sands Continent, because merit needs little qi; and the dead of the Severance built their kingdom under the Fallen Ladder. Most great beasts slept through it.
entries.truth: A few masters of the Age of the Ascent survived the whole ebb sealed inside their cave abodes. Some are still asleep.

entries.name: The Rekindling
entries.summary: The tide turned. Spirit veins swelled, sects multiplied, and most of today's great powers were founded.
entries.lore: As Severed Heaven swung back toward the Mirror, dead veins woke and new ones broke the surface. Ruins resurfaced, and the sects that looted them grew rich. The Armillary Pavilion rebuilt the transfer arrays eight thousand years ago, and the six continents became one market.

entries.name: The Sealed Era
entries.summary: Now, year 3,127: the richest qi in sixty-six thousand years, crowded sects and fierce competition, under a seal that has started to strain.
entries.lore: The calendar restarted at the Second Sealing. Three thousand years of rising qi have filled every vein and every sect. Small sects become great in a century, and great ones fall just as fast. The Mirror grows wider in the sky every generation, and rumor says someone means to rebuild the Ladder.
entries.truth: The Armillary Pavilion is building it. The Seal Watch has quietly doubled its garrison.

entries.name: The Unrecorded
entries.summary: Before records: the world gathers in the Void Sea, beasts and sea clans rule, and humans appear.
entries.lore: Every race tells it differently. The sea clans say the oceans were theirs first and the land rose later. The beasts say humans came out of the Mirror's light like moths to a lamp. Human sects teach that the first cultivator learned to breathe qi by watching a crane.

entries.name: Eternal Night Palace
entries.summary: The demonic power of the Black Frost Continent's black ranges: blood cultivators who rule by strength under the polar night.
entries.lore: In the Eternal Night Palace, rank is whatever you can take and hold. Disciples are encouraged to kill their seniors, and elders who weaken are eaten. The Night Sovereign has ruled for nine hundred years by never once looking weak. The Palace holds the black ranges, taxes the Frost Fair and raids the steppes, and despises the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's sermons more than its swords.
entries.truth: The Palace is the one thawing the Frozen Host. The Night Sovereign wants an outer demon's cultivation method. He reached Body Integration and found no road onward. That is why he wants a method from outside the world.

entries.name: The Outer Demon War
entries.summary: The First Seal cracked under the rising tide, and outer demons poured out of Heaven's Scar for 170 years.
entries.lore: Orthodox, demonic, Buddhist and ghost cultivators fought on the same walls, because the demons ate all of them alike. Three continents burned. The war ended when a lone cultivator walked into Heaven's Scar and sealed it from inside. Her name was the price of the seal. It is gone from every record and every memory, and the founding stele of the Seal Watch has a blank where it should be.
entries.truth: She did not die. The Nameless Sealer reached Tribulation Transcendence inside the seal and is now its keystone. If she ascends or dies, Heaven's Scar opens. It was a two-front war. While the defenders who would become the Seal Watch held the Scar, a second host climbed the [[Ice Stair]] over the north Rim and was frozen on the [[Demon-Sealing Glacier]]. The stair is still a door, and nobody guards it.

entries.name: The Hundred Sects War
entries.summary: Six hundred years of war over the waking spirit veins. Its end drew the borders the great powers still hold.
entries.lore: Every sect with a vein fought every sect without one. It ended without a treaty, in exhaustion: whoever still held a vein kept it, and the map has barely moved since.
entries.truth: Apricot Grove Valley sold healing pills to every side and came out the richest sect on the Morning Star Continent.

entries.name: The Severance
entries.summary: The Heaven Ladder broke. The central continent shattered, the upper span fell across the Long Dusk Continent, and Heaven's Scar tore open where the Ladder stood.
entries.lore: No account agrees. Orthodox sects teach that Heaven struck the Ladder down to punish demonic cultivators who tried to seize it. Demonic sects say the orthodox ancestors cut it behind them to keep immortality for themselves. Buddhists call it the ripening of greed. The ghosts of the Long Dusk Continent were there, and they will not discuss it.
entries.truth: As the tide ebbed the world drifted off, stretching the Ladder thin. Outer demons, drawn by the breach, climbed it toward the Mirror. The Upper Realm cut the Ladder from its end to save itself, leaving Severed Heaven to the swarm. The ancients spent their lives on the First Sealing of Heaven's Scar.

entries.name: Evergreen Deep
entries.summary: A forest the size of a kingdom in the Vast Wilds Continent's far south, grown around the Root Mother. The plants here fight back.
entries.lore: Herbs in the Evergreen Deep are tens of thousands of years old, and one root can make an alchemist's career. Walking trees, strangling vines and ginseng children that run when you look at them keep most of it unharvested. At its heart stands the Root Mother, a tree whose canopy covers a kingdom. Nobody knows her realm. Nobody who tried to find out came back.
entries.truth: The Root Mother sprouted from a seed that came down the Heaven Ladder. She is the oldest of the few Mahayana alive in Severed Heaven, and she does not care about anything that walks unless it cuts her.

entries.name: The Fallen Ladder
entries.summary: The broken upper span of the Heaven Ladder, lying two hundred thousand li across the Long Dusk Continent. Its shadow is why the continent never sees full day.
entries.lore: From the coast it looks like a mountain range of white jade. Inside are halls, stairways and tombs of immortals from the Age of the Ascent, and the bodies in them have not rotted in sixty-six thousand years. The Court of No Light claims every soul inside it; the Thousand Puppet Gate claims every body.
entries.truth: Parts of the span still answer to Upper Realm tokens.

entries.name: Frost Fair
entries.summary: A market city on the ice of the Black Frost Continent's southern coast, where tribes, demonic sects and southern merchants trade under a truce nobody trusts. A hub of the Heavenly Circuit.
entries.lore: The Frost Fair moves with the ice. Every winter the whole city is rebuilt a little further south, and every spring someone is found frozen into the old foundations.

entries.name: Floating Peak Continent
entries.summary: Mountains so steeped in qi that the highest have torn free of the ground and float. Home of the ancient clans and the array masters.
entries.lore: The Floating Peak Continent has the highest peaks, the thinnest air and the oldest families. The Conclave of Nine Clans claims descent from the Age of the Ascent and holds most of the floating mountains; the Armillary Pavilion watches the sky from the Star Dial and runs the world's transfer arrays. Ruins from the Age of the Ascent are commoner here than anywhere else, and so are the graves of people who went looking for them.
entries.truth: The floating peaks rise with the tide. In two thousand years the highest will touch the world barrier, and nobody knows what happens then.

top.note: the Nine Clans' Old Ancestor, hidden

entries.name: Baili Clan
entries.summary: The kun-blooded clan who herd the sky-whales. Lowest in the Conclave's seating, richest in its trade.
entries.lore: Kun blood lives in water or air, and a woken Baili breathes fog and swims through cloud. Their peaks float low, which costs them precedence at the Conclave, and they do not care: their whales carry most of the freight between peaks, and every clan owes them money. They hire ground-born whalers, lice scrapers and tamers, and they will take any beast tamer who can calm a frightened calf. They treat the sea clans as relatives they do not like.
entries.truth: The Baili hold the Huyan's debts and carry the Huangfu's freight, and they have promised each clan their best duelist for the challenge. They will deliver to whichever pays more.

entries.name: Half-Peak Kingdom
entries.summary: A ground-born kingdom whose king bought a small floating peak at the Peak-Pawn Market, the first ground-born ruler in the Floating Peak Continent to own one. The clans are deciding whether this is a joke or a war.
entries.lore: King Shi mortgaged his treasury and his daughters' dowries to buy a drifting peak with a Low-grade heart, then had it moored over his capital. His court spends half the year up there breathing through jade, and his people pay shade rent to their own king for the first time. The Conclave has not ruled whether a ground-born may own a peak. The Fallen Leaf Society, the Blood-Thief Gate and three clans have all offered to buy it. His eldest daughter is the best young pilot in the Geomancers' Guild.

entries.name: Broken Ridges
entries.summary: The graveyard of fallen peaks in southwestern the Floating Peak Continent: crater lakes, shattered spires and upside-down halls. A peak fell here thirty years ago, and the rush for its vein has not stopped.
entries.lore: The drift carries dying peaks southwest, and for twenty thousand years they have come down here. The land is crater lakes and broken spires, and the oldest falls have weathered into karst towers. Floatstone, rock that still wants to rise, is cut from the fallen hearts and is the keel of every flying boat in the Floating Peak Continent. Thirty years ago the Inverted Peak fell upside down onto a kingdom, and its heart is a Mid-grade vein; prospectors, sects and claim-jumpers have poured in since. The Tantai claim every fallen peak by salvage right and enforce it when they can be bothered.
entries.truth: Fallen hearts regrow. Several of the Broken Ridges's oldest craters will lift again within a century as the tide rises, carrying whatever has been built on them up into the thin air.

entries.name: Forest of Lightning Rods
entries.summary: A forest of Ascent Age bronze rods on a high mesa, each a hundred feet tall. They split tribulation lightning, and cultivators pay dearly to face their tribulations among them.
entries.lore: Nobody knows who raised the ten thousand rods, but they draw and split lightning so that a tribulation striking here lands as many smaller bolts. The Waking Thunder Sect rents places among them: a Nascent Soul's tribulation costs three hundred mid-grade spirit stones, and the higher realms' far more. Those who fail leave their ashes on the mesa, and scavengers sift the ash for melted artifacts. Rods sometimes fall, and the Huyan pay well for intact ones.
entries.truth: The rods were not built for tribulations. They are a tether staked over the Kui, and each one that falls loosens it.

entries.name: Sealed Furnace Peak
entries.summary: A small peak moored low over the plateau, wrapped in an array that kills anything flying within two thousand li. The Armillary Pavilion calls it a storehouse.
entries.lore: Nobody goes near the Sealed Furnace Peak. Its array shoots down birds, flying swords and the occasional curious Foundation cultivator, and the ground below is fenced with the Armillary Pavilion boundary stones. Smoke rises from it day and night, star-iron goes up its chain by the ton, and the porters who haul for it are paid triple and sworn to silence. After rain, herders below find beads of melted jade in the grass; they sell well, and the Measurers buy them back at any price.
entries.truth: The Sealed Furnace Peak forges the new Heaven Ladder in segments of star-iron and immortal jade. The finished segments are stored inside the Star Dial's peak, waiting for it to reach the barrier.

entries.name: Ice Spine Range
entries.summary: The great range of the northern Floating Peak Continent, whose summits rise above the cloud sea. Its glaciers feed the northern rivers and hold the continent's breath-jade seams.
entries.lore: The Ice Spine Range runs from the beacon coast in the west toward the whale coast in the east, and the Beacon-Terrace Range branches from its western end. Only one pass, at the Pass Town, crosses it at a height a mortal can survive. Cranes nest on its glaciers, cloud-yaks graze its flanks, and avalanches close its roads for half the year.

entries.name: Ice Tower Gate
entries.summary: A gate of blue ice that forms on a glacier saddle every seven years as its shard passes overhead. Foundation Establishment and below may enter; the climb is the first test.
entries.lore: The gate forms over three days and lasts thirty. It stands above the cloud sea, so anyone climbing to it needs breath jade or a Foundation cultivator's lungs. A Core Formation aura shatters it, which happened once and killed everyone inside. The shard is cold and silent, full of crystal herbs and ice spirits that can be bound as companions. The Zhangsun take a tenth of what comes out, at the gate, by eye. The next opening is next spring.

entries.name: Kingdom of Long Breath
entries.summary: A highland kingdom of herders who live higher than any other mortals in the Floating Peak Continent. Its people have deep chests, slow hearts and no patience for lowlanders.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Long Breath's herders drive cloud-yaks to summer pastures just under the cloud sea, and its children hold their breath for a count of five hundred in contests. The ruling family is mortal and pays its tax to the Zhangsun in yak wool and guides. Lowland cultivators come here to adapt before climbing, and the herders charge them twice what they charge pilgrims. Its children sometimes run off to the crane keepers, and the kingdom resents every one it loses.

entries.name: Sunken Stair
entries.summary: An Ascent Age causeway of grey jade that walks down from the cliffs into the Shattered Sea, step by step, toward the Stump.
entries.lore: The stair is forty paces wide and every step is a single block of jade. It starts on the cliffs north of Ruin-Dredge Harbor and descends straight toward the [[Ladder Stump]]; divers have followed it down four hundred steps before the depth turned them back. Halls open off its landings, most of them looted, some still sealed with live arrays. Pilgrims leave offerings on the top step on clear nights when the Stump shows.
entries.truth: The stair was the road from the Floating Peak Continent to the foot of the Heaven Ladder. Its lowest landings still hold waystones that answer to Upper Realm tokens, and the dead of the Kingdom of the Sunken Bell remember how to wake them.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Sunken Bell
entries.summary: A ghost fief in the drowned city beneath Ruin-Dredge Harbor, ruled by a magistrate who died at the Severance and still collects taxes. Divers who pay are left alone.
entries.lore: At night a bell rings under the harbor, and the drowned city's dead go about their business: clerks, watchmen, a magistrate on a jade chair. His law is simple. The living may dive his streets if they pay the tax, one breath per hall, blown into a jar left on the steps. Those who pay feel cold for a month. Those who do not are found with their lungs full of seawater and their purses untouched. Ghost cultivators come to trade with his court, and the [[Court of No Light]] has sent envoys.
entries.truth: The magistrate was the Sunken Stair's toll-keeper, and he still holds the ledger of everyone who climbed to the Ladder. He is waiting for the waystones to wake.

entries.name: Red Copper Kingdom
entries.summary: A copper-mining kingdom on the plateau's eastern scarp that supplies the rods every roof on the Thunder Plateau needs. Rich, nervous and a vassal of the Waking Thunder Sect.
entries.lore: The Red Copper Kingdom's copper is the reason anyone can live on the plateau, and its mortal kings have grown fat on it. The mines run deep into the scarp, where lightning strikes the ore seams and leaves them laced with qi; that copper sells to refiners at ten times the price. The kingdom pays the Waking Thunder Sect in copper for protection. Its children are small and quick and go down the mines at ten, and its people paint lightning on their doors for luck.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Double Shade
entries.summary: A small kingdom where a Huangfu peak and a drifting Huyan peak overlap. Both clans claim its shade rent, and its king has paid neither for six years.
entries.lore: When a Huyan peak slipped its moorings and drifted west six years ago, its shadow crossed the Kingdom of the Double Shade's border, and both clans now claim the rent. King Fan has paid neither, telling each that the other forbade it, and spent the money on walls and Foundation cultivators for hire. The dispute will be fought on the Cloud-Settling Terrace this autumn, and whoever wins will want an example made of the king. Until then the Kingdom of the Double Shade is the one place in the Hanging Shade where no clan's rootless can collect anything. Smugglers, deserters and servants run down from the peaks fill its inns, and its children earn more carrying their messages than their fathers do farming.

entries.name: Hanging Shade
entries.summary: The central massif under the thickest flock of floating peaks, where the Conclave of Nine Clans sits. On the ground, whole kingdoms live in shade that moves, and pay rent for it.
entries.lore: Forty-odd peaks hang over the Hanging Shade, the lowest a few li up and the highest, the Huangfu's, at a hundred and forty. The [[Conclave of Nine Clans]] seats its clans by the height of their highest peak, so every clan feeds its peak heart and cuts old chains to climb. Below, every field pays shade rent to whichever clan's peak darkens it. Shade ginseng grows in the deepest gloom and sells by the ounce. Scree falling from the peaks' undersides kills a few hundred people a year. A clan within twenty li of the seat above may challenge for it on the Cloud-Settling Terrace; the Huyan have challenged the Huangfu, and both are quietly hiring outside fighters.
entries.truth: Peaks are still tearing loose as the tide rises: three new ones in the last century. Within another, most of the Hanging Shade's fields will lie in permanent shade, and the clans' only plan for feeding the ground is to buy the Streams of the Luan's grain.

top.note: the Nine Clans' Old Ancestor, hidden

entries.name: Inverted Peak
entries.summary: The peak that fell thirty years ago and landed upside down. Its summit is buried, its roots point at the sky, and its halls hang from their ceilings.
entries.lore: The Inverted Peak came down on a moonless night and buried a kingdom's capital under its summit. Its upturned base still carries the halls built on its underside: rooms whose floors are ceilings and stairs that lead into the air. Its heart, a Mid-grade vein the size of a county, lies near the top and is fought over by three sects and the Tantai. The Huangfu owned it and have never said why they let it fall.
entries.truth: The Huangfu drained its heart to feed a dying elder and let it drop rather than admit it. The kingdom it crushed had paid them shade rent for nine hundred years.

entries.name: Peak-Pawn Market
entries.summary: The market where floating peaks are bought, sold, pawned and gambled. Every clan's debts end up here eventually, and so do the people who collect them.
entries.lore: The Peak-Pawn Market grew where the drift lanes cross, and its exchange hall registers peak deeds for the whole south. A small peak with a Low-grade heart costs as much as a kingdom; shares in larger ones trade daily. The [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] keeps a branch here, beside loan houses that take clan heirs as collateral. Peak pilots, shade surveyors and debt collectors are hired in the square. The market's one rule is that a peak belongs to whoever holds its heart, and it does not ask how they came to hold it.

entries.name: Cloud-Settling Terrace
entries.summary: The Conclave's duelling floor: a round terrace of white jade floating above the cloud sea, where clans settle disputes over peaks, marriages and precedence.
entries.lore: The Cloud-Settling Terrace is a single slab of jade three li across that has never drifted an inch, which is why the clans trust it. Duels are fought to yield or to death at the challenger's choice, under a Sikou referee, and peaks, shade rights and betrothals change hands here. Spectators stand on the Conclave's sufferance, and ground-born cultivators who catch an elder's eye in the stands have been taken on as retainers the same day. Outsiders may not duel unless a clan names them its champion, which every clan has done and none admits.
entries.truth: The slab is a step of the Heaven Ladder, flung here at the Severance. It hums with the [[Ladder Stump]] whenever the Mirror is overhead. The [[Armillary Pavilion]] has twice offered to buy it and twice been refused.

entries.name: City of the Rice Measure
entries.summary: The great grain market of the south, on the Silk Water. Its granaries feed the peaks, and this year they are being emptied for the Morning Star Continent.
entries.lore: The City of the Rice Measure is a ring of granaries around a market square, and it sets the price of rice for all of the Floating Peak Continent. Barges come down the Silk Water loaded and go back empty. This year Jing factors in dark blue robes buy every sack at triple the price, Nangong tithe-masters take their share, and the city's poor eat chaff. Grain guards, informers and rice smugglers are hired daily. Riots break out on market days, and Nangong singers are sent down to calm them.

entries.name: Kingdom of Two Masters
entries.summary: A coastal kingdom of fishers and lice scrapers that pays one tax to the Baili and another to the shark-folk, and is loyal to whoever came last.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Two Masters's boats work the fog banks and the whale lanes, and its queen pays the Baili in grain and scrapers and the shark-folk in fish and iron. Her capital stands on stilts over a harbor the shark-folk can swim into, which is the point. Children learn to swim, scrape lice and keep quiet. Young men go to the whales; young women are courted by the shark-folk quarter, and nobody talks about the half-blood children in the fishing villages.

entries.name: Overturned Realm
entries.summary: A secret realm gate cracked open by the Inverted Peak's fall. It opens for thirty days every three years and admits only those below Core Formation.
entries.lore: The gate was sealed in the peak's vault until the fall split it. It opens for thirty days every three years, and a Core Formation aura makes it slam; it has cut two elders in half. Inside, gravity points at the sky, and the shard's rivers and herbs hang upside down: inverted ginseng, sky-rooted lotus, and lodes of sinkstone, a floatstone that pulls down instead of up, which refiners want badly. The three sects fighting over the crater each take a third of the gate days.

entries.name: Kingdom of Plentiful Years
entries.summary: The largest rice kingdom in the south, a mortal dynasty that has fed the Nangong for two thousand years and is now selling its granaries to the Morning Star Continent.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Plentiful Years's paddies run to the horizon, and its calendar is the farming calendar: children are named for the solar term of their birth and go into the fields at six. The Lu dynasty pays tithe to the Nangong, but its ministers have found that Jing factors pay better, and the granaries are emptying. Hunger is new here, and the people do not understand it yet. A Low-grade vein lies under the palace, and the royal family keeps its few cultivators close.

entries.name: Beacon-Terrace Range
entries.summary: A range of bare granite running parallel to the northwest coast, crowned with the beacon line's towers. Its few passes are the only roads inland.
entries.lore: Every pass through the Beacon-Terrace Range is walled and every summit has a tower. Raiders who land must cross the range to reach anything worth taking, which is why the line has held for twelve centuries. Ice-wolves den on its high slopes, frost lichen grows on its north faces, and the pass forts hire hunters to keep the wolves off the supply roads.

entries.name: Storm-Eye Gate
entries.summary: A secret realm gate that opens in the eye of the great midsummer storm for three days each year. Everyone who enters is struck by lightning matched to their cultivation.
entries.lore: When the season's biggest storm stalls over the Thunder Plateau, a ring of calm opens at its center and the gate appears inside it. Anyone may enter, but the gate strikes each person with lightning matched to their realm, so in practice nobody above Core Formation survives the threshold. The shard beyond is a world of storms, with lightning-fed beasts and thunder stones that each hold a bolt. The Huyan tax it at the gate, and the Waking Thunder Sect disciples go in as a rite.

entries.name: Cloud-Plowing Sect
entries.summary: A spirit-farming sect that grows cloud rice on terraces climbing into the cloud sea. It teaches farming, herb lore, alchemy and medicine, and the blight is killing it.
entries.lore: The Cloud-Plowing Sect's terraces climb the hills until their highest steps stand in the cloud sea, where cloud rice grows a grain that glows faintly. A bowl a day keeps a Qi Condensation cultivator's progress steady, and the sect sells it to the clans and to anyone with silver. It teaches spirit farming, herb lore, alchemy and medicine, and it takes in farm children with green thumbs and no spirit stones. This year the black-ear blight is spreading through its upper terraces, and its elders will pay anyone who finds the cause.

entries.name: Gnomon City
entries.summary: The city at the foot of the Star Dial's mooring chains, where cargo and array travelers go up and down. Everything is taxed twice, once by weight and once by height.
entries.lore: Gnomon City is built around the Dial's four mooring chains, each wide enough to carry a road. Lift-cages climb them day and night; the ride to the bronze terrace takes three days and a breath-jade rental. Travelers who arrive by transfer array come down the same way, so the city has the best inns and worst thieves on the plateau. Measurers search every crate for array plates. The market sells breath jade, star-iron, formation flags and the Pavilion's secret realm calendars, along with forged copies of them.

entries.name: Shadow of the Dial
entries.summary: A high, dry plateau beneath the Star Dial, the highest floating peak in the world, whose shadow sweeps across it like a sundial's hand. The domain of the Armillary Pavilion.
entries.lore: The Star Dial hangs some three hundred li above the Shadow of the Dial, and its shadow crosses the plateau each day; locals tell time by it and call noon 'the needle'. The [[Armillary Pavilion]] rules without a throne: its Prefects appoint or oversee the kings of the Dial's nearest kingdoms, its tolls pay for every road, and its one law that matters is that nobody outside the Pavilion may study transfer arrays. Smugglers pay porters well to carry stolen array plates past the Measurers, who hang the ones they catch from the Dial's chains and pay Core Formation hunters for the rings behind them. Star-iron mines and formation academies hire everyone else. The Wenren clan's peak drifts within sight of the Dial.
entries.truth: The Armillary Pavilion means the Star Dial to be the first peak to touch the world barrier and the new Ladder to rise from it; the Sealed Furnace Peak forges the segments. The Dial's chains are lengthened every year, and the Pavilion pays the Tantai not to ask why.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Sea Corner
entries.summary: A fishing kingdom on the northwest coast that pays tribute to the clans and, quietly, to the raiders, and survives on both.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of the Sea Corner's boats work the strait's cod banks and seal rookeries, and its harbor faces the raiders' sea lanes. Its queen pays the clans' tax openly and the Palace raiders' tithe in secret, in salt fish and the occasional convict, and in return her villages are skipped. Everyone in the kingdom knows; nobody in the City That Refuses the Ice admits to knowing. Children can tell a raider's sail from a merchant's at twenty li and are taught to say nothing about either.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Cold Gate
entries.summary: A march kingdom behind the beacon line, ruled by rootless garrison families who were sent down from the peaks and never sent for again.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of the Cold Gate's lords are all rootless or their descendants, and they rule like officers: every household owes one soldier, and every child learns the bow and the beacon codes. Grandchildren are tested each year in case the blood wakes late; a woken child is taken up to the peaks, and the family gets a plaque and nothing else. The people are hard, loyal to the line and contemptuous of the clans who pay for it. The kingdom's name also means 'humble family', and they like the joke.

entries.name: Black-Ear Fields
entries.summary: Upper cloud-rice terraces where a black blight has taken hold. The rice ears turn to soot, and the soot clogs the meridians of anyone who breathes it.
entries.lore: The blight appeared four years ago and spreads a few terraces a season. Infected ears burst into black dust that clogs meridians: farmers who breathe it lose their qi sense, and cultivators cough soot for months. The Cloud-Plowing Sect has fenced the terraces and burns them, in vain. Alchemists from the Morning Star Continent have come to sell cures, which work for a season. The sect pays well for samples and better for the name of whoever started it.
entries.truth: The blight was seeded by an agent of the [[Apricot Grove Valley]] posing as a herb merchant. He is still in the City of the Rice Measure, selling the cures.

entries.name: Crane Burial Temple
entries.summary: A Buddhist temple on the glaciers that gives the dead to the cranes. The only Buddhist house of note in the Floating Peak Continent, and the only place a mortal may go above the cloud sea for free.
entries.lore: The Crane Burial Temple's monks carry the dead up to the glacier altars and give them to the cranes, teaching that a body should feed something on its last day. Pilgrims climb with their dead on their backs, and the temple lends them breath jade. The monks practice a slow breath method that needs little qi and lets them live above the clouds, and they teach it to anyone who stays a year. They treat altitude sickness and qi burn for free, the only healers in the Utmost Summits who do. The Zhangsun tolerate them because the cranes like them.
entries.truth: The Crane Burial Temple's founder fled the [[Thousand Lamps Temple]] six centuries ago, and his life lamp in the Myriad Sands Continent still burns. He sits alive under the glacier altar, and the Thousand Lamps Temple has finally sent someone to ask why he left.

entries.name: Huangfu Clan
entries.summary: The qilin-blooded first clan of the Conclave, holding the highest peaks over the Hanging Shade. Proud, rich, and unable to kill with their own hands.
entries.lore: Qilin blood sickens if its bearer kills, so no Huangfu has struck a killing blow in ten thousand years; the clan keeps the largest corps of rootless enforcers in the Floating Peak Continent and hires outsiders for the rest. Woken children command fire and earth, and grass is said not to bruise under their feet. Their highest peak, over a High-grade heart, gives them the Conclave's first seat, their alchemists brew Qilin Ember pills for every clan, and they recruit gifted ground-born as 'hands', on contracts that end the day a hand becomes inconvenient.
entries.truth: The Huangfu peak has stopped rising. Its heart is being drained to feed two failing elders, and the clan is borrowing spirit stones from the [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] to hold its height until the Huyan challenge is settled.

entries.name: Gate of Echoes
entries.summary: A secret realm gate in the cliff beside the Sunken Stair's top step, open one night every nineteen years when the Mirror stands over the Stump. Only Qi Condensation cultivators can pass.
entries.lore: When the Mirror stands straight over the [[Ladder Stump]], the Stump hums, and the Sunken Stair hums back; that night a door of green jade opens in the cliff beside the top step. Anyone above Qi Condensation who touches it is thrown back with broken bones. The shard beyond is a road-wardens' garden of the Ascent Age, with moon-blooming herbs and a waystation whose shelves still hold sealed manuals. The door shuts at dawn, and whoever is still inside waits nineteen years. The next night is in two years, and the Ruin-Seekers' Guild is already selling places in the queue.
entries.truth: The garden is the first waystation on the old road to the Ladder. Its manuals are Ascent Age travel permits, and the Armillary Pavilion has been buying every one that comes out.

entries.name: Huyan Clan
entries.summary: The thunder-blooded clan of the east, descended from the one-legged Kui. Loud, proud and the best duelists in the Conclave.
entries.lore: A woken Huyan's voice carries for miles and their blood calls lightning; their elders fight with drums of Kui hide whose beat can stop a heart. They hold the peaks over the Thunder Plateau and the thunder-ox herds below, and they have won more duels on the Cloud-Settling Terrace than any other clan. Their highest peak has climbed to within twenty li of the Huangfu's, which under Conclave law lets them challenge for the first seat, and they have. They recruit lightning cultivators from any sect and pay them in thunder-struck wood, and a cadet branch keeps a trading lodge across the northern strait in the Black Frost Continent.
entries.truth: For three generations the Huyan have poured their own blood into the ground at the Ridge of the Sleeping Kui, hoping the thing beneath will know them when it wakes.

entries.name: Tribe of the Shark Caves
entries.summary: A shark-folk tribe in the sea caves under the Whale Clouds's cliffs, sworn to the Azure Wave Palace. They collect the Sea Sovereign's toll and hunt whale calves born over the water.
entries.lore: The tribe has lived in the cliffs since before the clans, and its chief, a Nascent Soul shark-folk, carries the Sea Sovereign's seal. It counts every whale born over the sea as its own and takes them at night. Ships that pay toll sail safely; ships that do not lose their crews one by one. The tribe sells sea silk, pearls and shark-tear gems in the harbor and buys iron and captives. Humans who net its young are hunted down inside Fog-Shoal Harbor itself.
entries.truth: The chief spies on the Baili for the Sea Sovereign and sells what he learns to the Yuwen. He means to be paid by whoever ends up holding the pearl.

entries.name: Whale-Milk Fjord
entries.summary: A long fjord where sea fog pools so thick that sky-whales calve and nurse in it. The richest beast ground in the Floating Peak Continent and the most dangerous to be seen in.
entries.lore: Every late summer the herds come down into the fjord's fog to calve, and for two months the water is white with whale milk that sets into a qi-rich scum on the rocks. Gatherers skim it for spirit-fish feed and pills. Baili riders guard the fjord mouth, and shark-folk come up from the sea at night for calves. Anyone who gets close to a calf in its first week can bond it, if the mother lets them live.

entries.name: Whale Clouds
entries.summary: The Floating Peak Continent's foggy northeast coast on the Shoreless Sea, where sky-whales calve in sea fog and the Baili clan herds them between the peaks.
entries.lore: Sky-whales swim through cloud as fish swim through water, and in late summer they come to the Whale Clouds's fog fjords to calve. The Baili clan rides and herds them, and a laden whale can lift a village's harvest to the peaks in a day. Calves, whale lice and cloud ambergris are the coast's wealth. The sea clans claim every whale born over water, and shark-folk cut calves out of the herds at night; the Baili pay night riders to drive them off and bury a few each season. Every ship here pays the [[Azure Wave Palace]]'s toll, and the Palace's agents have lately been asking everyone about the Yuwen clan's pearl.
entries.truth: Kun blood is half sea. The Sea Sovereign has offered the Baili their herds' safety forever in exchange for help taking the pearl from the Peak of the Torch Dragon's Pearl, and half the Baili elders want to accept.

entries.name: Waking Thunder Sect
entries.summary: A lightning sect named for the spring thunder that wakes the insects. It teaches Lightning Dao, thunder talismans and how to survive a tribulation.
entries.lore: The Waking Thunder Sect's applicants stand on a hilltop in the afternoon storms holding a copper rod; those who are struck and live are accepted. The sect teaches the Lightning Dao, thunder talismans written on struck jujube, and tribulation craft, and its elders run the tribulation ground at the Forest of Lightning Rods for a fee. It is orthodox, proud and in debt to the Huyan, who own the plateau it stands on and remind it often.
entries.truth: The founder was a rootless Huyan whose blood woke at forty, too late to be taken back up. The sect keeps her diary, which describes a voice under the plateau that called her by name.

entries.name: City That Refuses the Ice
entries.summary: The fortress city of the beacon line, at the head of a long fjord. Its harbor chain is raised every winter and its walls are glazed with ice on purpose.
entries.lore: The City That Refuses the Ice's walls are sprayed with seawater each winter until they are smooth as glass. The line's Warden sits here, a rootless Huyan general at Core Formation with a famous temper. The markets buy raider heads, ice-wolf pelts and frost lichen and sell everything a fort needs, and a quiet trade ransoms captured raiders back to their tribes, which the Warden calls diplomacy. Recruiters sign anyone who can draw a bow, and deserters hang from the harbor chain.

entries.name: Utmost Summits
entries.summary: The highest grounded ranges in the Floating Peak Continent: glaciers, knife ridges and air too thin for mortals. Cranes nest on the ice, and the Zhangsun clan's peaks ride above them.
entries.lore: The Ice Spine Range runs through the Utmost Summits, and its summits rise above the cloud sea, about fifteen li up, where a mortal faints within the hour without breath jade and a Qi Condensation cultivator bleeds from the nose. Breath jade is mined here and sold wherever peaks are. The Zhangsun's cranes nest on the glaciers in tens of thousands; this year they are sickening, and the clan will pay well to learn why. Herb gatherers climb for cloud-tooth moss and frost-eye orchids and lose a few to the slopes every season. The Pass Town holds the only pass, and the clan's rootless toll everyone who crosses.
entries.truth: The high air grows richer in qi every decade, and qi that thick burns the lungs. Within a few centuries the summits and the highest peaks will kill anyone below Nascent Soul. The cranes are only the first to notice.

entries.name: Geomancers' Guild
entries.summary: The guild of peak pilots and geomancers who read the qi winds, steer drifting peaks and survey shade rights. Nobody in the Wandering Peaks moves a mountain without them.
entries.lore: The Geomancers' Guild pilots read the qi winds on compass plates and steer peaks by throttling their hearts, a craft that takes ten years to learn and one mistake to forget. The guild also surveys shade rights, settles boundary disputes on the ground and casts geomantic charts for tombs and sect halls. It takes apprentices of any birth who can feel qi currents, and its pilots are bonded for twenty years. The clans hate depending on it and pay anyway.
entries.truth: Half the deeds registered at the Peak-Pawn Market are forgeries. The Geomancers' Guild holds the true ones in its vault, which is why no clan has ever tried to break it.

entries.name: Star-Carving Realm
entries.summary: A shard world of broken Ascent Age observatories whose gate opens on the plateau every thirty-six years for nine days. The Armillary Pavilion auctions the entry tokens.
entries.lore: The gate opens in a ring of standing stones south of Gnomon City, and the next opening is in four years. It admits only those below Core Formation; a stronger aura cracks the ring. Inside are wrecked observatories, star-iron and bronze instruments whose purpose nobody remembers, guarded by puppets that still keep watch. The Armillary Pavilion sells three hundred tokens at auction and buys back anything with markings at a fixed price; selling elsewhere voids your token for life.
entries.truth: The shard is a piece of the Ascent Age station that surveyed the Ladder's route. The Armillary Pavilion buys the instruments back because it needs them for the new one.

entries.name: Ridge of the Sleeping Kui
entries.summary: A long, bare ridge in the middle of the plateau where the thunder is loudest and nothing grows. The Huyan kill anyone who digs there.
entries.lore: Every storm on the Thunder Plateau seems to start over this ridge, and the ground hums at night. Its rock is full of fulgurite, glassy tubes made by lightning that refiners prize. Prospectors who dig more than a few feet down find warm stone that beats like a heart, and they are found the next morning with burned-out meridians. The Huyan keep watch and kill trespassers. Plateau folk say a thunder ox the size of a mountain sleeps underneath.
entries.truth: The plateau folk are right. A thunder ox that reached Body Integration in the Age of the Ascent sleeps under the ridge, and the beating stone is its heart. The Huyan are its keepers by an oath older than their clan name.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Kui Herds
entries.summary: A herding kingdom on the open plateau that raises one-legged thunder oxen for the Huyan. Its children are drilled for lightning before they can read.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of the Kui Herds's herders follow the thunder oxen, which graze storm grass and hop on their single leg faster than a horse can run. A rootless Huyan drum-lord rules and beats the war drum once a year to call the levy. Children practice lying flat in storms and know a dozen signs that a strike is coming; those who are struck and live are sent to the Waking Thunder Sect's test. Ox hide, horn and milk are the kingdom's wealth, and rustlers are hanged on lightning rods.

entries.name: Wolf Smoke
entries.summary: The Floating Peak Continent's cold northwest coast, facing the Black Frost Continent across the strait. A chain of beacon forts watches for raiders, and in the hardest winters the pack ice reaches all the way across.
entries.lore: Beacon towers stand every hundred li on the Beacon-Terrace Range, burning wolf dung that smokes black. The clans pay for the forts in grain and rootless officers, and pay late. Most years the threat is the [[Eternal Night Palace]] raiders coming by sea for captives. In the hardest winters the strait freezes shore to shore and the [[Iron Bone Tribes]] war bands ride across: four times in recorded history, and the last two winters came within days of a fifth. Fire arrays wait along the shore to break the ice. The forts pay bounties on raider heads, triple for a Palace elder's, and sign anyone who can hold a wall. In summer the same harbors trade grain for Black Frost furs.
entries.truth: Some captives ransomed back from the Palace after last winter's raids hum a tune nobody taught them. The fort commanders have noticed and are quietly drowning them.

top.note: the blood-array elder in Blood Mist Valley; raiding Nascent Souls in bad years

entries.name: Domain of the Old Whale
entries.summary: A stretch of cloud forest and fog ruled by a wild sky-whale bull at Nascent Soul. Herds that are not the Baili's shelter there, and so do the villages that serve him.
entries.lore: The Old Whale has never been ridden. He drifts over his domain of fog and cloud forest with a wild herd, eats storms, and kills any rider who comes within a hundred li. The villages under him leave offerings of salt and spirit fish and in return are left alone by poachers and shark-folk alike. The Baili want his blood for their herds, the shark-folk want his ambergris, and he wants to be left alone. Every tamer in Floating Peak dreams of bonding one of his calves.
entries.truth: The Old Whale is learning to speak. He has begun sending dreams to the village children, and some of them have started singing whale-song in their sleep.

entries.name: Ruin-Dredge Harbor
entries.summary: The harbor of the ruin-divers, built on the drowned roofs of an Ascent Age city whose dead still keep house below. Everything raised from the sea is sold here.
entries.lore: Ruin-Dredge Harbor stands on pilings driven into a drowned city's rooftops, and at low tide you can see the streets below. The appraisal halls on the quay buy jade shards, array plates, guardian-puppet cores and sealed boxes nobody dares open; the boxes are auctioned unopened every new moon. Scavenger sects from the Shattered Sea come to sell and to steal. Breath pills, diving bells, ward-breaking talismans and rope are the other trades. Death notices are posted on the harbor gate, and the list is long.

entries.name: Thunder Plateau
entries.summary: A storm-beaten plateau in eastern Floating Peak where thunderheads off the Shoreless Sea break every afternoon. Home of the Huyan thunder clan and of anyone who must survive a tribulation.
entries.lore: Storms roll in from the sea each afternoon and break over the Thunder Plateau, and lightning strikes every hilltop most days of the year. Mortals live in sod houses with copper rods on the roofs. The Huyan clan rule from their peaks above the storms, herd one-legged thunder oxen and want the Conclave's first seat. Thunder-struck jujube, the best talisman wood there is, grows on the hills and is cut in the hour after a strike, if the cutter lives. Cultivators come from every continent to face their tribulations among the rods of the Forest of Lightning Rods. The storms get worse every decade.
entries.truth: The plateau's thunder is breathing. A Kui of the Ascent Age sleeps under the Ridge of the Sleeping Kui, and as the tide rises its breath grows louder. It is the Huyan's ancestor, and they mean to be standing beside it when it wakes.

entries.name: Heaven-Measuring Kingdom
entries.summary: The porter kingdom beside the Star Dial, ruled by an Armillary Pavilion Prefect. Its people haul the plateau's cargo, and its children are tested for array sense at seven.
entries.lore: The Heaven-Measuring Kingdom has a king for ceremonies and an Armillary Pavilion Prefect for everything else. Its people haul freight on the Dial's chains and the plateau roads, and its children grow up counting paces and reading shadow-time. At seven every child presses a palm to a formation plate; those who light it go to the Academy of the Chalk Line on a Pavilion stipend. Families with a gifted child are envied and often robbed. The kingdom's Low-grade spirit vein belongs to the Armillary Pavilion, and the Prefect is a Core Formation array master nobody has seen smile.

entries.name: Kingdom of Chain Bridges
entries.summary: A kingdom of villages on karst towers joined by chain bridges, ruled by a family of floatstone smiths. The towers are fallen peaks worn down to stumps.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Chain Bridges's towers are what remains of peaks that fell before any records, worn by twenty thousand years of rain into spires. Its people live on the tops and farm hanging gardens between them, and its bridges are buoyed with floatstone so they never sag. The Ke family, Core Formation smiths, rule and sell to the Cloud-Bearing Works. Children cross a bridge in a gale at four. Swiftlet nests and cave herbs are its other trades.

entries.name: Peak of the Torch Dragon's Pearl
entries.summary: The Yuwen clan's seat, a black peak sinking a few li each year toward the kingdom beneath it. Its sealed vault holds an Ascent Age dragon pearl.
entries.lore: The Peak of the Torch Dragon's Pearl once rode higher than any peak but the Star Dial. Now its lowest spurs are a day's climb above the treetops, and its servants' quarters have been abandoned to the wind. The vault at its heart is sealed with an Ascent Age array the Yuwen themselves cannot fully open; the pearl can be seen through a window of water, turning slowly. Thieves have tried the vault every decade for a thousand years, and their bones are kept on display.
entries.truth: The pearl is what holds the Peak of the Torch Dragon's Pearl up. Take it out and the peak falls on the Kingdom of the Falling Shadow within the day, and no Yuwen child will wake again. The Yuwen elders know, and the Sea Sovereign suspects.

entries.name: Luan-Song Falls
entries.summary: A stepped waterfall on the upper the Silk Water where luan birds roost by the thousand. Their dawn song carries qi, and cultivators come to meditate under it.
entries.lore: At dawn the luan on the falls sing together, and the song carries enough qi to smooth a cultivator's meridians. A season of meditation under it is said to be worth a year of practice, and ledges are rented by the month. The Nangong count the birds as kin and kill anyone who takes one. Spirit fern and singing reed grow in the spray, and flutes cut from the reed sell to Nangong musicians for a fortune.

entries.name: Streams of the Luan
entries.summary: The Floating Peak Continent's warm southeastern lowlands: terraced hills, rice deltas and streams where luan birds sing. The continent's breadbasket, and this year the Morning Star Continent's buyers are emptying it.
entries.lore: The Streams of the Luan feeds the peaks. Its terraces grow cloud rice, its deltas grow common rice, and the Nangong clan above take a fifth of every harvest. This year factors of the [[Great Jing Dynasty]] are paying triple for grain and shipping it south, the granaries are emptying, and the price of a bowl of rice doubles every month. Riots have started in the river towns. The [[Clear Heaven Sword Sect]] recruiters come across the strait to test children, which the clans call theft; recruiters who stray far from the ports tend to vanish. A black blight is eating the cloud-rice terraces. Barge guards, grain smugglers and blight hunters are all in demand.
entries.truth: The Jing factors are not trading. The Morning Star Continent's heartland harvests are failing, and the dynasty is quietly emptying the Floating Peak Continent's granaries to hide it. The Nangong know, and have already sold next year's crop.

entries.name: Valley of Falling Whales
entries.summary: An inland valley where old sky-whales sink out of the sky to die. Their carcasses rot into a gas that kills in one breath, and their bones are the best artifact timber in the Floating Peak Continent.
entries.lore: Dying whales come down into this valley from all over the coast, and nobody knows how they find it. The rot gas pools in hollows and kills in a breath; bone-crabs and gas-hawks that have learned to live in it kill most of the rest. Whale bone is light, strong and holds qi like iron, and refiners pay almost anything for a clean rib. The Baili forbid entry and sell licenses anyway.

entries.name: Fallen Leaf Society
entries.summary: The brotherhood of the rootless, clan children whose blood never woke and who were sent down to serve. They run the ground for the clans, and more and more for themselves.
entries.lore: A clan child whose blood has not woken by twelve is given a jade tag and a post on the ground. These rootless become stewards, rent collectors, generals and keepers of the mooring pillars, and the Fallen Leaf Society is how they look after one another. It keeps lodges in every city in the Floating Peak Continent, lends to members, finds work for ground-born talents who make themselves useful, and watches rootless grandchildren closely, since blood sometimes wakes a generation late and a woken child is taken back up. Its masters bow to the clans and keep the books.
entries.truth: The Society skims a fifth of the shade rent and has spent three centuries buying mooring pillars through ground-born proxies. Whoever holds a pillar can unmoor the peak above it.

entries.name: Silk Water
entries.summary: The great river of the southeast, rising under the central peaks and running through the rice country to the sea. Grain barges crowd it from source to mouth.
entries.lore: The Silk Water runs silty and slow, the color of milk tea, and its floods built the southern deltas. It rises in the shade of the Kingdom of Moss Lanterns, drops over the Luan-Song Falls, passes the City of the Rice Measure and spreads into the islands of the Kingdom of Level Sands. Barges, eel fishers, river bandits and the occasional river spirit share it. Its upper reaches run through shade and stay cold all summer.

entries.name: Kingdom of Fate Registers
entries.summary: A kingdom under the drifting Wenren peak where every child's fate is read at birth and written into a register that decides the rest of their life.
entries.lore: Wenren rootless read each newborn's fate and enter it in the register: soldier, farmer, scholar or ill-starred. An ill-starred child cannot inherit, marry above a farmer or enter a school, and families often sell them to plateau caravans before they are grown. A good fate is worth a dowry. The people are calm, fatalistic and unforgiving of anyone who tries to change their lot. A council of temple elders governs under Wenren eyes, a trade in forged register pages runs through its temples, and the Wenren hunt the forgers.
entries.truth: The readings are honest but edited. Wenren elders tell the readers which fates to record, so the registers supply the clan with what it needs: soldiers in a lean decade, scholars in a rich one.

entries.name: Drowned Ruins
entries.summary: The Floating Peak Continent's ragged inner coast, facing the Shattered Sea: drowned valleys, sea cliffs and Ascent Age stairs that walk into the water. On clear nights the Stump is a black line on the horizon.
entries.lore: When the central continent shattered, this coast was its outskirts, and its valleys drowned with their cities in them. Ruin-divers work the drowned halls under licenses from the Ruin-Seekers' Guild, and Ruin-Dredge Harbor buys what they bring up. Rifts drift in from the [[Shattered Sea]] and open without warning, and scavenger sects from its islands raid divers' boats. Last year a palace rose out of the silt off the Sunken Stair, and three crews have already died fighting over it. Rope-hands are always wanted, and so are divers who can break a live array.
entries.truth: The new palace did not surface by chance. It holds a peak heart and is rising like a floating peak; within twenty years it will lift clear of the sea, and whoever holds it then will own a peak no clan granted.

entries.name: Southern Crossing
entries.summary: The port where convoys leave for the Morning Star Continent, months away across the strait. Grain and floatstone go out; Jing silver, the Clear Heaven Sword Sect recruiters and the Apricot Grove Valley pills come in.
entries.lore: The Southern Crossing sits in a deep bay behind a breakwater of fallen-peak stone. The crossing to Morning Star takes a sailing convoy three months and a flying boat one, and most cargo still goes by sea and pays the Azure Wave Palace's toll. This year the quays are piled with grain bound for Jing granaries, and hungry dockhands steal what they can. Crews, escorts and convoy cultivators are always wanted. The rich skip the voyage and buy array passage to the Jing Capital at Gnomon City.

entries.name: Nangong Clan
