entries.summary: A Buddhist nunnery of healers that follows the wall and nurses the wounded of every winter's fighting. Its precious pills, made from Roof herbs and purified quicksilver, are famous across the Myriad Sands Continent.
entries.lore: The Pure Vase nuns compound the Roof's medicine: snow lotus, worm-grass, saffron and minerals ground for days and blessed for months into pills that can pull a Foundation cultivator back from a burst meridian. Their best, the Precious Pill, contains the Kingdom of Cinnabar quicksilver that only they know how to render harmless. They treat anyone who reaches the gate, monk or raider, and send the bill to the [[Lion's Roar Cloister]]. Novices learn medicine, alchemy and the Healing Sutra, and each spends a winter in the wall's field hospitals.
entries.truth: The nuns have treated three [[Eternal Night Palace]] raiders whose wounds closed overnight and whose blood was the wrong color. They burned the bandages and told only the abbess.

entries.name: Vulture Burial Temple
entries.summary: The sky-burial order of the Roof. Its monks break the dead and give them to the bone vultures, so that no body on the Roof can be refined, raised or sold.
entries.lore: The Vulture Burial Temple monks carry the bone hammer and the vulture whistle. They teach the Bone Release, a Death Dao method that loosens a corpse's last qi so the birds will take it, and they tame bone vultures that can strip a Core Formation beast in an hour. They take orphans as novices and pay herders in medicine. Since the glaciers began giving up the frozen dead, southern corpse buyers have offered fortunes for bodies, and the order now hangs the thieves it catches from its burial cliffs, alive, for the vultures to judge.
entries.truth: The abbot's ledger of released bodies has false lines. The order sells one cultivator body in ten to the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] and uses the money to buy the rest back from thieves.

entries.name: The Sheer Wall
entries.summary: The escarpment along the Roof's southern edge, where the plateau drops two thousand zhang to the Sand Sea. The Thousand Lamps Temple's lamps burn along its top.
entries.lore: The Wall runs from the high northwest to the cold northeast without a gap a caravan can use. Roads climb it in three places, the Prostration Stair among them. Its face is riddled with Dim Age hermit caves and the Kingdom of the Hive villages. Sandstorms break against its foot, and every evening cold air pours off the top onto the oases below, which is why their dates ripen slowly and sweet.

entries.name: House of City-Openers
entries.summary: A company of diggers, array breakers and appraisers that buys licenses to excavate surfaced Ascent Age ruins and sells what it finds in Fallen Star City.
entries.lore: The House of City-Openers holds digging charters on every major ruin in the Buried Cities, bought from the nomads, the Kingdom of the High Tower Sun family and anyone else with a claim. Its crews include formation breakers, puppet killers and sand-rats, children small enough to crawl into collapsed halls. Pay is a share of the finds, appraised at the company's own hall. The House recruits at every oasis and promotes anyone who comes back alive three times. It hates freelance looters, whom it calls thieves, and the Heavenly Scale Pavilion's appraisers, whom it calls partners.
entries.truth: The House of City-Openers is a [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] subsidiary in all but name. The Pavilion owns six tenths of it through three shell houses and sees every find before it is appraised.

entries.name: The Thirsting Sands
entries.summary: The dry heart of the Sand Sea, where dew never forms, wells are always dry and travelers who sleep wake as dry as paper.
entries.lore: The sand here is warm at night and cold at noon, which nobody can explain. Water leaves a cup in an hour and a sleeping body in a night, and a storage ring's water is gone by the time you cross the edge. These dunes do not walk; they stand still while the rest of the Sand Sea flows away from them. Every geomancer's rod points to the middle. The Thirsting Heart Sect goes in to pray, looters go in after the cities underneath, and City-Opener crews have found an Ascent Age causeway a hundred zhang down that runs straight toward the center.
entries.truth: Under the center sleeps the lord of the river cities, an Ascent Age cultivator who sealed himself away as the Ebb began. His preservation array has been drinking the land ever since, and as the tide wakes him it drinks faster. He sealed himself at Body Integration.

entries.name: Thirsting Heart Sect
entries.summary: A demonic sect that worships thirst. Its cultivators drink the water out of living bodies, leave mummies behind, and make pilgrimage into the Thirsting Sands.
entries.lore: The sect teaches that water is a debt the body owes the desert, and its Dry Blood Art collects it: a disciple's touch pulls the water from a victim and turns it into qi. Victims are found as light as paper. The sect raids caravans and poisons the wells of oases that refuse to pay. Inner disciples walk into the [[Thirsting Sands]] each year to pour water on the sand and pray, and most come back stronger. Recruits come from dying-oasis refugees, who are offered water and asked nothing. The [[Gate of Gathered Dew]] kills its disciples on sight.
entries.truth: Their prayers are answered. The thing under the sand gives back a little of what it drinks to those who feed it, and the sect master has heard it speak.

entries.name: Gate of the Empty City
entries.summary: A demonic illusion sect that hides in the mirages of the salt pan. It shows thirsty caravans a city with wells, then harvests whoever walks in.
entries.lore: The Gate cultivates illusion arts that ride on real mirages, so its phantoms are as solid to the eye as the pan's own. A caravan that turns toward a mirage oasis walks into a salt marsh, a pit or a camp of waiting disciples. The sect takes the goods, keeps useful people as servants and feeds the rest to its illusion furnaces, which turn terror into qi. It recruits salt-cutters' children who are good at seeing what isn't there. The Mirage-Watching Terrace diviners can spot its phantoms, and the sect has killed four of them.
entries.truth: Its illusions fail wherever the new mirages appear. Something else is painting pictures on the pan, and the sect master has forbidden his disciples to look at them.

entries.name: Stair of Prostrations
entries.summary: The pilgrim stair up the Sheer Wall to the Thousand Lamps Temple: thirty thousand steps cut into the rock. The devout climb it by lying full length on every step.
entries.lore: A pilgrim who climbs by prostration takes a year and arrives with a callus on the forehead that the temple honors. The stair is also the Thousand Lamps Temple's entrance trial: a child who wants the outer court must climb it without stopping, while monks watch from the top. Every three hundredth step holds a shrine with a water bowl that the Kingdom of the Hive refill for a fee. Cultivators who fly past the stair are not refused at the top, but they are always given the worst cells.

entries.name: The Withered Rivers
entries.summary: Red badlands between the Roof and the inner coast, cut by a hundred dry canyons and one living one, the Milk River Gorge. Cinnabar mines, flash floods, bandit sects and the road to the sea.
entries.lore: The caravan road from Fallen Star City to the coast threads the Withered Rivers's canyons for twenty days, and each day's stretch is named for the way someone died on it. The canyons stay dry for years, then run full in an hour after a storm on the Roof. The red rock bleeds cinnabar, which alchemists need and miners die of. The [[Blood Sand Gate]] robs the road, the heretic monks of the [[Temple of the Merciful Blade]] hunt the Blood Sand Gate, and the caravan houses pay both. In the Milk River Gorge, cliff villages ferry caravans across on rope bridges and charge whatever the river's mood allows.
entries.truth: Half the Ascent Age relics sold at the Grand Auction pass through the Withered Rivers on their way west, and a third of all of them were made here.

entries.name: The Bitter Lake
entries.summary: The bitter lake where the Tamarisk River ends, in the middle of the salt pan. Its brine grows spirit salt crystals, and its shores are pink with brine shrimp.
entries.lore: When the Tamarisk River runs at all, it runs here, and the lake swells for a season before shrinking back to a pink brine pool. Spirit salt crystals the size of fists grow on its bed, prized by alchemists as a preservative and by array makers as a qi conductor. Pink cranes wade the shallows eating the shrimp, and their feathers sell as talisman brushes. Swimming is easy; drinking is death.

entries.name: Ladder-Gazing Cliff
entries.summary: A headland from which the Stump can be seen on clear nights. A Dao stele on its tip was carved by a Seal Watch elder who never went back to his post.
entries.lore: The elder came here after his term at the Stump, sat on the headland for sixty years watching the Pillar, and carved one stele before he died. It holds a Space Dao insight and a column of numbers nobody has understood. Cultivators come to sit before it; most get a headache and a few break through. Pilgrims leave water bowls for his ghost, which is said to stand at the edge on nights when the Stump hums.
entries.truth: The numbers are dates: the years the seal weakened most. All but the last have already happened, and the last is less than ten years away.

entries.name: Kingdom of Linked Forts
entries.summary: A mortal kingdom of forts strung along the ice cliffs, joined by a wall built after the last Iron Bone invasion. Every boy serves three winters on it.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Linked Forts's kings are lay disciples of the [[Lion's Roar Cloister]] and rule from the bell-fort. Children learn to read ice before letters: grey ice holds, white ice lies, black ice is the sea waiting. The wall bells ring a code everyone knows from birth, one stroke for fog, three for raiders, nine for the ice bridge. When the bridge forms, the villages empty into the forts. Spirit-rooted boys go to the Cloister; spirit-rooted girls go to the forts' archer schools, which fight from the wall with talisman arrows.
entries.truth: The king pays the [[Eternal Night Palace]] a yearly tribute of twenty mortals to spare his own fort. The villages chosen believe raiders took them.

entries.name: Guild of Lead Camels
entries.summary: The caravan masters' guild of the eight roads. It schedules the great caravans, sells places in them and decides which roads are open, which is to say which kingdoms eat.
entries.lore: No single merchant can afford to cross the Sand Sea alone, so the Lead Camels organize convoys of a thousand beasts and sell space by the pack. A guild caravan carries water, guards, a geomancer and a Heavenly Scale Pavilion clerk, and its departure dates are posted in every oasis a year ahead. The guild hires the Kingdom of Escorts escorts, buys water at a discount and blacklists oases that overcharge. Caravan masters serve a seven-year apprenticeship that starts with mucking out camels and ends with a solo crossing. The guild's old enemy is the Thirsting Heart Sect, which it pays anyway.
entries.truth: The guild has quietly stopped routing caravans through four western oases. It knows their wells will fail within a decade, and would rather they die without its trade than with it.

entries.name: The Glass Plain
entries.summary: The plain of glass around the crater, made when the fragment struck. At noon it focuses the sun and burns travelers alive; at night it sings as it cools.
entries.lore: For a season's ride beyond the rim the sand was melted into green glass, now cracked into plates and hidden under a skin of drift. Where the drift blows away, the glass lenses noon light into points that can set a camel alight. Caravans cross before dawn or after dusk on the marked roads. Glass scorpions, clear and nearly invisible, nest in the cracks, and their venom goes into clarity pills. Off the roads the glass holds bubbles of Ascent Age air, which alchemists buy by the jar.

entries.name: Ambergris Strand
entries.summary: A beach where the cold current drops ambergris after winter storms. A lump the size of a head sells in Fallen Star City for mid-grade stones, and claims are settled with knives.
entries.lore: The fog coast's richest beach is a crescent of grey sand below the dunes, where storms bring in ambergris from the beasts of the deep trenches. After every winter gale, villagers, wreckers and passing cultivators race to the strand at first light, and the beach rule is simple: whoever's hand is on a lump owns it, and hands can be removed. Spirit ambergris from beasts at Core Formation or above burns with a scent that calms the heart demon and is worth ten times as much. When the sea clans come ashore for the biggest lumps, nobody argues.

entries.name: Strand of Tangled Space
entries.summary: A stretch of shore where a spatial rift came ashore three hundred years ago and never fully left. Space here is folded: a step can carry you ten li, or into the sea.
entries.lore: The rift closed, but the folds it left still shift with the tides. Footprints stop mid-stride, and a shout comes back from behind you. Things from the Shattered Sea wash up through the folds: Ascent Age debris, sea beasts far from home, sometimes the bodies of salvagers lost a thousand li away. The Sect of the Passing Crack disciples train here because the folds are small. The Harbor of Camels and Sails salvagers pay children to comb the edges at low tide, and pay their parents when they do not come back.

entries.name: Slope of the Bared Vein
entries.summary: A glacier slope where the retreating ice has uncovered a mid-grade spirit vein. Three years after it surfaced, a thousand cultivators are camped in the thin air fighting over it.
entries.lore: The vein runs out of the moraine like a seam of blue fire, and the qi above it is the richest on the Roof outside the Thousand Lamps Temple's halls. Nobody owned the ice, so nobody owns the vein: the Kingdom of Sutra Flags monasteries, Black Yak clans, lowland sects and freelance cultivators have all staked claims, and the claims are settled at night. The Black Yak Tribes charge for passage up the only trail. The Thousand Lamps Temple offered to arbitrate and was politely ignored, which it has not forgotten. The ice is still retreating, and every month uncovers another stretch.
entries.truth: The vein is not new. An Ascent Age array sealed it under the ice, and the array is still running further up the slope, beneath ice that has not melted yet.

entries.name: The Buried Cities
entries.summary: The oldest and deepest sand, where dunes a thousand zhang high walk with the wind and uncover Ascent Age cities for a season before burying them again. Looters, appraisers and worms.
entries.lore: Before the sand came, the Passing River ran through here to the outer sea and its banks were lined with Ascent Age cities. Now the dunes move a few li a year, and every few decades they open a street, a palace roof or a tower top to the sky. Looter crews race the [[House of City-Openers]]'s licensed diggers to each one, and the finds go east to Fallen Star City for appraisal. Sand worms a li long hunt by vibration: walk softly or ride a camel, whose steps they ignore. Wells here are dug fifty zhang deep and still go dry, and the deep sand is spreading east.
entries.truth: Every geomancer who has mapped the water table here has found the same thing: it slopes toward the [[Thirsting Sands]] from every direction, uphill included.

entries.name: Valley of Snuffed Lamps
entries.summary: A cold valley on the Roof where monks expelled by the Thousand Lamps Temple live after their lamps are put out. To the temple they are dead, and they act like it.
entries.lore: The Thousand Lamps Temple does not kill its vow-breakers. It snuffs their lamps, strikes their names and walks them to this valley, and after that no monk will speak to them. Most starve. The rest band together, keep their temple arts and drop the temple rules: they rob travelers on the Roof road, sell technique manuals from memory and take lowland students who cannot afford a real master. A Foundation cultivator who walks in alone rarely walks out. The Askers never go in.
entries.truth: The valley's eldest outcast was expelled for asking what the monk in the deepest hall is meditating on. He has a Nascent Soul and an answer.

entries.name: Ringing Bell Fort
entries.summary: The great bell-fort of the Precept Watch on the cliffs above the strait. Its bell warns the whole coast when the ice bridge forms, and its bounty board pays in pills.
entries.lore: The Ringing Bell Fort's bell was cast from the armor of the Iron Bone dead and can be heard a hundred li away. The fort-city holds ten thousand people, the Kingdom of Linked Forts's court and the Cloister's wall command. In summer, ships from Black Frost put in under truce flags; in winter the harbor freezes and the gates close. The market sells black iron and furs, Roof salt and medicine, and the best ice-fishing gear in the world. Bounties for raiders' heads are posted on the bell tower and paid in Foundation pills.

entries.name: Crown-Touching Peak
entries.summary: The highest mountain that touches the ground. Its summit stands inside the gang wind, and nobody has stood on it since the Ascent Age.
entries.lore: From the Butter Fair it looks like a white blade with the Mirror resting on its tip. Hermit monks live in caves up to the last ledge where breath still works; above it the gang wind strips skin and qi together. Climbers say a stele on the summit is carved with a Wind Dao insight, and that its strokes can be felt from the highest ledge as a pressure in the teeth. Each spring the hermits sell snow lotus from the ledges, three centuries old and colder than ice, to anyone who climbs up to buy it.
entries.truth: The stele is real. It was cut by the last cultivator who tried to fly from the summit to the Mirror after the Ladder broke, and his body is still sitting beside it.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Dusk Ferry
entries.summary: A kingdom of ferrymen on the western shore whose ships make the five-month crossing to the Long Dusk Continent. Ferrymen's families marry ghosts' families, and nobody there thinks it strange.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of the Dusk Ferry's boats have crossed the strait for eight thousand years, and its ferry guilds know every current and every ghost toll on the water. The guild masters elect the Ferry King from among themselves. Children learn to row before they can walk far and learn the courtesies owed to the dead before they can read. Every family keeps a shrine to its ancestors on the far shore, and some have married their dead to the Long Dusk Continent's dead, which binds the living families as in-laws. Ghost cultivators court spirit-rooted children, which frightens their mothers.
entries.truth: The Ferry King drowned four years ago. His ghost still rules, because the guild masters found him more reasonable afterward.

entries.name: The Pasture Garden
entries.summary: A shard world of endless grassland where Ascent Age sects bred their war mounts. Every fifteen years its gate opens on the steppe inside a ring of standing stones.
entries.lore: For twenty days the ring holds a gate onto a green, rainy world under a pale sky, where herds of spirit horses of Ascent Age breeds, long gone from Severed Heaven, run wild. The gate admits cultivators below Core Formation; a Core aura scatters the herds and closes the ring. A tamer who brings out a foal has a fortune. The tribes send their best young riders to every opening, and the khan has announced that this time every foal belongs to him. The next opening is in 3,128.

entries.name: Gate of Gathered Dew
entries.summary: A Water Dao sect that teaches cultivators to pull dew from dry air. In a land where water is power, its disciples carry their own.
entries.lore: The Gate of Gathered Dew's founding art, the Dew-Gathering Palm, condenses water from desert air; a Core Formation elder can fill a cistern under a cloudless sky. The sect sells dew arrays to oases, which makes it rich and makes the water court its enemy, since a dew array needs no allotment. It tests children by leaving them in a dry room with an empty cup for a day. Disciples study Water Dao, array making and medicine, and spend their third year on water service in a dying village, which is how the sect learns which villages to buy.
entries.truth: The dew arrays yield less every year. The air over the Sand Sea is drying faster than the elders can explain, and they have stopped publishing their measurements.

entries.name: The Milk River
entries.summary: The only river in Myriad Sands that reaches the sea every year. It rises from the Wet-Nurse Glacier, cuts the great gorge through the Withered Rivers and spreads into the white delta on the inner coast.
entries.lore: Its water is milky with glacier flour from source to mouth. In the gorge it is a white torrent no boat survives, crossed only on the Kingdom of the Cliff Dwellings rope bridges; below the gorge it slows, spreads and floods the delta every summer. Fishermen catch blind white river eels whose fat makes a renowned eye salve. The flow is steady because the Wet-Nurse never shrinks, and the Kingdom of the White Delta's kings call the river Heaven's one gift to the Myriad Sands Continent.

entries.name: Wet-Nurse Glacier
entries.summary: The great glacier at the head of the Milk River, called the Wet-Nurse because every drop of the river is her milk.
entries.lore: Her snout is a blue cliff six hundred zhang high, and the river leaves it through a cave, already white with rock flour. Herders bring sick yaks to drink at the cave mouth. Ice cultivators cut cores of thousand-year ice from her flanks to lay ice-element foundations, and the Cloister takes one core in ten as tithe. In summer the ice falls from her face as loud as war drums.
entries.truth: She is the only glacier in Myriad Sands that is still growing. Whatever is pulling water from under the Roof's other glaciers has not reached her yet.

entries.name: Forest of Three Thousand Years
entries.summary: The great desert poplar forest on the delta's tail, half alive and half standing dead. Its trees weep poplar tears, a cooling salt alchemists prize.
entries.lore: The living poplars turn gold in autumn, and the dead ones stand among them grey and twisted, some since before the Thousand Lamps Temple was built. Poplar tears crystallize on the bark in summer and are scraped off by the Kingdom of the Desert Poplars's children for a few coppers a jar. Spirit poplars, the trees that woke, move their roots at night toward water, and a grove can walk a li in a year. Foragers say the dead trees listen, and never say anything rude about them under their branches.
entries.truth: The spirit poplars are walking west, toward the [[Thirsting Sands]], following the water down. A grove that reaches the edge drinks itself to death in a season.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Salt Pans
entries.summary: A coastal kingdom of sea-salt pans on the southeastern shore, newly rich and newly hated. Its cheap sun-dried salt is breaking the old salt kingdoms' prices.
entries.lore: Sixty years ago an engineer from the ports showed the coastal fishing villages how to flood shallow pans with seawater and let the sun do the rest. Now the shore is a checkerboard of white pans, and the villages have become a kingdom under the Lu family, the engineer's in-laws. The Kingdom of the Salt Pans salt is coarse and grey and costs a third of pan salt. Children rake salt from dawn and are paid by the basket. The kingdom has no army and is hiring the Kingdom of Escorts escorts and anyone with a sword, because its caravans keep disappearing on the pan.
entries.truth: The Heavenly Scale Pavilion lent the Lu family the money to build the pans, and lent the Ban family the money to fight them. Whoever wins, the Pavilion owns the salt.

entries.name: Sand Whale Bay
entries.summary: A deep basin in the dunes where pods of sand whales gather each spring to calve. Their spouts bring up water from far below, and caravans camp on the rim to catch it.
entries.lore: Sand whales swim under the dunes as fish swim in water, sixty zhang long and blind, and surface only to breathe and to calve. Each spring the pods converge on this basin, and their spouts throw up plumes of damp sand and real water from the deep aquifer. Caravans camp on the rim and run out to fill skins between surfacings, which kills a few people every year. Nobody has tamed an adult, but a calf raised from birth will follow its tamer's footsteps through the sand. The pods are smaller every spring.
entries.truth: The oldest bull carries an Ascent Age harpoon in its back, stamped with the seal of the river cities. It slept through the Dim Age with the harpoon in it.

entries.name: Grotto of Deep Ice
entries.summary: A grotto in the Wet-Nurse Glacier that becomes the gate to a shard world of black ice every nineteen years, in the deepest month of winter.
entries.lore: The gate holds for twenty days and admits Core Formation cultivators and below; a Nascent Soul aura splits the ice and brings the grotto down on everyone. Inside is a windless world of ice caverns lit by blue fungus, where ice-silk worms spin the thread artifact refiners use for armor linings. The last opening was in 3,121. The Cloister sends its third-winter monks in as a trial, and the Kingdom of the Ice Crossing smugglers sell maps of the caverns that are wrong in interesting ways.
entries.truth: The black ice is not ice. It is the frozen blood of an outer demon killed at the Severance, and the worms that eat it are changing.

entries.name: The Mirage Sea
entries.summary: A white salt pan the size of three kingdoms, the bed of an inland sea that died in the Dim Age. At noon the mirages turn it back into a sea, with phantom cities and fleets.
entries.lore: The pan is so flat and white that by midmorning the horizon dissolves, and by noon the Mirage Sea shows what it is named for: water, harbors, towers, sometimes armies, all shimmering. Salt-cutters work in the cool hours and salt caravans cross by night, steering by the stars because the daytime landmarks lie. The Tamarisk River ends here in a bitter lake. Salt is money for the Myriad Sands Continent's mortals, and two salt kingdoms are fighting a price war that Heavenly Scale Pavilion is quietly refereeing. A demonic sect uses the mirages as bait.
entries.truth: The mirages have grown sharper every year since the tide began rising, and some now show places that are not in Severed Heaven at all. Even the sect that hunts with them is afraid of those.

entries.name: The Passing River
entries.summary: The river that falls off the Roof at the Hanging Curtain, feeds the delta oases and dies in the sand. Its dead bed runs on past the buried cities to the outer sea.
entries.lore: The living the Passing River is short: from the Roof's snows over the Sheer Wall to the Hundred Mouths, where it ends. Below that its old bed runs west for a hundred thousand li, a dry valley lined with half-buried Ascent Age quays that the looters use as a road. Once a generation, after a great snow year, a white flood runs the whole bed to the sea in a single night, and drowns whoever is camped in it.
entries.truth: Each year the river ends a few li further upstream. The last white flood was sixty years ago, and the bed has not run since.

entries.name: Lion's Roar Cloister
entries.summary: The Myriad Sands Continent's school of vajra-body fist monks and the Thousand Lamps Temple's border arm. They do not kill: they break you, heal you and offer to shave your head.
entries.lore: The Cloister teaches the Vajra Body in nine layers, each tempered with bronze bells, ice water and beatings, and a Fist Dao whose roar can stop a charging yak. Entry is the Bell: stand under the great bell while it is struck, and if you are still standing when the sound dies, you are in. Monks serve three winters on the wall before they may teach. They hate the [[Eternal Night Palace]] with calm thoroughness. Captured blood cultivators have their meridians broken and are then fed and taught sutras until they repent or die of old age.
entries.truth: Forty captured blood cultivators live in the lower cells. Six have truly repented. Two are spying for the Night Sovereign; the abbot knows which two and feeds them lies.

entries.name: Plain of Stone Men
entries.summary: A plain of ancient stone men, thousands of carved figures facing east across the steppe. Nobody knows who carved them, and the tribes say they turn at night.
entries.lore: Each figure holds a cup in its right hand and a sword at its belt, and the faces are worn smooth. They stand alone or in lines, and the tribes say each marks an enemy killed by a forgotten hero. Shamans meditate among them and claim to hear old battle songs. On the longest night of the year the stones are said to face west, and herders keep away. Formation masters have noticed that the lines make an array, broken in places, whose purpose nobody has worked out.
entries.truth: They do face west on the longest night. The array is a ward against something in the Buried Cities, and the broken places are where tribes took stones for their hearths.

entries.name: Hall of Vows
entries.summary: The vow-keepers of the Roof. Its monks take vows that become laws of their bodies, and it witnesses the karmic oaths behind the Heavenly Scale Pavilion's contracts.
entries.lore: A Hall of Vows monk chooses a vow, of silence, of standing, of never refusing a beggar, and keeps it until it carves itself into his meridians; then it is a power, and breaking it shatters his cultivation. Old vow-keepers are frightening: one has not lain down in three hundred years and cannot be knocked over. The Hall also witnesses oaths. Every karmic contract the [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] writes is sealed before a Hall of Vows monk for a mid-grade stone, and the Hall keeps a copy. It recruits by asking what you would never do, and waiting to see if you lie.
entries.truth: The archive can unmake an oath as well as witness it. The Hall has done it twice, both times at the [[Thousand Lamps Temple]]'s request, and the Heavenly Scale Pavilion has never learned which of its contracts failed.

entries.name: Kingdom of Grave-Keepers
entries.summary: A farming and fishing kingdom where every family keeps watch over its graves. Corpse thieves raid the coast for bodies to sell across the strait, and the Grave-Keepers have learned to fight.
entries.lore: In the Kingdom of Grave-Keepers the dead are buried with iron nails in the coffin lid, and a relative sleeps in a hut beside the grave for forty-nine days. Thieves come anyway, because a fresh body fetches a laborer's yearly wage in the City of Evening Light and a cultivator's corpse buys a farm. The ruling Kang family keeps a militia of grave guards and pays a bounty for every thief's head. Children learn grave-watch and staff fighting from eight. Spirit-rooted children are sent to the [[Vulture Burial Temple]] on the Roof, the only sect the Kang trust with bodies.
entries.truth: The grave militia sells the bodies of the thieves it kills to the same buyers, and paid for the kingdom's new walls that way.

entries.name: Water's End
entries.summary: The oases at the foot of the Sheer Wall, where the Roof's rivers fan out into inland deltas and die in the sand. The richest farmland in the Myriad Sands Continent, and it is shrinking.
entries.lore: Below the Hanging Curtain falls the Passing River splits into a hundred channels and feeds a crescent of oasis kingdoms: date groves, vineyards, spirit melon fields and poplar forests, watered by underground channels dug in the Dim Age. Every drop is allotted by the water court of the [[Thousand Lamps Temple]], which judges wells the way other courts judge murders. Each year the river's mouths close a few li further upstream, the tail oases die, and their people walk upstream with their goats into kingdoms that do not want them. Karez diggers, dew-gatherers and water diviners are the princes here.
entries.truth: The river is not failing at the top. The Roof sends down as much water as ever; the delta is losing it into the ground, and the lost water slopes west toward the [[Thirsting Sands]].

entries.name: Broken Jade Workshop
entries.summary: Artifact refiners who buy splinters of Ladder jade dug from the crater walls and work them into artifacts nobody else can make.
entries.lore: When the fragment struck it shattered, and splinters of Ladder jade are still found in the crater walls, each holding a trace of the arrays carved into the Ladder. The Broken Jade Workshop buys every splinter dug up, refines them over the crater's fire vein and sells the results at the Grand Auction: blades that cut space a little, rings that hold a room. Apprentices spend their first five years at the bellows and their first burn scar is a badge. The master is a Nascent Soul refiner who has not left the forge in eighty years.
entries.truth: Some splinters still answer Upper Realm tokens, as the Fallen Ladder does. The Workshop sells those to the [[Armillary Pavilion]] alone, at ten times the price, and asks no questions.

entries.name: Butter Fair
entries.summary: A market town on the high pastures where herders sell yak butter to the Thousand Lamps Temple's buyers each autumn, and lowlanders come up for snow lotus and worm-grass.
entries.lore: For eleven months the Butter Fair is three hundred stone houses and a monastery. In the twelfth, ten thousand tents go up and the butter is weighed on the temple's scales, one jar in ten taken as tithe. It is the only place on the high Roof where spirit stones are worth more than butter. Lowland alchemists buy worm-grass, the herb that is a caterpillar in winter and a blade of grass in summer, and pay double for live ones. Corpse buyers drink in the back rooms of the Red Door inn and call themselves salt merchants.

entries.name: Bronze Man Workshop
entries.summary: Puppet makers at the port who rebuild Ascent Age guardian puppets dug from the Buried Cities and dragged up from the Shattered Sea, and sell them as guards that never sleep.
entries.lore: An Ascent Age bronze guardian, rekeyed to a new master, fights at the realm it was built for, and the Workshop has learned to rekey them. It buys broken puppets from City-Opener crews and salvage captains, rebuilds them around new array cores and sells them to caravan houses, oasis kings and the Heavenly Scale Pavilion vaults. Apprentices learn puppetry, formations and casting, and spend their first year being knocked down by test puppets. The [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] has tried to buy the Workshop twice and burn it once, and the founder kept a puppet from each attempt.
entries.truth: Some rekeyed guardians still obey their first masters underneath. Three of the Workshop's puppets left their posts in the same month this year, all walking west.

entries.name: Cave of the Ebb Tide
entries.summary: A sea cave on the fog coast that opens on a drowned shard world at the lowest tide of an eighteen-year cycle.
entries.lore: Once every eighteen years the sea draws back further than at any other time, and for seven days the cave at the foot of the Teeth stands dry. Inside, a gate opens on a shard world of shallow seas and drowned Ascent Age quays, with pearl beds and sunken cargo in water clear to the bottom. Cultivators up to Core Formation may enter; a Nascent Soul aura makes the shard's sea rise and fill the cave. The last opening was in 3,117, the next falls in 3,135, and the shark-folk claim the cave as theirs.

entries.name: Harbor of Camels and Sails
entries.summary: The great port of the inner coast, where camel trains from Fallen Star City meet salvage ships from the Shattered Sea. Its quays are lined with appraisers and its taverns with liars.
entries.lore: Every caravan to the sea ends at the Harbor of Camels and Sails's camel yards, and every salvage ship unloads at its quays. The Heavenly Scale Pavilion, the Pavilion of True Assay and a dozen smaller houses keep appraisal stalls on the waterfront, and a lucky salvager can sell a sealed bronze box for a fortune before anyone opens it. The Port Syndicate, five shipping families, takes a twentieth of everything. Captains recruit crew in the Drowned Lamp tavern, where the pay is good and the odds of coming back are chalked on the wall.

entries.name: Camel Bell Tribes
entries.summary: Camel nomads of the deep dunes who read the sand like a book and know where the buried cities will surface next. They guide looters, and sometimes bury them.
entries.lore: The Camel Bell Tribes travel in clans of a few hundred, each with a bell tuned so the worms hear it as wind. They own nothing that cannot ride a camel, and they hold the deep wells by memory, never maps. Children learn to smell water in sand at four and to sing the dune-songs that record which cities surfaced where. Chiefs sell guidance to looter crews for a share of the finds; crews that cheat them die of thirst a day from a well nobody mentioned. Spirit-rooted children go to the clan's dune-singers, who teach Earth and Wind arts.
entries.truth: The oldest dune-songs describe the cities before the sand: green, rich, and singing about a lord under the river who must not be woken.

entries.name: Kingdom That Watches the Pillar
entries.summary: A port city-state on the cliffs facing the Stump. On clear nights the whole city climbs onto the roofs to watch the Pillar, and its astrologers sell what they see.
entries.lore: The ruling council is drawn from star-watching families who have recorded the Stump's hum and the Mirror's width for five thousand years. They sell tide tables and Shattered Sea weather to salvage captains, and divination to anyone. Children learn the stars before the alphabet and are taught that the Pillar will be climbed again one day. The Kingdom That Watches the Pillar's harbor is where most salvage expeditions into the Shattered Sea set out, and its widows' quarter is the largest in the Myriad Sands Continent.
entries.truth: The star families' records show the Stump's hum growing louder every decade. They have sold copies to the [[Armillary Pavilion]] and to a polite buyer who hums while he reads, and they did not recognize the [[Void Choir]] in him.

entries.name: City of Evening Light
entries.summary: The port of the Last Light Shore, where ships leave for the Long Dusk Continent and the Court of No Light keeps a registry office. Everything that crosses the strait, living or dead, is counted here.
entries.lore: The City of Evening Light's harbor faces the endless dusk, and its lamps are lit all day out of habit. Ships leave every morning on the five-month run to the Long Dusk Continent's sunlit coast, carrying salt, cloth and paying passengers; coffins ride in the holds and are not discussed. The Court of No Light's registry office, staffed by pale clerks who never eat, records every death in the city and issues passes to the living who want to visit the Pale City. Thousand Puppet Gate buyers keep a well-ventilated warehouse by the docks. The fish market is excellent.

entries.name: Kingdom of Fog Nets
entries.summary: Villages of fog nets on the dunes above the cold sea. Every family hangs fine nets before dawn, wrings them by sunrise and lives on what drips out.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Fog Nets is ruled by the Net Mothers, a council of the oldest women, because the nets have always belonged to the women and the nets are water. A household's wealth is its net frames, and a marriage is a negotiation over net rights. Children wake in the dark to wring nets, and many learn the call for fog coming before their own names. Spirit-rooted children are rare and precious, and most are sold to the [[Gate of Gathered Dew]] for dew arrays. The Kingdom of Fog Nets hates the wreckers next door, whose false lights bring ships but also sea-clan reprisals.
entries.truth: One of the Net Mothers is a shark-folk half-blood. She is the reason the Cold Tide Clan has never raided the Kingdom of Fog Nets, and the other Mothers know exactly what she is.

entries.name: The Eaves
entries.summary: The southern lip of the Roof, where the plateau ends at the Sheer Wall and the Thousand Lamps Temple's thousand lamps burn along the edge. Pilgrims, vow-keepers, lamp-makers and the Askers.
entries.lore: At night the lamps of the [[Thousand Lamps Temple]] can be seen from the sand a thousand li away, a line of light along the top of the Sheer Wall. Below it pilgrims climb the Prostration Stair one body-length at a time; above it lamp-makers, butter merchants and vow-keepers live off the temple. The Thousand Lamps Temple claims no land here and does not need to. When a monk's lamp goes out, the Askers walk down the stair to learn why, and nobody in the Eaves lies to an Asker twice. The temple's water court now sits every day, because the oases below are failing and every king is suing his neighbor.
entries.truth: One lamp in the deepest hall has not flickered in nine thousand years. Its monk is why the Askers always find their answer: he hears every lie told within sight of the Wall.

top.note: a hidden monk in the Thousand Lamps Temple; the Abbot is Body Integration

entries.name: Brine-Crust Marsh
entries.summary: A brine marsh under a salt crust, where the pan looks solid and isn't. Whole caravans have broken through and vanished into the black mud beneath.
entries.lore: The crust is a hand thick over most of the marsh and a finger thick in places nobody can see. Beneath it lies brine mud a hundred zhang deep that preserves whatever falls in, and drowned camels and men come up years later, pickled and perfect. Salt-cutters cross it in lines, probing with iron rods. The mud holds Dim Age caravans and their cargo, and divers in qi-shield arrays go down after it. Few come back up.

entries.name: Kingdom of Mended Antiquities
entries.summary: A town of master restorers in the eastern canyons who mend Ascent Age relics broken by looters. Their work is so good that the relics sometimes look better than new.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Mended Antiquities's guild houses take broken artifacts from the Buried Cities and the Shattered Sea and make them whole: recasting bronze, recutting jade, re-inking faded arrays. Apprentices learn the scripts and maker's marks of every Ascent Age school, and the guild's ancient-style refining is the best in the Myriad Sands Continent. The town is ruled by the Masters' Table. Its children grow up among bronze filings and old scripts, and they are taught never to say the word copy. Every appraiser in Fallen Star City knows the guild by name.
entries.truth: Most of what Kingdom of Mended Antiquities sells was never broken, because it never existed. The guild forges Ascent Age relics from scratch, and its work has sold at three Grand Auctions.

entries.name: Blood Sand Gate
entries.summary: A demonic bandit sect in the red canyons that robs the coast road. They turn their victims' blood into sand, and they claim the canyon floors are red because of them.
entries.lore: Blood Sand disciples cultivate a Saber Dao fed on blood: each kill is drawn into the blade and dried into red sand that hardens the body. They hold three canyon forts, raid caravans that do not pay, sell captives to corpse buyers and the Thirsting Heart Sect, and sell safe passage to those who do pay. The sect recruits by offer: survivors of a raid are asked whether they would rather join or die, and most join. The [[Temple of the Merciful Blade]] kills them, they kill the Temple of the Merciful Blade's monks, and the caravan houses pay both.
entries.truth: The Blood Sand Gate's master is the younger brother of the Temple of the Merciful Blade's abbot. They meet each year at the Dead Falls to agree how many of each other's people to kill.

entries.name: Snow Lion Ridge
entries.summary: A ridge of high crags ruled by a pride of snow lions under a Nascent Soul lion with a turquoise mane. The monks and the lions keep an old pact.
entries.lore: The Turquoise Mane has ruled the ridge for nine hundred years, and his pride of forty grown snow lions is the strongest beast power on the Roof. By the pact sworn with the [[Lion's Roar Cloister]]'s founder, the lions fight raiders on the ice and the monks never tame a cub. Herders on the ridge pay a yak a month and are left alone; the Black Yak Tribes refuse and lose ten. A lion's roar here can bring down a cornice, and avalanches are how they hunt. Beast tamers who try to steal cubs are found in spring.
entries.truth: The pact's full text, kept in the Cloister, gives the lions one human child every hundred years. The monks have paid it eight times and told no one.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Cliff Dwellings
entries.summary: Cliff villages in the Milk River Gorge, joined by rope bridges and ladders. Their people hold the only crossing for five hundred li and ferry caravans over it.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of the Cliff Dwellings live in houses cut into both walls of the gorge a thousand zhang above the white water, and cross between them on rope bridges that sway in the wind. The Bridge Elders set the toll by the river's height. Children are lowered on ropes to gather cliff swallow nests, which medicine halls buy as a lung tonic. A Kingdom of the Cliff Dwellings who drops a caravan's cargo owes its value; one who drops a passenger owes a life. Raiders who attack the bridges find the ropes cut behind them.
entries.truth: The Bridge Elders pay the [[Blood Sand Gate]] a tenth of every toll, and in return the sect robs every caravan that tries the fords instead.

entries.name: Kingdom of Salt Houses
entries.summary: A salt kingdom on the edge of the pan whose houses, walls and palace are built of salt blocks. It never rains, so they never melt, and the king fears clouds.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Salt Houses cuts salt in blocks from the pan's crust, builds with it and sells the rest by the camel-load. The ruling Ban family has held the cutting rights for twelve centuries and set the price of salt from Fallen Star City to the Roof, until the sea-salt pans on the coast began undercutting it. Children grow up licking the walls, which their mothers forbid, and cut their first block at ten. Spirit-rooted children learn the Salt Body, a slow tempering that makes flesh resist rot and poison. A rare rain is a disaster: whole streets slump in a night.
entries.truth: The Ban family has hired the Gate of the Empty City to lure sea-salt caravans into the pan. Three have vanished this year.

entries.name: Pavilion of True Assay
entries.summary: The world's second appraisal house, and the only one Heavenly Scale Pavilion does not own. Its seal on a certificate can double an item's price at auction.
entries.lore: The Pavilion was founded by appraisers who walked out of the Heavenly Scale Pavilion over a forged lot, and it lives on one promise: it will appraise against anyone, the Heavenly Scale Pavilion included. Its masters read age, origin and curse from a shard by touch, and its ledger of Ascent Age maker's marks is the best in the Myriad Sands Continent. Apprenticeship lasts ten years and begins with a year of sorting sand by grain. The Heavenly Scale Pavilion tolerates it because buyers trust an auction more when a rival has checked the lots, and hates it for the same reason.
entries.truth: Its founder left because he found that a third of the Grand Auction's Ascent Age relics were made in the Withered Rivers. The Pavilion of True Assay still has his notes and has never published them.

entries.name: Cliff of Welcoming Souls
entries.summary: A sea cliff where the shore villages gather in the seventh month to welcome back their dead. On the fifteenth night the dead walk up out of the strait to meet them.
entries.lore: Families climb the cliff with lanterns, food and the names of the drowned written on paper boats. At midnight on the fifteenth, when the [[Nether Shard]] is closest, figures walk up out of the water, the newly dead first. Most want only to see their families once. Some want more, and the Grave-Keepers stand at the top with iron staffs. Ghost cultivators come to meditate in the yin tide, which is stronger here than anywhere else in the Myriad Sands Continent, and make the villagers nervous.

entries.name: One Thread of Sky
entries.summary: The narrowest slot canyon in the Withered Rivers. Every twenty-one years, at noon on midsummer day, a single beam of sunlight reaches its floor and becomes a gate for one hour.
entries.lore: The beam is a gate only while the sun is overhead, about an hour, and anyone below Core Formation who steps in during that hour is carried into a shard world of red stone towers and fire springs. The way out is the largest spring, which throws people back onto the canyon floor each time it erupts; the eruptions stop after thirty days. Fire-element herbs grow around the vents, guarded by salamanders. The canyon fits about two hundred people, and the fighting for places starts a month early. The next midsummer noon is in 3,133.

entries.name: Kingdom of Luring Lamps
entries.summary: A wreckers' principality whose lords hang false lamps on the dunes to draw ships onto the shoals. Its people are rich in salvage and poor in friends.
entries.lore: On fog nights the lamps of the Kingdom of Luring Lamps look exactly like a harbor. Ships that steer for them break on the Teeth, and by dawn the wreckers are stripping the hulls. The ruling Gou family, two Foundation cultivators and a Core Formation patron nobody sees, takes half of every wreck. The Kingdom of Luring Lamps children learn to swim in surf that kills outsiders and to keep their mouths shut. The Cold Tide Clan takes its share too, which is why the shark-folk leave the wreckers alone. Salvage goes inland through Whalebone Harbor with forged papers.
entries.truth: Last spring the lamps brought in a [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] ship. The Gou family has its cargo and three of its crew in the cellars, and has not decided which is more dangerous to keep.

entries.name: Jade Bone Range
entries.summary: The crest range of the High Roof: white peaks running east from the outer coast, with the Crown-Touching Peak at the top. Its snows feed every river on the continent.
entries.lore: Herders say the range is the spine of a god who lay down to keep the Roof from blowing away. Its passes close for seven months a year and are strung with the Kingdom of Sutra Flags sutra flags. Snow leopards hunt the lower flanks and the hermits of the [[Crown-Touching Peak]] keep the upper. Ice cultivators cut thousand-year ice from its north faces, which fetch a mid-grade stone a block in Fallen Star City.

entries.name: The Last Light Shore
entries.summary: The Myriad Sands Continent's southern shore, facing the Long Dusk Continent across the strait. The southern sky never quite darkens or brightens, ghosts cross the water in the seventh month, and the corpse road ends at its ports.
entries.lore: Look south from any beach in the Last Light Shore and the horizon glows like an evening that never finishes: the twilight of the [[Long Dusk Continent]] under the shadow of the [[Fallen Ladder]]. The coast is cool and heavy with yin qi, which ghost cultivators love and farmers hate. In the seventh month, when the [[Nether Shard]] passes close, the dead drift north across the strait, and the shore villages set out food and bar their doors. The rest of the year the ports ferry the living to the Long Dusk Continent's sunlit coasts, and the dead as well: bodies from the Roof and the sand go aboard here for the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] buyers.
entries.truth: The [[Court of No Light]] counts the Myriad Sands Continent's dead from its registry office in the City of Evening Light as carefully as its own, and is preparing a legal claim on every soul that dies within sight of the strait.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Overflow
entries.summary: A small oasis kingdom watered by the overflow of Fallen Star City's crater spring. It is green, rich and entirely at Fallen Star City's mercy.
entries.lore: The spring's overflow leaves the crater through a tunnel cut in the Dim Age and spreads into fields of alfalfa, dates and spirit rice below the rim. The Kingdom of the Overflow feeds Fallen Star City, and Fallen Star City could close the tunnel any day. The ruling Fang family pays water rent to the city council, keeps no army and marries its daughters to the Heavenly Scale Pavilion stewards. Children grow up with the roar of the tunnel in their ears and a fear of its silence. Whenever the flow drops, the kingdom panics, and the Fang buy another decade with another daughter.
entries.truth: The overflow has fallen by a third in a century. Fallen Star City's council has already voted, in secret, to close the tunnel when it falls by half.

entries.name: Ruins of the Jade Towers
entries.summary: The largest buried city yet found: a district of jade towers that the dunes uncover about every forty years. The House of City-Openers has dug it four times and never reached its center.
entries.lore: When the dunes part, a hundred towers stand up out of the sand in rows, joined by bridges at their thirtieth floors. They are full of sand to that height and empty above, with bronze doors, cold arrays and guardian puppets that wake when touched. Each uncovering lasts about a year before the sand returns, and for that year the Ruins of the Jade Towers is the busiest place in the Myriad Sands Continent. The last was in 3,098. The next is not expected until 3,138, but the dunes over it are already thinning, and claim-jumpers are camped on the crest.

entries.name: Tomb of the Cloud Ship
entries.summary: An Ascent Age cloud-ship half buried in the dunes twenty thousand li inland, its bronze keel longer than a city wall. Its upper decks are stripped; its holds are still sealed.
entries.lore: Nobody knows how a ship built for the sky came to rest here. The dunes cover and uncover it every few decades, and right now its prow stands clear, hung with fog nets by the Kingdom of Fog Nets villagers who think it lucky. Its hull is warded by arrays that still burn anyone who cuts at it, and the hatches answer only to an Ascent Age token. Formation masters camp beside it for years trying to read the wards, which are said to include a flying array nobody alive can make.
entries.truth: The ship came down the Heaven Ladder, not up it. The log sealed in the captain's cabin names who was aboard, and some of those names are carried today by families in the Floating Peak Continent.

entries.name: Kingdom of Counting Houses
entries.summary: A city-state of clerks on the east road, where the Heavenly Scale Pavilion's debtors work off what they owe. Its children learn the abacus before they learn to talk.
entries.lore: Half the clerks in the Heavenly Scale Pavilion branches around the world were trained in the Kingdom of Counting Houses's counting schools, where a child who can sum ten thousand figures by sight is worth more than one with a spirit root. The Guild of Ledgers governs, and its prisons are offices: debtors bound by karmic oath sit at desks until the debt is paid, and their children inherit what is left. Spirit-rooted clerks learn the Abacus Heart, a Karma method that lets them feel when a number lies. The money market changes any currency in the world, at the worst rates in the world.
entries.truth: Some of the Kingdom of Counting Houses's debts were bought, not lent. A Guild bureau buys bad debts on six continents and brings the debtors here through the Fallen Star City array.

entries.name: Mirror-Gazing Lake
entries.summary: A glacier lake that holds the Mirror's reflection. Every twelve years, when the Mirror stands straight overhead at midnight, the reflection becomes a gate.
entries.lore: The gate stays open for nine nights and admits only Qi Condensation cultivators: a Foundation aura shatters the reflection and closes it for everyone. Inside is a shard world of wind and snow, the outer court of an Ascent Age wind sect, where frost cranes nest and wind-pattern jade forms in the drifts. The Kingdom of Sutra Flags monasteries send their herder children in with shopping lists. The next opening is in 3,129, and lowland sects are already renting tent ground on the shore.
entries.truth: The wind sect sealed its techniques in the frost cranes. Kill a crane and its method is lost; tame one and, in time, it teaches.

entries.name: Kingdom of Candlelight
entries.summary: The lamp-makers' kingdom on the plateau behind the Thousand Lamps Temple. It pays its taxes in butter, wicks and sons, and its kings have been temple vassals for four thousand years.
entries.lore: Everyone in the Kingdom of Candlelight works for the lamps: butter clarifiers, wick spinners, bronze casters, scripture copyists. The Ling family rules as Lamp Wardens; every first son goes to the temple at seven, and the second sons fight over the throne. Children learn the hundred and eight prostrations before they can read. Those with spirit roots go to the temple's outer court and come home a year later with shaved heads or not at all. This year the Thousand Lamps Temple raised the lamp tithe by a third, and the Warden is quietly buying lowland butter at a loss to cover it.
entries.truth: The tithe rose because nine hundred new lamps were lit last year, more than in any year since the Outer Demon War. The temple is recruiting, and it has not said what for.

entries.name: Iron Bone Tribes
entries.summary: Nomad clans of the Black Frost Continent's southern steppe who cultivate the body instead of qi. Some carry giant blood.
entries.lore: The tribes temper their bodies in blizzards and fight bare-handed to show contempt. A tribe's chief is whoever can lift the clan's ancestor stone. Every few generations they unite under a Great Khan and ride south across the ice, and every coast they reach remembers why it built walls.
entries.truth: The Bone Ancestor sleeping inside Ancestor Mountain is a Deity Transformation body cultivator from the Dim Age, and he is waking up. Two war chiefs have quietly reached Deity Transformation in body. The tribes only count the Ancestor.

top.note: two war chiefs; the Bone Ancestor waking

entries.name: Thousand Isles League
entries.summary: Island sects, pirate lords and free ports, allied only against anyone who tries to rule them.
entries.lore: The League meets in Ten Thousand Sails when an outside power threatens the islands, and otherwise robs itself.
entries.truth: Half the League's pirate lords pay tribute to the Azure Wave Palace for safe passage. The other half don't know. Three of the League's island masters are at Deity Transformation, and each believes the other two are not.

ties.why: We pay triple for Calm Seas' grain and ask no questions about its crews.
Our treasure ship lies in the Bay of Sunken Ships; we keep sending divers, and the wreckers keep killing them.

entries.name: Jade Strait
entries.summary: The strait between the Morning Star Continent and the Vast Wilds Continent, some thirty thousand li of sea crossed by a chain of islands that humans and beasts both claim.
entries.lore: At low tide reef roads join each island to the next. A mortal who walks the whole chain spends about two years on it, and a Foundation cultivator who flies the gaps about six weeks, if nothing eats them. Every frontier war of the last thousand years started on these islands.

entries.name: Jar-Mother Clans
entries.summary: Matriarchal Gu-raising clans of the Vast Wilds Continent's poison valleys. Harm one, and every Gu in the valleys remembers your scent.
entries.lore: A Jar-Mother seals a hundred venomous creatures in a jar and lets them fight until one remains; that one becomes the Gu. Their villages hang in miasma no outsider can breathe. They trade antidotes to Apricot Grove Valley and curses to anyone who pays, and they have never lost a war, because nobody who starts one survives the year.
entries.truth: The eldest Jar-Mother keeps a Gu that has eaten a Nascent Soul. It is the real reason the Beast Court of Ten Thousand Mountains leaves the valleys alone. She reached Deity Transformation forty years ago and lets the clans believe she is still Nascent Soul.

ties.why: The Stockade's strains are ours, stolen by its master, and we have known for years; we are waiting.

entries.name: Jing Capital
entries.summary: Capital of the Great Jing Dynasty and the largest city in the world, 400 li of walled wards built over three spirit veins, with forty million mortals and a palace the size of a county. A hub of the Heavenly Circuit.
entries.lore: Forty million mortals and well over a million cultivators live inside walls no Core Formation cultivator can break, under a palace array nobody has ever tested. Its wards are cities of their own, each with its gates, markets and sect halls, and the great avenues are li wide and patrolled by spear-guards on spirit horses.
entries.fromAbove: A walled city 400 li across at the plain's middle, its avenues radiating from a palace under a white dome of light, with three beams of vein-glow rising inside it.

ties.why: The prefecture's millet and rice feed us, and we send back law, auditors and registry slips.
Our transfer hall is the Circuit's busiest gate, and we pay its tolls and resent them.
The whole south's grain arrives through the Grain-Barge Mouth, and this year half of it does not.
The palace kitchens eat the prefecture's Jade Pearl rice, so the Household sends auditors when it falls.
The Geomancy Office reads our veins at the wells for the court, and lately will not let anyone look at the logs.

features.name: the palace array's wall of light
the Heavenly Circuit's transfer hall
the ward gates, shut at dusk by decree
the vein-wells under the great avenues

top.note: the Ancestor Emperor, in the palace

entries.name: Fallen Star City
entries.summary: The world's greatest market, built inside a crater a falling piece of the Ladder left in the Sand Sea. Seat of the Heavenly Scale Pavilion and a hub of the Heavenly Circuit.
entries.lore: The Grand Auction of Fallen Star City is held every ten years and sets prices for the world. A spring rose in the crater after the fragment struck, and it is the only reason a city can live there.

entries.name: The Mirror
entries.summary: The great thousand world that Severed Heaven circles. It hangs in the night sky as a pale disc three times the width of the moon, and it is slowly growing.
entries.lore: Mortals pray to the Mirror as Heaven. Cultivators know it as the Upper Realm, where ascension leads. Severed Heaven swings around it on a long, lopsided orbit of about ninety thousand years. When the world draws close, the Mirror's qi spills across the gap: the High Tide. When it swings away, qi thins: the Ebb. The Mirror has been widening in the sky for twenty-five thousand years.
entries.truth: The Mirror's immortals cut the Heaven Ladder from their end. They have not forgotten Severed Heaven, and they are watching the tide too.

entries.name: The Nether Shard
entries.summary: A cold shard world drenched in yin. Each year in the seventh month it passes closest, the barrier thins, and the dead walk.
entries.lore: Ghost Month is Severed Heaven's oldest festival and its most dangerous. Souls of the newly dead drift toward the Nether Shard as it passes, which is why rebirth is uncertain and why Ghost Way cultivators grow fastest in the seventh month.
entries.truth: Under the Fallen Ladder the barrier to the Nether Shard never fully closes. Things come through that were never alive in Severed Heaven.

entries.name: Night Banquet Sect
entries.summary: An aristocratic demonic sect in the Morning Star Continent's southern marshes, fifty thousand strong, with halls on a hundred lamplit islands. Every guest at their banquets is either a diner or the meal.
entries.lore: Night Banquet Sect cultivators devour qi from the living, and they do it with exquisite manners. They run the black markets of half of the Morning Star Continent, buy secrets from every court, and hold a banquet each new moon, in a hall nobody finds twice, to which rival cultivators are invited. Not all of them leave. The Clear Heaven Sword Sect has sworn three times to burn them out.
entries.truth: The Banquet Master reached Deity Transformation sixty years ago and is hiding it, waiting for the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's ancestor to die.
entries.fromAbove: A hundred lamplit islands in black water, pavilions on stilts linked by lacquered causeways, and a faint red glow where the new-moon hall stands, never in the same place twice.

ties.why: We buy indentures wherever families are starving, and King Hao's hired guards turn our buyers back.
We run the Market and guarantee its peace; whoever draws steel aboard is served at the next banquet.
Our chamberlain stands behind the king's throne and takes twenty youths from every county each autumn to serve at the banquets.
We hold the invitations to the Phantom Feast and send promising young cultivators of other sects in, all expenses paid.
We buy indentures from the camp's hungry and pick the rooted among them.
The Stockade's masters sell our guests the curses they cannot buy elsewhere.
The Sword Sect has sworn three times to burn us out, and we keep eyes on its peaks to see when it will try.
A disgraced Sword Sect disciple in the quarry kingdom has been writing to us, and we have answered.
Blackwater's loot is our best source of clean goods, and the harbor master we put there keeps its books.
Two of our fronts hold hills at the New Vein Market, buying ore and a look into the vein.
We have offered the Dawn League help, and our price is the three clefts over the Turtle-Spine.

features.name: the banquet hall, found only by invitation
lacquered causeways between the islands
the guests' wine cellars
the lantern pavilions

entries.name: Conclave of Nine Clans
entries.summary: Nine bloodline clans that claim descent from the Age of the Ascent and hold the floating peaks of the Floating Peak Continent.
entries.lore: Each clan carries a bloodline: thunder, crane, qilin and six more. Their children are born with it awake or not at all, and those without it are sent down to the ground to serve. They marry among themselves, sneer at every sect founded after the Severance, and settle disputes by duel on an arena floating above the clouds.
entries.truth: Three of the nine bloodlines come from Upper Realm envoys who stayed after the Severance. The Conclave's Old Ancestor is a Mahayana who still remembers the Mirror's language. Below him, the First Elder is at Body Integration and three clan ancestors are at Void Refinement.

ties.why: A son of ours whose bloodline was sealed at birth lives among the exiles of the Kingdom Facing the Peaks, and we mean to take him back without noise.

entries.name: Court of No Light
entries.meaning: Court of No Light (also: Court of Ignorance)
entries.summary: The ghost court that rules the Long Dusk Continent's dead from the Pale City, with laws, registers and judges older than any sect.
entries.lore: The Court registers every death under the Fallen Ladder, judges each soul and assigns it a place. Living visitors need a pass, paid in years of lifespan. The Pale Sovereign has ruled since the Severance; she was there when the Ladder fell, and she has never said what she saw.
entries.truth: The Sealer's name was erased from the living, not the dead. The Pale Sovereign remembers it and keeps it as leverage. Under her, the Chief Judge is a Body Integration ghost and two judges sit at Void Refinement.

entries.name: The Pale City
entries.summary: Capital of the dead under the Fallen Ladder. Living travelers arrive by array among ghosts and pay for their stay in years.
entries.lore: Streets of white stone, lanterns that burn without heat, and a market where a ghost will sell you a dead man's memories by the ounce.

entries.name: Thousand Lamps Temple
entries.summary: The great Buddhist monastery on the Roof of the Myriad Sands Continent, where a lamp burns for every monk alive.
entries.lore: Each monk who takes vows lights a life lamp in the great hall; when a lamp goes out, the temple knows its monk has died and sends someone to ask why. The Thousand Lamps Temple arbitrates disputes for all sides because it claims no territory. Its arhats will not kill, but they will beat a demonic cultivator to within an inch of his life and then offer to shave his head.
entries.truth: The Thousand Lamps Temple owns the water rights to two thirds of the Myriad Sands Continent's oases, and its compassion has a price list. A monk in the deepest hall has been meditating for nine thousand years and reached Mahayana without telling anyone. The Abbot is at Body Integration and believes he is the temple's peak.

ties.why: We sent the Temple of Alms-Food its abbot and its first monks, and our lamps burn for them still.

top.note: a hidden monk; the Abbot is Body Integration

entries.name: Morning Star Continent
entries.summary: The human heartland: great river plains, cloud-wrapped sect peaks and more kingdoms than anyone has counted. Most lives start here.
entries.lore: The Morning Star Continent holds more people than the other five continents together. The Great Jing Dynasty rules its mortal heartland, the Clear Heaven Sword Sect rules its northern peaks, and Apricot Grove Valley sells pills to both. In the southern marshes, the Night Banquet Sect waits for any of them to stumble. The continent's southwest tip nearly touches the Vast Wilds Continent across the Jade Strait, and that frontier is where humans and beasts bleed each other.
entries.truth: The three spirit veins under Jing Capital are being drained to keep the Ancestor Emperor alive, and the heartland's harvests are failing because of it.
entries.fromAbove: More than any one look holds: at its heart the river plains webbed with canals round the Jing Capital's white dome, the Sword Domain's seventy-two peaks ringed in sword-light at its northern tip, the red volcanic spine down its east, and beast wilds and karst along its frontier coasts.

top.note: the Ancestor Emperor, unseen and rumored dying

entries.name: Clear Heaven Sword Sect
entries.summary: The Morning Star Continent's foremost sword sect, some thirty thousand disciples on seventy-two peaks in the north. Proud, rule-bound and very good at killing.
entries.lore: Entry is the Sword Stair: nine thousand nine hundred steps up the face of the first peak, each heavier than the last, climbed in front of the whole sect gathered on the terraces below. Rank is decided by duels. The Clear Heaven Sword Sect calls itself the shield of the righteous and keeps a list of demonic cultivators it means to kill; the Night Banquet Sect's master has topped it for four hundred years. Its seventy-two peaks stand along the Snow Blade Ridge for twenty thousand li, each with its own halls and vassal sects beneath, and over the main peak a dome of pale sword-light holds the sect's great array.
entries.truth: The founding ancestor, a Void Refinement sword cultivator, is still in seclusion under the main peak. He stopped answering summons two hundred years ago, and the elders are afraid to look.
entries.fromAbove: Seventy-two summits along the ridge, each crowned with halls and a ring of pale sword-light, the main peak at their heart under a great dome of white array-glow, and the Sword Stair a single straight scratch up the first peak's face.

access.rank: disciple of the Clear Heaven Sword Sect

ties.why: Their master tops our list of demonic cultivators, and their spies climb our lower peaks every season.
Four of our elders went to serve their term and are past due home, and the Watch will not say when they return.
The Zhus have forged every sword our disciples draw for six thousand years, and we keep their forge under our shelter.
We hold the gate on the sixty-ninth peak and auction forty places to outsiders each opening.
We bury our dead's swords in the valley and send disciples among them on oath.
Every spring's Stair-climbers are fed, housed, healed and bet on by the city, so our peaks need not.
We hold the ridge's passes and charge toll on every traveler over them.
The kingdom cuts every whetstone and sword-step our peaks use, and its king is one of our outer disciples.
Its customs house taxes our ships' strait crossings, and we put up with it for the ferries and pilots.
General Yan Ku's garrisons ambush our recruiters at the passes when a registered child is with them.
The kingdom pays our tithe, and our outer disciples guard the north end of its bridge.
The Vermilion Talisman Sect is our vassal on paper, and its talismans arm our rivals' armies in practice.
We hold the top hundred steps and sell their Cloud-Silk rice at ten low-grade stones a catty.
The Thunder-Drawing Sect is our old rival, a loud and brutal one, and it never quite goes away.

features.name: the Sword Stair, nine thousand nine hundred steps up the first peak
the duel terraces where rank is settled
the sealed hall beneath the main peak

top.note: the founding ancestor, silent in seclusion

entries.name: March of Pacified Borders
entries.summary: The empire's frontier march, 12,000 li of hill country ruled by the Gongsun family of generals: some forty million farmers who plow with spears at hand, and a line of beacon peaks whose spirit-fire carries a raid warning across the march in a night.
entries.lore: The Gongsuns have held the march for nine generations and buried most of their sons on the wall. Every family owes one child to the garrison at sixteen, which keeps a million and a half under arms across the march, the [[Wall of Piled Bones]] and the coast. Rooted children are another matter: since the raids tripled, the Gongsuns hold a frontier charter, so the Registry's frontier tester comes at twelve, the age the march can put a child on the wall, and the garrison keeps every rooted child for its cadet school instead of sending them to the capital. Its best leave all the same, for the City of the Guarded Mouth or the Beast-Butcher Gate, so the march itself has no one past Foundation. Children here learn to read beast tracks before letters and to tell a raid horn from a hunt horn. A beast core turned in at a fort earns a bounty in rice or stones.
entries.truth: Lady Gongsun Wei, the general's widow, has been trading cores and captives to Shared Roost City to buy the weapons the capital stopped sending.
entries.fromAbove: Folded hill country with its counties' fields in the valleys, the beacon peaks' pillars of spirit-fire along its borders, and the pale dome over Pacified Fort.

ties.why: Lady Gongsun sends cores and captives to Shared Roost for the weapons the capital stopped sending.
Our garrisons hold the wall's southern stretch, and every cadet learns it by patrolling it.
Stone Eyes is ours on every imperial map, yet its clans pay no tax and send no sons to the wall.
We hold the march for the dynasty, though the capital has stopped sending the weapons to do it.

features.name: a village watchtower
a beast-pit
fields plowed with spears at hand

entries.name: Harbor of Stilled Waves
entries.summary: The one safe harbor on the storm coast, a city of six million behind a breakwater cultivators cut from the cliff. The Azure Wave Palace's toll office and the empire's customs house face each other across the quay.
entries.lore: Ships for the outer ocean leave from the Harbor of Stilled Waves, and every one pays twice: once to the empire and once to the sea clans' shark-folk factor, who keeps an office on the quay. Thunderwood, storm-pearls, lightning ink and puppets go out; sea silver and deep-sea herbs come in. Sailors swear the Rim's roar can be heard from the outer breakwater on windless nights.
entries.fromAbove: A great breakwater of cultivator-cut stone arcing 300 li across the bay mouth, a calm green harbor behind it among storm-black sea, wharves by the hundred and a ward dome pale over the quay.

ties.why: Every ship clears our quay only with the shark-folk factor's seal, and we pay for it.
Their puppets go out through our quay by the crate, and we take a cut of every one.

features.name: the quay, with the Palace's office and the customs house face to face
the breakwater walk above the surf
puppet and ink warehouses
the outer anchorage in the storm

entries.name: Turtle-Spine Mountains
entries.summary: The volcanic range down the Morning Star Continent's east side, a hundred thousand li of cinder cones and fire-veined cliffs separating the heartland plains from the outer coast. Legend says it is the shell ridge of a sleeping turtle.
entries.lore: The range is the reason the east coast feels like another country: three clefts cross it, each a gorge a day's flight long, and all are taxed. Its western slopes feed the heartland rivers; its eastern slopes drop straight to the sea. Mines, forge-towns and hermit caves dot its length by the tens of thousands, and fire-backed rock lizards the size of oxen bask on its warm cliffs. Every earthquake, villagers say the turtle turned over in its sleep.
entries.fromAbove: A red-brown spine of cinder cones running a hundred thousand li down the continent's east side, smoking along its flanks, with three pale clefts cut through it where the passes run.

ties.why: Every caravan between the east and the heartland crosses us through the Lis' taxed clefts.

features.name: warm cliffs where fire-backed rock lizards bask
a taxed cleft road between sheer walls
hermit caves high on the slope
abandoned mine shafts

top.note: a hermit in the high caves

entries.name: Kingdom of a Hundred Herbs
entries.summary: A tenant kingdom of two hundred and sixty million that grows herbs for the Apricot Grove Valley on contracts its grandparents signed. Its fields are healthy, its people well fed, and nobody is allowed to leave the debt.
entries.lore: Every household in the Kingdom of a Hundred Herbs owes the Apricot Grove Valley a quota of herbs, and every quota is a little higher than last year's; the herb terraces climb whole mountain ranges, and the quota barges leave for the valley in convoys. The king is an Apricot Grove Valley outer disciple's nephew. Children learn herb lore at five, identify a hundred plants by smell at ten and can recite their family's debt at twelve. Rooted children are sent to the valley as apprentices, never to the Registry, and the empire looks away because it needs the Apricot Grove Valley's pills.
entries.fromAbove: Whole hill ranges terraced in green to their summits, the quota roads running toward the valley's forest like the spokes of a wheel.

ties.why: We owe the valley a quota every harvest, and every year it is a little higher.
The Society's healers work our villages' lanes, and our granaries feed their camps.

features.name: the quota weigh-house
the herb terraces climbing the hills
the debt-ledger hall, every family's quota carved on its wall

entries.name: Kingdom of White Sands
entries.summary: A sleepy coastal kingdom of thirty million on dunes, palm groves and turtle beaches, ruled by an old mortal queen. Pirates take its children; nobody else remembers it exists.
entries.lore: White Sands grows spirit palms whose nuts feed beasts, gathers sea-turtle eggs from beaches that run a thousand li and pays the Registry tester to visit every twelve years. Its queen is ninety and has outlived three heirs. Pirate raids take a few children every year, and the fleet comes too late.
