A hidden cove holds a wrecked Ascent Age ship in the dunes, a hull the length of a ridge, which local children play in and adults avoid.
entries.truth: The wreck's hold is sealed and still warm.
entries.fromAbove: Pale dunes meeting a long white beach, dark palm groves in the lee of the dunes and the Ascent Age wreck showing as a ridge the wind never covers.

ties.why: Gao's raiders take our children each year, and the queen's petitions never reach the fleet.
We sell turtle eggs and spirit-palm nuts to the Sea Gate's markets and buy iron nails and rope.

features.name: the spirit-palm groves
the turtle beaches at egg season
the wreck in the dunes, its hold a dark maze

top.note: the Registry tester, every twelve years

entries.name: The Border Wilds
entries.summary: Sixty thousand li of karst hills on the Morning Star Continent's southwest coast, where the island chain to Vast Wilds begins. Three kingdoms hold a sliver of it and beasts hold the rest; smugglers cross at low tide and every family owes a child to the wall.
entries.lore: Across the [[Jade Strait]] lies beast country, and at low tide the island chain is a road in both directions, though walking it island to island is a season's travel at the least. Spirit beasts work north along the chain to raid herds and counties; human sects go over to hunt cores, eggs and herbs; half-bloods and smugglers pass goods island by island, by night, toward [[Shared Roost City]]. The empire holds the coast with the [[Wall of Piled Bones]], the fortress city at the chain's head and a conscript garrison more than a million strong, and pays for every beast core brought in. The kingdoms are islands of farmland in a sea of wild karst, honeycombed with caves where raiders, smugglers and beasts all hide. Raids have tripled in five years, and the beasts coming over are older.
entries.truth: The Beast Court is not sending the raids. Old beasts are waking in the Vast Wilds Continent's mountains and driving the young ones north across the strait.
entries.fromAbove: Karst hill country under a sea of cloud, stone pillars standing out of it by the hundred thousand, the Wall's bone-white line along the coastal hills, and the island chain stepping out across the Jade Strait.

ties.why: Walkers, poachers and smugglers leave our coast down the chain, and cores come back up it.

top.note: the City's commander, posted there; the Beast-Butcher Gate's master, there for the cores; the Stone Forest's python, in its lair

entries.name: The Sick Gardens
entries.summary: The blighted terraces and lingzhi caves of the Kingdom of Lingzhi Gardens, a black stain 8,000 li across where rot spreads to anything living. Mutant herbs grow in the rot.
entries.lore: The rot spreads by spores that cling to cloth and skin, and the Apricot Grove Valley has ordered a cordon around the gardens, a line of burned ground and signal posts that takes weeks to ride. Inside, the blight has bred strange herbs, black lingzhi and weeping ginseng that alchemists will pay for and that may be poison. Herb thieves go in masked and come out coughing.
entries.fromAbove: A black stain 8,000 li across spreading over the terraces, a pale cordon of burned ground around its edge and a low grey cloud of spores above.

ties.why: Herb thieves from the kingdom go in masked and sell black lingzhi back at the cordon's edge.
The Society's doctors sample our spores and treat the cordon villages.

features.name: the black lingzhi caves
the weeping ginseng beds
the cordon line of burned ground

entries.name: Grain-Barge Mouth
entries.summary: The canal port where grain barges from the whole heartland unload for the Jing Capital, a city of fifteen million. Its granaries, terraced along a hundred li of waterfront, are the largest in the world and, this year, half empty.
entries.lore: The Grain-Barge Mouth stands where the Grand Canal meets the [[Imperial River]], half a year west of the capital by barge. Its granaries rise in terraces like cliffs along the waterfront, and bargemen's guilds, granary clerks and the Registry's holding pens share the quays. A Heavenly Scale Pavilion branch here changes spirit stones and writes grain futures, and the bathhouses sell forged test slips at three low-grade stones apiece. Gangs of qi-laborers who failed the Registry fight for loading rights at night.
entries.fromAbove: A port city 250 li across at a river junction, its granaries a pale terraced cliff along the waterfront and the canal's basins fanning out like a comb.

ties.why: Every convoy we unload is bound for the capital's granaries, and its quota clerks sit on our wharves.
The Pavilion's branch changes our stones and writes grain futures on every convoy.
The river's convoys tie up at our wharves and its toll stations tax every one.
Every convoy of the Grand Canal ends at our basins, and its canal guard is paid from our tolls.
The Registry rents our berths for its holding pens, while our bathhouses forge the slips its wardens drink over.

features.name: the granary terraces along the waterfront
the lock basins where convoys wait their turn
the bathhouses selling forged test slips
the Registry's holding pens

entries.name: Kingdom of Lasting Peace
entries.summary: The fief of Prince Rui, the Ancestor Emperor's ninth-generation grandson: 11,000 li of orchard and horse country holding two billion people, and a spear prodigy who drills his household guard as if the succession war started yesterday.
entries.lore: Prince Rui reached Core Formation at forty and wants the throne before his uncles can agree on anyone else. His kingdom is orchards and horse farms that run to the horizon and a spear academy, one of the largest in the empire, that takes any rooted youth who passes the Registry and fails the palace cut. He hires rogue cultivators by the season, buys formation flags from anyone, and pays a bounty for proof of his cousins' crimes. Mortals here eat better than anywhere else in the domain, because the prince quietly stopped sending his grain quota to the capital.
entries.truth: The prince's 'grain shortfall' is stockpiled in a hollowed mountain under his horse farms, enough to feed an army of millions for two years.
entries.fromAbove: Orchard country in rows like combed hair, horse-farm grassland between, and the prince's spear academy on a ridge, its drill fields pale squares.

ties.why: The throne's auditors want our grain, and we send none and wait for the uncles to disagree.
We pay the Guard's junior officers' debts and want their spears at our back when the succession breaks.
Our agents buy the Stables' best foals through false sales, and its master has been paid to know.

features.name: the spear academy's drill fields
horse-farm paddocks
orchards under blossom

entries.name: South of the Tides
entries.summary: The Morning Star Continent's southern tip, 76,000 li of coast facing the Thousand Isles across open sea, where five billion live and the empire's southern fleet anchors. Most of the continent's legal trade with the islands passes through it.
entries.lore: The South of the Tides is the empire's sea gate: grain, iron and silk go out to the [[Thousand Isles]] in convoys of a thousand sails, and pearls, sea silver and island herbs come back. Every voyage pays the [[Azure Wave Palace]]'s toll and risks the pirate lords, which keeps the war junks of the southern fleet busy and the merchant houses rich. The fleet also ferries troops and supplies west to the Jade Strait frontier. Since the harvests failed, grain exports are banned, so the grain goes out at night instead.
entries.truth: The fleet's commander is Prince Rui's man. If the succession comes to war, the southern fleet will decide who controls the sea road to the frontier.
entries.fromAbove: A long southern coast of harbor cities each under a pale ward dome, the Sea Gate's fleet anchorage a white smear on the water, the Pagoda's column of light on the cape and a ring of grey fog over the ruins of Dead Harbor.

entries.name: Tidal Realm
entries.summary: A shard world whose gate sits in a sea cave that is dry only at the lowest tide of the year. It stays open for three days, and only those below Foundation can pass.
entries.lore: Inside is a shallow drowned world of coral forests and tide pools full of spirit shellfish, pearls and water herbs, its tide-flats stretching to a horizon. The cave floods on the third evening, and those still inside wait a year. Salt lords and the Tide-Watching Pavilion sell guides and tide tables; the Azure Wave Palace's shark-folk watch the cave mouth and take a share of whatever comes out.
entries.fromAbove: A ribbed sea cave at the tideline, nothing more; at the year's lowest tide a long strip of dry black rock and a column of pale light standing out of the cave mouth.

ties.why: The Pavilion sells the tide tables and gate-cave guides for the year's lowest tide.
The Palace's shark-folk hold the cave mouth and take a share of whatever comes out.
The salt lords' guides lead parties across the flats to the cave at the lowest tide, for a price.

features.name: the gate cave, dry for three days
coral forests on the drowned flats
tide pools of spirit shellfish

entries.name: Bay of Sunken Ships
entries.summary: A reef-choked bay 6,300 li across where a thousand years of wrecks lie stacked in shallow water. Reef eels, ghost lights and wreckers all hunt there.
entries.lore: The bay is full of salvage: cargo, artifacts, ship's spirit stones and the bones of their owners, wreck stacked on wreck from war-barges to sky-ships. Iron-jawed reef eels the length of a war-barge nest in the hulls, ghost lights lead divers astray in Ghost Month, and the Kingdom of Surf Rocks's wreckers kill rival salvagers on sight. A Thousand Isles treasure ship went down here forty years ago, and its pirate owners still send divers.
entries.fromAbove: A reef-choked bay 6,300 li across, a pale web of shoals and wreck-banks showing through green water, ghost lights drifting over it at night.

ties.why: Surf Rocks's wreckers hold our shallows and kill every rival salvager they find.
The Thousand Isles' pirates keep sending divers down to their sunken ship, and the wreckers keep killing them.

features.name: wreck-banks stacked in the shallows
the reef edge, where the shoal drops away
ghost-light channels through the hulls
the sunken Thousand Isles treasure ship

top.note: the strongest reef eels, and a wrecker captain

entries.name: Wind-Riding Gate
entries.summary: A Wind Dao sect of eight thousand on the plateau's edge whose disciples fly on kites and gusts. The empire's fastest couriers wear its badge.
entries.lore: The Wind-Riding Gate teaches flight before fighting: disciples ride spirit kites in the dust storms until they can ride the wind alone. The sect holds the imperial courier contract for the north, with a relay tower on every bare mesa, carrying sealed letters across the plateau in a week, faster than horses. It recruits light, quick children from the cave villages and trains them to read the sky. Its couriers know everyone's secrets and are paid not to.
entries.fromAbove: A mesa edge streaming with kites, a ring of wind-array pillars turning the dust storms aside around its halls and relay towers strung away across the plateau like a dotted line.

ties.why: We sell guided entry to the Wind Cave's gate and keep its guides.
The cavalry academies take the rooted children first and leave us the light ones.

features.name: the kite-launching ridges
the sealed-letter vault
the relay towers on bare mesas
the dust-storm training ground

entries.name: The Red Rocks
entries.summary: Sixty-five thousand li of volcanic highland along the Morning Star Continent's eastern spine: forge-fields, forty convict pits as wide as lakes, and a new spirit vein that broke the surface last year and started a stampede across the east.
entries.lore: The Turtle-Spine Mountains run hot here, a red range of cinder cones in rows, every river valley smoking. Fire veins feed forge-fields that supply half of the Morning Star Continent's artifact refiners, imperial convicts dig spirit ore in pits as wide as lakes, and the [[Imperial River]] and the [[Flood River]] both rise on its slopes. Last spring a mid-grade vein surfaced in a collapsed valley, and every clan, sect and desperate miner in the east came running, some from a month's flight away. The [[Great Jing Dynasty]] claims all new veins, the Blazing Furnace Sect claims everything in its forges' sight, and the claim-jumpers claim whatever they can hold until morning.
entries.truth: The new vein is not natural. It is the core of an Ascent Age fire array waking with the tide, and the whole range is its wall.
entries.fromAbove: A red-brown highland of cinder cones and cooled lava fields under a haze of furnace smoke, forty terraced pits sunk like crater lakes, the Blazing Furnace Sect's volcano glowing on one range and a raw pale wound where the new vein broke the surface.

ties.why: The dynasty claims every new vein in our range and sends its convicts to dig the old ones.

top.note: the Blazing Furnace Sect's master, there for the fire veins; a hermit in the high caves who stopped climbing

entries.name: City of First Sun
entries.summary: The east's great port of twelve million, where the sun rises first and ships leave for the outer ocean. Its quay has a toll office for the sea clans and a gallows for smugglers.
entries.lore: The City of First Sun trades salt, eastern silk and thunderwood for sea silver, deep-sea pearls and whatever the Thousand Isles are selling, down quays that run for a day's walk. The Azure Wave Palace's factor keeps a pavilion on the water, and no ship leaves without his seal. The city is the Dawn League's purse, and the imperial governor knows it. Sailors say the Morning Star rises here first, which is how Morning Star got its name.
entries.fromAbove: A harbor city 200 li across stepped up the shore round a half-moon bay, breakwaters of cultivator-cut stone, a forest of masts and the Azure Wave Palace's pavilion lit on the water.

ties.why: We pay the Palace's factor for the seal that clears every ship off our quay.
Our merchants' salt and silk profits fill the League's purse, and the governor knows it.
We buy the Pavilion's tide tables before every voyage, and a captain who sails without them pays double for insurance.

features.name: the quay's toll office for the sea clans
the smugglers' gallows
the Palace factor's pavilion on the water
salt and silk warehouses

entries.name: Jade Screen Ridge
entries.summary: A green ridge 63,000 li long that shields Apricot Grove Valley from the sea winds, its slopes wild with herbs older than dynasties. The valley's patrols guard the passes.
entries.lore: Mist from the inner sea condenses on the ridge and stands on its crest as a wall of cloud from end to end, keeping the valley wet. Wild herbs here are hundreds of years old, and the Apricot Grove Valley's ridge patrols arrest anyone picking them without a permit. Medicinal snakes and blue-tailed herb foxes live in the cliffs. The western slope looks out over the inner sea.
entries.fromAbove: A long green ridge with a standing wall of cloud on its seaward side, the pale gates of the valley's patrol passes notched along its crest.

ties.why: The valley's patrols hold my passes and arrest anyone picking without a permit.
Society doctors pick my herbs for the poor without a permit, and the patrols arrest them for it.

features.name: the wild herb slopes
the patrol passes through the crest
the cloud wall on the crest

entries.name: Cinnabar Hill Sect
entries.summary: The Apricot Grove Valley's last rival in alchemy, on a red hill east of the valley that stands as tall as a peak. Its gardens are dying, its masters are furious and its pills are still very good.
entries.lore: The Cinnabar Hill Sect teaches alchemy through the Fire Dao from furnace halls on the hill's crown, where the fires burn day and night, and refuses to grow its own herbs anymore, buying everything from outside the Apricot Grove Valley's network: Vast Wilds smugglers, shard-realm teams, the marsh. It recruits alchemy talents the Apricot Grove Valley rejected, and it pays bounties for proof of the blight. Its Nascent Soul master has sworn to burn the apricot forest if the proof comes.
entries.truth: The Cinnabar Hill Sect's master is buying blight samples from the Netherworm Stockade to make a blight of his own.
entries.fromAbove: A single red hill standing out of the green, a ring of furnace halls on its crown, a column of red smoke above them and brown dying gardens at its foot.

ties.why: The valley took every herb market and now seeds blight in our gardens; we want proof and then the forest.
Lingzhi Gardens grew our mushrooms for eight hundred years, and we pay the old price still.
We buy blight samples from the Stockade to make a blight of our own.

features.name: the summit furnace halls
the dying gardens at the hill's foot
the bounty board for proof of the blight

entries.name: Earth Dragon Wells
entries.summary: Nine ancient wells, each a round shaft eight li across, on the plain east of the Jing Capital where vein qi seeps up as warm mist. Geomancers have read the capital's veins here for two thousand years.
entries.lore: The Imperial Geomancy Office keeps a hall by the wells and logs the mist's height each dawn, from a stone stair down to each well's lip. Apprentice geomancers can be hired cheaply to read graves and fields, and the office sells its old logs to anyone with a court seal. Pilgrims drink the well water for long life. This year the mist barely clears the well lips, and the office has stopped letting outsiders look.
entries.truth: Anyone who compares the logs will see the mist has fallen by half in three centuries, starting the year the Ancestor Emperor withdrew.
entries.fromAbove: Nine round wells in a ring 120 li across, each wearing a collar of white mist, with the geomancers' hall on the rim of the eastern well.

ties.why: We log the capital's veins each dawn for the court and sell old logs to anyone with a seal.

features.name: the nine wells, each ringed by a collar of warm mist
the dawn log-stone at the geomancers' hall
the pilgrims' stair down to a well's lip

entries.name: The Eastern Corner
entries.summary: The Morning Star Continent's outer east coast behind the Turtle-Spine clefts, sixty-two thousand li of old kingdoms, salt flats and ports that see the sun first, and that remember being free.
entries.lore: The eastern kingdoms were old when the [[Great Jing Dynasty]] conquered them, and behind the mountains they still behave as if the conquest were temporary. They pay tax months late, test children for the Registry with suspicious results, and trade with the outer sea on their own terms with the [[Azure Wave Palace]]'s toll collectors. The harvest failures in the heartland have raised the grain levy on the east twice in two years. Now the eastern kings meet in secret, and the empire has started stationing spear cultivators at the passes.
entries.truth: The Dawn League has been offered help by the Night Banquet. The price is the passes, and the League's elder council is about to say yes.
entries.fromAbove: A long pale coast of salt flats, river deltas and port bays under the range's red wall, beacon-pillars strung along the shore, the harbor city's breakwaters curved out into the surf and a white line of sea cliff to the north.

ties.why: The Palace's toll collectors sit on every route to the outer sea, and we haggle with them on our own terms.

top.note: the Dawn League's leader, there for the old kingdoms' cause

entries.name: Realm of Broken Edges
entries.summary: A shard world whose gate opens on the sixty-ninth peak for one month every thirty years. Only cultivators below Core Formation can enter.
entries.lore: Inside is a battlefield from the Ascent Age, thousands of li across, frozen at the moment a sword array broke: shards of immortal swords, some as long as a mountain range, stuck in floating stone, and sword-phantoms that still fight each other. A single shard can be refined into a Core Formation flying sword. The Clear Heaven Sword Sect controls the gate and sells forty places to outsiders by auction. The next opening is in eleven years, and the auction has already begun.
entries.fromAbove: Nothing while it sleeps but the sixty-ninth peak's bare summit; for the month it opens, a rift of silver light standing over the peak with sword-phantoms flickering in it.

ties.why: Our gate stands on the sixty-ninth peak, and its keepers sell forty places to whoever bids.

features.name: the gate on the sixty-ninth peak, guarded by the sect
broken immortal swords standing in floating stone
sword-phantoms still fighting their last battle
the auction hall at the foot of the peak

entries.name: The Wall of Piled Bones
entries.summary: A wall of rammed earth and beast-king bone 9,000 li long along the coastal hills, as tall as cliffs and built over a thousand years of raids. On Ghost Month nights the bones howl.
entries.lore: Each garrison builds in the bones of the beasts it kills, and the oldest stretches are faced with the skulls of beast kings, each the size of a hill, their eye sockets now the wall's gates. Binding arrays run along the top as a thread of light and hold the beast spirits down, all but the seventh month, when they haunt it and ghost-hunters and bone-collectors come. Old bones from the wall are a refining material for beast-taming whistles and Slaughter Dao artifacts, and stealing them is a hanging offense. The [[March of Pacified Borders]] garrisons the southern stretch, and its cadets learn the wall by patrolling it.
entries.fromAbove: A bone-white rampart as tall as cliffs running 9,000 li over the coastal hills, beast-king skulls the size of hills for its gatehouses and a thread of binding-array light along its top.

ties.why: The Gongsun garrisons man the southern stretch and add their kills to the bones.

features.name: the patrol walk along the top
the old stretches faced with beast-king skulls, their eye sockets gates
bone heaps waiting to be built in

entries.name: Demon-Warding Dike
entries.summary: A seawall six thousand li long, three thousand years old, built in the Outer Demon War with a warding array in every stone. Most of Morning Star thinks it is a relic.
entries.lore: The dike runs for six thousand li along the inner coast, as tall as a sea-cliff and wide enough on its crown for a road, and its lanterns burn at night with a pale qi flame that shows as a cold line from far out at sea. Formation masters study its arrays, which no living sect can reproduce, and thieves pry out its stones for their array cores. Prying out a stone is a capital crime under a law nobody has enforced in centuries, until this year.
entries.fromAbove: A grey rampart 6,000 li long down the coast, a cold thread of lantern-flame along its crown by night and the surf breaking white against its seaward foot.

ties.why: Every Ghost Month ghost columns come marching out of the north toward our wall, and the Soul-Callers pretend they called them.
The Shens light every lantern along my crown and walk every li of me; without them my arrays go dark.

features.name: the lantern line along the crown, a pale flame every li
the array stones, each cut with warding script
the crown road, wide enough for a column of carts

entries.name: Dead Harbor
entries.summary: A port-city sacked by Thousand Isles pirates fifty years ago and never rebuilt, its ruins and the burned coast around them 5,000 li across. A pirate lord uses them as a mainland base.
entries.lore: The pirate lord Red-Sleeve Gao holds the ruins, a sacked port-city 150 li across, with a few thousand raiders, a captured war junk and a formation that turns the harbor into a maze of fog. The fleet has attacked twice and lost twice. Captives are held in the old customs cellars until ransomed or sold. Gao pays well for information about convoys.
entries.fromAbove: A dome of grey fog sitting on the outline of a ruined harbor-city, the burned scar of the sack still dark on the coast around it.

ties.why: Baisha's coves are the nearest unguarded children and fresh water; we land at night and the fleet is a week late.
The House insures grain ships and sells us their routes; we take the cargo and it pays the claim.
The fleet comes to dislodge us and gets lost in the fog; we sell their captured junks back to their own merchants.

features.name: the old customs cellars where captives wait
the fog maze over the harbor
the captured war junk at anchor

entries.name: Realm of the Wind Cave
entries.summary: A shard world whose gate opens in a loess wind cave during the autumn dust storms every nine years. Only cultivators below Foundation can pass.
entries.lore: Inside is a sky of endless wind and floating rocks, a world a thousand li across, where wind-crystal clusters grow on the windward faces. A crystal can carry a Wind Dao cultivator to Foundation. The gate stays open twenty days, and the storm outside kills as many applicants as the realm does. The Wind-Riding Gate sells guided entry; the cave villages sell it cheaper and guide worse.
entries.fromAbove: Nothing while it sleeps but a black mouth in a yellow cliff; for the twenty days it opens, a standing funnel of dust and light over the cave.

ties.why: The Wind-Riding Gate sells guided entry to our gate, and the cave villages undercut it.

features.name: the wind cave mouth in the loess cliff
floating rocks in the endless wind
wind-crystal clusters on the windward faces
the dust storm outside the gate

entries.name: Beneath the Peaks
entries.summary: Terraced foothills 67,000 li across between the capital plain and the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's peaks, where eight billion mortals farm the terraces, sect mountains rise straight out of the rice fields and two masters claim every rooted child.
entries.lore: In Beneath the Peaks the empire's law runs up the valleys and stops where the terraces end; the terraces climb the foothills in steps hundreds of li long, and above them the [[Clear Heaven Sword Sect]] and its vassal sects rule from peaks you can see from every paddy. The Registry tests children at six. The Clear Heaven Sword Sect's recruiters come at nine with the Sword Stair trial, and they do not ask whether a child is registered. Families hide their best children in hay carts, smugglers guide them up the mountain roads, and imperial bounty hunters wait at the passes. The upper terraces still yield; the lower ones, on imperial land, have started to fail.
entries.truth: The Clear Heaven Sword Sect has quietly doubled its recruiting since its founder fell silent. The sect masters want more swords before anyone tests them.
entries.fromAbove: Foothills carved into terraces to every horizon, green and glowing near the sect peaks and gray on the imperial lower slopes, vassal peaks rising out of the paddies with their summit halls lit, and the Snow River's white thread through the middle.

ties.why: We pay the peaks above their tithe in rice and children, and hide our best from them when we can.
The Registry tests our children at six and the sect comes for them at nine, and every county pays for both.

entries.name: Wave-Quelling Gate
entries.summary: An orthodox sect of pirate hunters who fight from a fleet of spirit ships, three of them a li long, with spear and Water Dao. They collect imperial bounties and pirate bribes with the same hand.
entries.lore: The Wave-Quelling Gate recruits sailors' children and drills them on decks until they can fight in a storm. Its three flagship spirit ships, each a li from stem to stern, and two hundred escorts patrol the coast, and its bounties are posted in every port. It holds an imperial commission and a quiet arrangement with two pirate lords, whose rivals it hunts with real zeal. It hires outside cultivators for raids on pirate nests.
entries.fromAbove: A fortress-harbor 200 li across on a headland, three long pale hulls moored at its quays and escort-hulls in lines along the coast beyond.

ties.why: King Dou's militia hangs pirates we have an arrangement with, and we take his bounty for the rest.
Blackwater buys the loot of the lords we hunt; our raids land a day after the warning does.
We keep a flagship off the shoals for the Pearl Queen, and her pearls pay half our bounties.

features.name: a flagship's main deck pitching in its storm array, the drill yard
the bounty board in the port
the spirit ships' moorings

entries.name: Floating Lantern Market
entries.summary: A black market of ten thousand boats lashed into streets that drifts through the marsh and moors somewhere different every night, a floating city 40 li across. You find it with a lantern token, or it finds you.
entries.lore: Anything banned anywhere in the Morning Star Continent is sold here: stolen sect manuals, Registry slips, demonic techniques, Gu, beast cores from protected species and people. Prices are in spirit stones or favors, and favors are worse. The Night Banquet runs the market and guarantees its peace; fighting aboard means being served at the next banquet. Lantern tokens sell in the City of Pecks and Bushels and Blackwater for a mid-grade stone.
entries.fromAbove: A raft-city of lanterns drifting over black water, thousands of boats lashed into streets, dark again when it moves; from above it is a smear of lamplight 40 li long.

ties.why: The Banquet's peace is the only law on our boats, and its wardens keep it.
We sell lantern tokens through Blackwater Port, and its pirates sell us loot nobody can ask about.
Nine Bends' channel-pirates ferry our goods out, and we moor off its delta when the Governor's cut is paid.

features.name: the lantern gate, where tokens are checked
raft streets lashed together over open water
the auction barge

entries.name: Kingdom of High Meadows
entries.summary: A high-valley kingdom of thirteen million yak herders, seven thousand li across under the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's glaciers. Its meadows are greener every year because the ice above them is melting.
entries.lore: High Meadows is thirteen million herders in felt tents, a monastery-turned-palace and a chieftain who calls himself king when the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's envoys are not listening. Its people trade yak butter, frost-lotus and glacier ice to the Zhu clan's Cold Forge, in caravans that take a season to the forge and back. Children grow up in felt tents, herd on the ice edge and dream of the Sword Stair. This year the glacier dropped a river onto the lower meadows overnight, and the herders found Ascent Age stonework under the retreating ice.
entries.fromAbove: High green valleys under a white wall of glacier, herds drifting across the meadows like cloud shadows, a monastery-palace on a spur and, new this year, a river braiding across the lower pasture.

ties.why: Our yak butter, frost-lotus and glacier ice go to the Cold Forge, and its iron and coin come back up the road.

features.name: the glacier edge where the herds graze
the monastery-turned-palace on its spur
the ice-cut caravan road to the Cold Forge
the new river and the Ascent Age stonework under the retreating ice

entries.name: Tide-Watching Pavilion
entries.summary: A sect of ten thousand sea diviners who read tides, winds and the pull of the Mirror from a wall of observatory terraces along the cliffs. Every captain on the east coast buys their charts.
entries.lore: The Tide-Watching Pavilion teaches the Water and Wind Daos through observation: disciples spend years on the sea wall, a line of terraces 600 li long, counting waves before they learn a technique. The pavilion predicts storms, sea-clan migrations and the tide's surges, and sells its tables to captains, farmers and other sects. It has served the eastern kings for centuries and despises the Armillary Pavilion for charging more for less.
entries.truth: The tide tables have stopped matching the sea. As the Mirror swells, its pull lifts the outer ocean a little higher every year, and the pavilion's tables were built for a world that is gone.
entries.fromAbove: A line of white observatory terraces and wind-vane pillars strung 600 li along the sea cliffs, a ring of array light standing over the chart hall at its heart.

ties.why: Every captain out of the harbor buys our charts before he sails.
The Armillary Pavilion charges more for less and calls us thieves for selling cheap.
Our wave-counters keep their longest watch on the cliff where the white line shows.
We sell the tables and guides to the Tidal Realm's gate cave, and every party needs both.

features.name: the sea wall's counting terraces
the chart hall, where the tables are copied
the wave-counters' stairs down the cliff

entries.name: The Granary
entries.summary: The southern river plains that feed the empire, 67,000 li of paddy and wheat along the middle of the Flood River and twelve billion people. The harvests are failing, the quotas are not, and the roads south are full of families walking toward the marsh.
entries.lore: The Granary ships two barges of grain north for every one it keeps, and for three years it has not had two to spare. Convoys a day long crowd the Flood River and the Imperial Canal, and vassal kings hide granaries from the [[Great Jing Dynasty]]'s auditors while spirit-farming sects blame the [[Apricot Grove Valley]]'s blight. Ash locusts that eat qi out of the stalks have appeared where the soil went thin, and buyers from the [[Night Banquet Sect]] markets move north along the river buying indentures from starving families, while the roads south fill with families on the half-year walk to the marsh. A cultivator who can grow anything, guard anything or find out where the grain is going will never lack work here.
entries.truth: The thinning spreads south from the Jing Capital along the old vein courses. The Granary's soil is fine; the qi under it is being pulled north.
entries.fromAbove: Flat paddy and wheat country cut by the Flood River's wide silver bends and the Imperial Canal's straight line, gray scars of dead fields spreading in the middle and convoys a white thread on the water.

ties.why: We ship two barges north for every one we keep, and the quotas arrive whether the harvest does or not.
Our hungry walk south toward the marsh, and its buyers follow the river north buying indentures.

entries.name: Spirit of the Old Scholar Tree
entries.summary: A scholar tree three thousand years old that woke with the tide, its crown a green island 40 li across, now dying of thirst beside a dry village well. It bargains with cultivators for answers.
entries.lore: The villagers of Huaixia have prayed to the tree for centuries; ten years ago it answered. Its roots run for a hundred li and reach deep enough to feel the capital's veins, and it trades leaves that clear the mind, seeds and old memories of the land for help. Lately it asks every cultivator the same question: where is the water going? Woodcutters with court permits have twice come to fell it for palace timber and twice been strangled by its roots.
entries.truth: The tree can feel the drain flowing toward the palace and could lead anyone to the array's outer nodes. It has not found anyone it trusts.
entries.fromAbove: A single green crown 40 li across standing alone on a brown plain, dry channels of roots running out from it toward the Jing Capital.

ties.why: The court's woodcutters have twice come to fell me for palace timber and twice been strangled, and I want to know where the water goes.

features.name: the dry well at the foot of the trunk
roots arched over the road like gates
the crown's shade, where offerings are left

entries.name: Kingdom of the Old Ramparts
entries.summary: A poor, proud kingdom of ninety million strung along three thousand li of the Demon-Warding Dike, ruled by the hereditary wall-wardens who still keep its arrays lit.
entries.lore: The Wall-Warden clan, the Shens, were charged three thousand years ago to keep the western wall manned, and they have, through famines and mockery. Every child learns to light the warding lanterns and recite the wall's array script, and every county owes the dike a levy of lamp-oil and lamp-keepers, a duty older than the crown. The empire pays a small stipend and laughs at the Shens. This year the [[Seal Watch]] sent an inspector for the first time in a thousand years, who checked every lantern along the kingdom's three thousand li of wall and left without a word.
entries.fromAbove: A grey seawall running the length of a poor green coast, the kingdom's counties strung behind it and a thread of lantern-flame along the wall's crown at night.

ties.why: We were charged to keep the dike manned and lit, and we have for three thousand years, on a stipend that barely buys the oil.
The Seal Watch sent an inspector to count every lantern for the first time in a thousand years, and left without a word; we wait to learn why.

features.name: the lantern stairs up the dike's seaward face
the wardens' hall, the wall's array script cut into its floor
a county lamp-oil depot

entries.name: The Sea Gate
entries.summary: The empire's southern port and fleet base, a city of twelve million at the tip of the Morning Star Continent, its harbor chained at night across a mouth ten li wide.
entries.lore: The Sea Gate's harbor mouth is chained at night with an array chain a dozen li long and patrolled by war junks. Its customs house taxes everything and seizes grain, which then reappears in warehouses on the far quay. Thousand Isles traders keep a walled compound by the docks, and the Azure Wave Palace's factor keeps a pavilion over the water. A cultivator with a sword and a clean record can sign onto a convoy for fifty low-grade stones a voyage.
entries.fromAbove: A harbor city 200 li across around a sheltered bay under a ward dome, the shining line of the harbor chain drawn across the bay mouth.

ties.why: We buy White Sands palm nuts for fleet beast-feed and turtle eggs for the officers, and sell back rope and nails.
The Coin Treasure Trading House's quay-quarter is our busiest berth, and its letters of credit settle our duties.
The Palace's factor keeps a pavilion over our water and collects its toll on every outbound hull.
The Sea Gate's customs owes the Pagoda a lamp-stone duty on every hull and pays it late.
We berth the fleet, victual it and fill its ranks with the quarter-city's sailors.

features.name: the chained harbor mouth
the customs house
the far-quay warehouses
the Isles traders' walled compound

top.note: Admiral Hou, when the fleet is in

entries.name: Sea-Silk Workshop
entries.summary: A weavers' guild of hidden half-bloods with shark-folk blood, working in sea-floor halls under a coastal kelp forest. Their sea silk turns blades and never gets wet.
entries.lore: The weavers spin silk from the threads of deep-sea mussels, whole beds of them a li across, and weave it underwater at night. Their robes are sought by every sect in the Morning Star Continent. Most members have a shark-folk grandmother and hide it; the gills close if they never swim. The guild trades quietly with [[Shared Roost City]] and smuggles half-blood children out of human villages that discover them.
entries.truth: The guild pays the Azure Wave Palace with information about the coast, not silk.
entries.fromAbove: Nothing but a dark kelp forest off a quiet cove, and at night a faint blue glow under the water as the looms work.

ties.why: We sell sea silk and send half-blood children to Shared Roost, the only market that takes them.
We pay the Palace in information about the coast, not silk.

features.name: the underwater loom-halls
the mussel beds
the cove village where the gills show in the dark

entries.name: Kingdom of Calm Seas
entries.summary: A merchant kingdom of six hundred million whose king owns four thousand ships. It is loyal to the throne because the throne's navy keeps the pirates off its cargo.
entries.lore: King Qian came from a shipping house and still runs the kingdom like one: offices instead of courts, contracts instead of oaths, counting-house cities strung two thousand li along the coast. Children of Calm Seas go to sea at twelve as deck boys or to the counting houses as clerks. The kingdom pays cultivators well to guard ships and better to recover stolen cargo. It is now quietly running grain to the Thousand Isles at triple price, and the crew members who object have stopped coming home.
entries.fromAbove: A chain of harbor cities along 2,000 li of coast, each under a pale ward dome, and the pale lines of the king's loading-quays reaching into the sea.

ties.why: We run grain over at triple price, and the crew who object stop coming home.
Our cargo sails under the fleet's convoys, and we pay cultivators to guard it better than the fleet does.

features.name: the contract hall, where every oath is a sealed paper
the harbor of ten thousand berths
grain barges loading by night

entries.name: The Cold Ford
entries.summary: A ferry city of six million at the Snow River's mouth where ships leave for the Shattered Sea's northern islands and the long run up the Floating Peak Continent's coast. The harbor freezes every winter.
entries.lore: Cold Ford is iron, fish and ferries. Scavenger crews winter here and sell salvage in spring; iron-sand barges load for the forges; Floating Peak exiles cross on the ferries. The Soul-Calling Sect keeps a hall where the bereaved can speak to the drowned. It is the cheapest port on the inner coast to hire a crew, because the crews are the worst.
entries.fromAbove: A harbor city a hundred and twenty li across on the Snow River's delta, its quays white with winter ice, iron-sand barges strung up the river like beads and the northern ferry lanes fanning out over the sea.

ties.why: Delta iron sand loads on our docks for the forges, and we sell the Ruans' ships their crews.
The Soul-Calling Sect keeps a hall on our quays for the bereaved, and the dead of the sea come to it.
Its dive crews winter on our quays and sell their salvage here in spring.

features.name: the ice-bound harbor in winter
the salvage yards
the iron-sand barge docks
the Soul-Calling Sect's hall for the drowned

entries.name: Zhu Clan of the Cold Forge
entries.summary: The hereditary swordsmiths of the Clear Heaven Sword Sect, a clan of forty thousand who forge spirit steel in halls cooled by glacier ice. A Zhu sword is worth more than a city's year of trade.
entries.lore: The Zhu clan has forged for the Clear Heaven Sword Sect for six thousand years and trains its children in Metal and Fire Daos from the cradle. Its forge-halls run for a hundred and fifty li along the glacier's foot, a smoke-banner visible from the plain. It takes outside apprentices with good fire roots and binds them for thirty years. The clan's Cold Forge quenches blades in glacier meltwater mixed with sword intent, and nobody has copied the method. The Zhus despise artifact refiners who use fire alone, and say so.
entries.truth: The glacier the Cold Forge depends on is melting as the tide rises. The clan has twenty years of ice left and has told nobody.
entries.fromAbove: A line of forge-halls a hundred and fifty li long at the glacier's foot, their chimneys a smoke-banner over the ice and steam rising where meltwater meets white-hot steel.

ties.why: We have forged for the Sword Sect for six thousand years, and its shelter is what keeps us a clan.
We buy High Meadows' frost-lotus and glacier ice, and the herders' caravans keep our forge cool and fed.
We buy the north's iron sand from the Ruan family and pay in coin and in blades.
We cool the Cold Forge with the ridge's ice and quench in its meltwater.
The Furnace Sect has matched us anvil for anvil for three thousand years; we answer its contests, and sometimes its knives.

features.name: the quench channels, glacier water running over white-hot blades
the ice wall behind the forge, its meltwater thinning each year
the racks of finished blades awaiting the sect

entries.name: Kingdom of the Held Pearl
entries.summary: A pearl-diving kingdom of a hundred and fifty million ruled by the Pearl Queen, a Foundation diver who can stay under for an hour. Its divers are the best on the coast and the shortest-lived.
entries.lore: Every child in the Kingdom of the Held Pearl dives from the age of six, and the strongest swimmers go to the queen's shoals. Spirit pearls are sorted by grade at the palace and sold to alchemists and refiners. A tenth goes to the sea clans by treaty. Rooted divers learn Water Dao from the queen herself, which is why the Registry finds so few roots here. Pearl thieves are tied to a reef at low tide.
entries.fromAbove: A coast of pale coves and warm turquoise shallows, the pearl-towns' domes strung along it like beads and the Bright Pearl Shoals a green-gold stain offshore.

ties.why: We hold the shoals by treaty and dive them under the sea clans' eye.
The Queen pays the Gate in pearls to escort her diving fleets and drive off poachers.

features.name: the queen's grading hall, where pearls are sorted by grade
the reef where thieves are tied at low tide
the diving platforms

entries.name: Blackwater Port
entries.summary: A pirate port of three million at the edge of the marsh where Thousand Isles pirates sell their loot, officially a fishing village. No questions, no Registry and no records.
entries.lore: Blackwater is where pirate ships unload slaves, plunder and stolen sect treasures, and where marsh buyers pay in clean stones. It is officially a fishing village. Its harbor master is a Night Banquet outer disciple, its tavern keepers are appraisers, and its fences will buy anything, including people. Imperial raids arrive a day after the warning does.
entries.fromAbove: A harbor-city 120 li across at the marsh edge, its docks a black fringe on the grey water and not one ward dome among it, only smoke.

ties.why: We sell the Market's lantern tokens on our docks for a mid-grade stone, and its buyers come aboard our loot.
The Gate's raids always hang the wrong people, and its bounty list never includes the lords it drinks with.
Our harbor master is the Banquet's man, and its marsh buyers pay clean stones for our loot.

features.name: the loot docks
the tavern-appraisers' back rooms
the slave pens under the east quay

entries.name: Realm of Mingled Blood
entries.summary: A shard world whose gate opens in a karst cave every seven years. It admits only those below Foundation who carry beast blood, or a tamer bonded to a beast.
entries.lore: Inside is a green world where beasts and humans once lived as one people, with ruined villages, bloodline altars and herbs that awaken dormant bloodlines. Half-bloods go in to learn what they are; tamers go in to strengthen their bonds; pure humans who try the gate are thrown back with broken bones. The Night Bridge Society guards the cave and charges entry. It last opened five years ago.
entries.fromAbove: Nothing while it sleeps, its gate a cave mouth in the karst; for the thirty days it opens, a column of green light stands over the cave.

ties.why: The Night Bridge Society guards the gate cave and takes a toll from all who enter.

features.name: the gate cave in the karst
a ruined village of the one people
a bloodline altar
herb meadows under a green sky

entries.name: The Flood River
entries.summary: The river of the south, 140,000 li long, from the Turtle-Spine Mountains through the granary plains into the Ink Marsh and out to sea at Nine Bends. It floods every summer and feeds half the empire.
entries.lore: The Flood River's floods lay down the silt that makes the southern plains rich, ten li across at the crest, and its barges carry the grain north to the canal. Below the City of Pecks and Bushels it slows into the marsh, where channels split and rejoin and river pirates know every one. Flood-dragon carp, river otter clans and black-shell turtles live in its lower reaches. This year's flood came late and thin.
entries.fromAbove: A silver river ten li across looping through green-gold plains, its floodplain a darker band, convoys a white thread on it and the delta fraying into channels at its foot.

ties.why: The river's convoys gather at the City of Pecks and Bushels before they head north.
Barges that run our lower reaches into the delta pay the pirates of Nine Bends for passage to the sea.

features.name: the silt banks left by the flood
the quays at the City of Pecks and Bushels, where barges gather
the lower channels, a maze of reed and mud

entries.name: The Imperial Domain
entries.summary: The Great Jing Dynasty's home domain, 68,000 li of canal-laced plain around the Jing Capital and the most crowded land in the world: twenty billion mortals, registry towns, princes' fiefs the size of countries, and every child tested for a spirit root at six.
entries.lore: Everything in the Imperial Domain points at the [[Jing Capital]]: canals as wide as rivers, army-kept roads, grain barges in convoys a day long, and the children. The [[Great Jing Dynasty]] tests every six-year-old at the county registry, and good roots go to the capital in sealed convoys under spear-guard, a season's journey from the far counties. Qi Condensation cultivators are as common here as clerks. The Ancestor Emperor has not been seen in three centuries, so the princes court cultivators openly, each from a fief that would be a kingdom anywhere else, and pay well for anyone who can win a duel or lose a witness. For three years the paddies nearest the capital have come up thin across a belt thousands of li wide, and the court blames blight carried in from the [[Apricot Grove Valley]].
entries.truth: The dead fields form rings around the Jing Capital that match the palace array's draw. Court astrologers who noticed were posted to the frontier; two never arrived.
entries.fromAbove: A green-gold plain cut into a grid of broad canals and roads, a registry town at every junction, the Jing Capital's white dome of light at its middle and pale rings of thin paddy spreading round it.

ties.why: Every barge of the Granary's grain comes north to our canals, and we send auditors and quotas south to meet it.
The court blames our thin paddies on blight carried in from the Valley and wants its Master to cure it.

top.note: the Ancestor Emperor, unseen and rumored dying

entries.name: The Imperial Canal
entries.summary: The Grand Canal that carries the south's grain from the Flood River to the Imperial River and on to the Jing Capital, 80,000 li long. Forty locks, a canal guard, and bandits at every one.
entries.lore: Dug by ten million laborers and ten thousand cultivators over sixty years, the canal is the empire's artery, wide enough for two convoys to pass abreast. Barges move in convoys of a hundred under canal guard escort, and lock-keepers are imperial officials who sell priority. With the harvests failing, the barges run light and the bandits have grown bold enough to rob convoys at the locks. Convoy guards are hired at the City of Pecks and Bushels for a low-grade stone a day.
entries.fromAbove: A straight silver line across the plain with forty lock-staircases glinting along it like beads, a pale town beside each lock.

ties.why: Our forty locks end at the Grain-Barge Mouth, where every convoy unloads.
Convoys hire their guards at the City of Pecks and Bushels for a low-grade stone a day.

features.name: a lock staircase, its gates opening one beyond another
the lock-keepers' tollhouses
convoy moorings where bandits strike by night

entries.name: Kingdom of Yellow Cliffs
entries.summary: A loess kingdom of fifty-two million cave-home dwellers along the Snow River gorge, ten thousand li across. Poor, tough and famous for producing the empire's best cavalry.
entries.lore: Yellow Cliffs grows millet on terraces cut into the gorge walls for hundreds of li and sends its sons to the imperial cavalry, because the cavalry pays in silver. Its king is a retired cavalry general who rules like a quartermaster. Children grow up in cave homes, ride before they walk and wrap their faces against the dust. Rooted children are prized by the Registry, which sends them to the horse-archer academies.
entries.fromAbove: Yellow loess cliffs cut into terrace after terrace along a black gorge, thousands of cave doors dark in the faces, dust plumes rising from muster plains and the Snow River glinting at the bottom.

ties.why: The Gate wants the same quick children our cavalry academies do, and bids against them.
Our riders break the Stables' yearlings, and the cavalry we raise rides its horses.
Our millet goes down the gorge on the river's barges, and iron sand comes up.

features.name: cave homes cut into the loess cliff-faces
millet terraces on the gorge walls
the cavalry muster plain
the gorge road above the river

entries.name: Realm of the Phantom Feast
entries.summary: A shard world that opens on the new moon of the seventh month in a sunken pavilion in the marsh, nine nights a year. Inside, a banquet is always being served.
entries.lore: The realm is a hall of endless tables, running past sight, laid with spirit foods: every dish raises cultivation, and every dish takes something back, a year of life, a memory, a name. Only those below Core Formation can pass the gate, which stays open nine nights. The Night Banquet invites promising young cultivators of other sects, all expenses paid. Some come back stronger. Some come back strange.
entries.truth: The sect's founder found this realm, ate at its table for nine nights and came out with the Banquet's devouring method.
entries.fromAbove: Nothing but black water and reeds, a sunken pavilion's roof ridge showing as a pale line at low water; for the nine nights, a column of red lantern-light stands over it.

ties.why: The Banquet's invitations are the only way in, and its guests eat at our tables nine nights a year.

features.name: the gate hall under the water
tables laid with spirit foods, past sight
the host's seat, always empty

entries.name: City of Returning Spring
entries.summary: The pill market at the mouth of Apricot Grove Valley, a city of twenty million where the valley sells its pills and the sick of the whole continent come to wait.
entries.lore: The Apricot Grove Valley's pill halls take up a whole quarter, with prices posted daily and a [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] banker at each counter. The rest of the city is clinics, herb markets, inns for patients and the families of patients, and appraisers who test pills for fakes. Beast emissaries in human form walk its streets under the valley's protection, and attacking one is the one crime the Apricot Grove Valley punishes itself.
entries.fromAbove: A city 250 li across at the valley's mouth, its pill-hall quarter shining under a gold ward dome and the road of patients winding in from the plains in a long pale thread.

ties.why: We buy the Bai lotus pods by the cartload for the pill halls.
A Pavilion banker sits at every pill-hall counter and changes our stones.
Beast emissaries buy medicine in our streets, and we protect them from everyone but the Butchers' friends.
The valley's pill halls fill our streets, and its guards keep the peace.

features.name: the pill halls' posted-price boards
the inns for patients and their families
the appraisers' lanes
the beast emissaries' quarter

entries.name: Fire Prison Valley
entries.summary: A caldera valley 7,000 li across, lit by a hundred vents and lava lakes, where fire spirits drift like smoke and the air kills a mortal in ten breaths. The Blazing Furnace Sect harvests fire essence here.
entries.lore: Earth-fire bubbles up through a hundred vents, each a lake of fire a day's walk round, and fire spirits born from it attack anything with qi. Fire essence condensed on the vent lips is the key ingredient for Fire Dao breakthroughs and sells for mid-grade stones. Mortals need masks; Qi Condensation cultivators need luck. The valley floor is littered with refiners' tools and bones, and the sect's harvest crews work the rim in arrays that hold for a season at a time.
entries.fromAbove: A caldera lit orange by a hundred vent-mouths and lava lakes, a standing column of smoke over it and a ring of pale harvest arrays along its rim.

ties.why: The Furnace's crews harvest our fire essence from the vent lips and pay for it in lives.

features.name: vent lips crusted with fire essence
lava pools between the vents
drifting fire-spirit smoke
refiners' bones and tools on the valley floor

top.note: fire spirits, and the Furnace's harvest crews

entries.name: Gate of Fine Grain
entries.summary: A spirit-farming sect of twenty thousand disciples that bred half the spirit rice strains grown in the Morning Star Continent, on terraced valleys across 1,200 li. Its fields have failed, and it is selling its disciples' contracts to stay solvent.
entries.lore: The Gate of Fine Grain teaches the Wood and Earth Daos through farming: disciples learn to read soil, call rain and graft spirit herbs before they learn a single attack. It recruits farm children with good roots and sells its seed strains everywhere. Now its elders blame the [[Apricot Grove Valley]] for a blight they cannot cure, and its young disciples are being hired out as field hands to anyone who pays the sect, including people who should not have them.
entries.truth: Half of the Gate of Fine Grain's failure really is the Apricot Grove Valley blight, planted ten years ago. The other half is the drain. The elders cannot tell the two apart, and that is the problem.
entries.fromAbove: Valley country stepped into emerald and amber terraces, the Gate's halls on three ridge-tops and the nearest terraces gone brown.

ties.why: The sect's disciples come in each opening for wild seed, and we sell what they cannot carry.
Our elders blame the Valley for a blight we cannot cure, and we cannot prove it.
We hire out disciples as field hands and granary guards, and King Hao pays in land titles.

features.name: the seed vaults, strains sealed in jade jars
terraced fields where disciples learn soil first
the rain altar on the high ridge

entries.name: The Sword Domain
entries.summary: The Clear Heaven Sword Sect's seventy-two peaks, strung along ninety thousand li of snow ridge at the Morning Star Continent's northern tip and facing the Floating Peak Continent across the strait. Four billion mortals farm and quarry for the sect, and every road here ends at a sword.
entries.lore: The Sword Domain belongs to the [[Clear Heaven Sword Sect]], and the sect does not pretend otherwise: its seventy-two peaks, each crowned with halls and ringed in pale array light, are the region's government, its duel rankings its law and its vassal kingdoms, each the size of a country, its farms. The valleys between the peaks are the strokes of its ancestors' swords, cut dead straight for hundreds of li, and four billion mortals plough, quarry and herd along them for the sect. Applicants from all over Morning Star climb the Sword Stair each spring, in front of the whole sect. Four elders sent to the [[Seal Watch]] were due home last year and have not come, and the sect has stopped saying when they will. Spies from the [[Night Banquet Sect]] are caught on the lower peaks every season, more of them each year.
entries.truth: The main peak's sword hum, which every disciple hears in meditation, faded two hundred years ago. The elders replaced it with an array that imitates it.
entries.fromAbove: A snow range of seventy-two summits, each crowned with halls and a ring of pale sword-light, the main peak's great dome at its heart, canyons cut straight as sword strokes between them and the strait's dark water at its foot.

ties.why: Our peaks tithe the terraces below and take their rooted children at the Sword Stair.
We sell the North Wind meltwater and sword-steel silt down the Snow River, and buy its horses.

top.note: the founder in seclusion; Qingxiao's masters at Deity Transformation

entries.name: Valley of the Sword Graves
entries.summary: The valley where the Clear Heaven Sword Sect buries the swords of its dead, 4,800 li across. Their intent lingers and cuts anyone who walks in without the strength to bear it.
entries.lore: Swords stand in the snow by the hundred thousand, each over a grave, rows of them running to the horizon, and the oldest, the swords of the sect's first ancestors, as tall as hills. Walking among them is a test of Sword Dao: those who endure the intent come out with insight, those who don't come out in pieces. The Clear Heaven Sword Sect lets its disciples in on oath and outsiders never. Thieves still try for the swords of fallen elders, which can be worth a sect's ransom.
entries.truth: Some graves are empty. The Clear Heaven Sword Sect buries the swords of disciples it executed in secret beside the honored dead.
entries.fromAbove: A snowfield 4,800 li across bristling with swords in rows to the horizon, the oldest standing like pale hills, and a faint blue shimmer of sword intent hanging over it.

access.rank: sworn disciple of the Clear Heaven Sword Sect, on oath

ties.why: The sect's dead lie under our swords, and only its sworn disciples walk among them.

features.name: the rows of grave-swords running to the horizon
the oath gate where disciples swear to enter
the oldest swords, tall as hills, their intent a standing storm

entries.name: The Jiao Nest
entries.summary: Sea caves cut into 6,000 li of cliff where a jiao of the Azure Wave Palace's court raises its young. Any human who enters dies, and their village pays for it.
entries.lore: Fishermen steer wide of the caves, a cliff-face of mouths each as wide as a harbor, and coast law forbids even pointing at them. Jiao eggshells and shed scales wash up nearby and sell for fortunes to refiners, who pay beachcombers not to ask where they came from. The young jiao are said to be worth a Core Formation breakthrough each. The sea clans have punished one village for a single stolen scale.
entries.fromAbove: A cliff coast pierced by hundreds of dark cave mouths, a white scatter of shed scales along the tide line and a slow whirl of cloud always over the water above the nest.

ties.why: The jiao is a prince of the Palace's court, and our young are the reason it stays on this coast.
Stone Forts' beachcombers sell our shed scales to refiners, and one village already paid for a stolen scale.

features.name: the sea caves, each mouth as wide as a harbor
the shed-scale beach
the egg cavern where the young jiao grow

entries.name: Boundary Head Town
entries.summary: A market city of four million where the imperial road ends and the mountain paths begin. Registry officers, sect recruiters and smugglers all drink in the same three teahouses.
entries.lore: Boundary Head Town is where Beneath the Peaks trades: cinnabar and talismans going down, rice and iron coming up, in caravans of thousands. A Registry checkpoint searches every caravan heading uphill, a Clear Heaven Sword Sect recruiting hall sits across the great square, and the Mountain Road Gang owns the noodle shop between them. Duels in the square are legal if both parties are cultivators and the magistrate is paid. Talisman seconds from the [[Vermilion Talisman Sect]] sell here for a few low-grade stones.
entries.fromAbove: A walled city a hundred li across on the last of the plain, the imperial road running in from the south and the first mountain paths unspooling from its north gate into the terraces, a Registry array dome over the checkpoint ward.

ties.why: The Gang owns the noodle shop between the checkpoint and the recruiting hall, and our magistrate takes its coin.
Its outer disciples sell talisman seconds in our market at a third of the price.
The bridge kingdom's barges bring us rice and iron and carry talismans back down.

features.name: the Registry checkpoint at the uphill gate
the Sword Sect's recruiting hall across the great square
the Mountain Road Gang's noodle shop between them
the talisman-seconds stalls

entries.name: Sea-Pacifying Command
entries.summary: The Great Jing's southern fleet: three thousand war junks with array-armored hulls, conscripted cultivator marines and an admiral with ambitions.
entries.lore: The Command patrols the southern sea lanes, escorts convoys to the Thousand Isles and ferries troops to the Jade Strait, its great junks a li from stem to stern and its anchorage three hundred li across. Its marines are Registry conscripts who drew sea duty, and its spear-and-water drills are brutal. It pays bounties for pirates, buys pearls cheap from captured smugglers and hires outside cultivators as convoy guards. Admiral Hou, a Nascent Soul, answers to the throne on paper and to Prince Rui in letters.
entries.fromAbove: Drydock quays in ranks along the coast under a ward dome, and war junks at anchor so thick the water shows white.

access.rank: Registry sea-duty conscript or hired convoy guard

ties.why: The Sea Gate's harbor is our base: we keep its chain and its customs men keep our stores.
We draw our sailors and our pay from the throne, though the admiral writes to Prince Rui.
Gao holds a mainland harbor under our noses; we have attacked it twice and lost twice.
We convoy the kingdom's ships and keep the pirates off them, and the king pays for guards in stones.
We sail in the pagoda's circle and guard the cape when the stones run late, because every wreck lands on us.

features.name: the war-junk drydocks
the spear-and-water drill yard
the bounty board for pirates

entries.name: Capital Prefecture
entries.summary: The crown's own prefecture around the Jing Capital: 12,500 li across, four and a half billion farmers, a registry office in every market town and the palace lights on the horizon every night.
entries.lore: The Capital Prefecture has no king; a Grain Intendant rules it for the throne and answers for every missing bushel and every untested child. Its counties are each a country's worth of people. Children here grow up on millet porridge, march drills and stories of village boys who tested well and came home in silver armor. Families with a rooted child are paid a bounty of ten low-grade spirit stones; families caught hiding one lose their land. The black trade in clean test results runs through the bathhouses of the Grain-Barge Mouth.
entries.fromAbove: The densest farmland in the world, paddies to the horizon every way, a registry town at each canal junction and the Jing Capital's dome of light standing over all of it.

ties.why: The capital eats what we grow, and we answer for every missing bushel.
The Registry's office in every market town takes our children and our land when we hide a rooted one.

features.name: the registry office in every market town
the drill grounds where village boys march
millet paddies under the palace lights

entries.name: Golden Spear Guard
entries.summary: The imperial clan's own spear guard, forty thousand cultivators picked from the Registry's best roots, camped in a ring of cities on three hills south of the capital. Every prince wants it, and it has started to split along their lines.
entries.lore: The Guard trains the empire's finest rooted conscripts in the imperial spear method and the Metal and Slaughter Daos, then posts them to the palace, the princes and the frontier. Its parade ground is a plain, and a full parade is forty thousand spears in one ring of gold light. A Guard captain outranks a provincial governor. Its commander, a Nascent Soul, swears loyalty only to the Ancestor Emperor, whom she has never seen. Its junior officers drink in factions and duel at night, and the princes pay their debts.
entries.truth: The commander has received orders under the Ancestor Emperor's seal for forty years. Lately the brushwork has changed.
entries.fromAbove: A great circular drill plain on three hills, ringed by barracks-cities, with a gold spear-shaped pillar of light standing over its center on parade days.

ties.why: We serve the Ancestor Emperor, whom our commander has never seen, and the princes serve themselves through us.
The prince pays our officers' debts, and in return he gets their drill-hall gossip and, when it comes, their spears.

features.name: the parade plain, where forty thousand spears stand in one ring
the officers' wine-houses, where duels start after dark
the armory of imperial spears

entries.name: Terrace of Nine Thunders
entries.summary: A bare headland 300 li across where lightning strikes nine times in every storm, always in the same nine places. Cultivators come to watch it and comprehend the Lightning Dao.
entries.lore: The nine strike-points are scorched into fields of glass, each a day's walk across. Sitting between them during a storm is the fastest way to grasp Lightning Dao and the fastest way to die. The Thunder-Drawing Sect owns the headland and charges entry. Glass from the strike-points is an artifact refining material for lightning weapons.
entries.truth: The nine points form a fragment of an Ascent Age tribulation array. Someone could finish it.
entries.fromAbove: A bare black headland 300 li across thrust into the surf under permanent storm cloud, nine pale glass fields set on it in a ring and a bolt forever walking somewhere in the dark.

ties.why: The Thunder-Drawing Sect owns the headland and charges every cultivator who comes to watch.

features.name: the nine glass strike-points
the bare headland, open to the sky
the sect's entry gate

entries.name: Kingdom of Nine Bends
entries.summary: The delta kingdom at the Flood River's mouth, 8,000 li across and home to forty-six million: a maze of channels, river pirates and an imperial governor who has not seen his salary in years and does not need it.
entries.lore: Nine Bends is nominally an imperial prefecture. In practice, the river pirates who know the channels, some of them wide as inland seas, decide which barges reach the sea, and Governor Pei decides which pirates he arrests. Children here learn the channels by heart and learn early which boats not to look at. Grain barges from upriver come in light this year, and smuggled cargo going out goes heavier.
entries.fromAbove: A delta fanning into hundreds of channels, braided silver through reed-green islands, the governor's walled seat a pale fleck at the first bend and pirate anchorages hidden in the lower maze.

ties.why: We know every channel, and we decide which barges reach the sea.
Governor Pei decides which pirates run cargo to the Market's moorings, and takes his cut.

features.name: the nine bends, a channel maze
pirate anchorages behind reed islands
the governor's tollhouse

entries.name: Miners' Brotherhood
entries.summary: A secret society of miners and convicts, millions strong across the pits, planning to break the penal pits open. Its oath is sworn on a lump of ore.
entries.lore: The Brotherhood smuggles food, medicine and cultivation manuals into the pits and smuggles people out, through galleries under the pit walls that run for hundreds of li. Its members are miners, escaped convicts and a few disgraced cultivators who learned Earth Dao underground. It wants the Convict Prefecture emptied and the Kangs dead. It pays in ore, recruits anyone the overseers have whipped, and is already planning to use the vein rush as cover.
entries.fromAbove: Nothing a map would show: the pit-heads among the forty, a few sealed shafts whose spoil heaps never grow, and ore-carts on tracks that end in the rock.

ties.why: We mean to see the Kangs dead and their shafts opened to the miners they own.
We smuggle food, medicine and manuals into the pits and people out, and mean to break the prefecture open.
We sell ore for food and powder in the stampede's crowd, where nobody asks whose ore it is.

features.name: a smuggling gallery under the pit wall
the oath-ore altar in a worked-out shaft
an ore-cart track running to nowhere

entries.name: The Withered Plain
entries.summary: Sixteen thousand li of dead fields beside the Flood River, where ash locusts swarm and drain the qi out of anything that stands still.
entries.lore: Ash locusts came out of the dead soil two years ago: gray insects that strip qi instead of leaves, in swarms that darken the sky over hundreds of li. A swarm can empty a Qi Condensation cultivator's dantian in minutes. Their wings are a talisman ink ingredient and sell well in the City of Pecks and Bushels, so desperate hunters go in with nets and fire. The swarms are spreading toward the [[Kingdom of Wheat Waves]].
entries.truth: The locusts are hatching from soil emptied of qi. Wherever the drain runs deepest, they appear first.
entries.fromAbove: A gray-and-ochre scar across the green plain, its edges ragged, with dark swarms moving over it like smoke.

ties.why: Hunters wade into our swarms with nets and fire and carry the wings out to the City of Pecks and Bushels.
The swarms spread east toward Wheat Waves' standing wheat, wherever the soil is emptiest.

features.name: dead fields, gray stalks to the horizon
a hatching ground in cracked soil
the hunters' fire-lines

entries.name: Heaven-Peeping Abbey
entries.summary: Astrologer-priests who watch the Stump and the Mirror from an observatory cut into a sea-cliff a li high, and sell fortunes to kings and sects.
entries.lore: The Abbey has logged the Stump's hum and the Mirror's width every night for two thousand years, from a stack of bronze rings and star-terraces cut into the cliff, its largest dial open to the whole sky. It teaches divination, star-reading and a slow Time Dao method that ages its masters gracefully. Kings buy horoscopes; sects buy dates for breakthroughs; the Armillary Pavilion buys the logs and pretends not to need them. Its novices are orphans of the coast with good eyes and no families to miss them.
entries.truth: The logs show the Stump's hum rising with the tide, faster each decade. The abbot sent the figures to the Armillary Pavilion and has been paid every year since to stop publishing them.
entries.fromAbove: A bronze-ringed observatory cut into a sea-cliff, its ring-dials catching the light and a thin array dome over it that glows with the Mirror's phases.

ties.why: King Wen pays us a barge of rice a month to read his dreams, and we send him a horoscope for every harvest.
We take Laver's orphans with good eyes as novices and send a priest each new moon to read the shrine's bowl.
The abbot sends the Stump's figures to the Pavilion and has been paid every year since to stop publishing them.
We pay the beach's scavengers to log each rift's hour and width, numbers the Stump's hum seems to follow.

features.name: the bronze ring-dials on the cliff
the log hall, two thousand years of nightly records
the novices' dormitory in the cliff

entries.name: Kingdom of Blue Stone
entries.summary: A quarry kingdom of eighty-eight million under the eastern peaks, cutting the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's whetstones and sword-steps out of blue cliffs worked for hundreds of li. Its king is a Clear Heaven Sword Sect outer disciple and rules like one.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Blue Stone's blue whetstone takes an edge on spirit steel, and every stone is cut for the Clear Heaven Sword Sect, from quarry-cliffs worked in terraces for hundreds of li along the eastern range. The king, a Foundation outer disciple named Fang Ru, settles disputes by duel and lets any subject challenge a magistrate. Children work the quarries from ten and spar with wooden swords at night. Rooted children go up the mountain at nine with no Registry paperwork, which makes the Kingdom of Blue Stone the empire's least favorite place.
entries.truth: Fang Ru was sent down from the inner sect for a crime the sect never names. He has been writing to the Night Banquet.
entries.fromAbove: Blue cliffs cut back in great terraced steps across the eastern range, quarry-dust plumes over every cut, and a pale sword-array ring marking the king's seat.

ties.why: We cut every whetstone and sword-step for the Sword Sect, and our king is its outer disciple.
Our king, sent down from the inner sect for a crime the sect never names, has been writing to the Banquet.
Sword-Asking Town's swordsmiths buy our whetstones by the thousand.

features.name: quarry cliffs cut in terraces
the night spar yards where children train with wooden swords
the whetstone sheds stacked for the sect
the magistrates' duel ground

entries.name: Thunder Wolf Clan
entries.summary: Packs of thunder-wolves, three hundred thousand strong, in groves burned grey across 3,000 li of forest, led by a Core Formation wolf king who has learned to bargain with the loggers instead of eating them.
entries.lore: The wolves den where lightning strikes most, and their fur stores enough charge to stop a heart. The wolf king lets logging crews into the groves in exchange for salt and the bodies of poachers. Beast tamers prize thunder-wolf pups above any other beast in the north, and poachers who take them start feuds that last generations. The king speaks in a growl that sounds like words to anyone with good ears.
entries.truth: Beast Court envoys have offered the king a seat at the Court's lowest table if his packs drive the loggers out of the groves for good. He has not decided.
entries.fromAbove: A scar of burned pine groves 3,000 li across, ash-grey among the green forest, with a pale storm-glow flickering over the dens at night.

ties.why: We let their logging crews into our groves for salt and the bodies of poachers.
The Court's envoys offered me a seat at its lowest table if my packs drive the loggers out for good, and I have not decided.

features.name: the burned pine groves
a den hollow in the root-mounds
the wolf king's lightning-struck hill
the salt-for-bodies trading clearing

entries.name: Jiao Clan of Thunderwood
entries.summary: A clan of ten thousand puppeteers who carve fighting puppets from lightning-struck pine. Their puppets move faster than a Foundation cultivator can draw a sword.
entries.lore: The Jiao clan buys every thunder-struck pine in the Thunder Cliffs and carves it into puppets animated by lightning arrays, in timber yards that cover a mountain's shoulder. Its best puppets fight at Core Formation and sell to princes and sects across the Morning Star Continent. Outsiders can apprentice for ten years of service. The clan hates the Thousand Puppet Gate, whose corpse puppets it calls 'grave meat on strings', and refuses to sell to anyone who buys from it.
entries.truth: The Jiao patriarch has bought one of the Gate's immortal-corpse puppets in secret to study it. It watches him when he works.
entries.fromAbove: A mountain shoulder of timber yards stacked in rings under a pale lightning-array dome, long lines of felled storm-pine converging on it down sledge roads from the groves.

ties.why: Our puppets ship through Stilled Waves, and its warehouses keep them dry until the weather lets a ship leave.
The king borrowed against his crown, and we buy every struck pine at the price we set.
We call the Gate's corpse puppets grave meat on strings and sell to nobody who buys from them.

features.name: the carving yards among stacked pine
the lightning-array workshop where puppets wake
the patriarch's private study

entries.name: Thunder Cliffs
entries.summary: Seventy-two thousand li of storm-pine forest on sea cliffs at the Morning Star Continent's northeastern corner, facing the Shoreless Sea, where thunderstorms come ashore three days in four.
entries.lore: Storms off the outer ocean break on the Thunder Cliffs's cliffs all year, and lightning strikes the headlands so often that the pines grow scarred and the rocks are magnetized. It is poor country for farming and rich country for anyone who can use lightning: talisman makers buy thunder-struck wood, puppeteers carve it, and lightning cultivators come to be struck on purpose.
