The coast pays toll to the [[Azure Wave Palace]] for every boat that fishes past the reefs. The empire's writ is thin here; the Registry tester comes by ship, when the weather allows, and a season can pass between his visits.
entries.truth: The storms have doubled in ten years. Something far out toward the Rim is drawing them, and the lightning sect's elders have felt it calling.
entries.fromAbove: A dark forest stepping down to white sea cliffs under a lid of storm cloud that never clears, lightning forking into it, the Thunder-Drawing Sect's forest of rods on the highest cliff and the coast's coves picked out in surf.

ties.why: Every boat that fishes past the reefs owes the Palace a toll, and the coast pays it.

top.note: the Thunder-Drawing Sect's master, there for the storms that come ashore

entries.name: Rift Beach
entries.summary: A beach 6,000 li long where spatial rifts from the Shattered Sea wash ashore after storms, drifting like jellyfish as tall as hills. Touch one and you are elsewhere, or in pieces.
entries.lore: Rifts come in on the tide, hang above the sand for hours, some as tall as a hill, and fade. Things come through them too: driftwood from other continents, ancient coins, once a live sea serpent a li long. Space Dao cultivators meditate on the rifts from a safe distance; scavenger fleets wait offshore to grab whatever falls out. Nobody walks the beach at night.
entries.truth: One rift in ten opens toward the Scar. What comes through those does not wash back out.
entries.fromAbove: A pale beach stretching 6,000 li, the air above it shimmering and bent after each storm, and the dark specks of scavenger fleets waiting offshore.

ties.why: The Abbey's priests pay us for the hour and width of every rift, and ask nothing about what we pull out of them.
Scavengers sell whatever falls out of the rifts at Evening Glow's salvage market.

features.name: a rift drifting above the sand like a jellyfish
the wrack-line of salvaged flotsam
the Space Dao watchers' rock terraces

entries.name: Court of the Spirit Registry
entries.summary: The imperial bureau that tests, registers and conscripts every spirit-rooted child in the Great Jing Dynasty's lands, through a registry office in every county. Its gray-robed testers are the most hated officials on the continent.
entries.lore: The Registry keeps a jade slip for every rooted child in a hundred kingdoms, in an archive that fills a mountain, and sends testers on a six-year circuit with a root-reading mirror, each tester working a hundred counties. Top roots go to the palace academies, middling ones to the army, poor ones to the arsenals and granaries as qi laborers. Sect recruiters who take a registered child are outlaws in the Great Jing Dynasty. The Registry pays informers, hires bounty cultivators to track runaways, and quietly sells its rejects' slips to the highest bidder.
entries.truth: Since the harvests failed the Registry has been ordered to send every root above middling straight to the palace, unrecorded. None of those children have been assigned anywhere.
entries.fromAbove: An archive mountain terraced with jade-slip vaults, its gray walls ringed by testers' camps and the road-lines of the six-year circuits converging on it.

ties.why: We test and register for the throne, and what the throne wants it takes.
We rent berths at the Mouth for the pens, and its bathhouses sell test slips that hide the children we are sent to find.
The prefecture's families hide rooted children from our testers, and we pay ten stones a head and take the land of anyone caught.
The temple's kitchens turn rooted children into monks beyond our reach, and we do not forgive it.
The Bais hand us one child in three, and we count it a full quota.
Beneath the Peaks is where the Sword Sect takes registered children from under our testers.
The prefecture's garrison backs our testers and carries our slips against the sect.
The Li grandson's conscription is in our rolls; they write every year and we answer nothing.

features.name: the mirror hall where roots are read
the archive of jade slips
the holding pens for rooted children

entries.name: Camp of the Displaced
entries.summary: A sprawling refugee camp 120 li across on the marsh's northern edge, six million famine refugees strong and growing by thousands each day. Night Banquet buyers walk its lanes with full purses.
entries.lore: Families from the dead plains arrive daily with nothing. The Temple of Alms-Food runs kitchens with ladle lines li long; imperial officers run a census to find rooted children; marsh buyers run indenture contracts. Gangs run the water. A cultivator can hire a hundred laborers here for a sack of rice, or adopt a rooted orphan before the Registry does.
entries.fromAbove: A smear of gray tents and pale roofs 120 li across at the marsh's edge, spreading a little each week, kitchen smoke in hundreds of threads and the dust of arriving columns on every road.

ties.why: Our hungry come from the streets of Pecks and Bushels, and we send it laborers for a sack of rice.
The Temple of Alms-Food runs a kitchen that keeps thousands of us alive each day.
The Banquet's buyers walk our lanes with full purses and leave with whole families on contract.

features.name: the Temple's kitchen lines, li long
the census post where officers test children
indenture-buyers' tents
the water gangs' wells

entries.name: Kingdom of Reed Flowers
entries.summary: A stilt-city kingdom over 10,300 li of reeds and thirty-one million people, ruled by a gentle mortal king and his Night Banquet chamberlain. Each autumn it sends twenty youths from every county to serve at the banquets.
entries.lore: Reed Flowers fishes, cuts reeds and paddles everywhere. Its king writes poetry and signs whatever the chamberlain puts in front of him. The kingdom is safe: no pirates, no bandits, no imperial auditors, because nobody wants to offend the sect. Every autumn twenty young people from every county go to the banquet halls as servants, and most come back in a year with gifts and silences. Children grow up among herons, leeches and stories about the ones who did not.
entries.truth: The ones who come back are not all the ones who left. A few are Banquet disciples wearing their faces, and they go on to serve in noble houses across the Morning Star Continent.
entries.fromAbove: A sea of reeds in russet and green, stilt towns strung along the channels like beads, herons in drifting clouds and the king's pale city on a rise at the center.

ties.why: We are safe because nobody offends the sect, and each autumn we send its halls twenty young people from every county.

features.name: stilt-houses over open water
the reed-cutters' flats
the royal pavilion, where the chamberlain stands behind the throne

entries.name: Kingdom of Wheat Waves
entries.summary: A dry wheat kingdom 11,000 li across on the plain's eastern edge, in open famine. Its king fled to the Jing Capital, and a peasant army calling itself the Barefoot Banner, millions strong, holds the granaries.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Wheat Waves was the poorest vassal before the harvests failed, and now it is lawless. The Barefoot Banner has opened the royal granaries and hangs tax collectors, and its leader is a Qi Condensation hedge cultivator who claims Heaven has withdrawn its mandate from the Jing. The empire has sent a punitive column of a hundred thousand soldiers and a few hundred cultivators. Both sides are hiring, and so are the slavers following the column.
entries.truth: The Banner's leader hums a tune nobody taught him, and his followers have started humming it too.
entries.fromAbove: Dry wheat plain gone gold-brown, smoke rising from burned granary-towns along the capital road, a dark smear of the Banner's camp and the dust of a column crawling in from the north.

ties.why: The Jing's quota starved us, and its column is marching in to collect it.
The locusts are spreading toward our last fields, and the Banner has no answer to them.
The Banner's leader hums a tune nobody taught him, and his followers have started humming it too.

features.name: the royal granaries, thrown open
the Banner's camp of ten thousand cookfires
the tax-collectors' gallows at the crossroads

entries.name: Realm of Grain in Ear
entries.summary: A farming shard world whose gate opens in a wheat estate east of the Jing Capital for forty days every twelve years. Only cultivators below Foundation can pass.
entries.lore: Inside is an endless autumn of wild spirit grain guarded by straw-golem scarecrows as tall as halls and harvest mice the size of dogs. Seeds brought out sprout in any soil, and with the harvests failing, the court has promised a minor title for every hundred catties of seed. The princes each field their own teams of young cultivators, and the teams fight inside. The gate next opens in two years.
entries.truth: Straw golems that are smashed reform in the shape of whoever smashed them.
entries.fromAbove: A golden wheat estate 30 li across under a faint shimmer; for the forty days it is open, a column of gold light stands over it.

ties.why: The court holds the wheat field where our gate opens, and its teams come in to carry out what they can.
The Gate sends its best young disciples through every opening to carry wild seed out for its failing strains.

features.name: straw-golem scarecrows in rows
wheat to the horizon
harvest-mouse burrows

entries.name: Imperial Horse Pastures
entries.summary: The empire's stud farms across nine thousand li of high plateau grass, where wind-maned spirit horses are bred by the hundred thousand for princes and cavalry. Horse thieves hang from every gate.
entries.lore: The Imperial Stables run the pastures as a prefecture of 140 million, and every herder family is bound to the herds by law. The herds take a week to ride past, and the wind-maned horses can run a thousand li a day and sell for a mid-grade stone each, so thieves come from everywhere, including the princes' own households. Children herd foals and learn horse medicine before letters. A herder who raises a champion is freed with his family.
entries.truth: Prince Rui's agents have been buying the best foals through false sales. The Stables' master knows and has been paid to know.
entries.fromAbove: Grass to every horizon, the herds' trails worn into it like braided rivers of dust and the stud-farm steadings as pale rings of array-fenced pasture.

ties.why: Yellow Cliffs' riders break our yearlings for the cavalry, and its sons ride the horses we breed.
Prince Rui's agents have been buying our best foals through false sales, and our master has been paid to know.

features.name: wind-maned herds on open grass
the foaling barns and horse-medicine halls
the gibbets at every gate
the champions' paddock

entries.name: Soul-Lost Stone Forest
entries.summary: A maze of stone pillars 12,000 li across, each pillar a peak in its own right, where a great python from the Vast Wilds Continent has made its den. Its illusions turn the forest into a trap no map survives.
entries.lore: The Golden Python's grandson, a Nascent Soul serpent several li long, crossed the strait six years ago and took the stone forest as its hunting ground. Its illusions make travelers walk in circles until they starve. A shed skin of its is worth a fortune, and its den is said to hold the treasures of everyone it has eaten. Three imperial expeditions have gone in.
entries.fromAbove: Stone pillars by the hundred thousand under a lid of mist that never lifts, the mist turning slowly at its heart round the python's den.

ties.why: The serpent of the stone forest is the Golden Python's grandson, and his den answers to the lair.

features.name: stone pillars that shift in the illusion
narrow lanes between the pillars
the python's den

entries.name: Netherworm Stockade
entries.summary: Demonic Gu raisers on a mud island 400 li across in the marsh, who buy Gu eggs smuggled from the Vast Wilds Continent and sell curses to the Night Banquet's guests.
entries.lore: The Stockade breeds Gu in jars sunk in marsh mud, crossing Vast Wilds strains with marsh leeches and corpse worms, in rows of jars that run for li across the island. Its masters teach Gu raising to anyone who survives a year of feeding the jars, and their curses kill from twenty li, given a hair or a name. They buy eggs from frontier smugglers at any price and are terrified of the Jar-Mothers ever finding out where their strains came from.
entries.truth: Three of their strains were stolen from a Jar-Mother village. The thief is the Stockade's master, and the Jar-Mothers already know.
entries.fromAbove: A mud island 400 li across ringed with black reed and pocked with ranks of sunken jars like a honeycomb, a thin green mist lying on it that does not drift.

ties.why: We sell curses to the Banquet's guests at its own tables.
We buy the Society's Gu eggs at any price, from whichever crew brings them off the chain.
Three of our strains were stolen from a Jar-Mother village, and we dread the day they learn it.
Our jars want the fen's blood-leeches and corpse worms, and we pay the leech-catchers on stilts.
The Hill's master pays well for blight samples and never says what he'll do with them.

features.name: the jar fields, rows of sunken jars
the feeding yard where a year's trial begins
the curse hall where hair and names are kept

entries.name: Bright Pearl Shoals
entries.summary: Spirit-oyster beds across 800 li of shallow, warm water where the best pearls on the coast grow. Divers, pirates and sea-clan wardens all claim them.
entries.lore: The oysters feed on qi from a vein under the seabed, and a hundred-year pearl can be ground into Foundation pills. The Kingdom of the Held Pearl holds the shoals by treaty with the sea clans and must leave a third of the beds untouched. Poachers come at night in black boats. The giant spirit clams in the deepest beds, each the size of a hill, have taken more divers than the pirates.
entries.fromAbove: A green-gold stain 800 li across in the warm shallows, flecked white with diving fleets and the buoy-lines of the sea-clan wardens' protected third.

ties.why: The Pearl Queen's divers work my beds, leave a third of them whole and a tenth of every catch to the sea clans.
A third of my beds lie untouched under the Palace's treaty, and its wardens count the buoys.

features.name: the oyster beds over the qi vein
the giant spirit clams in the deepest beds
the untouched third, marked by the sea clans' buoys

entries.name: The Ink Marsh
entries.summary: The black-water marshes of the Flood River delta, 75,000 li of reed, channel and mud and the seat of the Night Banquet Sect. Every forbidden thing in the Morning Star Continent is for sale here, usually after dark.
entries.lore: The Ink Marsh is the [[Night Banquet Sect]]'s country. Its stilt kingdoms are ruled by puppets, its channels by smugglers and its nights by the sect's banquets, held each new moon in a hall nobody finds twice. Black markets float through the reeds selling stolen manuals, Gu, slaves and secrets from every court. The famine has filled the marsh's edges with refugees by the million, and the sect's buyers pick through them. The marsh is spreading north a hundred li each year, and the land it takes does not come back.
entries.truth: The marsh grows wherever the Banquet Master's aura settles. That cultivation has outgrown Nascent Soul, and the land is the first thing that cannot hide it.
entries.fromAbove: A black-and-silver maze of channels and reed beds under a low mist, delta fans of ink-dark water, floating-market lanterns pricking the dusk and the marsh's northern edge creeping over green fields.

ties.why: Famine families walk south into our edges, and our buyers go north up the river after them.
The marsh's buyers take living convicts from the Prefecture's warden, bought as dead men.

entries.name: Kingdom of Spirit Herders
entries.summary: A kingdom of beast tamers on 9,000 li of grassland, who raise war mounts for the empire by the hundred thousand from eggs smuggled out of the Vast Wilds Continent. The Beast Court has put a price on every one of them.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Spirit Herders's ranches raise thunder-horned deer, scale-horses and war hounds from eggs and cubs bought from smugglers, in herds that take days to ride past. The empire buys every mount at a good price, and the herder families are rich, armed and hunted. Beast Court agents, half-bloods in its pay and now and then an old beast, cross the strait to kill tamers and free their beasts. Children are bonded to a hatchling at seven and grow up with it.
entries.truth: The kingdom's best stallion bloodline comes from a beast that wandered over the strait on its own and asked to stay. It speaks, though it has never shown a realm that should allow it, and has asked them to keep that quiet.
entries.fromAbove: Open grass to every edge, the herds' trails worn into it like braided rivers, and the ranch steadings as pale rings of array-fenced pasture.

ties.why: The Gate spits on us as collaborators and seizes any bonded beast that strays near its hall.
Our hatchlings come over the strait in Night Bridge crates, and we pay whatever they ask.
The Court has priced every tamer's head and sends agents over the strait to collect.
The frontier command buys every war mount we raise, at a good price.

features.name: ranch corrals of thunder-horned deer and scale-horses
open grass to the horizon
the hatchling barns

entries.name: Cloud-Climbing Terraces
entries.summary: Spirit-rice terraces climbing a whole mountainside, three hundred li across, to the gates of the sect peaks. The upper steps glow green; the lower steps, on imperial land, are turning gray.
entries.lore: The mountainside is a stair three thousand steps tall, each step a band of farms worked by families for generations, watered by a vein that runs down the mountain. The top hundred steps belong to the Clear Heaven Sword Sect and grow Cloud-Silk rice that sells for ten low-grade stones a catty. The bottom steps grow mortal rice for the empire's tax. Spirit farmers come to study the terraces' irrigation arrays, which nobody has been able to copy.
entries.truth: The vein feeding the lower steps has started running backward, downhill toward the Jing Capital.
entries.fromAbove: A mountainside carved into a stair of terraces three hundred li across, glowing green at the top and gray at the foot, with irrigation-array light threading down the vein.

ties.why: The top hundred steps of our terraces are the sect's, and they grow its Cloud-Silk rice.
Our lower steps' rice tax feeds the garrison, and the harvests are failing.

features.name: the irrigation arrays at the head of the vein
the Cloud-Silk rice steps at the top
the terrace walls, a long drop between steps
the sect's boundary stone at the hundredth step

entries.name: Abyss-Diving Society
entries.summary: A scavenger sect with fleets of dive-ships on the inner coast, that dives the drowned provinces of the Shattered Sea for Ascent Age ruins. Half its members die rich, the other half just die.
entries.lore: The Society teaches water-breathing arts, appraisal and formation breaking, and outfits crews for months-long dives among the shattered islands and the drowned provinces beneath them. Its drydocks build dive-ships a li long with pressure arrays in their hulls. It buys anything brought up, sells to the [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] and the marsh, and runs the coast's best appraisal hall. New divers sign a ten-year contract and get a tenth of what they find. The Seal Watch has forbidden them to sail inside the marker buoys, and the Society has lost two crews who tried.
entries.truth: The last crew back brought up a jade token that hums in time with the Stump. The Society's master has hidden it and is selling dive rights to the spot.
entries.fromAbove: A crescent of drydocks and dive-ship quays on the inner coast, and the line of the Seal Watch's marker buoys drawn across the sea beyond.

ties.why: We winter our crews at the Cold Ford and sell the drowned valleys' salvage there in spring.
Evening Glow's market buys everything we bring up, and our halls on its waterfront are our shopfront.
We sell the best finds to the Pavilion, the only buyer that can pay in high-grade stones.

features.name: the appraisal hall, where every find is weighed and priced
the drydock of dive-ships
the marker-buoy line where the Seal Watch's ban begins

entries.name: Kingdom by the Bridge
entries.summary: A river kingdom of 1.2 billion built around the Ninefold Bridge, a day's walk across the Snow River. It pays tax to the throne, tithe to the Clear Heaven Sword Sect and bribes to everyone else.
entries.lore: The Kingdom by the Bridge's king is a mortal of an old house who keeps power by never choosing a side. Imperial spearmen guard the south end of the Ninefold Bridge, nine arches and a day's walk from end to end, and the Clear Heaven Sword Sect outer disciples guard the north end, and neither may cross armed. Children grow up fishing off the bridge piers and watching cultivators duel in the river mist. A rooted child born here is a diplomatic incident, and families sometimes sell the news to both sides.
entries.truth: The king's eldest daughter tested as a heaven-grade root. He hid it, and now both sides know.
entries.fromAbove: A river plain, rice-green to every horizon, split by the Snow River and crossed by the Ninefold Bridge, a pale nine-arched line a day's walk long with a gate-array glowing at each end.

ties.why: We pay the Sword Sect its tithe and let its outer disciples hold the bridge's north end.
Our barges carry rice and iron up to Boundary Head and bring talismans back.

features.name: the Ninefold Bridge's nine arches over the Snow River
the bridge piers where children fish
the river mist where cultivators duel
the two end-gates and their wardens

entries.name: Kingdom of Three Passes
entries.summary: The kingdom that holds the three clefts over the Turtle-Spine Mountains, nine thousand li across, and with them the only roads between the east and the empire.
entries.lore: Three Passes lives on tolls. Its ruling family, the Lis, are Core Formation cultivators who have served the throne loyally for six hundred years because loyalty pays. Every caravan, conscript column and tax cart crosses their gates: three gorge-fortresses a hundred li deep, each under a ward array, with caravans queued at them for weeks. The Dawn League needs the passes to rebel; the empire needs them to stop it; the Lis have taken gifts from both and promised nothing.
entries.truth: The Li patriarch's grandson was conscripted by the Registry eight years ago and has not been heard from. The patriarch blames the throne.
entries.fromAbove: Three clefts cut through the red range, each sealed by a gate-array glowing across the gorge, caravan roads queued in thin pale lines up to each and the Li hall on the central pass.

ties.why: Our three gates are the only roads through the Turtle-Spine Mountains, and every caravan pays us to cross.
We took the League's gifts and promised nothing, and they keep sending more.
We hold the passes for the throne, and have for six hundred years because loyalty pays.
The patriarch's grandson went into the Registry's levy eight years ago and no word has come since.

features.name: a gate-array across the cleft
the cleft road between sheer walls
the caravan queue's camp below the gate
the spear cultivators' new post

entries.name: Mountain Road Gang
entries.summary: Smugglers forty thousand strong who guide rooted children past imperial checkpoints to the Sword Stair for a fee, over goat trails braided across the whole range. Most arrive; some are sold elsewhere.
entries.lore: The Gang charges a family a year's harvest to take a child uphill, and it knows every goat trail and every bribable patrol across thousands of li of foothills. Its leaders are failed Clear Heaven Sword Sect applicants with Foundation cultivation and no love for either master. It also runs forged Registry slips, contraband talismans and runaway soldiers. General Yan Ku has hanged four hundred of its guides this year.
entries.truth: One in ten children never reaches the Stair. They go south down the river to the marsh buyers, and the Gang tells the families they failed the climb.
entries.fromAbove: Nothing a patrol could find: goat trails braided up the terrace walls into the high passes, and now and then a lantern in a cleft at night.

ties.why: Boundary Head is where we collect the children and pay the officers who look away.
General Yan Ku hangs our guides at the pass gates and pays for our heads.
We pay in iron and salt to take our children through the Stockades' high passes.

features.name: goat-trail ladders up the terrace walls
a cleft way-station above the checkpoint road
the forged-slip workshop behind a teahouse

entries.name: City of Pecks and Bushels
entries.summary: The river city where the south's grain is weighed, taxed and gambled on: twelve million people on 150 li of exchange halls and quays. The Heavenly Scale Pavilion sets the price at dawn, and by noon people are fighting over it.
entries.lore: The City of Pecks and Bushels sends its grain east to the [[Flood River]], where the barges gather for the trip north. Its grain exchange is the busiest market in the south, and its streets are full of refugees, speculators, imperial auditors and buyers for the marsh. Rooms are cheap, information is not, and a hired guard for a grain barge earns thirty low-grade stones a trip if the barge arrives.
entries.fromAbove: A river city 150 li across, its exchange halls a pale cluster by the water and quays reaching into the Flood River like the teeth of a comb, convoys gathered below it.

ties.why: Our quays send the south's grain into the river, and the convoys that gather there hire our guards.
We hire out convoy guards for the canal and send every barge into it.
We buy locust wings for talisman ink, so hunters keep going into the plain.
The Pavilion's branch sets the grain price at dawn, and we fight over it by noon.
The families we cannot house walk south to the Camp, and marsh buyers hunt our streets for them first.

features.name: the grain exchange floor at dawn
the quays where convoys gather
refugee lanes along the walls
the Pavilion's weighing hall

entries.name: Kingdom of Stone Forts
entries.summary: A coastal kingdom of ninety million where every county seat is a walled fortress and every adult keeps a crossbow, because the pirates come every autumn.
entries.lore: King Dou, a retired pirate hunter, rules from a fortress city on a headland and pays a bounty for pirate heads in salt. Beacon pillars of signal fire line the coast, a few hundred li apart, and the militia, eight million strong, drills monthly. Children learn to shoot before they can write and to hide in cellars when the bells ring. The kingdom hires cultivators every autumn and is always short of them.
entries.truth: King Dou sells captured pirates to the Convict Prefecture as miners instead of hanging them. Three of his recent captures were pirate lords' sons, sent to recruit in the pits.
entries.fromAbove: A headland coast strung with fortress-cities under pale ward domes, a pillar of beacon fire standing every few hundred li along it.

ties.why: The Gate collects imperial bounties for the pirates we caught and bribes for the ones it lets sail.
The sea clans burned one of our villages for one stolen scale, and our beachcombers still sell what washes up.
We send captured pirates to the Prefecture as miners instead of the rope; three of them were lords' sons.

features.name: the headland fortress, whose bells are the kingdom's alarm
the beacon pillars along the coast
the weigh-house where pirate heads are paid in salt

entries.name: The Man-Eating Fen
entries.summary: A fen of sinkholes and blood-leech swarms 11,000 li across, where the marsh swallows bodies whole. The Night Banquet leaves its leftovers here.
entries.lore: Corpse qi pools in the black water and draws blood-leeches by the billion, in swarms that smoke across the water like fog. A swarm can bleed a horse in a minute. Their engorged bodies sell to demonic alchemists, and leech-catchers wade in on stilts. Some of the dead in the fen still walk at night in Ghost Month.
entries.fromAbove: A black-water fen pitted with round sinkholes like old wounds, red-tinged where the leeches mass and a cold fog lying on it at noon.

ties.why: Leech-catchers wade into us for the Stockade's buyers, who pay better than anyone.

features.name: sinkholes where bodies vanish
leech-catchers' stilt platforms
corpse-qi fog

entries.name: Temple of Alms-Food
entries.summary: A Buddhist temple founded by monks from the Myriad Sands Continent, now running famine kitchens across the south: eight thousand monks, kitchens in a hundred cities and converts arriving by the thousand, while the court starts to worry.
entries.lore: The temple feeds anyone who asks, and asks only that they listen to a sermon and leave their name in the merit ledger. Its mother-house is a hall-city on a river terrace, and its branch kitchens feed millions. Its monks cultivate karma and the vajra body, heal for free and refuse to fight unless a mortal is attacked in front of them. Rooted children fed at its kitchens often take vows, which puts them beyond the Registry's reach. The abbot, a Nascent Soul monk from the [[Thousand Lamps Temple]], has been offered land by three princes.
entries.truth: The abbot has read the drain in the earth and knows who causes it. He keeps silent because the court has promised the temple a hundred thousand acres when the famine ends.
entries.fromAbove: A hall-city on a river terrace, saffron roofs round a great pagoda, with lines of the hungry streaming to it along every road.

ties.why: The Registry's testers hunt the children we feed, and vows are the one door they cannot enter.
We run kitchens for the Camp's hungry and take its rooted orphans in.
Our abbot comes from the Thousand Lamps, and the mother-house sends us monks.

features.name: the alms-kitchen's serving yard
the merit ledger hall
the sermon terrace

entries.name: Kingdom of Stone Eyes
entries.summary: Nine thousand li of sinkhole karst ruled by a council of cave clans. The great sinkholes hold whole towns down their walls; half-blood families hide here, and nobody asks what is in the lower caves.
entries.lore: Stone Eyes is named for the round sinkholes that pock its karst. The great ones are tens of li across, each a town terraced down its walls with the farms at the bottom; the small ones hold a village each. Its people farm in the sinkholes, keep bats for guano and guide smugglers through caves that run for thousands of li and that no map shows. The empire counts it as part of the march; the cave clans pay no tax and give no soldiers. Children grow up knowing which neighbors have scales under their sleeves and never saying so.
entries.fromAbove: Pillar karst pocked with round sinkholes, the great ones dark as eyes from above, with cloud pooling in them at dawn.

ties.why: We guide the Society's runners through the lower caves for a share, and never ask what is in the crates.
The march calls us its own and wants our taxes and our sons; it gets neither.

features.name: a sinkhole rim with terraces down the walls
caves no map shows
bat roosts heaped with guano

entries.name: City of the Guarded Mouth
entries.summary: The empire's frontier headquarters, a fortress city of eight million on the coast where the island chain begins. Its walls rise out of the surf as tall as sea cliffs, faced with the skulls of the beast kings that tried them.
entries.lore: The City of the Guarded Mouth holds the narrow coast where the chain begins, a ring of walls 150 li across with a garrison of three hundred thousand soldiers and five thousand cultivators, under a commander who has reached Nascent Soul. A ward array caps the harbour mouth, and its bounty office pays for cores by grade. Its markets sell beast parts, smuggled Vast Wilds herbs and frontier saber steel. Every sect with a frontier interest keeps a hall here. At low tide, the reef road appears below the walls.
entries.fromAbove: A ring of sea-cliff walls 150 li across rising out of the surf, faced with beast-king skulls, a ward dome over the harbour mouth and the reef road showing at low tide.

ties.why: The Gate leads our raids across the chain and fills our bounty office with cores.
Our cavalry rides Spirit Herder mounts, and we buy every one they raise.

features.name: the sea-cliff walls, faced with beast-king skulls
the bounty office, paying for cores by grade
the beast-part market
the reef road below the walls at low tide

entries.name: The Frost Mausoleums
entries.summary: The sealed tombs of the dynasty's early princes on a frost-rimed massif 5,400 li across, north of the Jing Capital. Spear-spirits patrol the avenues and kill anyone without a clan token.
entries.lore: The princes were buried with their spears, and the spears woke. Grave robbers still try for the jade armor and spear manuals inside, because one manual can make a family. The frost on the massif never melts, even in summer, and its avenues of stone beasts and spear-stelae run for hundreds of li between the great barrows. The imperial clan is buried here, so trespass is treason, and the guards at the gate are bribable only on Ghost Month nights.
entries.truth: The mausoleum's guardian array runs off the same veins as the palace. Since the drain began, the spear-spirits have been starving, and they have started to wander off the hill.
entries.fromAbove: A frost-white massif with avenues of stone statues running between barrow peaks, rows of spear-shaped stelae and a pale ring of rime that never melts.

ties.why: The imperial clan is buried in us, and we kill whoever comes without its token.

features.name: the avenues of stone beasts and spear-stelae
a barrow gate sealed with spear-array light
the gate guards' lodge

entries.name: Kingdom of Dawnlight
entries.summary: A far eastern kingdom nine thousand li of golden coast, whose royal house is older than the Jing and keeps the crown it was forbidden to wear.
entries.lore: Dawnlight's queen is a Foundation cultivator of the Yu family, which ruled the whole east before the conquest. Each morning at sunrise the court bows to the sea, an old rite the Jing banned and the Yus never stopped; beacon-pillars along the coast light at the same moment, one after another, down the length of the kingdom. Children here learn that the Jing are a passing weather and that the first light of the world touches their beaches. The queen leads the Dawn League and is quietly buying spears by the shipload.
entries.fromAbove: A long golden shoreline with a white palace-terrace on its headland, beacon-pillars strung down the coast, and green fields in the river valleys behind.

ties.why: Our queen leads the League, and our treasury pays for its spears.
The Jing banned our sunrise rite and we never stopped keeping it.

features.name: the court's sunrise terrace on the headland
the beaches where the first light lands
a coastal beacon-pillar

entries.name: The North Wind
entries.summary: A windswept loess plateau 91,000 li across in the Morning Star Continent's northwest, cut by the Snow River's gorge. Cave-home counties, imperial horse pastures and the oldest battlefield on the continent.
entries.lore: Dust storms come off the plateau every spring, walls of yellow a thousand li wide, and bury whole counties; its people live in cave homes cut into the yellow cliffs. The empire breeds its spirit horses here, the [[Snow River]] carries meltwater and sword-steel silt to a cold delta, and the Morning Star Continent's largest battlefield from the [[Hundred Sects War]] lies unburied on the high plain, where it has been haunted for twelve thousand years. Ghost cultivators keep the dead in place for a fee the empire pays reluctantly. Millet still grows, but the plateau's springs are sinking.
entries.truth: The ghosts on the battlefield have started marching in formation toward the coast every Ghost Month, as if called to a wall.
entries.fromAbove: A yellow plateau cut into terraces and cave-cliffs, the Snow River's black gorge slicing across it, brown dust-storm walls rolling over the high plain and, far off, a grey battlefield pale with bone.

ties.why: We send the Sword Domain horses and iron sand, and drink the Snow River its glaciers feed.

top.note: the Soul-Calling Sect's master, there for the battlefield's dead; the ghost generals of the Ten Thousand Graves

entries.name: The Dawn League
entries.summary: A secret alliance of eastern kings and cultivator houses sworn to break the east away from the Great Jing Dynasty, a million strong from clerks and couriers to a Nascent Soul on its council.
entries.lore: The League began as a drinking society of eastern princes and is now a conspiracy with treasury, couriers and a Nascent Soul elder on its council. It hides rooted children from the Registry, runs salt to fund itself and recruits cultivators with grudges against the empire. Members know each other by a rising-sun token cut in half. Its plan needs the passes, a navy and a reason; the famine levy may provide the reason.
entries.fromAbove: Nothing a map would show: courier roads running down the coast, counting-houses behind the salt warehouses, and beacon-fires lit on the kings' hills at the new moon.

ties.why: The city's merchant houses are our purse; we keep the governor's eyes off their books.
Our gifts sit in the Lis' vaults, and we have never been told no.
Dawnlight's crown is the League's banner and its queen leads our council.
The Night Banquet has offered us help, and the price is the passes. The elder council is about to say yes.
We mean to break the east away from the dynasty.
The salt lords' smugglers move our untaxed salt, and the silver it fetches pays for spears.

features.name: a counting-house behind the salt warehouses
a king's hill where beacons burn at the new moon
a courier relay-inn

entries.name: Kingdom of Pine Shade
entries.summary: A forest kingdom twelve thousand li across of loggers and charcoal burners under the Snow Blade Ridge, whose thunder-struck pines are worth more than gold to puppeteers.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Pine Shade's king is a logging boss's grandson with a crown from the Jing court and a debt to the Jiao puppet clan. Lightning-struck pine sells for its weight in silver, so logging crews go out in storms on purpose, and the kingdom buries a few thousand every season. Children grow up in the smell of pitch and learn to climb before they walk. Thunder-wolves den in the burned groves, and their pelts hold a static charge for years.
entries.fromAbove: A dark storm-pine forest rolling to the horizon under the white teeth of Snow Blade Ridge, long scars of felling and charcoal smoke along the river valleys, and burnt grey patches where groves have been struck.

ties.why: Every logger who is struck and lives is taken by the sect, and it is the only road up for a logger's son.
The wolf king lets our logging crews into the burned groves for salt and the bodies of poachers.
We owe the Jiao clan for the crown's debts, and every struck pine goes to them at their price.

features.name: a felling camp among the struck pines
the charcoal kilns
storm-pines tall enough to climb above the cloud
the log-sledge road

entries.name: Kingdom of the Grain Plain
entries.summary: The largest vassal of the south: 12,400 li of endless paddies and some 730 million people, a mortal king who owes the throne a quota he cannot meet, and a Registry office he pays to look the other way.
entries.lore: King Hao of the Kingdom of the Grain Plain is a decent mortal with a bad hand: his yields have fallen a third, his quota has not moved, and the auditors arrive in autumn. He has started hiring cultivators to guard secret granaries hollowed into hills and to scare off the Night Banquet's indenture buyers, and he pays in land titles rather than stones. Children here grow up in the paddies, learn to swim before they walk, and know the Registry tester by the color of his robe.
entries.truth: King Hao's court geomancer has found that the soil's qi runs north like water down a drain, and is too frightened to tell him why.
entries.fromAbove: Endless paddies glittering under floodwater in a square grid to the horizon, the royal city a pale smudge of walls and a dike-line along the Flood River.

ties.why: We hire the Gate's young disciples to guard our secret granaries and pay in land titles, since the stones are gone.
Its buyers walk our paddies buying indentures from starving families, and we pay cultivators to turn them back at the border.

features.name: flooded paddies, waist-deep
the hired guards' granary posts
the Registry office the king pays to look away

entries.name: Kingdom of Pool Creek
entries.summary: A lake kingdom of lotus farmers and fishing villages, 8,900 li across and home to 190 million, ruled by the Bai cultivator family from an island palace in its biggest lake.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Pool Creek grows spirit lotus in three hundred lakes, and the seed pods sell to alchemists for a low-grade stone apiece. The Bai family are Foundation cultivators of the Water Dao, with a Core Formation patriarch, who treat the villages as tenants and pick their servants from rooted children before the Registry arrives. The lakes are still healthy, which makes the Kingdom of Pool Creek the envy of the plain and a target. A family of ash-scaled eels has started taking villagers at dusk.
entries.truth: The Bais bribe the Registry with one rooted child in three to keep the other two. They do not choose randomly.
entries.fromAbove: A mirror-country of lake after lake, pink and green with lotus, the Bai island palace a bright fleck in the biggest and causeways ruling lines between.

ties.why: We give the Registry one rooted child in three, chosen by us, to keep the other two.
Our lotus seed pods go to the Returning Spring alchemists at a stone apiece.

features.name: lotus lakes crossed by rafts and punts
the causeway to the Bai island palace
fishing villages on stilts, lit at dusk

entries.name: Kingdom of Surf Rocks
entries.summary: A kingdom of fishing coves and wreckers' counties along 9,000 li of storm coast, ruled by sea lords who light false beacons on bad nights.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Surf Rocks's lords are three mortal families and one Foundation cultivator, Old Ma, who sits on the reef rock and takes a cut of every wreck. Children learn to dive for wreck salvage at eight and to read storms before they can count. The kingdom pays the [[Azure Wave Palace]]'s shark-folk collectors a tenth of its catch, and anyone who takes a sea-clan child in a net is drowned by their neighbors before the sea clans can come for the village.
entries.truth: Old Ma has been luring the Azure Wave Palace's own toll ships onto the reefs, and blaming the storms.
entries.fromAbove: A ragged storm coast of cove after cove under white surf lines, reef-fields breaking the sea a day's flight out, and Old Ma's black rock standing like a tooth on the reef.

ties.why: The Bay of Sunken Ships is our wreckers' wealth, and we kill rival salvagers on sight.
We pay the shark-folk collectors a tenth of our catch and call it fair.

features.name: Old Ma's reef rock
the false beacon fires on the headlands
a wreckers' cove
the reefs a day's flight out

entries.name: Rim-Gazing Cliff
entries.summary: A sheer sea cliff 1,200 li long where, on the clearest winter mornings, a white line shows on the eastern horizon. Scholars call it a mirage; sailors call it the edge of the world.
entries.lore: A Dao stele on the cliff edge, carved by an unknown hand, describes falling water without end. Cultivators of Water and Space come to meditate on it, and pilgrims climb the cliff stairs in their hundreds of thousands each winter. The cliff is also where eastern kings swear oaths, because nothing said facing the Rim can be taken back, or so they say.
entries.truth: The stele's carver was an Ascent Age master who walked out along the falling water, as the old texts claim, and came back. The worn last line tells how.
entries.fromAbove: A long white sea cliff 1,200 li over the surf, one stair-terrace cut into its crown, and in winter a thin white line on the eastern horizon beyond it.

ties.why: The Pavilion's wave-counters watch from our edge and log every morning the line shows.

features.name: the stele on the cliff edge
the sheer drop to the surf
the oath ground facing the Rim

entries.name: Coin Treasure Trading House
entries.summary: The largest merchant house in the southern Morning Star Continent, with branches in Ten Thousand Sails and Shared Roost City. It banks, ships, insures and smuggles, in roughly that order.
entries.lore: The Coin Treasure Trading House issues letters of credit the Heavenly Scale Pavilion will honor, which makes it the second most important bank in the south. It runs fleets to the Thousand Isles and caravans to the frontier, hires appraisers and guards by the hundred thousand and has a standing arrangement with half the pirate lords. Its young masters are cultivators of middling talent and expensive habits.
entries.truth: The Coin Treasure Trading House insures grain ships, then sells their routes to pirates. It profits twice and has done so for forty years.
entries.fromAbove: A district of warehouse-quays 60 li along the shore under a ward dome, the roads of its caravans fanning inland toward the frontier.

ties.why: Gao buys the routes of the grain ships we insure, so we collect twice: the premium, then the wreck.
We keep our biggest quay-quarter at the Sea Gate, and its customs clerks take our papers at a discount.

features.name: the vault-hall where letters of credit are honored
the insurance counter where ship routes are filed
the guards' barracks by the bonded warehouses

entries.name: Kingdom of Copper Ridge
entries.summary: A mining kingdom ten thousand li across, ruled by the Kang family of mine-masters, who own every shaft, every forge and most of its ninety million people.
entries.lore: The Kangs are a Foundation clan of Earth and Metal cultivators who hold the kingdom from the throne by contract: so many barge-trains of copper and spirit iron a year, no questions asked. Every shaft in a country-sized land is theirs. Miners are paid in scrip only Kang shops accept. Children work the sorting tables from seven, and rooted ones are sold to the Blazing Furnace Sect before the Registry hears of them. A cave-in last month buried thirty thousand miners, and the Kangs have not dug.
entries.truth: The cave-in was deliberate. The buried shaft broke into an Ascent Age gallery, and the Kangs wanted no witnesses.
entries.fromAbove: A red country scored with open-cast terraces and shaft-heads in their tens of thousands, pale ore-barge canals running to the rivers, and the smelter smoke of the Kang hall standing over one ridge like a cloud.

ties.why: We sell the sect copper and spirit iron, and any rooted child it asks for before the Registry hears of him.
We hang any miner found with an ore-oath on him and pay scrip for the names.

features.name: the sorting tables at a shaft-head
the sealed shaft of last month's cave-in
a Kang scrip shop
the ore-barge canals

entries.name: Beast-Butcher Gate
entries.summary: A frontier sect of three thousand saber cultivators who raid across the strait for beast cores, on three peaks its founder sheared flat with one cut. Brutal, rich and the beasts' favorite target.
entries.lore: The Beast-Butcher Gate teaches Saber and Slaughter Daos and recruits frontier orphans who have already lost someone to beasts. Disciples earn rank by cores taken. The sect sells cores to the Apricot Grove Valley, hides to the Zhu clan's rivals and meat to anyone, and leads the empire's punitive raids across the island chain. It despises beast tamers as collaborators and half-bloods as vermin.
entries.truth: The sect's Nascent Soul master killed a young Beast Court prince fifty years ago. The prince's mother has finally woken from seclusion.
entries.fromAbove: Three peaks above the karst with their tops sheared flat, the halls on them lit red by the core furnaces, under a blood-red sect array.

ties.why: We raid across the strait for their cores, and their young come back over it for our disciples.
The herders raise beasts for coin and call it taming; we take their mounts at our gates and their riders for collaborators.
Apricot Grove buys every beast core we bring home, at a price we never argue.
We keep a hall in the city and lead its punitive raids down the chain; the bounty office pays us first.

features.name: the drill yard, where rank is counted in cores
the core vault
racks of frontier sabers

entries.name: Ladder-Gazing Coast
entries.summary: The Morning Star Continent's inner coast, 67,000 li of river delta, seawall and drowned shore at the mouth of the Imperial River, where nine billion live under the Ladder Stump's black line across the Shattered Sea. Scavenger fleets sail west from it, astrologers read it, and its elders keep going to the Seal Watch and not coming back.
entries.lore: Everyone on this coast has seen the [[Ladder Stump]] and has an opinion about it. Fishing fleets of ten thousand sails read weather from its shadow, astrologers read fate from its hum, and scavenger crews sail west toward it to dive the drowned valleys of the [[Shattered Sea]], whole ruined provinces of the Ascent Age lying under the water. The coast still has the seawalls of the Outer Demon War, thousands of li of them, kept by families who were told to watch the west and never stop. Lately the Stump hums on nights when the Mirror is not overhead, spatial rifts wash up on the beaches after storms, and elders sent to the [[Seal Watch]] are not coming home.
entries.truth: Those who sit on the beach long enough start to hear the hum as a song. Some fishing villages have been singing along for a year.
entries.fromAbove: A coast of rice deltas and sea-flats under the grey line of the Demon-Warding Dike, the Imperial River fanning into the sea through nine mouths, the red ward dome of Evening Glow at its head and one dark thread on the western horizon where the Stump stands.

entries.name: Kingdom Facing the Peaks
entries.summary: A strait kingdom of six hundred million, ferry cities and fishing coasts along ten thousand li of northern shore, where on some clear mornings a stray floating peak, drifted far out over the strait, stands on the horizon.
entries.lore: The Kingdom Facing the Peaks lives off the four-month strait crossing: ships, pilots, inns and a customs house that taxes both the Clear Heaven Sword Sect and the Floating Peak clans. Its harbor cities are full of Floating Peak exiles, children of the [[Conclave of Nine Clans]] born without their bloodline and sent down to serve, who fled across the water instead. They teach formation basics for a meal and resent everyone. The Kingdom Facing the Peaks children learn to swim in cold water, read the strait currents and spot floating peaks by their shadows.
entries.truth: One exile is not bloodless: his bloodline was sealed at birth by a rival clan. The Conclave has learned of it and wants him back, quietly.
entries.fromAbove: A long northern coast of harbor cities strung along the strait, pilot beacons burning on every headland, ferry lanes laying white lines across dark water, and on clear mornings a floating peak's shadow far out on it.

ties.why: Our customs house taxes the Sword Sect's strait traffic, and we feed its ferries and pilots.
One of our exiles had his bloodline sealed at birth, and the Conclave has learned of him and wants him back quietly.

features.name: the customs house on the harbor mole
the exiles' quarter of the great harbor
the strait ferry lanes
pilots' beacon towers on the headlands

entries.name: City of Evening Glow
entries.summary: The great port at the Imperial River's mouth, a city of thirty million where river barges meet sea junks and scavenger fleets sail west toward the Stump.
entries.lore: Evening Glow handles the heartland's trade with the Shattered Sea islands: grain and iron out, salvage and sea herbs in, across quays that run forty li along the river mouth. Its salvage market is the best place in the Morning Star Continent to buy a broken Ascent Age artifact and the worst place to be sure of what it is. Abyss-Diving Society halls line the waterfront, and Floating Peak exiles sell formation services in its alleys. Sunsets here turn the harbor red behind the Stump's silhouette.
entries.fromAbove: A dome of ward-light over a city 300 li across, canals radiating into the delta behind it and the river mouth thick with white wakes, red at dusk against the Stump's thread.

ties.why: We take the river's grain and iron out to the islands and send salvage and sea herbs up it.
Rift Beach's scavengers bring us coins, driftwood and the odd live thing, and we sell them as fast as they land.
The Society's halls line our waterfront and every salvage deal passes through our market, where we take the fee.
Setting Sun's rice barges are most of our river traffic, and its Registry office sells us the quay passes.
Our harbor masters hire the sect's pilots for every junk and barge crossing the bars.

features.name: the salvage market, where every broken artifact has a story
the Abyss-Diving Society's waterfront halls
the sunset quay facing the Stump
the exiles' formation alleys

entries.name: Plain of Ten Thousand Graves
entries.summary: The high-plain battlefield of the War of a Hundred Sects, never buried, 9,600 li across. Twelve thousand years of ghosts, broken artifacts and spirit-vein scars.
entries.lore: Bones and broken weapons cover the plain under a thin skin of dust, drifted deep enough to bury hills. Ghosts of whole sects still fight their last battles on it, worst in the seventh month. Appraisers and grave-diggers go in for ancient artifacts, manuals and the jade tokens of dead sects, and ghost cultivators go in to harvest yin. Anyone who dies there joins the war.
entries.fromAbove: A grey plain 9,600 li across, pale with bone under the dust, scarred with old vein ruptures like dried riverbeds, and on Ghost Month nights faint armies of light moving across it.

ties.why: The sect pens our dead with banners and harvests our yin, and the empire pays it to keep us from walking south.

features.name: bone drifts burying whole hills
the ghost armies, fighting their battle lines on Ghost Month nights
a spirit-vein scar breathing yin mist
the grave-diggers' camps at the plain's edge

top.note: the strongest of the ghost generals; the dead are not counted

entries.name: Sword-Asking Town
entries.summary: The city of four million at the foot of the Sword Stair, where a hundred thousand hopefuls wait each spring to climb. Swordsmiths, healers and bookmakers live off them.
entries.lore: Every spring the city fills with youths, their families and the people who prey on them, a hundred thousand hopefuls camped on the plain below the Stair. Bookmakers take bets on who will reach which step; healers set bones for those who fall; swordsmiths sell 'Stair-proven' blades. Failed climbers who reached the five-thousandth step are hired as guards across the Morning Star Continent. Sect recruiters from smaller sword schools wait at the bottom with offers for the ones who fail.
entries.fromAbove: A walled city a hundred li across on the plain under the first peak, the Sword Stair a straight pale line rising from its north gate and a vast encampment of spring tents spread over the fields round it.

ties.why: The Sword Stair is the sect's, and every spring's crowd of hopefuls is ours to feed, house and bet on.
Our swordsmiths grind every blade on Blue Stone whetstones.

features.name: the Stair Road, lined with bookmakers' stalls
the healers' halls by the Stair's foot
the swordsmiths' row selling Stair-proven blades
the recruiters' pavilions at the Stair's foot

entries.name: Convict Prefecture
entries.summary: The empire's penal prefecture: forty mining pits, each as wide as a lake, worked by some twenty-five million convicts, failed conscripts and debtors under imperial overseers with whips that cut qi.
entries.lore: A sentence to the Convict Prefecture is a sentence to dig spirit ore until you die or pay, and convict columns walk in from every prefecture of the Jing, months on the road. Overseers are Foundation cultivators with suppression collars for unruly convicts; the warden is a peak Foundation officer who sells early release. Children born in the pits belong to the prefecture. Cultivators who lose a duel to the wrong prince sometimes end up here, which means some of the convicts are dangerous.
entries.truth: The warden has been writing off living convicts as dead and selling them south to the marsh buyers.
entries.fromAbove: Forty pits terraced down like red crater lakes, each ringed by an overseers' array dome and streets of barracks, convict roads converging on a pale seat the size of a city.

ties.why: King Dou's shipments fill our pits with pirates, and three of them are lords' sons recruiting in the dark.
They smuggle our convicts out through the pit walls, and every overseer is paid to catch them.
We dig the throne's ore with the throne's convicts and answer to it for every pit.
Our warden writes off living convicts as dead and sells them south to the marsh buyers.

features.name: the lip of a pit, terraces falling away
the overseers' gallery with its whips and collars
the warden's office, where release is sold
the pit galleries at the bottom

entries.name: New Vein Market
entries.summary: A boomtown of tents and claim stakes around the newly surfaced vein, a year old and already three million strong. Law is whoever holds the hill.
entries.lore: Prospectors, claim-jumpers, refiners, gamblers and imperial surveyors crowd a valley a hundred li across that smokes day and night. Spirit ore changes hands raw at a third of the city price, claims are sold three times over, and the imperial surveyor's stamp costs more than the claim. The Blazing Furnace Sect, the Kangs and two Night Banquet fronts each hold a hill. Good pay for guards, appraisers and anyone who can tell real ore from painted rock.
entries.fromAbove: A smoking valley a hundred li across, white with tents and claim stakes round a raw red wound where the vein broke the surface, four hills each flying a different faction's banner-array.

ties.why: The Furnace says the whole valley lies in sight of its forges, and its claim teams shoot first at our stakes.
Two of our hill-holders are Night Banquet fronts, buying ore, appraisers and a look into the vein.
Miners with no stamp and no questions sell us ore by the sack, and we ask for none.

features.name: rows of tents and claim stakes
the surveyor's stamp office
appraisers' stalls with painted rock on the table
the four faction hills

entries.name: Kingdom of the Setting Sun
entries.summary: The delta kingdom at the mouth of the Imperial River, a billion and more farmers and fishers on rice flats cut by nine river mouths, where every evening the sun sets behind the Stump.
entries.lore: Setting Sun is ruled by King Wen, a mortal scholar and amateur astrologer who pays the [[Heaven-Peeping Abbey]] to interpret his dreams. Its delta rice still yields well enough to feed half the coast, so imperial grain auditors arrive twice a year with fleets of barges and leave with more each time. Children here fish, row and climb the seawall at dusk to watch the Stump take the sun. The Registry office in the capital is one of the most corrupt in the empire and sells exemptions openly.
entries.fromAbove: Rice flats ruled into a green quilt by canal grids, the nine river mouths shining like fingers into the sea and a long pale line of sea-dike along the shore.

ties.why: I pay the Abbey to read my dreams, and it writes me a fortune for every visit of the grain auditors.
Our rice and fish go down the nine mouths to Evening Glow and come back as iron and silver.
Laver's barges bring seaweed to our delta market, and we sell them rice at a price our clerks set.
We pay the River Sect a tithe of rice every harvest, and every spring it holds the flood off our delta.

features.name: the canal-locks of the nine river mouths
the seawall at dusk, where children watch the Stump
the Registry office's exemption counter

entries.name: Society of the Hanging Gourd
entries.summary: Wandering healers, mostly Apricot Grove Valley dropouts, who treat the poor for free and teach medicine to anyone. The valley calls them charlatans and uses them as cheap labor.
entries.lore: Members carry a gourd on a staff and go where the famine and the raids are, a chain of roadside healing camps across the continent. They teach acupuncture, herb lore and the Life Dao at the camps, and their students become village doctors across the Morning Star Continent. The Apricot Grove Valley tolerates them as long as they sell no pills. They know which villages are sick before anyone else does.
entries.truth: The Society's doctors have mapped the blight's spread across three regions. Their map points back to the valley.
entries.fromAbove: Nothing a pilot would notice: a chain of roadside healing camps that glow green at night wherever a famine is.

ties.why: We treat the debt-poor villages of Baicao for free, and their granaries feed us in lean years.
We work the cordon villages for free, sample the spores and carry what we learn to the roadside camps.
We take only what a famine village needs from the ridge, and the valley arrests us and then rehires us as cheap labor.
The valley tolerates us as long as we sell no pills, and sends us the dying it cannot profit from.

features.name: a roadside healing camp
the herb-drying racks at the camp's edge
the teaching tent, where anyone may sit

entries.name: Snow River
entries.summary: The great river of the north, 131,000 li from the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's glaciers past the terraced foothills and through the loess gorges to a cold delta on the inner sea.
entries.lore: Its water is cold enough to numb a mortal in minutes and, swordsmiths swear, carries sword intent from the peaks. The upper river is the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's, the middle river is the empire's, and the delta belongs to whoever is dredging it this season. Gorge barges haul iron sand and millet in fleets of thousands, and the river's ice in winter is a highway for sledge-trains.
entries.fromAbove: A white river 131,000 li long braiding out of the glaciers, cutting a black gorge through the loess and fanning into an ice-grey delta, the Ninefold Bridge a pale thread across it.

ties.why: Yellow Cliffs' millet is half the cargo of our gorge barges.
Its Ruan dredgers raise our iron-sand silt at the delta and sell it on.

features.name: the gorge barge lanes
the winter ice road
the Ninefold Bridge's arches
the iron-sand dredging reaches at the delta

entries.name: Snow Blade Ridge
entries.summary: The snow-covered range, ninety thousand li long, across the Morning Star Continent's north on which Clear Heaven Sword Sect's seventy-two peaks stand. Its passes are guarded and its glaciers feed the Snow River.
entries.lore: Every peak on the ridge has a Clear Heaven Sword Sect hall, a vassal sect or a hermit on it, along ninety thousand li of range. Snow apes and frost cranes nest on the highest slopes, and their cores are prized for Ice and Wind Dao pills. The few passes, each a gorge a day's flight long, are customs posts. The ridge's meltwater is said to carry sword intent, and swordsmiths downstream quench blades in it.
entries.fromAbove: A white range ninety thousand li long, its seventy-two main summits crowned with halls and rings of sword-light, glaciers pouring from its flanks and a few dark gorges cutting through to the south.

ties.why: Our peaks carry the sect's halls and our passes close at its customs posts.
The Zhus cut our glacier's ice and draw our meltwater, and pay our passes' tolls.

features.name: the customs posts in the passes
the hanging glaciers above the gorges
snow-ape and frost-crane nests on the high slopes

top.note: the founding ancestor under the main peak

entries.name: Kingdom of Misty Waves
entries.summary: A cold delta kingdom of 157 million at the Snow River's mouth, 7,900 li across, ruled by the Ruan cultivator family. Its silt is full of iron from the north, and its fog never quite lifts.
entries.lore: Misty Waves dredges iron sand from the delta for forges, fishes the cold inner sea and runs ships north toward the Floating Peak Continent's western coasts. The Ruan family are Foundation cultivators of the Water Dao who sell iron to both the Zhu clan and the Blazing Furnace Sect and play them against each other. Children here dredge, row and know the fog by smell. Sword-steel silt sometimes carries flecks of real sword intent, and finding one can make a family.
entries.fromAbove: A grey delta fanned into a hundred channels under a bank of permanent fog, dredger barges strung along each like beads and a ring of dark iron-sand banks at the sea's edge.

ties.why: We sell iron sand to the Zhus and play them against the Blazing Furnace Sect.
We send our iron sand up the coast through the Cold Ford and hire most of our crews there.
We dredge the Snow River's iron-sand silt and ship it out through the delta.

features.name: the iron-sand dredging flats
fog banks over the delta channels
the Ruan family's counting-houses at the river mouth
the fishing fleets of the cold sea

entries.name: Kingdom of Salt Pans
entries.summary: A kingdom of salt flats and salt lords ten thousand li across on the flat southeastern shore. Imperial salt tax is the law; salt smuggling is the economy.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Salt Pans's pans produce a third of the Morning Star Continent's salt, white flats from horizon to horizon along a shore 9,000 li long, and the empire takes half of it in tax. Salt lords, mortal families with cultivator guards, run the pans and the smuggling both. Spirit salt crystallizes in a few pans after storms and sells to alchemists. Children rake salt barefoot and grow up knowing which patrols can be bribed. A salt lord's son who reaches Qi Condensation is married off to a cultivator house before he can blink.
entries.fromAbove: A white shore of salt flats in their millions of pans, pink and grey in the sun, tide-gates and canals threading through them and barge-roads running out to the sea.

ties.why: Our salt lords guide parties out to the gate cave, and every one pays for a guide.
The League's agents buy our untaxed salt by the barge-load and pay in silver, asking nothing.

features.name: the pan-walks between the flats
a salt lord's pan-house and its guards
the smugglers' creek behind the sea-gates
a spirit-salt pan after a storm

entries.name: Blazing Furnace Sect
entries.summary: A sect of fifteen thousand artifact refiners who forge inside a live volcano. They make the best fire weapons in the Morning Star Continent, and they mean to own the new vein.
entries.lore: The Blazing Furnace Sect teaches the Fire and Metal Daos at the anvil: its forge-halls step down a volcano's flanks in rings, lava channels run through them, and disciples stoke vent-forges for three years before they may strike. The sect takes apprentices with fire roots from any family, sells weapons to anyone and hires out refiners to repair sect treasures. Its rivalry with the Zhu Clan of the Cold Forge is three thousand years old and mostly settled by forging contests, sometimes by murder. Its claim teams, a few hundred disciples each, shoot first at the new vein.
entries.fromAbove: A volcano ringed by forge-halls stepped down its flanks, lava channels glowing through them in rings, a smoke column standing over it and a red sect array flickering at its mouth.

ties.why: We harvest fire essence from the valley's vent lips for Fire Dao breakthroughs, and sell it at mid-grade stones.
We buy the Kangs' copper and spirit iron, and the rooted children they send us before the Registry hears.
Our claim teams hold the new vein's valley, which lies in sight of our forges, and no market comes between us and it.
Our claim teams hold the new vein, and the dynasty says every new vein is the throne's.
The Zhu Clan of the Cold Forge has matched us anvil for anvil for three thousand years, in contests and sometimes in murders.

features.name: the vent-forges, where disciples stoke for three years
the lava channels between the halls
the contest anvil, where rivals settle disputes
the claim team's camp at the new vein

entries.name: The Medicine Ridges
entries.summary: Green hills on the Morning Star Continent's western side, 64,000 li across, terraced to their summits around Apricot Grove Valley: herb ranges, apricot forests and kingdoms that owe the valley everything, including their debts. Five billion live under its sway.
entries.lore: These hills belong to whoever buys their herbs, and the [[Apricot Grove Valley]] buys them all. Tenant kingdoms grow herbs on the Apricot Grove Valley contracts, whole mountain ranges terraced to the summit, rival gardens wither under blight nobody can explain, and patients arrive from every corner of the Morning Star Continent, and from beyond it: beast emissaries in human shape come up from the strait for medicine, under the Apricot Grove Valley's protection. The empire blames the famine on the Apricot Grove Valley's blight and the valley denies it, and both are partly right. Herb thieves, alchemists and sick people all come here, and the valley profits from each.
entries.truth: The blight the Apricot Grove Valley seeds in rival gardens has started jumping to its own tenants' fields, and the valley's healers cannot cure what their elders made.
entries.fromAbove: Green hill ranges terraced to the summits, a dark sea of apricot forest a thousand li across at the valley's heart, Jade Screen Ridge a long green wall with its cloud to the west and a black stain spreading in the east.

top.note: the Valley Master, by rumor older than the trees

entries.name: Night Bridge Society
entries.summary: Half-blood smugglers who run the island chain in relays, one crew to a stretch, passing people, Gu eggs, beast cubs and herbs from island to island at low tide between the Morning Star Continent and Shared Roost City.
entries.lore: The Society knows the tides, the reefs and which islands have something living on them this month. Most of its runners are Qi Condensation or Foundation half-bloods who know one stretch by heart, and each crew waits on its own tide, so a cargo takes about half a year to pass end to end; only the Core Formation leaders fly the whole chain, in about a month. It runs half-bloods out of human villages, beast eggs to the Kingdom of Spirit Herders's ranches, Gu to the marsh and Vast Wilds herbs to anyone. Its leaders are half-bloods with beast senses and long grudges. It pays tribute to nobody and has informers in every fort. Passage costs five low-grade stones, or a favor.
entries.fromAbove: Nothing they would let you see: sea caves along the chain, and lantern lights moving island to island at low tide.

ties.why: The ranches pay well for every egg and cub we carry over at low tide.
Everything we run along the chain ends at Shared Roost, the only market that takes it all.
The cave clans guide our cargo through caves no map shows, for a share and no questions.
We hold the cave where the gate opens and charge every blood that goes in.
The marsh Stockade buys every Gu egg we run, and pays without haggling.

features.name: a tide pool island on the chain
the low-tide reef between islands
a smugglers' sea cave

entries.name: Thunder-Drawing Sect
entries.summary: A lightning sect of ten thousand on the highest sea cliff, whose disciples draw thunderbolts into their bodies to temper them. One in five does not survive the first year.
entries.lore: The Thunder-Drawing Sect recruits from storm survivors: anyone struck by lightning and still alive gets an invitation. Its method tempers meridians with lightning, fast and brutal, and its disciples reach Foundation years ahead of most sects; hundreds of rod-spires crown the cliff to feed them. It sells lightning-charged talisman ink, trains tribulation survival for a fee and treats the Clear Heaven Sword Sect as an old rival. Its Nascent Soul master has not left the cliff in ten years.
entries.truth: The master can hear a voice in the storms from the east. He believes it is his Dao calling him to the Rim.
entries.fromAbove: A sea cliff higher than any around it, crowned with a forest of lightning-rod spires, storm cloud stacked over it and bolts walking down the spires into pale halls cut into the rock.

ties.why: We send an invitation to every logger in Pine Shade who is struck by lightning and lives.
We own the Terrace of Nine Thunders and take a toll from every cultivator who sits between the points.
We have been the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's old rival since before either of us kept a ledger.

features.name: the rod-spires that draw the bolts
the tempering halls cut into the cliff
the recruit yard, where survivors are counted

entries.name: The Imperial River
entries.summary: The great river of the heartland, 190,000 li long and eight li wide at the capital, from the Turtle-Spine Mountains west past the walls of the Jing Capital to the delta at Evening Glow on the inner sea.
entries.lore: Half of the Morning Star Continent's trade rides the Imperial River, and the Grand Canal joins it at the Grain-Barge Mouth to carry the south's grain to the capital. Imperial toll stations every thousand li tax barges, and the river guard is a posting for princes' sons. Spirit carp in its middle reaches leap the Jing Capital weir, a dam as tall as a hill, each spring, and catching one is a festival. This year the water runs low and warm past the capital, and the carp have not come.
entries.truth: The river's qi drops sharply as it passes the Jing Capital and recovers a hundred li downstream. Fishermen have noticed; officials have not written it down.
entries.fromAbove: A river eight li wide shining across the plain in great bends, barge convoys a white thread along it and the capital weir a pale bar across it.

ties.why: The Grand Canal pours the south's grain into us here, and the Mouth's quays load our convoys.
Our barges carry the heartland's grain and iron down to Evening Glow, and the river guard taxes every thousand li of it.

features.name: the capital weir, a hill-high dam the carp leap each spring
the toll stations on the banks
the river guard's patrol boats

entries.name: Imperial Grain Prefecture
entries.summary: The palace's private spirit-rice county, 9,700 li of terraces around a low-grade vein: 1.8 billion serfs of the Imperial Household, whose harvest has fallen by a tenth each season for three years.
entries.lore: The Imperial Grain Prefecture grows Jade Pearl rice for the palace kitchens, and its farmers are serfs of the Imperial Household. The Lu family, spirit farmers of Foundation Establishment with a Core Formation patriarch, has run it for nine generations and is now being audited for the shortfall. Rumor says the Lus will hang a village headman to satisfy the auditors. Anyone who can make the paddies yield again, or find out why they will not, will have the Household's ear.
entries.truth: The vein under the Imperial Grain Prefecture is a capillary of the Jing Capital veins. It is not failing. It is being pulled.
entries.fromAbove: Green-gold rice terraces stepping up a whole county in contour rings, a low vein's pale glow at the center and a ring of paddies at its edge gone gray.

ties.why: Our Jade Pearl rice goes to the palace kitchens, and we are audited for every shortfall.

features.name: rice terraces stepping up the hillsides
the vein-head, where the Lus draw water by array
the audit hall, where the Household's auditors sit

entries.name: Kingdom of Cloud Stockades
entries.summary: Forty stockaded seats in high valleys under the peaks, each ruling a county the size of a country, twelve million people in all under a council of elders and visited by the outside world once a season. The backwater every hero claims to come from.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Cloud Stockades has no king, no roads a cart can use and no Registry office; the testers come once every few years if the passes are open. Its people herd goats, gather wild herbs and hunt cloud-leopards with crossbows across valleys that take weeks to cross. Every nine years the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's recruiters make their circuit, a season's walk from seat to seat, and every child dreams of the Sword Stair. The elders keep a cave of old manuals left by a cultivator who died here, and nobody in the valleys can read the script.
entries.truth: The manuals are a Dim Age Wind Dao method, complete through Core Formation.
entries.fromAbove: High valleys above a floor of cloud, forty stockade rings pale on their terraces and thread-thin trails strung between them.

ties.why: The Gang's guides pay iron and salt to cross our valleys, and some of our own children go with them.

features.name: stockaded seats with crossbow platforms
the cave of old manuals
the cloud-leopard grounds above the cloud floor
pass-trails that close with the snow

entries.name: Soul-Calling Sect
entries.summary: Ghost cultivators of some thirty thousand who keep the dead of the old battlefield in place, sell seances to the bereaved and raise ghost soldiers for anyone who pays.
entries.lore: The sect has lived at the battlefield's edge for four thousand years, cultivating yin from its ghosts and keeping them penned with a line of banners nine thousand li long. The empire pays it to stop the dead from walking south, and orthodox sects hold their noses and let it. It teaches the Ghost and Death Daos, talks to the dead for a fee and recruits children who see things others don't. Its strength peaks in the seventh month.
entries.truth: The sect's banners can no longer turn the dead. They are being pulled toward the coast by something stronger, and the sect is pretending it planned the marches.
entries.fromAbove: A line of tall black banners, each a pillar of grey binding light, strung 9,000 li along the battlefield's edge like a wall, with the sect's halls under a dark-grey array dome at its middle.

ties.why: We keep a hall at the Cold Ford where the bereaved speak to the drowned, and it pays well.
We pen the plain's dead with banners and harvest their yin, and the empire pays us for it.
Our banners can no longer turn the old sects' dead; every Ghost Month they march toward the coast, toward your wall, and we say we sent them.

features.name: the banner line, pennants of binding light
the seance halls
the yin-harvesting pits
the ghost soldiers' barracks

entries.name: Northern Garrison Prefecture
entries.summary: A military prefecture of the empire at the foot of the hills, 8,800 li across and garrisoned by a million and a half conscripted soldiers, run by a general who hates the Clear Heaven Sword Sect.
entries.lore: The Northern Garrison Prefecture exists to stop the flow of rooted children uphill. General Yan Ku, a Core Formation spear cultivator who failed the Sword Stair as a boy, commands a million and a half soldiers, strung along the hills' foot in fortress after fortress, and the Registry's northern office. Families here serve in the garrison by law, and children learn drill before letters. The general pays well for smugglers' heads and better for proof that a Clear Heaven Sword Sect disciple took a registered child.
