entries.fromAbove: A belt of foothill fortresses strung along the hills' foot, each under its own pale array dome, drill plains between them and signal-smoke columns rising along the pass roads.

ties.why: We hunt every Sword Sect recruiter who takes a registered child, and pay for proof of it.
We take the lower terraces' rice tax to feed the garrison, and it comes in short.
We hang the Gang's guides and pay well for the heads of the rest.
We house the Registry's northern office and make its slips hold at the passes.
We buy exploding talismans for the garrison by the thousand.

features.name: the spear-wall forts across the passes
the Registry's northern office
the gibbets along the pass roads
the drill yards of a garrison city

entries.name: Sea-Calming Pagoda
entries.summary: A nine-tiered lighthouse pagoda rising a li above the southern cape, whose array calms storms for three hundred li around its lamp. It burns a spirit stone every night.
entries.lore: The pagoda was built with the Armillary Pavilion's help two thousand years ago, and its array still holds a circle of calm water three hundred li across around the cape, the lamp seen from the sea a hundred li out. Formation masters study it from outside; only imperial engineers may enter. When the stones run late, wrecks follow. The keeper's office now spends more on stones than it gets, and the pagoda has gone dark twice this year.
entries.fromAbove: A column of white lamp-light standing out of the southern cape, a ring of glassy calm water 300 li across around it in the surf.

ties.why: The pagoda is owed a stone from every hull that docks here, and the treasury sends it up the chain slower each year while our docks lose ships to the dark.
The fleet sails in my calm water and sends marines to the cape when my lamp goes dark.

features.name: the lamp room, where a spirit stone burns each night
the keeper's office and its stone ledger
the ring of calm water below the cape

entries.name: Kingdom of Lingzhi Gardens
entries.summary: Once the richest herb gardens outside the Apricot Grove Valley's control, now a kingdom of forty million among dead terraces and angry people. Its lingzhi caves went black in a single summer.
entries.lore: Lingzhi Gardens grew mushrooms for the Cinnabar Hill Sect for eight hundred years and refused every offer the Apricot Grove Valley made. Ten years ago a black rot took the caves, then the terraces, and it has crept across a thousand li since. The king sold his crown jewels to buy cures that did not work. Children here grow up poor and hating the valley, and the youths who can fight hire on as herb thieves.
entries.truth: The Apricot Grove Valley's blight was carried into the caves by a gardener the valley bought. He still works for the king.
entries.fromAbove: Terraced hills going from green to grey to black from west to east, a pale cordon drawn across them and the dark mouths of the lingzhi caves.

ties.why: Our youths hire on as herb thieves, and the black lingzhi they bring out pays the king's debts.
We sold the Hill every lingzhi for eight hundred years and refused the valley; now we have none to sell and the Hill still pays.
The valley bought every herb market but ours, and when the rot came it sold us the cure that did not work.

features.name: the dead terraces
the blackened lingzhi caves
the burned fields of the cordon line

entries.name: Vermilion Talisman Sect
entries.summary: A talisman sect on a cinnabar peak above the terraces. It mines its own ink, recruits farm children and sells talismans to the empire and the Clear Heaven Sword Sect alike.
entries.lore: The Vermilion Talisman Sect disciples learn calligraphy before cultivation and spend their first three years grinding cinnabar from a peak mined red for thousands of years. The sect teaches the Fire and Lightning Daos through talisman script, and its exploding talismans are standard issue in the imperial army. It is a Clear Heaven Sword Sect vassal on paper and a supplier to everyone in practice. Its outer disciples sell seconds in Boundary Head Town at a third of the price, some of which work.
entries.truth: The Vermilion Talisman Sect's cinnabar seam runs into the root of the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's main peak. The miners have started hearing a sword hum in the rock, very faintly.
entries.fromAbove: A peak stained red from foot to crown, cinnabar galleries cut into it in terraces, drying-yards of vermilion paper on its shoulders and a rust-colored sect array over the summit.

ties.why: We are the Sword Sect's vassal on paper and a supplier to everyone in practice.
Our outer disciples sell seconds at Boundary Head for a few low-grade stones.
The garrison prefecture is our best buyer of exploding talismans.

features.name: the cinnabar galleries cut into the peak
the grinding halls
the drying-yards of talisman paper
the outer disciples' stalls at the gate

entries.name: The Pearl Shore
entries.summary: A coast of headlands, coves and pearl shoals 63,000 li long, facing the Thousand Isles and the sea clans' waters, where two billion live behind fortress walls. Pirates raid it, pearl divers work it and every county seat is a fort.
entries.lore: The Pearl Shore looks south and east toward the [[Azure Wave Palace]]'s waters and the [[Thousand Isles]], and both look back. Pirate fleets raid for slaves and grain, shark-folk collectors take toll on every catch, and pearl divers bring up spirit pearls that pay for both. Imperial pirate-hunters collect bounties and bribes in equal measure. Half-bloods with sea-clan blood live quietly in the coves, and the marsh's black markets begin at its western edge.
entries.truth: A jiao of the Azure Wave Palace's court nests its young in a sea cave off this coast. If one is ever taken, the sea clans will come ashore.
entries.fromAbove: Dark headlands cut by pale coves, warm turquoise pearl shoals glowing in the shallows, fortress-cities strung along the coast under their domes and the sea-caves of the Jiao Nest a cluster of dark mouths in the eastern cliffs.

entries.name: Kingdom of Laver
entries.summary: A tide-flat kingdom of twenty million seaweed farmers so poor the Registry rarely bothers testing them. They have watched the Stump every night for a thousand years.
entries.lore: Laver's people farm seaweed on ropes across the flats, thousands of li of them from the sea-dike out to the tide line, and dry it on their roofs. There is no king, only a Tide Warden elected by the villages. They keep a shrine facing the Stump in every county and leave a bowl of rice for it every new moon. A Qi Condensation hedge cultivator is the strongest person in the kingdom, and outsiders come only to buy laver or hide.
entries.truth: The villagers have started humming a tune nobody taught them, all at the same hour of the night.
entries.fromAbove: Brown-silver tide flats combed into lines by rope-farms for thousands of li, the sea-dike a thin green seam behind them.

ties.why: The Abbey takes our orphans with good eyes as novices, and their priest rides in each new moon to read our shrine.
We trade seaweed for rice at the delta market, and pay the clerks to look away from our rooted children.

features.name: rope-farms across the tide flats
the shrine facing the Stump, with its new-moon bowl of rice
laver drying on the roofs

entries.name: Spirit Beasts
entries.summary: Beasts that woke to qi. They grow slowly, live long, and from Nascent Soul on can take human form.
entries.lore: A beast's core holds its cultivation, so humans hunt beasts for cores and beasts hunt humans for revenge. They rule the Vast Wilds Continent and the deep places of every continent.

entries.name: Ghosts
entries.summary: Souls that never moved on. Most are mindless; the old ones of the Long Dusk Continent keep courts, laws and grudges older than any sect.
entries.lore: Ghosts grow by gathering yin and resentment. A ghost that keeps its mind for a thousand years becomes a power; the Pale Sovereign has kept hers for sixty-six thousand.

entries.name: Half-bloods
entries.summary: Children of humans and spirit beasts or sea clans. Strong bloodlines and no home.
entries.lore: Humans call them beasts and beasts call them human. Most hide what they are; the rest live in Shared Roost City or die young.

entries.name: Humans
entries.summary: The most numerous race and the most divided. Most cultivators are human, and so are most of their victims.
entries.lore: Humans hold the Morning Star Continent, the Floating Peak Continent and the Myriad Sands Continent outright and cling to the edges of the other three continents. They live short lives and make up for it in numbers and ambition.

entries.name: Outer Demons
entries.summary: Predators from the Void Sea that possess, devour and corrupt. Every child is told they are gone.
entries.lore: They came through Heaven's Scar twice. Survivors describe them as hunger with a shape, and say the worst ones speak in your own voice.
entries.truth: They are not gone. A few slipped out during the war and wear human faces. The Void Choir hears the rest singing through the seal.

entries.name: Spirit Plants
entries.summary: Herbs and trees that woke. Most are prey for alchemists; the ones in the Evergreen Deep fight back.
entries.lore: An old enough spirit herb grows legs and runs. An old enough tree grows a mind and holds a grudge for centuries.

entries.name: Sea Clans
entries.summary: Jiao flood dragons, shark-folk, turtle sages and the things of the deep trenches. They hold the Shoreless Sea.
entries.lore: The sea clans were here before the land, or so they say. Every ship on the outer ocean sails by the Azure Wave Palace's leave, and every human port pays toll in one form or another.

entries.name: Safe Passage Stockade
entries.summary: The richest pirate lordship in the isles, whose sixty sails raid as far as the Floating Peak Continent and have not lost a hull to the sea in forty years.
entries.lore: The Safe Passage lord is a Nascent Soul water cultivator with flawless manners. His islands are paved, his mortals are fed, and his captains' children are tutored in three scripts. Other lords call him lucky. He funds the League's treasury and votes for whatever keeps the League from looking too closely at anything.
entries.truth: He is the Sea Sovereign's chief tributary in the League, and his ships are how the [[Azure Wave Palace]] means to carry the dragon pearl home once someone steals it from the [[Floating Peak Continent]].

entries.name: Tomb of a Hundred Ships
entries.summary: A lagoon where the pirates sink the ships they cannot sell. Hulls lie twenty deep, and the oldest are warships from the Outer Demon War with cargo nobody bothered to take.
entries.lore: Scavengers may dive for a fee paid to the queen's clerks. The upper hulls are stripped; the lower ones hold sealed holds, drowned crews and the occasional ghost that wants its cargo delivered. An appraiser can make a career here learning the ship-marks of every navy and sect in the world. The water is so thick with rotting spirit wood that it glows faint green at night.
entries.truth: The bottom hull is a supply ship of the Scar's defenders, sunk in the Outer Demon War. Its hold is still sealed, and it still hums.

entries.name: White Scale Barrier
entries.summary: The sea clans' toll post on the Toll Line: a ring of coral towers round a lagoon, where every ship bound past the Morning Star Continent's outer coast stops to pay.
entries.lore: A turtle clerk assesses toll by the cargo's weight and the crew's cultivation; a Foundation passenger costs more than a hold of rice. Payment is in spirit stones, pearls or service. Ships that pay fly a white scale pennant and are left alone as far as the [[Rim]] mist. The post is commanded by a white jiao, the Sovereign's grand-nephew, who is bored, ambitious and known to start fights for entertainment.
entries.truth: The white jiao wants a war to make his name. He pays poachers to raid his own nursery reefs so he can blame Jing fishermen.

entries.name: White Fang Stockade
entries.summary: A pirate lordship of beast-raiders on a ring of jungle islands. Its lord pays bounties for cores by grade and sells cubs to tamers by the cage.
entries.lore: The White Fang lord is a Core Formation saber cultivator who took the title by killing a Beast Court envoy, and his hall is roofed with the envoy's hide. His islands are a frontier town of raiders, tanners, core-cutters and tamers' agents; children learn to skin before they can swim and to grade a core by its smell. Mortal fishing villages tithe to him for protection, which mostly means the beasts come for him first.
entries.truth: He survives by selling the Beast Court the camps of rival raiders.

entries.name: Raider Isles
entries.summary: The western isles nearest the Vast Wilds Continent, where pirate crews raid beast lairs on the jungle coast for cores and cubs, and the Beast Court raids them back.
entries.lore: A fast ship reaches the [[Vast Wilds Continent]]'s coast from here in two days. Raiders slip up estuaries, take cores, eggs and cubs, and sell them in the isles to tamers and alchemists from every continent. The [[Beast Court of Ten Thousand Mountains]] answers with flights of storm birds, the odd sea serpent, and every few decades something much worse. Half-blood crews from [[Shared Roost City]] sign on as trackers, because they can smell a lair and pass for either side.
entries.truth: The Beast Court's Storm Roc lets the raiders operate. Nearly every cub they take comes from the White Ape King's lineages.

entries.name: Marker-Stone Town
entries.summary: The isles' claims town, where scavenger sects register their stakes, sell salvage and settle disputes in a duel ring paved with Ascent Age flagstones.
entries.lore: A claim is a carved marker stone and a line in the registry; the registrars are neutral, underpaid and bribed by everyone. Disputes go to the ring: one champion a side, below Core Formation, to first blood or worse. The market sells talisman fragments, bronze, old jade slips and sifted beach sand by the sack, which now and then holds a spirit stone. Sects scout the ring for fighters.

entries.name: Ice Bridge Sea
entries.summary: The cold strait between the Floating Peak Continent and the Black Frost Continent. In hard winters it freezes from shore to shore, and the Iron Bone khans ride across.
entries.lore: In summer it is a lane of icebergs and fog, worked by sealers and by the [[Eternal Night Palace]] raiders who wait in the fog for the Floating Peak Continent's grain ships. In winters cold enough an ice bridge forms, and the [[Iron Bone Tribes]] have crossed it four times in recorded history to raid the Floating Peak Continent's lowlands. The Floating Peak Continent's lowland lords keep fire arrays along the shore to break the ice, and the tribes' shamans curse them for it.
entries.truth: The last two winters came within days of a full bridge, and the tribes are choosing a Great Khan.

entries.name: The Ice Stair
entries.summary: Where the polar sea pours over the Rim and freezes on the way down: terraces of ice a thousand li wide descending into the void. Things climb it.
entries.lore: Sailors who reach the mist see blue terraces going down into darkness, lit from below by something that is not the sun. Ice from the lower steps never melts and is prized for Ice Dao weapons; a sliver sells for a high-grade stone. Every expedition to cut it has lost people to the cold, the fall, or the shapes seen moving on the lower steps. The Black Frost Continent's shamans call it the back door and will not sail within sight of it.
entries.truth: Outer demons climb it whenever the tide runs high. Most freeze on the upper steps. The ones that don't come ashore wearing whalers' faces.

entries.name: Market of Water-Parting Beads
entries.summary: A stilt town over the shallowest valley, where divers rent water-parting beads by the hour, sell what they bring up and drink away what they don't.
entries.lore: A bead wraps a diver in air and a ward against the deep: a Low-grade bead lasts an hour at fifty fathoms, a High-grade one a day at three hundred. The bead-makers here are the best water-art refiners in the Shattered Sea and kill to keep their recipes. Appraisers grade salvage on the dock before it dries, and grade it low. The Gate of Sinking and Rising collects one part in five of everything landed, and the [[Corpse-Diver School]] undercuts everyone from the next island over.

entries.name: Hall of Array Mending
entries.summary: The formation masters who maintain the seal's outer arrays under contract to the Seal Watch. They take apprentices from any sect, and few apprentices ever go home.
entries.lore: The Hall teaches formations the hard way: apprentices redraw seal script on the forts' outer walls while the walls are live, and a wrong stroke burns off fingers. It examines candidates every spring in the [[Harbor of the Changing Watch]]; anyone with a steady hand and a Qi Condensation base may sit. Its graduates are the best seal-script masters alive. The [[Armillary Pavilion]] has tried for three thousand years to buy the Hall's methods and been refused every time; the Hall's masters call the Armillary Pavilion's arrays toll booths.
entries.truth: The Hall's master has worked out that the outer arrays now carry load meant for the center. He told the Warden, and the Warden ordered him to tell no one else.

entries.name: Reef of Broken Jade
entries.summary: A slab of the fallen span nine li long, jutting from the sea along the fall line. Its halls are flooded, its jade is immortal, and two courts say its dead belong to them.
entries.lore: Immortal jade cannot be cut by anything below Nascent Soul, so scavengers work the cracks and sell the dust to refiners at a mid-grade stone a jin. Inside are flooded halls whose bodies have not rotted. The [[Court of No Light]] sends ghost clerks to register each corpse; the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] sends crews to steal them. Whoever is caught by the other side is added to the count.
entries.truth: One sealed hall still answers to Upper Realm tokens, like parts of the [[Fallen Ladder]], and last winter it opened briefly for someone.

entries.name: Tide Gate Strait
entries.summary: The strait between the Morning Star Continent and the Floating Peak Continent, where the tide pours between the inner and outer seas twice a day like a river in flood.
entries.lore: Tidal races here can roll a ship end over end, and the safe hours are posted in every harbor on both coasts. The [[Conclave of Nine Clans]] keeps a chained floating rock over the narrows and charges ships for passing beneath it; the [[Great Jing Dynasty]] calls that piracy and sends warships through at the wrong hour to prove it. It is also the shortest sea road from the [[Azure Wave Palace]]'s waters to the Floating Peaks, and both coasts have begun counting sea-clan scouts.

entries.name: Pavilion of the Rising Tide
entries.summary: The largest sect of the central isles: water and storm cultivators who teach tide-reading, sell escort fleets and sit on the League council.
entries.lore: The Pavilion of the Rising Tide teaches the Water and Wind Daos through the tides: disciples meditate in the surf and rise a rank for every tide-race won against the current. Its escorts guard convoys through the isles for a twentieth of the cargo, and a convoy that declines is usually robbed within the week. It recruits at the Kingdom of Hazy Waters auctions and pays the best prices for spirit-root children. Its patriarch hates the [[Raider Isles]] raiders for drawing the Beast Court's anger onto the isles.
entries.truth: The patriarch pays the [[Azure Wave Palace]] for his escort routes, which is why his convoys never lose a hull to sea beasts.

entries.name: Sea of Sunken Valleys
entries.summary: Clear water over the drowned valleys of the old central continent. Ascent Age towns lie intact on the bottom, and divers from every continent come to loot them.
entries.lore: The valleys sank whole when the central continent broke, so halls, gardens and treasuries sit under fifty to three hundred fathoms of clear water. Divers buy water-parting beads in the [[Market of Water-Parting Beads]] and go down on the bead's clock: when it dims, you rise or drown. The shallows were stripped ten thousand years ago; the rich ruins, like the furnaces of the [[Valley of the Pill Furnaces]], are deep, sealed and still guarded by Ascent Age arrays. The [[Gate of Sinking and Rising]] sells the licenses, and most of what comes up goes to the [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] buyers bound for [[Fallen Star City]].
entries.truth: The Heavenly Scale Pavilion buyers on the docks fix salvage prices together, and the Pavilion holds the notes on half the bead-makers in the Market of Water-Parting Beads.

entries.name: Whale-Spear Gate
entries.summary: A sect of whale hunters who cultivate the Spear Dao on the ice. A disciple's rank is the size of the largest whale they have helped kill.
entries.lore: The Whale-Spear Gate teaches the Spear and Ice Daos and a cold-blooded body art for working wet in winter wind. Disciples hunt from floes with harpoons tempered in whale blood and sell cores to refiners at the [[Frost Fair]]. It recruits whaling children by the throw: put an iron harpoon through a seal's skull at forty paces and you are in. It is at war with the whale-riding sea clans, who sink its boats, and pays the [[Eternal Night Palace]] to be left alone on land.
entries.truth: Its elders have seen what climbs the [[Ice Stair]]. They chip the frozen ones out of the upper steps and sell them to the [[Eternal Night Palace]], which wants an outer demon's cultivation method.

entries.name: Harbor of Waiting Winds
entries.summary: The harbor on the storm belt's eastern edge where ships wait, sometimes for months, for the lull. A city of gamblers, weather-readers and captains going broke.
entries.lore: Diviners sell forecasts of the next lull by the hour, and the good ones are richer than the captains. Betting houses take wagers on which ships come out the far side. Cargo spoils, crews desert, and moneylenders buy holds cheap from desperate captains. Divination students apprentice with the forecasters, who test them by asking for the next lull's hour; three wrong answers and you are sent home.
entries.truth: The best forecaster in the harbor does not read the sky. She bribes an elder of the [[Abbey of Drawn Lightning]], whose rods feel the drum in the eye before every lull.

entries.name: Realm of the Pill Scriptures
entries.summary: The drowned alchemy sect's library shard. Its gate on the valley's lowest terrace opens for ten days every twenty-four years, only to those below Nascent Soul carrying a lit furnace.
entries.lore: The Armillary Pavilion's tables list the date; the condition is not in the tables. The gate admits only cultivators holding a pill furnace with a live fire in it, so alchemists hire divers to escort them down and keep the furnace dry in a bubble ward. Inside is a dry library of jade slips on fire control and formulas lost since the Severance, kept by furnace golems that test visitors by making them refine. Bad pills are punished. A Nascent Soul aura cracks the gate. The next opening is five years off.
entries.truth: The golems copy what visitors refine. The library has been learning the Sealed Era's alchemy for three thousand years, and some of its newer slips are better than anything outside.

entries.name: Valley of the Pill Furnaces
entries.summary: A drowned valley lined with the pill furnaces of an Ascent Age alchemy sect. Sixty-six thousand years underwater, some of them are still warm.
entries.lore: Over two hundred furnaces stand on stone terraces at ninety fathoms. The cold ones were looted down to the bricks; the warm ones are sealed, and divers who pry at them come up boiled. Ash scraped from their outer walls steadies a pill's fire and sells for its weight in low-grade stones. The [[Apricot Grove Valley]] alchemists pay divers to bring the ash up and, quietly, to report on the seals.
entries.truth: The warm furnaces are still refining. They have tended the same batch since the Severance, and it is nearly done.

entries.name: Town of Fixed Space
entries.summary: The one island on the fall line where rifts never open, held still by an Ascent Age anchor stone. Crystal hunters sleep, trade and bury each other here.
entries.lore: The anchor is a black pillar bound with nine bronze bands; within forty li of it, space behaves. The town sells rift wards, crystal tongs, cold-proof furs and bunks priced by distance from the pillar. The Pavilion That Holds the Void buys crystal at the quay, and so do smugglers who pay a little more and ask nothing. Every season some crew comes back one member short, or one extra.
entries.truth: The bands are failing. Four have cracked since the tide turned, the last this decade, and the town council has agreed not to count them aloud.

entries.name: Soul-Ferry Landing
entries.summary: The Court of No Light's floating customs house, where drowned souls are netted from the current, registered and shipped to the Pale City. The living may land with a pass.
entries.lore: The landing is a raft of white-lacquered boats lashed together, staffed by ghost clerks with nets and ledgers. Families pay to have a drowned relative searched for in the registers, and pay more to have one released before shipping. Living workers are hired to haul the nets, because ghost clerks cannot haul nets; the pay is days of lifespan returned. Shark-folk patrols circle it constantly.
entries.truth: The clerks enter one soul in twenty as lost to the sea and sell it to a broker who sets it into the cores of the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] puppets. This is why some of the Gate's puppets are not empty.

entries.name: Ocean of the Dividing Line
entries.summary: The waters off the Morning Star Continent's outer coast, cut by the Toll Line: inside it, the Great Jing's fishing fleets; outside, the sea clans' toll and law.
entries.lore: The line runs between two reef pillars, one carved with the Jing seal and one with the Sovereign's, and a ship that crosses without paying is fair game. Jing fishing towns live off the shoals inside it; the richest shoals lie outside. Sea-clan young hatch on the outer reefs each spring, and poachers sell their scales to alchemists for ten times the price of fish. Every few years a poachers' port burns: the Jing call it a raid, and the sea clans call it law.
entries.truth: The [[Great Jing Dynasty]] court wants a sea war. War would let it conscript the coast's fishing families, who hide the last untested spirit-root children in the empire.

entries.name: Gate of Sinking and Rising
entries.summary: The diving sect that rules the drowned valleys: it sells the dive licenses, keeps the claim maps and teaches breath arts nobody else can match.
entries.lore: The Gate of Sinking and Rising teaches turtle breath, the Water Dao and a body art that hardens the chest against the deep. Its divers map the valleys and sell licenses by the season; an unlicensed diver is tied to a stone and allowed to keep whatever he finds at the bottom. It recruits the dock children who stay under longest in the summer contest. It is at war with the [[Corpse-Diver School]], whose corpse divers need no beads and no licenses.
entries.truth: The claim maps are wrong on purpose. The Gate of Sinking and Rising's elders keep the richest valleys off them and drown anyone who finds one.

entries.name: Chain of Floating Bells
entries.summary: The marker line around the Scar: three thousand six hundred bronze buoys chained in a ring twenty-two thousand li from the Stump, each hung with a bell. The Watch sinks anything that crosses.
entries.lore: Each buoy carries a plate of seal script and a bell that rings when anything with qi crosses the line, so the forts know where to aim. Buoy-tenders row the line in pairs to scrape weed and replace chain; it is the best-paid safe job in the Shattered Sea until a bell rings next to you. Broken plates sell in [[Ten Thousand Sails]] as protective charms for a mid-grade stone, and the Watch treats taking one as an attack on the seal.
entries.truth: The buoys are the outermost ring of the seal array, not markers. For eleven years the northern bells have rung on still nights with nothing crossing, and always from the inside.

entries.name: Graveyard of the Tax Barges
entries.summary: A reef where a Great Jing tax fleet carrying a year of southern revenue broke up in a typhoon two hundred years ago. The empire still claims every coin.
entries.lore: The imperial seals on the chests still hold, and anyone who breaks one is entered in the Jing registry as a thief of the throne, with a bounty that never lapses. Raiders dive the wreck anyway and melt what they find. Jing patrols sweep the reef on every pass. An appraiser can tell a coin's mint and year from its rim, and so can the registrars, which is how most divers get caught.

entries.name: Turtle Archive
entries.summary: The turtle sages of the Azure Wave Palace's court, who keep the sea's law, set its tolls and remember every debt owed to the sea clans for fifty thousand years.
entries.lore: The archive is carved into the shell of its eldest sage, a turtle the size of a hill who has not moved in nine thousand years. Its scholars write law on shells: what a ship owes, what a poacher owes, which human ports are in debt. Their faction holds the Sovereign back from war. Humans may petition the archive to lower a toll or settle a blood debt; it takes years and costs more than the debt, but it is the only appeal there is.
entries.truth: The eldest sage is brother to the [[Beast Court of Ten Thousand Mountains]]'s Old Tortoise. Through the two of them, the sea and the land beasts have been talking for a century, and the subject is humans.

entries.name: Sea of Passing Whales
entries.summary: The narrows between the Myriad Sands Continent's outer coast and the Rim, where the whale road runs so close to shore that a monk on the cliffs can count the pods.
entries.lore: Every autumn the great whales pass south along this coast from the polar sea toward their calving grounds, and every spring they come back. The [[Kingdom of Whale Oil]] whalers wait for them, and so do the monks of the [[Sea Lotus Temple]], who pay to have harpooned whales cut free. Under the narrows runs a trench where the inkfolk keep [[Inkwell City]] and sell the best talisman ink in the world. The sea clans count every whale that does not come back.
entries.truth: The whale road is narrowing. Each year the pods swim closer to the coast, as if something were pushing them away from the Rim.

entries.name: Sea Lotus Temple
entries.summary: A daughter temple of the Thousand Lamps Temple on a sea cliff above the whale road. Its monks ransom harpooned whales and preach to anything that surfaces.
entries.lore: When a whaler has a whale on the line, a monk rows out with spirit stones and pays its price to have it cut free. Whalers have learned to harpoon more whales. The temple teaches the vajra body and a chant that calms sea beasts, and takes in the orphans of drowned whalers, who make devout and very strong monks. Sea-clan pilgrims come to its lower caves to hear the sutras, and a few shark-folk have taken vows.
entries.truth: The temple tags ransomed whales with prayer beads and sells their tracks to a [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] whaling consortium. Compassion here has a price list too.

entries.name: Realm of the Sea Mirage
entries.summary: A shard world that shows itself as a mirage city above the Confluence Isles every three years at the spring equinox. For seven days its gate is real, and only Qi Condensation cultivators can pass.
entries.lore: The mirage hangs over open water a day's sail from [[Ten Thousand Sails]]; boats row into it and do not come out the other side. Inside is an empty Ascent Age market town on a ring of islets, its stalls still stocked with goods that have half-rotted into spirit materials, and its tide pools full of pearl clams the size of carts. A Foundation aura dispels the mirage, so island sects send their youngest disciples, who fight each other harder than anything inside.
entries.truth: The market is not empty. Its shopkeepers are still there, a half-step out of phase, and they remember every customer who did not pay.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Pearl Crescent
entries.summary: A mortal kingdom of pearl divers on a crescent of reef islands, where every child learns to dive before reading, and learns which pearls must never be touched.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of the Pearl Crescent queens rule by the pearl ledger: every pearl brought up is weighed at the palace, and a tenth goes to the crown. Black pearls that glow in the dark are shark-folk tears; touching one is death, and the queen's executioners carry it out before the sea clans can. The kingdom farms spirit pearls in caged beds, the best eye-brightening pill ingredient in the isles. Spirit-root children are bought by League sects; the rest dive until their ears bleed.
entries.truth: The queens have married shark-folk for twelve generations. The royal children are half-bloods, and the sea spares the kingdom for their sake.

entries.name: Black Throat Abyss
entries.summary: Where the deepest drowned valley drops into a crack in the sea floor. Divers who go near it come back without their cores, or don't come back.
entries.lore: The crack runs a hundred li, and no rope has found its bottom. Bodies float up from it with their dantians emptied and no wound on them. The Gate of Sinking and Rising marks it on every map with a black ring. Core Formation divers go anyway, because the ruins on its lip are the best preserved in the sea and their arrays still glow.
entries.truth: An Ascent Age master sleeps sealed in a cave abode on the crack's wall. His arrays are drawing qi from divers to wake him, and he is close. He sealed himself at Body Integration.

entries.name: Cliff of the Dragon's Becoming
entries.summary: A cliff on the trench's lip, blasted bare, where the Sovereign has prepared the ground for his dragon tribulation. Leftover thunder strikes anything that enters.
entries.lore: The court has spent three centuries building tribulation arrays here: coral pillars, buried pearls and the bones of nine jiao who failed before. Thunder with nowhere to go strikes the cliff on its own every few days. Scavengers who sneak in after the pearls are found turned to glass. When the Sovereign finally rises, everything within a thousand li will lie under his tribulation clouds.
entries.truth: The arrays are built for a tribulation he cannot survive without the pearl. If age or war forces him to rise early, he dies, and the court splits between generals and sages.

entries.name: Harbor of the Changing Watch
entries.summary: The Seal Watch's supply harbor on a cracked jade terrace that was once a stair of the Ladder. Every rotation, grain barge, convict and volunteer lands here.
entries.lore: Each continent's ships moor in a separate basin so their crews never meet off duty. The Merit Office trades Watch tokens for pills, manuals and passage, and rotation disciples sell spare rations on the quay. The [[Clear Heaven Sword Sect]] swordsmen and the [[Eternal Night Palace]] blood cultivators eat in one canteen under one rule: a fight costs both sides their term's merit. Qi Condensation laborers sign three-year contracts at a low-grade stone a day plus board, double what a kingdom pays a cultivator guard.
entries.truth: Forged Watch tokens from [[Ten Thousand Sails]] circulate on the quay. The Merit Office lets them, because anyone desperate enough to buy a forgery is worth following, and some of them lead to the [[Void Choir]].

entries.name: Yellow Fog Sea
entries.summary: The strait between the Myriad Sands Continent and the Long Dusk Continent, where dust blown off the Sand Sea meets the Long Dusk Continent's dusk and makes a yellow fog that never lifts.
entries.lore: Ships cross by compass and sound, ringing bells every hundred breaths. Ghost pilots from [[Long Dusk Continent]] offer to guide them through for a price in days of lifespan, and they are the only pilots who never get lost. The Heavenly Scale Pavilion cargo bound for the [[Pale City]] comes this way, and so do the pirates who know it. The fog has thickened every year for a century, and the strait's fishing villages are moving away.
entries.truth: The fog thickens because the Sand Sea is spreading west, faster than anyone in Myriad Sands admits.

entries.name: Stockade of Ashes
entries.summary: The strongest raider lordship on the black reefs, ruled by a Core Formation fire cultivator who was once a Jing magistrate's son.
entries.lore: The Ash Lord's family was executed when a Jing prince wanted their spirit vein, and he has burned eleven Jing coastal towns since, always ones that prince owns. His people are runaway conscripts, escaped bondservants and their children, who grow up knowing the imperial registry as the thing that takes you away. He splits plunder evenly and hangs anyone who sells a captive to the Night Banquet, which makes him unusual on these reefs.
entries.truth: The prince quietly funds his raids. Every burned town drives the Ancestor Emperor's other heirs to beg that prince for protection.

entries.name: Confluence Isles
entries.summary: The crowded heart of the Thousand Isles, where four currents meet: Ten Thousand Sails's harbor, the League's hall, and a hundred islands that live off both.
entries.lore: Every current in the archipelago passes through here, and so does every ship. [[Ten Thousand Sails]] sells anything, and its array platform is the only the Heavenly Circuit hub at sea. The [[Thousand Isles League]] meets here when an outsider threatens the isles and otherwise lets its members rob one another. Island sects hire out as escorts, the yards build spirit ships for half the world's navies, and children with spirit roots are auctioned at the spring tests. The [[Great Jing Dynasty]] is said to be building a fleet to end all of it.
entries.truth: The League's current speaker pays the [[Azure Wave Palace]], and the agenda of its next meeting was written in the Sea Sovereign's court.

top.note: the Isles League's three island masters

entries.name: Islet of Sealed Voices
entries.summary: A rock outside the buoy line where the Seal Watch keeps anyone caught humming a tune nobody taught them. No ship stops there, and no prisoner has ever been released.
entries.lore: The islet is a single prison tower inside a ring of silencing arrays. Guards wear wax in their ears and talk by hand. The Watch says everyone inside is touched by the [[Void Choir]]; families who come asking are handed an urn. Fishermen say that on still nights the whole tower hums the same tune, in harmony.
entries.truth: Fewer than half the prisoners are Choir. The rest saw something on duty they were told never to speak of, and spoke.

entries.name: Peak of Sword Graves
entries.summary: An island that was the peak of an Ascent Age sword sect, where ten thousand swords stand planted in the slopes as grave markers. Two scavenger sects have fought over it for ninety years.
entries.lore: Each sword marks the grave of the cultivator who carried it, and many still hum with their owner's intent. A Sword Dao cultivator who sits among them can feel the old sect's forms; one who pulls a sword must win a duel with what is left of its owner. The lower slopes hold the sect's herb terraces, which is why the [[Hall of Seed-Seekers]] wants it.

entries.name: Islet of the Jiao's Bones
entries.summary: An islet made of the ribs of a flood dragon the League's founders killed. Every lord who joins the League swears on its skull.
entries.lore: The jiao was an Azure Wave Palace toll-collector that sank fishing fleets over unpaid toll; nineteen pirate captains burned it with fire ships two thousand years ago and founded the League on its bones. Oaths sworn on the skull are binding, and a lord who breaks one is said to drown within the year. The marrow was sold long ago, but the ribs still hum with water qi, and Water Dao cultivators meditate between them.
entries.truth: The jiao's soul is still in the skull. It hears every oath and reports it to the Sea Sovereign, which is how he knows which League lords to buy.

entries.name: Abyss of the Flood Dragon
entries.summary: The Sea Sovereign's home waters: a deep blue basin over the trench where the Azure Wave Palace stands, patrolled by shark-folk and closed to any ship without a toll pass.
entries.lore: The [[Azure Wave Palace]] stands on a ridge at the trench's lip, and the [[City of Pearl Light]] glows in the wall below it. Humans come only as envoys, hostages, tribute or invited scholars. The court is split: the [[Iron Gill Host]] generals want war with the [[Floating Peak Continent]] for the dragon pearl now, and the [[Turtle Archive]] sages say a Sovereign who starts a war on land before his tribulation dies in it. Tribute ships from the [[Isles of the Following Current]] arrive at night and leave lighter.
entries.truth: The Sovereign has chosen theft over war. He is quietly shopping among human sects for thieves who can walk into the Floating Peaks.

top.note: the Sea Sovereign, one pearl short of a true dragon

entries.name: Town That Meets the Clouds
entries.summary: A market town on the broad back of a low shard, reached by chain lifts from a floating harbor below. Everything sold here came down from higher up.
entries.lore: The Town That Meets the Clouds hangs a few hundred feet above the waves and strains at its chains, so its harbor is rebuilt every decade. The market sells pristine Ascent Age fragments, sky-crane eggs, wind-cured cloud moss for alchemy, and maps of the upper shards, half of them lies. There are no walls, only the drop. Debts are settled at the edge, in front of witnesses.

entries.name: Whale-Rib Town
entries.summary: A summer whaling town built inside the ribs of a whale that died on the ice a thousand years ago. In winter it is left to the dark and whatever walks on the ice.
entries.lore: Whalers from the Black Frost Continent's northern coast haul up here in the third month and leave before the first snow. The town renders blubber into lamp oil, cuts spirit bone for refiners and sells kun-whale cores when someone lands one, which happens every few years and makes a crew rich for life. The sea clans call each kill murder and send a reckoning every few summers. Anyone still in town when the sun sets for the winter is not found in spring.
entries.truth: Last spring two whalers who stayed the winter walked back into town. Their families took them home and have let no one see them since.

entries.name: Kingdom of Whale Oil
entries.summary: A whaling kingdom on the islands off the Myriad Sands Continent's outer coast. Its oil lights half the lamps in the Myriad Sands Continent, including, quietly, the life lamps of the Thousand Lamps Temple.
entries.lore: The Harpoon Throne passes to whichever royal child kills the largest whale in their eighteenth year. Children learn the oar before they walk and the harpoon at ten; spirit-root children train in the royal harpoon hall and become the kingdom's only cultivators above Qi Condensation. It sells oil, spirit bone and ambergris to the [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]], which also holds its debts. The Sea Lotus monks' ransom money is now a third of its income.
entries.truth: The [[Thousand Lamps Temple]] is its largest oil buyer, through a merchant front, and has privately asked it not to stop whaling.

entries.name: Ocean of Mad Winds
entries.summary: A belt of permanent storm across the northern Shattered Sea. Ships between the Floating Peak Continent and Myriad Sands cross it in a lull or go the long way past the Black Frost Continent's raiders.
entries.lore: The storm never stops, but it breathes: every forty-nine days it slackens for about a day, and the ships waiting in the [[Harbor of Waiting Winds]] race through. Those who cannot wait hug the [[Black Frost Continent]]'s south coast and pay the [[Eternal Night Palace]] raiders instead. Lightning here is dense enough to temper a body, and talismans drawn under it hold twice the charge. The [[Abbey of Drawn Lightning]] owns the reefs where it strikes most. In the middle lies a calm eye, the [[Isle of the Thunder Drum]], that nobody living has reached.
entries.truth: The lulls are getting shorter and less regular, and the abbey has stopped publishing its count of them.

entries.name: Isle of the Kun's Grave
entries.summary: The carcass of a kun whale that died two thousand years ago, grown over with reef until it became an island. Its bones still seep qi, and everything in the sea comes to feed.
entries.lore: The skull alone is a hill. Spirit marrow seeps from the bones into the water, so the reef teems with fish, crabs and the things that eat them, and sea-clan and human divers fight over the marrow channels. Ambergris from the gut washes up after storms and sells as incense for its weight in mid-grade stones. The Sea Lotus monks hold a funeral here every year; the whalers hold an auction the same week.

entries.name: Court of the Old Kun
entries.summary: The summer domain of an ancient kun whale, a Nascent Soul beast lord whose pods gather under the ice each year. In his waters, whaling is war.
entries.lore: The old kun has taken human form once in living memory, to walk into Whale-Rib Town and eat its headman. His pods, a few hundred whales and the sea-clan riders who herd them, feed in the krill blooms from the fourth month to the eighth, then swim south down the whale road. The riders trade with anyone who does not hunt and sell whale song sealed in shells, which calms beasts and is worth a fortune to tamers.
entries.truth: He feeds near the Ice Stair on purpose. Whatever climbs it, he eats, and he is the only reason the climbers are few.

entries.name: Isle of the Thunder Drum
entries.summary: The calm eye of the storm belt: a circle of still water around an island no one has reached alive in living memory. Every forty-nine days a drumbeat from it carries a thousand li.
entries.lore: A ring of lightning walls the eye, so it can only be approached in a lull, and lulls end without warning. Through a spyglass the island shows a bronze drum the size of a hill under a roof of black tile. The [[Abbey of Drawn Lightning]] calls the eye holy ground and forbids attempts. A reward posted in the [[Harbor of Waiting Winds]] for a rubbing of the drum's inscription stands at three high-grade stones.
entries.truth: The drum is the heart of a storm wall raised around the Scar in the First Sealing, and the belt is its last working arc. Each beat answers a pulse from the Scar, and the beats are coming closer together.

entries.name: The Cold Whirl
entries.summary: Where the outer sea's currents meet and sink: a slow whirlpool of grey water thick with souls, cold enough to frost a ship's sails in summer.
entries.lore: Ghost Way cultivators meditate on its rim, because the yin is the densest in the Shoreless Sea, and those who misjudge it join it. A living person who falls in is not drowned so much as outnumbered. In Ghost Month it rises into a waterspout that reaches the clouds, and on those nights the [[Nether Shard]] is said to show in the water instead of the sky.
entries.truth: It drains toward the Nether Shard. Every Ghost Month a few thousand souls go down it, registered by neither court.

entries.name: Kingdom of Two Waters
entries.summary: A kingdom of fishing islands astride the Toll Line that pays tribute to both the Great Jing and the Azure Wave Palace, and spies on each for the other.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Two Waters kings are Jing vassals by registry and sea-clan clients by toll, and have lasted nine hundred years by being too useful to crush. Children learn two scripts and two sets of manners. Spirit-root children are supposed to be reported to the Jing registrars; the kings hide one in three and send them to sea-clan tutors instead. The current king is sixteen, and both sides have a candidate for his regent.

entries.name: Sea of Torn Sky
entries.summary: The path the Ladder's upper span tore as it fell toward the Long Dusk Continent. Space along it never healed: rifts open in the air and on the water, and close on whatever is halfway through.
entries.lore: Rifts here last from a breath to a season. Small ones are a nuisance; large ones open onto the void sea, and the cold pouring out freezes rigging solid. Rift edges leave void crystal, which every storage ring and bag needs, so crystal hunters swarm the field and race the closings. The [[Pavilion That Holds the Void]] reads the rifts and buys the crystal. Debris from the span lies along the line, and the [[Court of No Light]] claims every body in it, as it does in the [[Fallen Ladder]].
entries.truth: Not every rift opens onto empty void. Twice this century something has come through a large one, and the [[Seal Watch]] burned the nearby islands and called it a fire.

entries.name: Drift-Ice Sea
entries.summary: The polar sea north of the Black Frost Continent, where pack ice drifts toward the Rim and the falling ocean freezes on its way down into a stair of ice.
entries.lore: For half the year the sun never rises here, and the Rim's roar carries across the ice for days. In the brief summer the great whales come up the western whale road to feed on krill blooms along the ice edge, and whalers and sea clans follow them. The whalers work out of the [[Whale-Rib Town]] and hunt under the eye of the [[Court of the Old Kun]]. The Seal Watch guards the frozen host on the [[Demon-Sealing Glacier]] to the south. Nobody guards the Rim.
entries.truth: The frozen host faces south because it came from the north. It climbed the [[Ice Stair]] while the war raged at the Scar, and the stair is still a door.

entries.name: Keel Docks
entries.summary: The shipyards beside Ten Thousand Sails where spirit ships are built for anyone who pays: keels of sea-beast bone, hulls of ironwood, sails woven with wind arrays.
entries.lore: A good spirit ship takes three years and a Core Formation refiner's attention, and costs as much as a small kingdom's treasury. The docks take apprentice refiners and array masters on ten-year bonds; those who survive the bond are hired anywhere. Keels are the bones of jiao and great whales, which is why the docks pay hunters well, and why the [[Azure Wave Palace]] considers every launch a corpse wearing sails.
entries.truth: The yards are laying a hundred hulls for a buyer paying through the [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]]. It is the Great Jing's admiralty, and the fleet is meant for these isles.

entries.name: Strait of the Sleeping Beast
entries.summary: The strait between the Long Dusk Continent and the Vast Wilds Continent, crossed by a chain of long, ridged, warm islands that sailors swear is the spine of something asleep.
entries.lore: The islands have moved: Rekindling charts put them three hundred li further east. Neither the [[Beast Court of Ten Thousand Mountains]] nor the [[Court of No Light]] claims them, which tells sailors all they need. Ships that anchor too long report the ground breathing. Everyone fights over the strait's real cargo instead: immortal corpses from the Long Dusk Continent's coast, smuggled to the [[Jar-Mother Clans]] of the Vast Wilds Continent, who pay well for flesh that never rots.
entries.truth: It is an Ascent Age sea beast, one of those the tide is waking, and it rolled over in its sleep last spring.

entries.name: Sea of Maze Pillars
entries.summary: A maze of sea stacks and fallen arches south of the Stump, where the inner sea's pirates hide their ships, their money and their prisoners.
entries.lore: The stacks are the broken teeth of mountains on the old continent's southern rim. Channels between them shift as arches fall, and only local pilots know which are open this year. The haven preys on the southern route between the [[Morning Star Continent]], the [[Long Dusk Continent]] and the [[Myriad Sands Continent]], which every captain takes to avoid both the Scar and the storm belt. Its pirates answer to the queen of the [[Iron Bridge Stockade]], and her law is stricter than [[Ten Thousand Sails]]'s, which is to say it exists.

entries.name: Bay of the Silent Sinking
entries.summary: A shallow bay where a pirate lord's whole fleet of thirty ships sank in a dead calm in one night, every hull intact and every sailor still at his post.
entries.lore: It happened twenty years ago; at low tide you can see the masts. The holds are full of plunder from a raid on the [[Morning Star Continent]]'s coast, and none of it has come up: divers who touch the cargo feel hands close round their ankles. League lords call it a curse. The lord's widow offers half the cargo to whoever brings back his body.
entries.truth: He had stopped paying the [[Azure Wave Palace]]. His crews' souls serve in the Sovereign's court now, and the hands on the divers' ankles are theirs, begging to be taken up.

entries.name: Inkwell City
entries.summary: A city of the inkfolk, cuttlefish sea clans who live in a trench under the whale road and sell the best spirit ink in the world to talisman makers.
entries.lore: Inkfolk ink holds qi better than cinnabar: a talisman drawn in it keeps its charge for a century. They sell it by the drop at a raft market above the trench and take payment in spirit stones, books and secrets. Down in the trench the city is lit by their own skin, which changes color as they speak. They answer to the [[Azure Wave Palace]] in theory and to nobody in practice. Talisman makers from every continent apprentice here for the ink trade alone.
entries.truth: Their best ink is not theirs. It is milked from something much larger at the trench bottom, and keeping it calm is getting harder.

entries.name: Realm of the Crane Pastures
entries.summary: A shard world whose gate hangs under a floating shard and opens for thirty days every nine years. Only cultivators below Core Formation can pass; inside, Ascent Age cranes still graze.
entries.lore: The Armillary Pavilion's tables put the next opening in the coming autumn. The gate is a ring of white stone on the underside of a shard, so entrants climb down to it on ropes; a Core Formation aura cracks it. Inside are cloud meadows and crane herds bred from the mounts of Ascent Age immortals. An egg sells for a mid-grade stone in the [[Town That Meets the Clouds]], a tamed adult for ten. Cranes defend their nests in flocks, and the meadows have edges.
entries.truth: The herds are not wild. Something still whistles them home at dusk, and it has noticed the egg thieves.

entries.name: Pavilion That Holds the Void
entries.summary: Space Dao specialists who predict rift openings and turn void crystal into storage rings. Most rings sold anywhere in the world started here.
entries.lore: The Pavilion That Holds the Void teaches the Space Dao, rift-reading and the refining of storage artifacts, and its ring-smiths are the best artifact refiners in the Shattered Sea. Crystal hunters sell to it because nobody pays better. It tests children for spatial sense: blindfolded, a candidate must find a coin hidden in a fold of space. It is locked in a bitter quarrel with the [[Armillary Pavilion]], which wants its rift charts and calls its rings unlicensed.
entries.truth: Its forecasts come from an outer demon it keeps caged in nested space, which feels the void sea pressing on the world.

entries.name: Kingdom of Calm Waves
entries.summary: The only human kingdom inside the Sovereign's waters: a ring of atolls that pays tribute in children and has not seen a storm, a pirate or a war in two thousand years.
entries.lore: Every tenth child born in the Kingdom of Calm Waves is sent at seven to serve in the Azure Wave Palace court; some come home at seventy, rich and strange. The rest grow up safe, fed and governed by sea law: no nets in the breeding months, no killing anything with scales. Kings are crowned by a jiao and buried at sea. The Kingdom of Calm Waves-born servants are the only humans the court trusts, so every sect that wants a spy below the sea tries to buy one.
entries.truth: Each Kingdom of Calm Waves servant carries a sea-clan sigil under the tongue. Whoever buys one buys the Sovereign an ear.

entries.name: Beast-Cutters' Harbor
entries.summary: The isles' core market: a harbor of butchers, appraisers and buyers' agents where a beast's core, gall, hide and young are sold by the pound.
entries.lore: Cores are graded on the quay by color and weight, and a Core Formation beast's core sells for more than the ship that brought it. Half-bloods from Shared Roost City work as appraisers because they can smell a fake; Jar-Mother agents buy venom glands and say nothing. The stink carries ten li downwind, which makes the harbor easy for the Beast Court to find. Twice a century something huge comes out of the sea and eats it, and the next tide of hunters rebuilds.

entries.name: Abyss of a Thousand Gaps
entries.summary: The densest stretch of the rift field, where the span's heaviest section struck the sea. Rifts open every hour, and the large ones open onto the void.
entries.lore: Ships that go in lose time as well as space: crews come out with beards grown or wounds still fresh. The best void crystal on the fall line forms here, fist-sized, and one buys a Foundation Pill. The cold from the large rifts kills more hunters than the closings do. Time Dao cultivators come to study the slips in time, and a few stay longer than they meant to.
entries.truth: Something on the far side holds the large rifts open a few breaths longer every year.

entries.name: Stele of the Missing Name
entries.summary: The founding stele of the Seal Watch, raised at the Second Sealing. It lists every founder but one, and the blank where her name should be is worn smooth by hands.
entries.lore: Watch recruits swear their oath with a palm on the blank. Pilgrims from every continent come to touch it, and some leave sure they almost remembered something. Carving anything into the blank is punished by drowning; three scholars have tried in the last century, each certain they had recovered the name, and each carved a different one. Core Formation cultivators meditate before it to steady their hearts against inner demons.
entries.truth: Every name carved so far was wrong. The right one would unpay the price of the seal, and the Pale Sovereign of the [[Court of No Light]] knows exactly what that would cost.

entries.name: Corpse-Diver School
entries.summary: Demonic puppeteers who send refined corpses down to loot the drowned valleys. Corpses need no beads, no license and no share, which is why the Gate of Sinking and Rising wants them dead.
entries.lore: The school buys drowned bodies from fishing villages, and from anyone else who can supply them, and refines them into diving puppets that work the deep for a month at a time. It sells salvage under the Gate of Sinking and Rising's prices and teaches puppetry, corpse refining and the Death Dao to anyone who pays tuition. Its puppets are crude beside the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]]'s, and the Gate sells it the cores that run them. The Gate of Sinking and Rising has burned its island twice; twice it moved.
entries.truth: Its best puppet came up from the [[Black Throat Abyss]] holding something and has refused every command since. The master keeps it chained in his cellar and is afraid to unmake it.

entries.name: Sect of Gleaned Relics
entries.summary: The largest scavenger sect in the isles, sponsored by the Clear Heaven Sword Sect. It digs old sword graves and trains the best relic appraisers in the Shattered Sea.
entries.lore: The Sect of Gleaned Relics teaches appraisal before fighting: a novice must date a potsherd to the right millennium before learning a sword form. It sends its finds to the [[Clear Heaven Sword Sect]] first, which keeps the swords and returns a stipend. It recruits from the beach sifters by watching which children find things. It despises the [[Hall of Seed-Seekers]] as the Apricot Grove Valley's gardeners and has fought it over the [[Peak of Sword Graves]] claim for ninety years.
entries.truth: The Clear Heaven Sword Sect has told the Sect of Gleaned Relics to find one sword above all others, and not to draw it if they do.

entries.name: Realm of the Water Bridge
entries.summary: Every thirty-three years a shard world swings so close past the Rim here that the falling ocean bends into a bridge to it. For nine days, anyone below Nascent Soul can walk across.
entries.lore: The Armillary Pavilion's tables give the date to the hour, and sailors know before that, when the Rim's roar changes pitch. The bridge is falling water bent into a road by the shard's pull, and a Nascent Soul's weight breaks it. The shard is cold, bright and full of Ascent Age ruins that have never been looted, because anyone still on it when the bridge drops is carried off into the void. The last crossing was twenty-nine years ago.
entries.truth: The old texts about Ascent Age masters walking out along the falling water describe this. The shard was a waystation, and its far side faces the void sea, not Severed Heaven.

entries.name: Isles of the Following Current
entries.summary: The eastern isles facing the open Shoreless Sea: rich, quiet and strangely safe. Sea beasts here leave ships alone, and nobody asks why.
entries.lore: These are the isles nearest the [[Azure Wave Palace]]'s waters, and their pirate lords are the richest in the League: they raid far, never lose ships to storms or serpents, and always seem to know where the [[Great Jing Dynasty]] patrols are. A current runs through them to the open sea that carries a ship two days' sail in one. The pearl beds are the best in the archipelago, and divers from poorer islands learn quickly which pearls are taken and which are left.
entries.truth: Every lord here pays the Sea Sovereign, and turtle sages below steer the current that names the isles. A lord who stops paying finds out when the current turns.

entries.name: Fort That Quells the Sea
entries.summary: The Great Jing's forward naval fort on a northern reef, from which its punitive fleets sail. Raiders have burned it three times, and it was rebuilt larger each time.
entries.lore: Its admiral, a Nascent Soul spear cultivator of the imperial clan, is assembling a hundred war junks for the Pacification of the Isles, which the court has announced every decade for a century. Five years' service earns a pardon in the registry, so the garrison is full of runaways the empire caught. Garrison and raiders trade at night through a sea cave that nobody officially knows about.
entries.truth: The quartermaster sells patrol schedules to the raiders, and the admiral lets him. Every raid justifies a bigger fleet.

entries.name: Locked Gate Strait
entries.summary: The best-guarded strait between any two continents, between the Black Frost Continent and the Myriad Sands Continent. Islets string the narrows, and whoever fortifies them can close it with chain booms.
entries.lore: Whoever holds the chains holds the cheapest road between the inner sea and the Myriad Sands Continent's outer coast. Four powers have raised them in the last thousand years. Today the [[Eternal Night Palace]] holds the northern windlass forts and a consortium backed by the [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] holds the southern ones, and ships pay both. Currents in the narrows are vicious, and the bottom is a field of wrecks from the last time the two sides tried to cut each other's chains.

entries.name: Hot Spring Town
entries.summary: The raiders' harbor town, built around volcanic springs that close a sword wound overnight. Its back streets hold the captive market.
entries.lore: Wounded raiders soak in the springs at a low-grade stone a night, and the town's healers sell medicines compounded from the sulfur crust; there is no faster place in the isles to learn field medicine. The captive market opens at dusk: spirit-root children go to island sects, the rest to plantations, and the leftovers to quiet buyers with banquet invitations. Two raider lords have died arguing over the Mid-grade fire vein under the springs.

entries.name: Sand-Sifting Isles
entries.summary: A chain of islands that were once the peaks of the central continent's eastern ranges. Scavenger sects each hold a peak and sift its ruins, its beaches and each other.
entries.lore: Every island was a mountain sect's peak, and its broken halls turn up talismans, bronze and bones after every storm. Scavenger sects register claims in the [[Marker-Stone Town]] and fight over the rest. The Morning Star Continent's great sects sponsor scavengers as proxies, so a beach brawl here can end as a debt between the [[Clear Heaven Sword Sect]] and the [[Apricot Grove Valley]]. Mortal sifters work the beaches for coppers a day and the chance of a spirit stone in the sand; the sects recruit the lucky ones.
entries.truth: The registry keeps two ledgers. Every rich claim in the isles has been sold twice, and the registrars decide which sale is real by who pays last.

entries.name: Iron Bridge Stockade
entries.summary: The pirate queen's realm: three hundred sea stacks linked by iron chain bridges, forty thousand people and one law, which is hers.
entries.lore: The Iron Bridge queen, a Nascent Soul water cultivator who widowed herself, rules by ledger: every prize is logged, every share paid on time, and a captain who cheats is hung by the ankles from a bridge until the tide decides. Children grow up running the chain bridges, and the quick ones become pilots. Mortals here eat well, pay a tenth and never leave. Her nephews are already quarrelling over who inherits the ledger.
entries.truth: She pays the [[Seal Watch]] in information, reporting every ship that drifts toward the buoys, and in return no Watch elder has ever come to clean out the stacks.

entries.name: Iron Gill Host
entries.summary: The shark-folk war host of the Azure Wave Palace: the Sovereign's generals, his toll enforcers and the hands that drag unpaying ships under.
entries.lore: Iron Gill warriors cultivate the Water and Slaughter Daos and fight with tridents and teeth; a general's rank is the number of hulls he has opened. They enforce the tolls in all the Sovereign's waters and hunt poachers down in their own ports, sometimes years later. Their chief, a Nascent Soul shark lord, leads the faction that wants war with Floating Peak now. They despise the turtle sages as cowards and the [[Thousand Isles League]] as thieves who have been allowed to live.
entries.truth: The chief general keeps a spy among the vault guards on the Floating Peaks, and has not told the Sovereign.

entries.name: Sea of the Ladder's Root
entries.summary: The black, glass-calm water around the Heaven Ladder's stump: the Scar, the Seal Watch's fortress ring, and the only harbor where orthodox and demonic disciples queue at the same gate.
entries.lore: Inside a ring of bell buoys lies the [[Heaven's Scar]], and in its middle the [[Ladder Stump]] rises from the water, ringed by forts. Just outside the buoys sits the seat of the [[Seal Watch]]. Everything arrives by ship, because transfer arrays scramble near the Scar. The Watch hires porters, cooks and buoy-tenders at Qi Condensation and pays in merit tokens that buy pills and manuals no market sells; Core Formation elders serve terms for their sects. Since the garrison was doubled, nobody has been granted leave, and the ships home sail half empty.
entries.truth: Elders whose terms have ended are still on the walls. Their sects keep receiving letters in their handwriting, written by the Watch's scribes.

top.note: the Warden; something sealed below is higher

entries.name: Academy of the Listening Deep
entries.summary: A quiet academy on a reef that teaches water arts, navigation and sea-clan law to island children. Its graduates make the best toll negotiators in the isles.
entries.lore: The master is a gentle old scholar who never leaves the reef and never seems to age. The academy teaches the Water Dao, the eighteen tolls of the Shoreless Sea, the etiquette for addressing a jiao, and the sea clans' script. Captains who want to pay toll and survive the conversation hire its graduates. It takes ten students a year, chosen by an essay on the law of the sea.
entries.truth: The master is a turtle sage of the [[Turtle Archive]] in human form, and the academy is how the Sovereign chooses which island lords to buy next.

top.note: the master, a turtle sage in human form

entries.name: Society of Substitutes
entries.summary: Drowned ghosts who can only move on by drowning someone in their place. They have organized, keep a waiting list and take bribes to pass a ship by.
entries.lore: Folk belief holds that a water ghost is freed when it drowns a living soul to take its place. The Society runs that as a business: its ghosts keep a strict queue, and a captain who pays toll in grave goods at the right buoy is passed by. Unpaid ships lose a sailor a night. Its living members, mostly Ghost Way cultivators, sell protection, broker substitutes from prisons and slave markets and teach the Death Dao. The Court of No Light calls them unregistered.
entries.truth: Substitution frees no one. The drowned soul goes into a court's ledger either way. The founder knows; the queue is simply the most profitable lie on the sea.

entries.name: Ship-Swallowing Vortex
entries.summary: A whirlpool forty li across on the belt's western side that has never closed. Ships caught in its outer current circle for days before they go down.
entries.lore: The vortex drains into something under the sea floor. Wreckage from it surfaces in the [[Sea of Sunken Valleys]] months later, scoured clean and smelling of lightning. Divers with strong water arts have ridden the current down and come back with Ascent Age bronze; most do not come back. Water Dao cultivators meditate on the outer current lashed to a mast, and some come away with a comprehension.
entries.truth: It is the storm wall's intake. Everything it swallows is carried down to cool the drum, and the chamber around the drum is full of ships.

entries.name: Sea of Lost Souls
entries.summary: The grey waters south of Long Dusk where the drowned of six continents drift in on converging currents. The Court of No Light and the Azure Wave Palace both claim them.
entries.lore: Currents from the whole outer sea meet here, carrying wreckage and the souls of the drowned. The [[Court of No Light]] says every soul that dies within sight of the Long Dusk Continent's shadow is its subject; the [[Azure Wave Palace]] says whatever drowns belongs to the sea. Ghost clerks in paper boats and shark-folk patrols meet on the water and argue jurisdiction over each corpse. The living sail through fast, with coins to throw overboard.
entries.truth: The two courts settled the dispute in secret centuries ago and split the souls between them. The arguing on the water is theater to keep human sects out of the trade.

entries.name: Heaven-Gazing Shard
entries.summary: The highest of the hanging shards, now above the clouds, where the air is too thin for mortals and lightning strikes the summit every day out of a clear sky.
entries.lore: Qi near its crown is richer than any vein in the Shattered Sea, and Core Formation cultivators climb it to break bottlenecks. The daily lightning hunts whoever on the summit has the most cultivation, like a tribulation, and it has killed eleven Nascent Souls. The halls on its crown are sealed with characters no scholar can read. On clear nights the Mirror above it looks close enough to touch.
entries.truth: It will touch the world barrier within a century, long before the Floating Peak Continent's peaks. The [[Armillary Pavilion]] keeps a hidden post on its underside to record exactly what happens when it does.

entries.name: Black Rock Isles
entries.summary: Black basalt reefs a day's sail from the Morning Star Continent's southern coast: the raiders' anchorage for strikes on the Great Jing's shore, and the Jing navy's favorite target.
entries.lore: Raiders from these reefs hit Jing salt towns and rice barges and take spirit-root children before the empire's registrars can. The [[Night Banquet Sect]] buys the ones nobody else wants. Jing punitive fleets come every few years, burn whatever stands above the tide line and leave; the raiders are back within the month. The reefs are volcanic and riddled with hot springs where wounded raiders soak.
entries.truth: Jing registrars on the coast sell the raiders lists of villages with untested spirit-root children, and take a share of every sale.

entries.name: Tethering Gate
entries.summary: The scavenger sect that chained the lower shards to anchors on the sea floor. It owns every chain, charges toll to climb them and decides who salvages what.
entries.lore: The Tethering Gate disciples cultivate the Wind and Earth Daos for climbing and forge chain from black iron and beast tendon, which makes its smiths decent artifact refiners. Recruitment is a climb: any child who reaches the first shard up a chain without help is taken in. The Gate fights a quiet war with sky pirates who cut chains to drop shards on rival claims. Its master wants a chain on the [[Heaven-Gazing Shard]] before the [[Conclave of Nine Clans]] gets one there.
entries.truth: Its anchor fees are paid in secret by the [[Armillary Pavilion]], which wants the shards held at fixed heights as relay posts for a new Ladder.

entries.name: Sea of Hanging Isles
entries.summary: Chunks of the old central continent hanging in the air over the sea, some a few hundred feet up, some above the clouds. A few creep higher every year, and their chains must be lengthened.
entries.lore: The shards float on the same rich qi that holds the [[Floating Peak Continent]]'s peaks aloft, so their qi is the richest in the Shattered Sea and their Ascent Age halls have never been under water. Getting up is the problem: by kite, by crane, or by a chain someone else owns. The [[Tethering Gate]] has tethered the lower shards to anchors on the sea floor and charges toll to climb. Rockfall from the shards sinks a ship a month. The [[Conclave of Nine Clans]] calls the shards lost kin of its own peaks and sends hunters after any bloodline relic found on them.
entries.truth: The shards that rise are the ones with intact Ascent Age halls. They are not drifting; something on the Mirror's side is pulling them home.

entries.name: Hall of Seed-Seekers
entries.summary: A scavenger sect sponsored by the Apricot Grove Valley that digs Ascent Age seed vaults for herbs extinct since the Severance, and replants them.
entries.lore: The Hall teaches spirit farming, the Wood Dao and vault-breaking. Seeds sixty-six thousand years old sometimes sprout in its terraced gardens, and one living strain can make an alchemy hall's century. The [[Apricot Grove Valley]] buys first and pays well. Recruits are handed a dead seed; the ones it sprouts for stay. It claims the [[Peak of Sword Graves]] because the sword sect's herb terraces lie under the graves.
entries.truth: The Apricot Grove Valley uses the Hall's revived strains to breed the blights it seeds in rival gardens. The Hall's master knows and takes the money.

entries.name: Kingdom of Hazy Waters
entries.summary: A mortal kingdom of eighty islands on the approaches to Ten Thousand Sails. Its kings collect harbor dues for the League and are allowed to keep a tenth.
entries.lore: The Kingdom of Hazy Waters house has reigned nine hundred years by never being worth replacing. Its people pilot, caulk, cook and smuggle for Ten Thousand Sails; a child's first job is diving for coins dropped under the moorings. Spirit-root children are auctioned to island sects at the spring tests, and the crown takes the price. The crown prince wants to stop paying the League and has been meeting the [[Great Jing Dynasty]] envoys about it.
entries.truth: The [[Pavilion of the Rising Tide]] rigs the spring auctions. The crown is paid a fixed fee, and the best children never reach the block.

entries.name: Night Oar Gang
entries.summary: The poachers of the Toll Line: night rowers who take sea-clan hatchlings from the outer reefs and sell them to alchemists who pay without asking.
entries.lore: Night Oar boats are low, black and silent, rowed by Qi Condensation fishermen with hush talismans on the oarlocks. The gang buys from anyone and sells to the best price, and teaches its rowers enough water arts to swim home when the boat goes down. Its boss is a Core Formation former Jing customs officer who knows every patrol on both sides. The fishing towns hate it, because they are the ones that burn when it fails.
entries.truth: Its biggest buyer is the [[Apricot Grove Valley]], through three layers of middlemen. The white jiao at the [[White Scale Barrier]] knows, and is saving the name for when he needs a war.

entries.name: Realm of the Left-Behind
entries.summary: A stable rift that opens for twenty days every seven years into a shard world still peopled by descendants of Severance survivors. Only cultivators below Foundation can pass.
entries.lore: The Armillary Pavilion's tables list it as a minor herb shard and say nothing of the people. They speak an Ascent Age dialect, farm terraces around a dead transfer array and believe the world outside ended. They trade spirit rice and old manuals for salt and iron, and kill anyone who tries to take their children back through the gate. A Foundation aura cracks its edges, so sects send their best Qi Condensation disciples. The next opening is next spring.
entries.truth: They have waited sixty-six thousand years for the array to be repaired, and they still keep its keys. It once linked to the Heaven Ladder.

entries.name: Kingdom of Yin Sails
entries.summary: A fleet of four hundred ships drowned in one storm during the Outer Demon War, still sailing in formation under its admiral: a fief of the dead with its own law.
entries.lore: The fleet was carrying refugees from the burning continents when it sank, and the admiral has kept everyone aboard ever since: sailors still stand watch, children still go to deck school, and the purser still pays wages. Living ships it meets are hailed and asked for papers from a war that ended three thousand years ago. Those who play along can trade for antique spirit stones and Rekindling manuals; those who don't are boarded.
entries.truth: The admiral refuses to register with the Court of No Light. The moment the fleet is registered, its souls belong to the Pale Sovereign, and he promised them they would stay together.

entries.name: Abbey of Drawn Lightning
entries.summary: A storm-cultivating abbey on a reef of iron lightning rods inside the belt. Its disciples bathe in lightning and sell the storm by the jar.
entries.lore: The abbey teaches the Lightning and Wind Daos and a body art that requires being struck: novices begin on the lowest rod with a copper chain round one ankle. It makes the best thunder talisman paper in the world, charged under the storm for a year, and sells sealed jars of storm qi to refiners. It recruits from wrecks: children pulled alive out of the belt are held to be chosen by thunder. It hates the [[Eternal Night Palace]] raiders who steal its jars and blames them for every novice lost.
entries.truth: The rods are draining the drum in the eye. The abbot knows the storm is part of a seal, and has decided the abbey's growth matters more.

entries.name: Pilots' Guild
