entries.summary: The pilots of the stacks, who alone know which channels are open this year. They serve the queen, but they are paid by the voyage, and anyone can hire them.
entries.lore: Pilot families sound the channels every spring after the winter falls and keep the maps in their heads; writing one down is death under guild law. Pilots read stone the way geomancers read land and can tell which arch will fall within the year. Merchant captains pay them to go through instead of around, which is either a bargain or an ambush. The guild teaches Earth and Water sense to its children and adopts orphans with good ears.
entries.truth: The guild knows which stacks will fall next, and is waiting for the one above the queen's hall.

entries.name: Reef of Young Scales
entries.summary: The spawning reefs just outside the Toll Line where sea-clan young hatch each spring. Their scales fetch ten times any fish, and taking them is death.
entries.lore: Hatchling scale ground fine clears blocked meridians, so alchemists pay well and do not ask. Poachers come at night in small boats with shuttered lanterns. The reef is guarded by hatchling mothers who will chase a boat into a harbor, and by Iron Gill patrols who will chase it into a city. Fishermen inside the line hear the mothers singing in spring and keep their children indoors.

entries.name: Ape's Palm Reef
entries.summary: A reef in the shape of a giant handprint, left when the Beast Court's White Ape King struck the sea and sank a whole raiding fleet with one blow.
entries.lore: It happened three hundred years ago. Forty ships still lie in the fingers with their holds full of caged cubs that drowned. Salvagers come for the cores in the wrecks; sometimes the Court leaves a sentinel in the palm, and sometimes it doesn't. Raiders sail past it bareheaded. A Fist Dao cultivator who meditates inside the print can feel the shape of the blow.

entries.name: Sea-Taming Sect
entries.summary: Beast tamers who raise sea serpents, war crabs and storm gulls in a lagoon, and buy the raiders' cubs to break them.
entries.lore: The Sea-Taming Sect teaches taming by blood contract and the Wood and Water arts that keep a bonded beast healthy. Its serpents tow the fastest ships in the isles, and its gulls carry letters to [[Ten Thousand Sails]] in a day. Every apprentice is handed a cub and told their rank depends on what it grows into. The Beast Court calls the sect slavers and has posted a price: one tamer's core for every beast they free.

entries.name: Ledger Harbor
entries.summary: The haven's market harbor, where the queen's clerks divide plunder, fences buy anything, and captives are ransomed at posted prices.
entries.lore: Ransoms are posted on boards by realm: a Qi Condensation disciple of a known sect is a hundred low-grade stones, a Foundation elder one mid-grade, a Core Formation elder whatever the sect can bear. Captives not ransomed by the new moon go to the second board. Fences appraise everything low on purpose. Agents of the [[Night Banquet Sect]] keep a permanent table beside the second board.

entries.name: City of Pearl Light
entries.summary: A shark-folk city cut into the trench wall below the Azure Wave Palace, lit by the pearls in its stones. Humans may enter with an air pearl and a sponsor.
entries.lore: The City of Pearl Light's streets are terraces in the trench wall, and its light comes from pearls the shark-folk weep and set in the stone. Its market sells dragon silk that sheds water, coral and kelp pills, and air pearls that let a human breathe for a month. Spirit kelp farms line the upper terraces. A human visitor must be sponsored by a sea-clan household, which answers for every insult. Shark-folk weavers will trade silk for human poetry, the one thing they think humans make well.
entries.truth: The pearl walls are a ledger. Each pearl was wept for a shark-folk killed by humans, and the generals mean to collect on all of them.

entries.name: Seal Watch
entries.summary: The garrison that guards Heaven's Scar and the Frozen Host, staffed by every great power in rotation. The one place where orthodox and demonic stand on the same wall.
entries.lore: Founded at the Second Sealing, the Seal Watch answers to no sect. Every great power sends elders to serve a term, and refusing is the one thing all the others will punish. Its fortress rings the Ladder Stump, and a second fortress watches the Demon-Sealing Glacier. Seal Watch elders are forbidden to speak of what they see on duty.
entries.truth: The seal is failing faster than the Seal Watch reports. It has doubled its garrison and stopped granting leave.

ties.why: The Sword Sect sends elders in rotation like every power, and we cannot let them go or tell it why.
We check the Shens' lanterns because the dike may be the last wall between the Stump and the continent, and we are no longer sure it is only a relic.

entries.name: The Shard Worlds
entries.summary: The small thousand worlds that circle Severed Heaven. Their orbits bring them close on fixed cycles, and when they pass near, their gates open as secret realms.
entries.lore: Some shard worlds are minor worlds caught by Severed Heaven's pull. Many are pieces of the central continent flung out when the Ladder broke. The Armillary Pavilion publishes tables of their openings: one herb-rich shard opens every sixty years and admits only cultivators below Foundation, because a stronger aura would crack its gate.
entries.truth: A few shards still hold descendants of Severance survivors, cut off for sixty-six thousand years.

entries.name: Star Dial
entries.summary: The Armillary Pavilion's observatory on the highest floating peak in the world, and the center of the Heavenly Circuit.
entries.lore: Travelers arriving by array step out above the clouds onto a bronze terrace the size of a town, under a sky so close the Mirror looks near enough to touch.

entries.name: Shattered Sea
entries.summary: Where the central continent stood before the Severance: broken islands, floating shards and storms around the Ladder Stump.
entries.lore: Scavenger sects live on the islands and dive for ruins from the Age of the Ascent in the drowned valleys. Spatial rifts open and close without warning. No great power holds the Shattered Sea; the Seal Watch holds its center, and nobody argues with the Seal Watch.
entries.truth: A few of the floating shards are slowly rising toward the Mirror.

entries.name: Heaven's Scar
entries.summary: The sealed tear in the world barrier beneath the Ladder Stump. Outer demons have come through it twice.
entries.lore: The sea around the Ladder Stump is glass-calm and black, and divine sense slides off it. The Seal Watch sinks anything that sails inside the marker buoys.
entries.truth: The seal is the Nameless Sealer. Her cultivation has held Heaven's Scar shut for 3,127 years, and the rising tide is pulling it open faster than she can mend it.

entries.name: The Ladder Stump
entries.summary: What is left of the Heaven Ladder: a pillar as wide as a kingdom, rising from the Shattered Sea and ending in broken jade above the clouds.
entries.lore: On clear nights it is visible from the inner coast of every continent, a black line against the Mirror. The Seal Watch's fortress rings its base. The Ladder Stump hums when the Mirror is overhead.
entries.truth: Armillary Pavilion survey teams have climbed it in secret. The top is not broken. It was cut clean.

entries.name: Thousand Isles
entries.summary: An archipelago in the Shoreless Sea between the Morning Star Continent and the Vast Wilds Continent: closer to ten thousand islands than a thousand, and every one has a lord.
entries.lore: Island sects cultivate water and storm arts, pirate lords raid every coast, and free ports buy anything without asking where it came from.

top.note: the Isles League's three island masters

entries.name: Thousand Puppet Gate
entries.summary: Demonic corpse refiners who mine the Fallen Ladder's tombs for immortal bodies and turn them into puppets.
entries.lore: A body that once held immortal qi never rots. The Gate digs them out of the Fallen Ladder, refines them into puppets that fight at their old realm, and sells them to anyone who pays. The Court of No Light calls this theft of its subjects and is at war with the Gate in all but name. Nobody makes better puppets.
entries.truth: Some of their best puppets are not empty. The Gate's master does not know. The fullest of them holds the soul of a Body Integration immortal from the Age of the Ascent, awake and patient.

ties.why: The Jiao clan sneers at corpse-craft from behind its lightning-struck wood and sells to none who deal with us.

entries.name: Heavenly Scale Pavilion
entries.summary: The merchant house of the whole world. It runs the great auctions, changes spirit stones between grades and enforces contracts with karmic oaths.
entries.lore: From Fallen Star City, the Heavenly Scale Pavilion runs branches in every great city on every continent. Its one law is written over every door: no blood on the scale. Fight inside a hall of the Heavenly Scale Pavilion and every branch in the world will refuse you, forever. It lends to empires, bankrolls both sides of most wars, and sets the price of a Foundation Pill for the whole world each spring.
entries.truth: The Heavenly Scale Pavilion holds the debts of four great powers. If it called them in at once, two would fall. Every karmic oath the Pavilion writes is sworn to the Founding Scale, a Body Integration merchant no living client has met. Two of its Scale-Keepers are at Void Refinement.

ties.why: Our branch at the Mouth writes futures on the heartland's grain, and no blood is ever spilled on its scale.
Our dawn price is the south's grain price, and our weighing hall is the one floor where no blood is spilled.
The Society's appraisal hall sends us its finds first, and we pay in stones no one else on the coast has.
We keep a banker at every counter in the pill halls and take our cut of every sale.

entries.name: Void Choir
entries.summary: A secret cult that hears the outer demons singing through the seal and wants to let them in.
entries.lore: Most people think the Void Choir is a story to frighten disciples. Its members hide in every sect and every city. Their sign is a cultivator humming a tune nobody taught them.
entries.truth: Some of its leaders are possessed by outer demons who slipped out during the war. They are patient.

ties.why: We let the hunger spread our tune through the Banner; a starving crowd is the easiest gate to open.

entries.name: The Void Sea
entries.summary: The endless dark between worlds. Worlds drift in it like islands, and the great ones' gravity gathers the smaller around them.
entries.lore: Great thousand worlds hang in the Void Sea like suns, each with a crowd of middle thousand worlds circling it, and each of those with its own swarm of small worlds. Nothing lives in the void that a sane cultivator wants to meet.
entries.truth: Outer demons are the Void Sea's native life. They feed on worlds' qi and are drawn to anything that pierces a world barrier.

entries.name: Ten Thousand Sails
entries.summary: The free port of the Thousand Isles: no laws, no questions, and ten thousand sails in the harbor. A hub of the Heavenly Circuit.
entries.lore: Anything can be bought in Ten Thousand Sails, including people, and anything can be sold, including your name.

entries.name: Severed Heaven
entries.summary: A prosperous middle thousand world: a flat disc of land and sea about a million li across, drifting in the Void Sea around the great world mortals call the Mirror.
entries.lore:
Scholars call the world Severed Heaven, after the day its ladder to the Upper Realm broke. Maps carved before the break call it Tongtian, Heaven-Reaching. Most mortals never learn either name; to them it is simply all under heaven.

Six continents ring the Shattered Sea, where the Ladder Stump still rises from the water. Past them lies the Shoreless Sea, then the Rim, where the ocean pours over the world's edge into the void.

It is year 3,127 of the Sealed Era. Qi is the richest in sixty-six thousand years and still rising. Sects crowd every spirit vein, geniuses are born every generation, and everyone races to climb before the tide turns.
entries.truth: The tide will peak in about two thousand years. The same pull that floods the world with qi is stretching the seal over Heaven's Scar, and the Seal Watch knows it is failing faster than it admits. A handful of Tribulation Transcenders are alive. Most hide from their last tribulation or wait for the tide's peak to ascend; the Nameless Sealer is bound inside the seal.

entries.name: Shoreless Sea
entries.summary: The outer ocean around the six continents. Sea clan territory: ships pay toll or vanish.
entries.lore: Its name comes from the old saying that life has a shore and knowledge has none. Beyond the continents the water deepens into trenches no human has sounded, and the sea clans' cities glow at the bottom.

top.note: the Sea Sovereign, one pearl short of a true dragon

entries.name: Apricot Grove Valley
entries.summary: The greatest alchemy and medicine sect on the Morning Star Continent, a forest of a billion apricot trees around the richest herb gardens in the world. Everyone needs them, so nobody touches them.
entries.lore: Apricot Grove Valley's founder healed the poor for free and asked only that each patient plant an apricot tree. The valley is now a forest of a billion trees a thousand li across, around the richest herb gardens on the continent, the pill towers of the Alchemy Hall standing out of the canopy like peaks. They heal all sides for a price, sell pills to empires and demonic sects alike, and their Alchemy Hall heads are courted like princes.
entries.truth: Apricot Grove Valley keeps its grip on the herb trade by quietly seeding blight in rival gardens. The Valley Master calls it hygiene. The Valley Master is a Void Refinement alchemist who has outlived three dynasties by keeping all of them in his debt.
entries.fromAbove: A dark-green sea of apricot forest a thousand li across, the pale pill towers of the Alchemy Hall standing out of the canopy and the smoke of its furnaces drifting east in a long column.

ties.why: The Butchers are our steadiest source of beast cores, and we pay them enough to keep it that way.
The court accuses us of its blight and still sends its princes to buy our pills.
The Gate blames our herbs for its failed fields, and still buys our pills.
The tenant kingdom grows our herbs on contracts older than its king; we keep the ledger, and we lend the apprentices.
The ridge keeps the sea winds off our gardens, and our patrols keep thieves off the ridge.
The Hill is our last rival, and we keep it small: its gardens die and its bounties go unclaimed.
The city at our mouth sells our pills at posted prices and holds every sick traveler until they pay.
The Society's dropouts treat the poor we will not, and we use their camps as cheap labor for the epidemics.
Lingzhi Gardens would not sell us its caves, and now it blames the blight on us.

features.name: the apricot forest, a tree for every patient healed
the Alchemy Hall's furnace towers
the herb gardens' terraces

entries.name: Hundred Herb Market
entries.summary: The basin's market town, where Palace buyers, tribe traders and Frost Fair merchants bid for fire-and-ice herbs at the first-dawn auction.
entries.lore: Built on stilts over warm ground, the town has more herb sellers than houses. The great auction is held at first dawn, when the polar night ends and the year's herbs are cured, and its prices are quoted at the Frost Fair for the rest of the year. Appraisers grade herbs by age for a fee. Faking an herb's age is a hanging offense under market law, enforced by Cold Flame Valley's disciples. Alchemists rent furnace rooms by the day.

entries.name: White Bone Flats
entries.summary: The sky-burial ground of the Iron Bone Tribes, where the dead are left for eagles and wolves. The bones of a hundred generations of body cultivators whiten the flats.
entries.lore: A body cultivator's bones outlast stone; a chief's thighbone can be used as a hammer. The tribes lay their dead here and never come back for them. Dawnless City refiners pay a mid-grade spirit stone for a Foundation body cultivator's skeleton, and bone thieves come every winter. A tribe that catches one breaks every bone in his body and leaves him here alive. The Eagle-Master tribe keeps watch from the cliffs, for a fee.
entries.truth: On still nights the bones shift a little toward Ancestor Mountain. The Bone Ancestor is drawing what is left of his descendants back to him.

entries.name: The White Blind
entries.summary: A stretch of ice sheet west of the glacier where the blizzard never stops. The tribes say this is where the demons' bad dreams come out.
entries.lore: Inside the White Blind the wind never drops below a gale and you cannot see your own hand. Divine sense frays in it like rope. Caravans that cut through it between the Spine and the fortress lose a third of their animals; Qi Condensation cultivators who lose the rope freeze within a day. Ice Dao cultivators who survive a month inside come out with a cold in their meridians that never leaves, and sometimes with a breakthrough.

entries.name: Kingdom of White Walls
entries.summary: The largest coastal kingdom, behind three rings of whitewashed walls. It has paid tribute to every Great Khan for three hundred years and is proud never to have fallen.
entries.lore: The Lin dynasty rules by one rule: keep the walls white and the tribute ready. Every adult serves a month a year on the walls, and children learn the bell signals before their letters. The royal guard has a dozen Foundation cultivators trained by the North Wind Sword Gate. The kingdom ships ivory and furs through Stone Ship Harbor and imports the grain it cannot grow. Its treasury is empty: the last tribute was paid with a [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] loan, and the loan falls due the same winter the next Great Khan is expected.
entries.truth: Sea-Crossing Temple has quietly bought the loan. If the kingdom defaults, the monks own the walls.

entries.name: Blizzard Camp
entries.summary: The Iron Bone Tribes' winter school of the Fist Dao, open to outsiders who survive the entrance. Most foreigners leave with broken hands; a few leave unbreakable.
entries.lore: The camp sits in the open on the northern steppe for the whole polar night. Entrance is the Blizzard Run: a night walking naked in the storm, and whoever stops, dies. Those who finish are fed, beaten, and taught to break stone with their fists and take a sword cut on the forearm. The teachers rode with the last Great Khan; they despise qi cultivators and teach them twice as hard. A student who reaches Foundation Establishment in body gets a tribe name and a place in the next raid.
entries.truth: The camp's master is training a hundred outsiders, not tribesmen, as the Snow Wolf claimant's personal guard. He thinks a khan's guard should owe nothing to any tribe.

entries.name: Court of the Northern Bears
entries.summary: The white bears of the pack ice, ruled by a Nascent Soul bear king who has taken human form. They hunt seals, walrus and humans with equal interest.
entries.lore: The Bear King walks among humans as a huge, silent man in a sealskin coat and buys salt and honey at the Floe Market. His court is a dozen Core Formation bears and several hundred lesser ones. They hold the pack ice and the shore cliffs, hunt anyone who takes their cubs and leave alone those who leave them alone. Beast tamers prize white bear cubs above any mount on the continent. The Seal Tribe blames the bears for its missing hunters, and the Bear King has let it.
entries.truth: The Bear King knows what is taking the hunters, because it has taken bears too. He is afraid of it, and he has never been afraid of anything.

entries.name: Ice Bridgehead
entries.summary: The headland where, in the hardest winters, the sea ice reaches across the strait toward the Myriad Sands Continent. A fort and a shrine mark where raiders set out and refugees come home.
entries.lore: In most winters the strait is open water and drifting floes. In a hard one the ice runs from this headland toward the Myriad Sands Continent's northern cliffs, a crossing only cultivators and spirit-beast riders survive. The last Great Khan's vanguard crossed here, and few came back. The fort is held by whichever kingdom paid the North Wind Sword Gate most recently, and the shrine is the temple's. Ice guides gather at the first freeze and sell their services by the day.

entries.name: Ice-Fisher Tribe
entries.summary: Seal hunters and ice fishers who winter on the bay's western ice. They know where the sea ice is thin, and every caravan and every raid needs them.
entries.lore: Ice-Fisher camps move out onto the frozen bay at the first freeze and come ashore at the thaw. Their children learn to read ice by its color and its sound before they learn to swim, because swimming will not save them. They hunt seals at breathing holes and fish through the ice on lines a li long. The Iron Bone tribes despise them as fish-eaters and need them as guides. Their elders charge a low-grade spirit stone a day to guide a caravan across the ice.
entries.truth: The last Great Khan died on the sea ice because an Ice-Fisher guide led his army onto a current lead. The tribe has never admitted it, and the Snow Wolf chief has started asking.

entries.name: Realm of the Unsetting Sun
entries.summary: A shard world that passes closest at midsummer every seven years and opens as a ring of light on the steppe for twelve days. Only cultivators below Foundation Establishment can enter.
entries.lore: Inside, the sun hangs at noon and never moves: a grass world full of sunfire grass, golden locust swarms and herds of fire-maned horses. The tribes send their youths in as a rite, and a youth who comes back with a sunfire horse is made a rider on the spot. Alchemists pay a low-grade spirit stone a stalk for sunfire grass, which keeps meridians warm through the polar night. A Foundation aura cracks the gate, and whoever is inside when it cracks stays until the next opening.
entries.truth: Time runs slower inside. The few who have been shut in through a closing came out seven years later having lived a single day.

entries.name: Fief of the Broken Tower
entries.summary: A cultivator family's fief inside a half-buried Ascent Age tower. The Mu family claims salvage rights on every ruin within three thousand li and takes a tenth.
entries.lore: The Mu family moved into the Broken Tower two centuries ago, broke the guardian puppets that still walked its halls and found the lower floors full of formation plates. They sell plates, puppet parts and appraised relics through agents at the Frost Fair, and their tower is the only warm, walled place in the waste, so scavenger crews winter there and pay for it. Four Foundation cultivators and a hundred guards keep the tenth collected. Mu children learn appraisal before letters, and the family's young appraisers are the best on the continent.
entries.truth: The Mu salvage decree is a forgery. The Palace knows, and lets it stand because the Mu send their best finds to the Night Sovereign every year.

entries.name: Keep of the Long Lamp
entries.summary: A small, prosperous frost fief whose lord keeps a great lamp burning on his tower through the whole polar night. Travelers lost on the ice steer for it.
entries.lore: Forty years ago the lord was mauled by a white bear on the ice and carried home for dead. He recovered, lit the Long Lamp, and since then nobody in his fief has frozen or starved. His people are healthy, his granaries full, and he takes in anyone who reaches his gate. He rarely leaves his tower and has not visibly aged. His people hum a harvest song at work that nobody remembers learning. Seal Watch patrols have stopped there twice and reported nothing unusual.
entries.truth: The lord died on the ice. The outer demon that escaped the Palace wears him now, feeds on travelers who steer for the lamp and keeps its own villagers fat and warm. The song is the Frozen Host's.

entries.name: Midwinter Tide Realm
entries.summary: A gate under a western fjord that rises above the water only at the lowest tide of midwinter, every third year, for three days. Only Qi Condensation cultivators can pass.
entries.lore: When the great midwinter ebb pulls the fjord down, a stone arch rises from the water with a drowned island behind it: tide pools full of spirit pearls, crab-folk who fight with stolen harpoons and a shrine nobody has opened. A Foundation aura cracks the arch. The Whale Tooth kings sell passage to young cultivators for twenty low-grade spirit stones. The sea clans consider the island theirs and sometimes wait inside.

entries.name: Slumbering City
entries.summary: An Ascent Age city frozen whole into the permafrost. Its outer streets are tunnels that scavengers work; its inner city still runs its formations and kills.
entries.lore: The outer city has been picked over for centuries: tunnels through ice-choked streets, empty shops, a frozen guardian puppet that still twitches. The inner city is another matter. Its walls still run their formations, and anything that crosses them without the right token is cut apart by ice blades that form out of the air. Crews pay for maps, for tokens taken off earlier crews' bodies and for appraisers who can tell a working formation plate from a dead one. Thousand Puppet Gate buyers wait at the edge to buy whole puppets.
entries.truth: At the center, behind the last ward, an Ascent Age master sits frozen in meditation. He chose to sleep through the Ebb, and the rising tide is thawing him.

entries.name: Red Spring Fief
entries.summary: Warm valleys on the south side of the ranges where red iron springs keep barley growing through the polar night. Its mortal lords pay the Eternal Night Palace in children.
entries.lore: The Lan family has ruled the Red Spring valleys for four hundred years by paying the Palace's blood tithe on time: a hundred youths every Long Night, drawn by lottery in the village squares. Families hide children with spirit roots in the steam caves, because the Palace takes the gifted first. The springs feed barley, black goats and the only orchards north of the strait. No child of a noble house has been drawn for nine years running, and the villages have begun to count.
entries.truth: The lottery is rigged, and the Lan heir hates it. He has been smuggling hidden children south to the [[Sea-Crossing Temple]], and the Palace will notice the missing count by spring.

entries.name: Kingdom of Ship Timber
entries.summary: A mortal coastal kingdom that cuts black pine masts and builds ships for the Floating Peak Continent and the Shattered Sea's scavenger sects. Its queen was born into one of the Floating Peak Continent's clans.
entries.lore: The Gao kings have built ships for three hundred years, and their yards are the only ones north of the strait that can lay a keel for an ocean hull. The present king married a Floating Peak clanswoman born without her clan's bloodline and sent down from the floating peaks to serve; she is cleverer than he is, and the court knows it. Children grow up in the yards and timber camps. Those with spirit roots are sent to the Thunder-Feather Lodge for testing, and those who pass are never seen in the kingdom again.

entries.name: Kingdom of Spring Gardens
entries.summary: A mortal farming kingdom in the basin's warm south, ruled by a council of farm elders. It grows the only fresh greens on the continent and pays tithes to three masters.
entries.lore: Children here grow up barefoot in warm mud in the middle of the polar night, which no other child on the continent can say. Nine farm elders rule by harvest weight: the families who bring in the most herbs sit highest. They pay the Palace in herbs, the Musk Ox Tribe in grain and the Seal Watch in labor, and marry daughters into the tribes for grazing peace. A child who can tell a ten-year snow ginseng from a hundred-year one by smell is apprenticed to Cold Flame Valley, and the family's tithe is forgiven for a year.

entries.name: Cornerstone Gang
entries.summary: A Frost Fair gang of smugglers and ice-burial killers. Pay them, and your problem ends up frozen into a foundation.
entries.lore: The Cornerstone Gang runs the Fair's smuggling, pickpockets and protection, and it helps rebuild the Fair every winter, which is where it got its name. Its real trade is the ice burial: a body set in the foundations as the water freezes, found in spring when nobody can say when it died. It is mortals and Qi Condensation cultivators with a few Foundation enforcers, and it recruits orphans off the docks. It pays the Palace's tax collectors more than the honest merchants do, and they leave it alone.
entries.truth: Its boss failed the Palace's Ash Gate thirty years ago and swore to bury a Palace elder in the ice before he dies. He has finally found a client who will pay for it.

entries.name: Earth's Eye Spring
entries.summary: A boiling spring a li across in the middle of the basin, over a mid-grade fire spirit vein. Three powers share it under an arrangement none of them likes.
entries.lore: The spring boils from below with a slow heartbeat, and its steam carries so much fire qi that a Qi Condensation cultivator who sits in it for a month can break through, if he survives the heat. The Palace, the Iron Bone tribes and Cold Flame Valley each hold a third of its shore under an agreement made sixty years ago, after a battle that boiled forty men alive. Fire Dao cultivators pay a low-grade spirit stone a day to sit at the edge. The water has dropped three feet this year.

entries.name: Field of Broken Spears
entries.summary: The Outer Demon War battlefield south of the glacier, where the northern line held for eleven years. Broken artifacts and frozen defenders still lie under the snow.
entries.lore: Every thaw uncovers something: a spearhead that still hums, a talisman case, a defender frozen with his hands up. Outer demons left no bodies, only black glass where they died, and Frost Fair appraisers pay well for glass and gear alike. The Left-Behind fief claims a tenth of every find and enforces it. Demon glass gives off a cold that keeps meat for a year, and a smell that draws ice wolves from fifty li.
entries.truth: Some of the black glass is not dead. It warms in the hand when someone nearby hums.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Sheer Cliffs
entries.summary: A cliff-walled fjord kingdom of wreckers and pirates who prey on the Whale Tooth fleet and sell captives at Chain-Gate Harbor.
entries.lore: The fjord's mouth is so narrow that one chain can close it, and the Sheer Cliff lords have lived behind that chain for four centuries, raiding everyone else's boats. They light false beacons on the outer cliffs to draw ships onto the rocks and keep whatever washes ashore. Their warriors climb sheer ice with hand-claws, and their children start by robbing gull nests. They hate the Whale Tooth kings and would love to watch the sea clans finish them.
entries.truth: Their queen has sent an envoy to the Cold Jiao Mansion offering to guide its hunters into the Whale Tooth fjord.

entries.name: Sea-Crossing Temple
entries.summary: The Thousand Lamps Temple's northern mission on the Sand-Gazing Shore. Its monks treat frostbite and raid wounds for anyone, preach to raiders and ransom captives.
entries.lore: Forty monks and a Nascent Soul abbot crossed from Myriad Sands two centuries ago and built a hospital before they built a hall. They teach medicine, the vajra body and patience. They will not kill, but they have broken the arms of three Palace slavers who came for their orphans. They ransom captives from the tribes with temple money and settle the freed on temple land, and raiders who wake in the temple's beds sometimes stay. The coastal kings love them and owe them, which is how the temple prefers it.
entries.truth: The temple has been buying the coastal kingdoms' debts through the Heavenly Scale Pavilion brokers for fifty years. Within a generation it will own the Sand-Gazing Shore without converting a single king.

entries.name: Marsh of Boiling Springs
entries.summary: The eastern marsh of the basin, where pools boil up without warning under a skin of moss. Frostflame lotus grows thick at its heart, guarded by ember toads and steam leeches.
entries.lore: The ground is moss over hot mud, and new pools open under it every day. Steam leeches the length of an arm drink qi rather than blood, and ember toads spit burning slime. At the heart, where a cold spring rises among the hot ones, frostflame lotus grows thicker than anywhere else in the world. Pickers rope themselves together in lines of five, and a line that comes back with four is considered lucky.

entries.name: Forest of Wind Pillars
entries.summary: A field of basalt columns on the tableland where the wind sings through ten thousand pillars. Wind Dao cultivators come to listen, and ice wolf packs den among the stones.
entries.lore: The columns are six-sided, packed like a honeycomb and broken off at every height, and in a north wind they sing a chord you feel in your teeth. Wind Dao cultivators sit among them to learn to hear qi move in air, and a few learn to ride the gusts between the pillars. Ice wolf packs den in the gaps. The Snow Wolf tribe takes pups here each spring and loses a rider or two to the mothers every year.

entries.name: Floe Market
entries.summary: A summer trading post on the shore of the Utter North, where whalers, seal hunters, smugglers and sea clan envoys meet while the ice is out.
entries.lore: In winter it is forty empty longhouses under the snow. When the pack ice breaks up in early summer it fills: seal oil, walrus and mammoth ivory, white bear pelts, glacier relics smuggled from the south and sea clan pearls change hands under the midnight sun. A sea clan envoy sits in a tide pool at the end of the pier and takes toll from every boat. Disputes go to the market's three elders: one human, one half-blood and one jiao.

entries.name: Fief of Ancient Tusks
entries.summary: A fief of fossil-ivory diggers who mine the permafrost for the tusks of mammoths dead seventy thousand years. Some of the old tusks still hold beast cores.
entries.lore: The Dou family holds the fief by right of having killed the family that held it before, and sells to the Floating Peak Continent's artifact refiners through Harbor of Distant Peaks. Diggers thaw the permafrost with fire and dig out tusks, bones and now and then a whole frozen mammoth with its meat still red. A tusk from an Ascent Age mammoth king can hold a core worth more than the fief. The Giant-Blood tribe calls it grave robbing and has burned the diggings twice. Diggers are paid by the tusk, and most die of the cold or the herds.

entries.name: Seal Tribe
entries.summary: Seal hunters of the ice edge, who follow the pack ice out each winter. Their hunting parties are the ones disappearing.
entries.lore: Seal Tribe hunters can lie still on the ice by a breathing hole for a day and a night, and their children practice by lying still in the snow until a fox comes to sniff them. They trade oil, hides and walrus ivory at the Floe Market and pay the sea clans one seal in ten, left on the ice for the jiao. They fight the white bears for the same seals and lose a hunter or two each winter. In the last forty years they have lost eleven whole parties, each found as an empty camp. The young hunters have started to go armed against men.

entries.name: Petrel Kingdom
entries.summary: A mortal merchant kingdom on the east shore of Glass Bay that owns the Frost Fair's land side: wharves, warehouses and the summer town.
entries.lore: The Fu merchant kings have ruled for three hundred years by paying protection to the Palace and tribute to whichever khan is strongest, and by never building walls high enough to insult either. Children grow up as dock hands and ice-cutters. A child with a spirit root is sold at the Fair's root market to the highest sect bid, and the family eats well for ten years. The old king is dying, and his two sons have chosen patrons: the elder the Palace, the young Snow Wolf claimant.
entries.truth: The king is not dying of age. The elder son's Palace patron has been salting his bread with Blood Salt Lake salt, a pinch a day.

entries.name: Kingdom of Cold Souls
entries.summary: A ghost fief on the northern barrens. A kingdom froze here in a single night during the Outer Demon War, and its dead still keep court through the polar night and fade in the midnight sun.
entries.lore: When the sun sets for the half-year, the old kingdom's ghosts rise in their frozen capital: a king, his court, his tax collectors. Living settlers rent land from the dead by leaving lamps lit and a drop of blood at each threshold every month; those who refuse wake colder each morning until they do not wake. Children learn never to let a lamp go out. The ghost king judges disputes fairly and remembers everything. Ghost Way cultivators come to bargain for the court's lore, and the [[Court of No Light]] has sent an envoy to enter its dead in the registers.
entries.truth: The kingdom did not freeze by accident. Its king bargained with an outer demon for a cultivation method and paid with his people's warmth. His court has forgotten the bargain, and the Night Sovereign's envoys have started asking the ghost king to remember it.

entries.name: Cold Flame Valley
entries.summary: An alchemy and medicine sect in a steaming side valley of the basin. It makes fire-and-ice pills and the body-tempering baths the tribes buy by the barrel.
entries.lore: The Valley's founder learned to balance fire and ice herbs in one cauldron, and its pills are the only ones on the continent that treat frozen meridians and fire deviation alike. It brews tempering baths for the Iron Bone tribes, salves for the Seal Watch and, quietly, blood pills for the Palace. It recruits farm children with good noses and teaches alchemy, medicine and the Fire and Ice Daos. It wants the Earth's Eye Spring's vein for a new furnace hall, and hates the Palace's herb officers, who take the best roots before the auction.

entries.name: Black Pine Tribe
entries.summary: A forest tribe of trappers and elk riders in the deep taiga. They are Iron Bone in name and nobody's in fact, and they worship the Pine of Ten Thousand Ages.
entries.lore: Black Pine hunters ride spirit elk through timber too thick for horses and trap sable, lynx and ice marten for the fur trade. They temper their bodies like the steppe tribes but fight with axes, which the steppe tribes find embarrassing. Their children are given a sapling at birth and are buried under it. They tolerate loggers who cut where they say and kill those who do not, and the coastal kingdom's timber camps push further in every year. Their shamans tend the ancient pine and say it dreams in spring.

entries.name: Obsidian Ranges
entries.summary: The black volcanic ranges of the west, where lava glows through the polar night and the Eternal Night Palace rules from the heights. Black iron, obsidian, sulfur and slaves flow out of every pass.
entries.lore: Fire runs under the ice here. The Burning Spine's vents keep lakes open and passes warm through the polar night, and the Eternal Night Palace holds all but the Hearth Clan's. Its fiefs mine black iron with slaves taken on steppe raids and pay a blood tithe of youths each Long Night. In the first month of darkness anyone may climb to the Palace's Ash Gate; those who survive a season in its outer court become disciples, and the rest go to the mines. Elders buy each other's deaths through the Contract Hall in Dawnless City. Three elders have vanished in ten years, and the Palace has stopped claiming it ate them.
entries.truth: The vanished elders were sent to the thaw works under the glacier. The Night Sovereign lets nobody who has seen a thawed demon come home.

top.note: the Night Sovereign, who never sleeps

entries.name: Realm of Returning Light
entries.summary: A gate in a ring of standing stones where the aurora touches the ground every nine years at the depth of the polar night. It stays open nine days, and a Core Formation aura cracks it.
entries.lore: When the gate opens, the aurora pours down into the stone ring like water into a funnel, and anyone below Core Formation can walk into a shard world of blue ice and slow light. Inside are ice spirit veins lying open on the surface, aurora moths whose wing dust makes the finest talisman ink, and the ruins of a town. The Frozen Radiance Observatory announces the date a year ahead, and the Armillary Pavilion's tables agree to the day. The next opening is in two years.
entries.truth: The town is still inhabited. Its people descend from Severance survivors, speak an Ascent Age dialect and kill outsiders on sight, because the last visitors took their children.

entries.name: Hearth Clan
entries.summary: A mountain clan that lives in lava tubes in the eastern half of the Burning Spine, warm all year, with bodies tempered in volcanic heat.
entries.lore: Hearth Clan children are bathed in vent steam until their skin stops blistering, and their warriors can hold a coal until it goes out. They answer to neither the Palace nor the Iron Bone Tribes and live by guiding both through lava tubes that kill everyone else. They gather ember moss and fire salamander skins for Dawnless City. The Palace has asked twice to lease their three deepest vents, and twice the clan's old mother has refused.
entries.truth: The Palace wants those vents to pipe fire under the glacier for its thaw works. A third refusal will be answered with an army, and the old mother knows it.

entries.name: Amber Kingdom
entries.summary: A small coastal kingdom that digs amber from buried ancient forests. The Floating Peak Continent's array masters buy it, because clear amber holds a formation better than jade.
entries.lore: Under the coastal dunes lie forests drowned a hundred thousand years ago, and their resin has turned to amber: honey-gold, sometimes holding insects, sometimes something larger. Array masters pay well for clear amber, which holds a formation for centuries, and the Armillary Pavilion's agents buy the best and set the price. The Shen amber-merchant family rules, with a Foundation cultivator heir who studies formations. Children dig the dunes for pocket money, and a child who finds spirit amber, with qi trapped inside, can clear a family's debts.

entries.name: Aurora Waste
entries.summary: The northwestern barrens between the Obsidian Ranges and the Rim coast, where the aurora hangs lowest and Ascent Age ruins break through the permafrost. Ice Dao cultivators come to watch the sky.
entries.lore: During the polar night the aurora hangs so low over these flats that it hums, and Ice Dao cultivators sit at the [[Forest of Frost Steles]] for weeks waiting for insight; some freeze where they sit. Wherever the ground heaves, Ascent Age walls and towers break through the permafrost, and scavenger crews from the Frost Fair camp here every summer and fight each other for the best ground. The richest is the Slumbering City, whose inner wards still kill Core Formation cultivators. Reindeer herders follow the lights and treat the scavengers like weather. The Eternal Night Palace claims the waste and enforces the claim about once a decade, brutally.
entries.truth: The aurora is the world barrier glowing where it is thinnest, close to the Rim. It has doubled in brightness in a century as the tide stretches the barrier, and the steles have started to answer it.

entries.name: Silent Plain
entries.summary: A plain in the south of the Utter North where the wind stops and sound dies. People who cross it alone do not arrive, and lately neither do groups.
entries.lore: Inside the Silent Plain your footsteps make no sound and your shout does not reach your own ears. Hunters have always gone around it, though the trail around takes ten days longer. In the last forty years parties that went around have vanished too, and tracks have been found leading into the plain from both sides and none coming out. The seal hunters say something lives in the silence. The Seal Watch marked it forbidden after its second patrol.
entries.truth: It is where the escaped demon first fed. It eats voices first, so its prey cannot call for help, and it can speak in every voice it has eaten.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Whale Tooth
entries.summary: A whaling kingdom in the largest fjord, ruled by harpooner kings. Its whale oil lights the polar night on half the continent.
entries.lore: The Hu dynasty won its crown with harpoons and keeps it the same way: the king throws the first iron of the spring hunt, and a king who misses is replaced by whoever does not. Children with spirit roots become harpooners, whose thrown iron can pierce a whale's skull. Oil, bone and ambergris go out through the Frost Fair and pay for grain. This winter one of their ships killed an ice jiao calf, and the Cold Jiao Mansion has demanded the captain, his family and the king's eldest son. The king has offered spirit stones instead.

entries.name: Ember Realm
entries.summary: The gate of a shard world of cooling lava, opening in the throat of a dead volcano every twelve years for thirty days. Only cultivators below Core Formation can pass.
entries.lore: When the Ember Shard swings close, the volcano's throat fills with red light. Anyone below Core Formation can walk in; a Core aura cracks the gate and burns whoever wore it. Inside are black glass plains, fire spirit stones lying loose, salamanders the size of oxen and, in deep pockets, seeds of earth fire that refiners would kill for. The Palace auctions entry tokens in Dawnless City. The next opening is in four years, and tokens already sell for a mid-grade spirit stone.
entries.truth: The shard is a piece of the central continent's old foundries, thrown out in the Severance. Somewhere inside is a forge that still remembers how the Ladder's jade was made.

entries.name: The Old Fairs
entries.summary: A line of abandoned Frost Fair foundations stretching up the bay, each frozen where it was left. Scavengers pick them over every spring and find someone frozen in the ice.
entries.lore: The Fair has moved south for as long as anyone remembers, and its old sites stay where they were: rings of piling, rotted platforms and sunken stalls, all locked in ice that never fully thaws. Spring scavengers find lost goods, spirit stones dropped through the cracks and, every year, at least one body frozen upright in a foundation. Ice-Fisher children dare each other to sleep there. The truce council investigates each body and has never named a killer.
entries.truth: The bodies are the Cornerstone Gang's work, paid for by whoever wants someone gone. The council knows, because two of its members are clients.

entries.name: Giant-Blood Tribe
entries.summary: A tribe of giant-blooded half-bloods who live with the mammoth herds. Grown, they stand twelve feet tall; one in five does not survive the fever that wakes the blood.
entries.lore: Giant-Blood children look human until about fifteen, when the blood wakes in a month-long fever. Those who live grow a head taller every year until they stop at ten or twelve feet, with bones like iron and tempers to match. Most of the continent calls them half-beasts. The Iron Bone tribes call them cousins and want them as champions, and the Mammoth Tribe's chief has offered marriages. The elders refuse every alliance: they go where the herds go. Their young, who want glory, have started slipping away to the claimants' camps.

entries.name: Weeping Hills
entries.summary: The ruins of a coastal kingdom burned by the last Great Khan sixty years ago. Its dead have not left, and in Ghost Month they walk the walls.
entries.lore: The kingdom refused tribute, and the Khan made an example of it: walls broken, every adult killed, children taken north. Sixty years on the hills still weep at night, and the resentment has curdled into ghosts strong enough to kill a Foundation cultivator in the seventh month. Ghost Way cultivators from Long Dusk come to harvest them, monks from Sea-Crossing Temple come to release them, and the two have fought here twice. The old royal vault is still somewhere under the ash.
entries.truth: Some of the children taken north are grandparents in the Snow Wolf tribe now. The ghosts know their own blood when they see it, and do not touch it.

entries.name: Clan of the Old Mammoths
entries.summary: The awakened mammoths of the tableland, led by the Gray Matriarch, a Nascent Soul mammoth who has taken human form only once in living memory.
entries.lore: The herds migrate in a great circle around the tableland and down to the Warm Basin's edge, and the matriarchs choose the route. The Gray Matriarch took human form sixty years ago to bargain with the last Great Khan; he got his mammoths for the ride south, most of them never came back, and she has not forgiven the tribes. Anyone who harms a calf is trampled. Anyone who returns a stolen one is owed a favor. Her herds would decide any war on the continent, and both claimants know it.

entries.name: Thunder-Feather Lodge
entries.summary: The trading lodge of a branch of the Floating Peak Continent's thunder-blooded clan, on the hill above Harbor of Distant Peaks. It buys, lends and tests local children for bloodlines.
entries.lore: A Nascent Soul elder of the thunder clan runs the lodge with twenty clan members and two hundred hired guards. It buys amber, ivory and mammoth calves, lends to the coastal kingdoms at kind rates, and tests local children for traces of old bloodlines; any who show one are shipped to the Floating Peak Continent. Its walls have been rebuilt three times in ten years, each time thicker. The Black Pine Tribe says the lodge is cutting a road into the forest toward the Pine of Ten Thousand Ages.
entries.truth: The clan wants the tableland's Ascent Age mammoth-king cores to refresh its thinning bloodline, and is buying the Fief of Ancient Tusks' debts to get them. The road is for the Pine's heartwood.

entries.name: Cold Jiao Mansion
entries.summary: The sea clans' northern court, a lodge of ice jiao under the outer fjords that collects the Azure Wave Palace's tolls along the Black Frost Continent's western and northern coasts.
entries.lore: The Cold Jiao Lord is a Nascent Soul flood dragon of the cold seas, sworn to the Sea Sovereign of the [[Azure Wave Palace]], ruling from a palace of ice beneath the outer fjords. Every ship that sails past the fjord mouths pays a tenth of its catch or a tenth of its crew. The jiao leave alone humans who pay and hunt to the last cousin those who kill their young. This winter a Whale Tooth ship killed one of the Lord's grandchildren, and the Lord has given the Whale Tooth king until the first dawn to hand over the captain's line.
entries.truth: The Lord failed a dragon tribulation two centuries ago and is hoarding cold for a second try. He covets the glacier more than any toll.

entries.name: Lake of the Two Forms
entries.summary: A lake divided down the middle: one half boils, the other is frozen solid, and the line between them never moves. Fire and Ice cultivators both come to sit on the line.
entries.lore: A hot spring feeds the east half and a glacier stream the west, and they meet along a line as straight as a ruler that has not shifted in recorded history. Sitting on the line is said to give insight into the Fire and Ice Daos at once; most who try are scalded on one side and frostbitten on the other. Cold Flame Valley disciples sit there as their final trial. A Nascent Soul cultivator once tried to push the line with his qi, and the lake drowned him.
entries.truth: The line is a formation. An Ascent Age alchemist built the lake as a cauldron, and the lid is still down there.

entries.name: Chain-Gate Harbor
entries.summary: The Eternal Night Palace's ice-free port on the western fjords. A black iron chain across the fjord mouth decides who sails in and who leaves.
entries.lore: Slaves, black iron, blood pills and whale oil go out; grain, salt, spirit stones and prisoners come in. The Palace's harbor master is a Core Formation elder who settles disputes by drowning the loser. The sea clans keep a tide-house on the quay where captains pay toll before sailing into the Shoreless Sea, and it is the one building in the harbor Palace disciples will not enter. Sailors, guards and dock hands are hired on the quay every morning, and some of them are sold there by evening.

entries.name: Cliff Over the Ruin
entries.summary: The northernmost cliff of the Utter North, where an Ascent Age beacon tower faces the Rim. On some nights its dead formations flicker on their own.
entries.lore: The tower is older than the Severance, built of a gray stone that frost does not crack, and its beacon formation still holds a faint charge. Texts in the Broken Tower's library call it a Rim watch: the ancients kept a garrison here to watch the world's edge, though no text says for what. Scavengers have stripped everything that could be carried. On the nights the beacon flickers, the seal hunters will not camp below it.
entries.truth: Outer demons climb the Rim here. The Frozen Host's scouts came up this way during the war, and the beacon flickers whenever something is climbing now.

entries.name: Flowing Fire Flats
entries.summary: A lava field on the north flank of the Spine where glacier meltwater pours over living rock. Frostflame lotus grows on the steam line, and the crust breaks without warning.
entries.lore: Meltwater runs over a crust of cooling lava as thin as a door, and where it boils away frostflame lotus blooms: a fire-and-ice herb that treats qi deviation up to Core Formation. One bloom fetches two mid-grade spirit stones in Dawnless City. The crust breaks under weight it held the day before, and the Palace's herb officers take half of whatever comes out alive. Experienced pickers cross on their bellies, alone.

entries.name: Glass Bay
entries.summary: A long sound on the southern coast where the Frostmilk River meets the Shattered Sea. Each winter it freezes clear as glass, and the Frost Fair is rebuilt on the ice.
entries.lore: The [[Frost Fair]] is where tribes, Palace disciples and southern merchants trade under a truce nobody trusts, and its transfer array is the continent's only fast road south. The Eternal Night Palace taxes every stall. In summer the bay thaws, the merchants retreat to the Petrel Kingdom's wharves and ships sail for the Shattered Sea. Each winter the sea ice reaches further out than the year before, and the Fair moves to stay at its edge. Ice-cutters, porters and guards are hired by the thousand in the first week of the freeze. A seat on the truce council has stood empty since its holder was found in the ice.
entries.truth: The ice spreads further each winter because the glacier's cold is spreading. Within thirty years the Fair will stand on ocean ice half the year, and the Snow Wolves will be able to reach it in a night's ride.

entries.name: Deer Call River
entries.summary: The eastern river, running from the Tusk Ridge down off the Mammoth Tableland and through the taiga to the eastern strait. Timber floats down it in summer, and elk herds cross it in autumn.
entries.lore: It is named for the autumn crossing, when spirit elk swim it by the hundred thousand and their calls carry for days. The Black Pine Tribe hunts the crossing, and so do wolves and taiga tigers. In summer rafts of black pine logs a li long float down to the coast yards. It freezes for seven months, and its ice road is the tableland's way to the sea.

entries.name: Khanate of the Dismounted
entries.summary: A tribe that conquered a coastal valley three generations ago and settled down to farm and trade. The tribes call them the Dismounted, and they took the insult as their name.
entries.lore: Their grandfathers rode in with the Great Khan before last, liked the valley and stayed. They still cultivate the body and fight bare-handed, but they live in stone houses, grow barley and sell horses to the coastal kingdoms, and their children learn to plow as well as to ride. The coastal kings call them barbarians and hire them as mercenaries; the steppe tribes call them soft and want them as a gate. When the next Great Khan rides, they will be the first asked to join and the first burned for refusing. Their khan has not decided.

entries.name: Bone-Burial Fjord
entries.summary: A fjord where old sea beasts come to die, its floor heaped with leviathan bones. The sea clans hold it sacred and drown anyone who enters.
entries.lore: Whales, jiao and stranger things swim into this fjord when their time comes, and their bones pile up in the cold water: ribs like temple beams, skulls the size of houses and, in the deepest heap, Ascent Age leviathans with their cores still inside. Bone refiners would give a fortune for one rib. The sea clans post guards at the mouth, and boats that cross the line are dragged under. The Cold Jiao Lord does not negotiate about the dead.

entries.name: Woolly Mammoth Tribe
entries.summary: The largest of the Iron Bone tribes, who ride and herd woolly mammoths on the northern steppe. Their chief, a giant-blooded woman, is one of the two claimants to Great Khan.
entries.lore: Mammoth Tribe children are put on a mammoth's back before they can walk and learn to sleep there through a blizzard. The tribe holds the best winter grazing on the steppe and forty thousand head of mammoth, and its chief lifted three ancestor stones at once at the last gathering. She means to become Great Khan by persuasion: grazing rights for every tribe that joins her, and a ride south only when the herds are fat. Her riders call the Snow Wolf claimant a dog who listens to dreams.
entries.truth: She is losing. Two of her own sub-chiefs have taken Snow Wolf gold, and the Old Mammoth clan has stopped sending calves to her herds.

entries.name: Dreaming Ice
entries.summary: The ice sheet of the far north around the Demon-Sealing Glacier, where an outer demon army stands frozen mid-charge and the Seal Watch keeps its northern fortress. The ice creeps south every year.
entries.lore: The tribes call it the Dreaming Ice because their shamans say the demons inside the [[Demon-Sealing Glacier]] dream, and that the dreams come out as blizzards. The Seal Watch fortress of the [[Ice-Guard Fortress]] holds the glacier's southern edge and kills anyone found on the ice without a pass. Scavengers come anyway, for war relics in the old battlefield and in the rubble the glacier pushes out at its snout. The Watch hires porters and wall-builders at three times steppe wages and lets none leave early, and a Core Formation outsider who serves a season on the wall earns a Watch token every great power honors.
entries.truth: The glacier began creeping faster forty years ago, the year the first thawed demon escaped. The Watch's geomancers have measured it, and the Warden has sealed their report.

entries.name: Frozen Radiance Observatory
entries.summary: A small orthodox sect of Ice Dao cultivators who study the aurora from an observatory beside the Frost Steles. They sell aurora readings and rent seats at the steles.
entries.lore: A Morning Star sword cultivator came north for the steles three centuries ago and never left; the Observatory she founded keeps sixty disciples, teaches the Ice Dao and aurora divination, and recruits only those who can sit a full night at the steles without moving. Its readings predict storms, secret realm openings and, its elders claim, deaths. It rents the best stele seats for fifty low-grade spirit stones a week. It hates the Palace, which raids it once a generation, wants the Broken Tower's library, and resents the Armillary Pavilion, which calls its readings guesswork and copies them.
entries.truth: The master has worked out why the aurora is brightening and sent her figures to the Armillary Pavilion. The reply asked her, politely, to stop publishing.

entries.name: Warm Basin
entries.summary: A sunken basin between the ranges, the glacier and the steppe, where hot springs melt the ice into steaming marsh. The richest herb ground on the continent, and three powers tax it.
entries.lore: Fire runs close under the ground here, and the basin stays green through the polar night under a sky lit orange by its own steam. Spirit farmers terrace the springs for fire-and-ice herbs: frostflame lotus, ember moss, snow ginseng where the steam freezes. The Frostmilk River gathers in its marshes. The Eternal Night Palace, the Iron Bone tribes and the Seal Watch's quartermasters all take a share, and the farmers pay all three. Mammoth herds winter at its edges, and so do the wolves that follow them. This decade the springs at the north end have begun to cool, and nobody admits to knowing why.
entries.truth: The Palace is drawing the northern springs' fire through lava tubes to heat its thaw works under the glacier. When those springs die the north basin freezes, and the Musk Ox Tribe will blame the farmers.

entries.name: Cliff-Climb Khanate
entries.summary: A khanate that holds the three ramps up the tableland's southwestern cliffs and tolls every herd, digger and calf thief that climbs them.
entries.lore: Whoever holds the ramps holds the tableland's door, and the Cliff-Climb khans have held them for two centuries by fortifying the switchbacks and charging a head of cattle per hundred. Their warriors fight from ledges with throwing axes and fall-ropes, and their children climb before they ride. The present khan is the elder half-brother of the Snow Wolf claimant and has promised him the ramps, which would give the Snow Wolves a road to the herds. The Mammoth Tribe has promised to bury the khan in his own switchbacks if he does.

entries.name: Court of a Thousand Tents
entries.summary: The great tent camp of the Iron Bone Tribes below Ancestor Mountain. It swells to a city each summer for trading, and for the stone-lifting every third summer and shrinks to a garrison in the long night.
entries.lore: At midsummer a hundred thousand people camp here: tribes, Frost Fair traders, beast tamers, Myriad Sands monks and body cultivators come to fight in the pits. Mammoth ivory, furs, musk, eagle chicks and tempering herbs change hands for salt, tea, iron and spirit stones. Pit fights are bare-handed by law, and a foreigner who wins three in a row is offered adoption into a tribe. In winter only the stone-keepers and a few hundred guards stay.

entries.name: Utter North
entries.summary: The northeastern horn of the Black Frost Continent, pointing toward the Rim: ice cliffs, pack ice and lonely fiefs of hunters and exiles. Lately, fewer of the hunters come back.
entries.lore: From the cliffs of the Utter North the Shoreless Sea runs toward the Rim, and on still nights a pale glow rises over the world's edge. The sea freezes far out each winter; seal hunters and whalers work the ice edge and pay tribute to the sea clans when they meet them. Exiles from every faction end up here: Palace deserters, tribal outcasts, Seal Watch men who would not go home. In the last forty years hunting parties have begun to vanish whole, and the two patrols the Seal Watch sent found only empty camps with the fires still warm.
entries.truth: The second patrol found one survivor. He hummed all the way back to the fortress and was quietly killed there, and the Watch has told no one.

entries.name: The Burning Spine
entries.summary: The volcanic range that runs across the western Black Frost Continent from the fjords to the edge of the Demon-Sealing Glacier. Its vents glow red through the polar night.
entries.lore: Forty volcanoes, a dozen awake at any time. Lava tubes run for hundreds of li under its ice, and whoever knows them can cross the Spine in winter without seeing the sky. Black iron, obsidian and sulfur crop out along its flanks; fire salamanders and ash wolves hunt its slopes. Its eastern end dives under the glacier, and steam rises from the ice there all year.
entries.truth: The Spine is warming with the tide. Three volcanoes dead since the Dim Age began smoking this decade, and one of them is the mountain the Palace is built on.

entries.name: Circling-Sun Stone
entries.summary: An Ascent Age gnomon on a northern headland. In midsummer its shadow circles a full turn without the sun ever setting, and Time Dao cultivators sit inside the circle.
entries.lore: The stone is a black needle forty feet tall inside a ring of carved marks that count something other than hours. Under the midnight sun its shadow sweeps the ring once a day. In the polar night it casts a shadow anyway, from no light anyone can see, and that shadow moves backward. The Armillary Pavilion sends astronomers every few years to measure it and will not say what they find. Time Dao cultivators sit in the ring for a summer and come out disoriented, and now and then enlightened.
entries.truth: The backward shadow is cast by the Mirror. The stone is counting down the years to the tide's peak, and its count agrees with the Armillary Pavilion's own tables.

entries.name: Melt Caves
entries.summary: Meltwater caves at the glacier's southwestern edge, where the last vent of the Burning Spine runs under the ice. The Eternal Night Palace works them as a frost-fire crystal mine.
entries.lore: Steam pours from cracks in the ice here all year, and the caves below are lined with frost-fire crystal, a stone cold on one face and hot on the other that refiners buy by the ounce. The Palace has held the mine for sixty years under a lease from the Seal Watch, guards it with its own disciples and kills anyone who comes near. Miners are hired in Dawnless City on five-year terms. None has come back early, and few at all.
entries.truth: The caves are the Palace's thaw works. Its tunnels reach the Frozen Host from below, and the demon that escaped forty years ago walked out through them.

entries.name: Frostmilk River
entries.summary: The steppe's great river, milky with glacier silt, running from the foot of the Burning Spine through the Warm Basin to Glass Bay. In winter it freezes into the ice road that feeds the Frost Fair.
entries.lore: The tribes call it their mother, because its valleys are where the herds survive the polar night. From the first freeze to spring its ice carries sledges, mammoth trains and riders down to the Frost Fair, and the Palace's toll posts take a fifth of every load. In summer it floods its valleys with gray water too cold to swim. Every Great Khan has ridden south along it, and every coastal kingdom watches it in winter.

entries.name: Musk Ox Tribe
entries.summary: An Iron Bone tribe that winters its musk ox herds around the basin's northern springs and counts the whole basin as its winter pasture.
entries.lore: The Musk Ox Tribe has wintered here for a thousand years. Every spring when the herds move out the farmers plant over the grazing, and every autumn the tribe tramples it. Their warriors wear musk ox horn on their fists and fight in a wall, shoulder to shoulder, and their children learn to stand in the wall at ten. They collect the basin's grain tithe in person, and a farmer who shorts it loses a field. Their northern springs are cooling, and the tribe has decided the farmers are poisoning them.

entries.name: Stone Ship Harbor
entries.summary: The main port of the Sand-Gazing Shore, built around an Ascent Age ship of stone stranded on the beach. Every cargo bound for Myriad Sands passes its customs house.
entries.lore: The stone ship is three li long, its hull a single piece of gray rock carved with formations nobody can read, and the customs house sits in its stern. The Myriad Sands Continent's oasis merchant houses keep warehouses here, and a Heavenly Scale Pavilion branch changes spirit stones and lends at interest. Ivory, furs and black iron go south; grain, tea, cloth and lamp oil come north. In summer the harbor holds two hundred ships. In a hard winter it holds none.
entries.truth: The ship came down the Ladder. Its hold is sealed, and the harbor master's family has kept the key for a thousand years without knowing what it is.

entries.name: River of Passing Water
entries.summary: A river that runs north from the Burning Spine across the Aurora Waste toward the world's edge. It is frozen ten months of the year.
entries.lore: It flows away from every other river on the continent, north toward the Rim, and herders say water that reaches its mouth never comes back as rain. For two months in midsummer it runs fast and black with meltwater; the rest of the year it is a frozen road from the Palace's northern mines to the coast. Palace slave trains walk its ice in winter, and the Reindeer Tribe sells them meat and now and then buys a slave free. Ice Dao cultivators study stillness on its ice, and Time Dao cultivators study it in the weeks it runs.

entries.name: Ice-Keeper Tribe
entries.summary: A small tribe that swore itself to the Seal Watch at the Second Sealing. They haul the fortress's supplies, herd reindeer on the ice margin and listen to the glacier.
entries.lore: Ice-Keeper children read crevasses before they can count, and every adult has hauled sledges to the fortress. The Watch pays them in grain, salt and iron and keeps the khans off them; the khans call them the Watch's dogs. Their grazing shrinks every year as the ice moves south, and the young want to leave for the steppe. Their shamans sleep on the ice to hear the demons dream, and sell what they hear as weather forecasts.
entries.truth: Two of their shamans have started humming the same tune in their sleep, and their children have picked it up without being taught.

entries.name: Forest of Frost Steles
entries.summary: A field of Ascent Age steles carved with fragments of an Ice Dao treatise. Under the aurora the carvings glow, and cultivators sit before them for weeks.
entries.lore: There are three hundred and twelve steles, each sheathed in ice and each carved with a few lines of a treatise on the Ice Dao that nobody has read whole. When the aurora is strong the carvings shine through the ice; when it fades they vanish. Cultivators sit before them for weeks, and the frozen ones who never got up still sit among the living. A Foundation cultivator who comprehends one stele gains a technique; nobody has ever comprehended ten. The Frozen Radiance Observatory controls the best seats and rents them out.
entries.truth: The treatise was carved by the sect that built the Slumbering City, and its last chapter is not about ice. It is about sealing outer demons, and whoever froze the Frozen Host had read it.

entries.name: North Wind Sword Gate
entries.summary: A small orthodox sword sect that guards the Sand-Gazing Shore for pay. Its swordsmen fight in the cold better than any south of the strait, and cost accordingly.
entries.lore: A Myriad Sands Continent-born sword cultivator came north to hunt the tribe that killed his family and stayed to sell his sword to the coast. The Gate he founded teaches a Sword Dao made for cold: short, fast forms that do not need warm muscles, and qi circulation that keeps blood moving in a blizzard. It recruits from the coastal kingdoms' guard families and rents its disciples to whichever king pays. It hates the Iron Bone tribes and the Palace equally, and it wants a fief of its own; the debt-ridden White Walls kingdom is starting to look like one.

entries.name: Pine Surge Forest
entries.summary: The southeastern taiga and coast facing the Floating Peak Continent across the eastern strait. Furs, ship timber, amber and beast mounts go south, and the Floating Peak Continent's clans keep a foothold on this shore.
entries.lore: The only real forest on Black Frost grows here, black pine and larch on hills the sea keeps milder than the steppe. The Deer Call River floats timber to the coast, and ships carry it to the Floating Peak Continent's lowland yards. The Floating Peak Continent's Nine Clans buy furs, amber, masts, mammoth calves and beast mounts, and one of them has built a trading lodge above the harbor that looks more like a fort every year. The forest tribes trap, hunt and log, and despise the coastal kingdoms for selling the forest by the shipload. Beast tamers from four continents gather here for next winter's opening of the ancestral beast realm.
entries.truth: This is the only corner of the continent getting warmer: the forest edge has crept north a hundred li in a century. The Black Pine shamans think the Pine of Ten Thousand Ages is doing it, and they are right.

entries.name: Fief of Steaming Fields
entries.summary: Spirit rice terraces on hot springs above the fjords, held by an old farming family of orthodox exiles. The only rice that grows north of the strait.
entries.lore: The Qiu family fled Morning Star eight hundred years ago after backing the wrong prince and brought rice seed with them. Their terraces step down the fjord walls through the steam, fed by springs hot enough to cook an egg at the top and cool enough for rice at the bottom; Qiu children learn each terrace's water by taste. The rice sells to the Palace, the Frost Fair and the fortress. The family trains spirit farmers, pays them well and asks only that nobody carries seed out. They keep orthodox rites quietly, and the Palace ignores it while the rice comes.

entries.name: Runaways' Stockade
entries.summary: A stockade of exiles from every faction on the edge of the Utter North. No questions asked, no extraditions honored, and a smuggling road for the glacier's relics.
entries.lore: Palace deserters, oathbreakers from the Seal Watch, tribal outcasts and foreign fugitives built the stockade a century ago, and its only law is that nobody asks why you came. It runs the smuggling road for relics from the Field of Broken Spears and the glacier's snout, around the Watch's patrols to the Floe Market. Its chief is a one-armed Core Formation woman who deserted the Palace after killing her master. Newcomers pay a year's labor or a year's wages.

entries.name: Irongrass Steppe
entries.summary: The southern steppe heartland of the Iron Bone Tribes around the lone peak of Ancestor Mountain. Grass grows waist-high under the midnight sun and dies to iron-gray stalks in the long night.
entries.lore: The Iron Bone Tribes graze mammoths, shaggy horses and musk oxen here in summer and pull back to the river valleys when the polar night falls. Each tribe holds its grazing by force, and the tribes meet only at the [[Ancestor Mountain]], where chiefs lift the ancestor stones to prove their right. The last Great Khan died sixty years ago; the cycle says the next is due, and two claimants are gathering riders. Body cultivators from every continent come to learn the Fist Dao in the blizzard camps. A stranger who survives a night in the open may be adopted; the rest are left for the wolves.
entries.truth: The summer grass line has crept a thousand li south in a lifetime as the glacier's cold spreads. That, more than any dream, is why the tribes are ready to follow a Great Khan south.

top.note: two war chiefs; the Bone Ancestor waking

entries.name: Ice Listeners
entries.summary: A fellowship of shamans, hermits and Seal Watch dropouts who sleep at the glacier's edge and write down what the demons dream. They sell blizzard warnings.
entries.lore: The Listeners live in snow huts just past the Watch's patrol line, write the Host's dreams in ledgers and sell blizzard warnings to caravans and the fortress alike; their forecasts are right more often than anyone's. They take in anyone who hears singing in their sleep and cannot stop hearing it, and teach them to write it down. They want the Watch to let them closer to the ice, and resent the Palace miners who chase them away from the Melt Caves. The Watch thinks them harmless.
entries.truth: They are a cell of the [[Void Choir]]. The ledgers are hymns, and the Listeners are waiting for the one who got out to call them.

entries.name: Pushed-Stone Moraine
entries.summary: The ridge of rubble the advancing glacier pushes ahead of itself. It spills out Ascent Age stones, demon glass and, now and then, bodies nobody can identify.
entries.lore: As the glacier creeps south it scrapes the ground and drops what it carried at its snout: boulders, carved Ascent Age blocks, war debris and things older than the war. Three years ago a cultivator in robes of a cut nobody recognized came out of the ice whole, and the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] bought the body for a sum nobody will name. Scavengers work the moraine in summer. In winter the snout calves without warning and buries whoever is under it.
entries.truth: The robed body was not dead, only sealed. It woke on the ship to the Long Dusk Continent, and neither it nor the puppet master who bought it has been seen since.

entries.name: Cloud-Swallowing Fjord
entries.summary: The deepest fjord on the west coast, so full of steam from the hot springs at its head that clouds seem to sink into it. Ships navigate it by bells.
entries.lore: The fjord runs two thousand li inland between black cliffs, and its head is a cauldron of boiling springs fed from the Burning Spine's roots. Steam fills it from wall to wall, so ships ring a bell every hundred strokes and steer by the echoes. Fire coral grows in the warm shallows at its head, along with the ember eels alchemists prize. Pilots who know the echoes charge a low-grade spirit stone a day and are worth it.

entries.name: Sand-Gazing Shore
entries.summary: The southwestern coast facing the Myriad Sands Continent across a cold strait: walled mortal kingdoms, a Buddhist mission and ports that grow rich on summer trade and burn when the khans ride.
entries.lore: In summer, cultivator-crewed ships carry furs, black iron and mammoth ivory to the Myriad Sands Continent and bring back grain, tea and lamp oil. In the hardest winters the sea ice reaches across the strait: no caravan can cross that much ice, but a Great Khan's riders on ice wolves can, and have. Every town here has a wall and a bell. The Thousand Lamps Temple's mission heals raiders and raided alike and is quietly becoming the richest landlord on the coast. With a Great Khan due, the kingdoms are hiring swords, building walls and arguing about tribute.
entries.truth: The strait has frozen across in four of the last seven winters, where once a decade was a hard run. The monks have told the Myriad Sands Continent. Nobody has told the coastal kings.

entries.name: Pine of Ten Thousand Ages
entries.summary: A black pine taller than any tree on the continent, deep in the taiga. It is a spirit plant that has woken twice in recorded history, and its sap cures frost in the meridians.
entries.lore: Its trunk takes two hundred people to ring and its crown is lost in cloud. The Black Pine Tribe tends it and kills anyone who cuts it. A drop of its sap cures frost damage in the meridians and is worth a mid-grade spirit stone to any alchemist in the north. It woke once in the Rekindling and walked a hundred li, and again three centuries ago, when loggers cut a root and the forest closed over their camp in a night. The Thunder-Feather Lodge's new road points straight at it.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Evening Bell
entries.summary: A small harbor kingdom named for the warning bells that ring from its towers at dusk. Its king is a lay disciple of the Thousand Lamps Temple, and half his people have converted.
