entries.lore: For three centuries the bells rang every dusk to show the towers were manned; now they also call the faithful to Sea-Crossing Temple's evening sutra. Children are raised on sutras and sword drills both, and the temple takes any orphan the kingdom gives it. The king wants to cede the harbor to the temple in exchange for arhat protection. His nobles want Palace mercenaries instead, and one of them has already sent an envoy to Dawnless City.

entries.name: Warm Array Workshop
entries.summary: The formation masters who lay the heat arrays under the Frost Fair's ice platforms and sell warming talismans to half the continent. Without them the Fair freezes in a night.
entries.lore: Each winter the Workshop lays the Fair's foundation arrays: heat circles under every street that keep the ice firm but not lethal. It sells warming talismans in three grades, from a mortal's one-night charm to a Foundation cultivator's month-long seal, and teaches formations and talisman making to apprentices who pay with five years' labor. Everyone needs it, so it is neutral. Its masters want the empty seat on the Fair's truce council, and despise the Armillary Pavilion array keepers, who treat them as tinkers.
entries.truth: The Workshop can switch off the Fair's heat with one command array. It has used the threat twice, and the Palace has quietly started training formation masters to replace it.

entries.name: Black Iron Fief
entries.summary: A mining fief on the north slopes of the Burning Spine, where steppe slaves dig black iron in tunnels the polar night never leaves.
entries.lore: The She family has held the fief for the Eternal Night Palace for six generations: four Foundation cultivators and a hundred overseers. Free miners' children grow up in warm tunnels and see the sun only in summer. Slaves who show a spirit root are sold to the Palace at eight; the family keeps the ones who show two. Black iron ore fetches a low-grade spirit stone a cartload at the mine head and five times that in Dawnless City. A giant-blooded slave from the Snow Wolf tribe has been organizing the lower galleries, and the overseers have noticed.
entries.truth: The She heir has been selling the family's best veins to the Yin Fire Sect behind his father's back, and means to hand his father to the slaves when the revolt comes.

entries.name: Dawnless City
entries.summary: The market city below the Eternal Night Palace, carved into a black cliff and lit by lava channels. Slaves, black iron, blood pills and blades are sold here, and its Contract Hall hires anyone.
entries.lore: The city is warm and red in the darkest month. Forge Street refiners turn black iron into blades with a blood groove and sell them to anyone, including orthodox buyers in hoods. The Palace's Contract Hall posts bounties on elders' rivals; anyone may take one, and it pays in high-grade spirit stones. Slaves are sold in the lower market by the dozen. The only law is the Palace's tax, collected by outer disciples who keep whatever they can squeeze above it.
entries.truth: Forge Street's best refiner is a [[Clear Heaven Sword Sect]] sword elder who faked her death forty years ago. She copies every blade order the Palace places and sends the list south.

top.note: Palace elders come down to trade

entries.name: Mammoth Tableland
entries.summary: A high basalt tableland in the east where the great mammoth herds graze through the polar night. Mammoth matriarchs, a giant-blooded tribe and calf thieves share it badly.
entries.lore: Black basalt cliffs lift the tableland above the steppe, and its winds strip snow from the grass, so the herds come up to graze through the polar night. The herds are older than the tribes, and the greatest are led by mammoth matriarchs at Core Formation and above. The giant-blooded tribe that follows them claims kinship with the herds, and the herds seem to agree. Beast tamers pay fortunes for mammoth calves, and calf thieves climb the cliff ramps every winter; the herds trample the ones they catch and the tribes hang the rest. Both Great Khan claimants want the herds for the ride south.
entries.truth: The giant blood comes from the herds. Mammoth matriarchs who reached Nascent Soul took human form in the Dim Age and took human husbands, and the tribe's elders know it.

entries.name: Mammoth Graveyard
entries.summary: A valley where old mammoths go to die. Its floor is ivory and bone, and the herds kill anyone they find digging there.
entries.lore: When a mammoth knows it is dying it leaves the herd and walks to this valley, and the herd follows to see it die. Ten thousand years of bones lie here in drifts, and tusks lie like fallen trees. Beast cores from old matriarchs rest in the skulls. Ivory diggers and bone refiners would pay anything for one season inside, and some have tried; their bones are in the drifts too. The Giant-Blood tribe buries its dead here, which no other humans may do.

entries.name: Snow Silkworm Stockade
entries.summary: A stockade of exiled Jar-Mother daughters from Vast Wilds who raise snow silkworms and cold Gu at the basin's edge, where warm ground meets frozen.
entries.lore: Their founders were cast out of the [[Jar-Mother Clans]] for breeding Gu that survive cold, and came north to prove it could be done. Snow silkworms live on frostleaf at the basin's edge and spin ice silk, which refiners make into robes that turn blades and hold heat; a bolt sells for a mid-grade spirit stone. Their cold Gu stop a heart without leaving a mark, and the Palace buys them. They teach Gu raising to girls only.
entries.truth: The Jar-Mothers want them dead and have sent a Gu north to do it. It is already inside the stockade, and it is patient.

entries.name: Snow Wolf Tribe
entries.summary: Wolf-riding raiders of the southern steppe near the coast. Their young chief says the Bone Ancestor speaks to him in dreams and that he will be the next Great Khan.
entries.lore: Snow Wolf children raise ice wolf pups in their own tents, and a rider and wolf who survive their first raid are bound for life. The tribe raids the coastal kingdoms and the Frost Fair's caravans, sells captives in Dawnless City and spends the proceeds on more wolves. Its chief is twenty-six and already Core Formation in body, and every tribe that has bet against him has lost its herds. He says the Ancestor has told him to ride south this winter, across the frozen strait, and that the ice will hold.
entries.truth: The dreams are real. The Bone Ancestor is choosing a Khan and a vessel, and does not care whether the boy survives the choosing.

entries.name: Blood Salt Lake
entries.summary: A warm crater lake below the Palace, red as blood and thick with salt. Palace disciples soak in it to temper their bodies for blood cultivation.
entries.lore: The water is warm, red and salty enough to float a man, and the crust on its shore is the best body-tempering salt on the continent. Outer disciples soak until their skin splits and heals, and rank in the outer court is partly decided by who can stay in longest. Salt rakers from Red Spring Fief work the far shore for wages; a sack sells to body cultivators at the Frost Fair for a low-grade spirit stone. Nobody fishes it.
entries.truth: The lake is red because nine hundred years of blood tithe have been drained into it. The salt tempers so well because of what it remembers, and the oldest rakers hear it whisper.

entries.name: Reindeer Tribe
entries.summary: Reindeer herders of the Aurora Waste who follow the northern lights, believing the lights lead the herds to grazing. They are the only people who live here all year.
entries.lore: The Reindeer Tribe moves its herds along the River of Passing Water and out onto the barrens, steering by the aurora; their shamans read its colors as other diviners read stars, and are right about storms more often than not. Their children can walk a day in a blizzard and find the camp at the end of it. They pay the Palace a tithe of hides when it comes to collect and ignore everyone else. Scavenger crews keep digging up their burial grounds for the ruins beneath, and the tribe has started killing crews that dig without asking.

entries.name: Tusk Ridge
entries.summary: The black basalt escarpment that walls the Mammoth Tableland on its west and southwest, curving like a tusk from the edge of the Utter North down toward the southeast coast.
entries.lore: Its cliffs are columns of black basalt a thousand feet high, and frost rocs nest on the ledges. The ridge breaks the north wind for the herds and funnels it everywhere else. Old lava tubes run through it, and the Hearth Clan says its ancestors walked east through them before the Burning Spine cooled. Egg hunters climb it each spring; a frost roc egg sells to beast tamers for five mid-grade spirit stones, if the climber lives.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Salt Houses
entries.summary: A small kingdom of salt pans and smokehouses on the bay's northern shore. Salt keeps meat through the polar night, and the salt families have grown rich and nervous on it.
entries.lore: Seven salt families rule by council and marry only each other. Their pans run along the shore for three hundred li: in summer they boil seawater over peat, in winter they rake frost salt off the bay. Every tribe needs salt for the dark months, so every tribe fosters a hostage child in a salt house as surety for fair prices. The foster children grow up as brothers and sisters across tribal feuds, which has stopped two wars and started one.
entries.truth: The Snow Wolf chief was a salt-house hostage. The families know exactly which of their children he loved, and which he swore to kill.

entries.name: Harbor of Distant Peaks
entries.summary: The main port facing the Floating Peak Continent. Sailors swear that on the clearest winter days the floating peaks hang over the southeastern horizon, which is how the harbor got its name.
entries.lore: Ships from the Floating Peak Continent's lowland ports bring spirit stones, formation plates and grain, and leave with furs, amber, masts, ivory and live beasts. The beast market here is the largest on the continent: frost eagle chicks, ice wolf pups, spirit elk, white bear cubs and, under the counter, mammoth calves. A Heavenly Scale Pavilion branch changes and lends. The Thunder-Feather Lodge stands on the hill above, and its people walk through the market as if they own it, which they nearly do.

entries.name: Fief of Herb Fields
entries.summary: The Eternal Night Palace's herb plantation on the basin's western slopes, worked by indentured farmers under a Palace overseer. It grows the herbs for the Palace's blood pills.
entries.lore: A Core Formation Palace elder holds the fief as a reward and runs it as a business. Farmers indenture themselves for ten years to clear a debt or spare a child from the blood tithe; few finish, because the overseers add a year for every failed crop. The fields grow blood lichen, ember moss and nightbloom, the core herbs of the Palace's pills. Indentures who escape run to Spring Gardens, and the Palace sends hunters after them.
entries.truth: The overseer skims a third of the harvest and sells it at the Hundred Herb Market. Three people knew; two of them are buried in the lichen beds.

entries.name: Fief of the Left-Behind
entries.summary: A fief of the descendants of the Outer Demon War's northern line, who stayed where their ancestors fought and still man the old walls south of the glacier.
entries.lore: When the war ended, the survivors of the northern line were promised relief that never came, so they stayed. Their descendants keep the old earthworks, drill their children on them from the age of six and consider the Seal Watch a newcomer. They own salvage rights to the battlefield by an old Watch decree and kill scavengers who skip the tenth. Their ancestral hall holds the shields of three thousand dead, and the elders read the names aloud every Long Night.
entries.truth: One shield in the hall has a blank where its owner's name should be, like the blank on the Seal Watch's founding stele. The elders have never shown it to the Watch.

entries.name: Shadow Pavilion
entries.summary: An Ascent Age hall drowned at the bottom of Glass Bay. On the coldest days the ice is clear enough to see its roofs, and divers cut holes to reach it.
entries.lore: In deep winter, when the bay ice is clear as glass, a building shows through it a hundred feet down: tiled roofs, a courtyard, a bronze gate. Divers go down on ropes with warming talismans, and the cold kills most within a quarter hour. What they bring up sells at the Fair's appraisal stalls: jade tiles that hold formations, bronze fittings and once a sealed box that three Core Formation cultivators fought to the death over. The gate has never opened.
entries.truth: The hall was a waystation for envoys coming down the Ladder, and its gate opens to an Upper Realm token. The [[Armillary Pavilion]] has been quietly buying every fitting the divers raise.

entries.name: Eagle-Master Tribe
entries.summary: Falconers of the western steppe who tame frost eagles. Every tribe uses their birds for scouting and messages, and every tribe suspects they read the messages first.
entries.lore: An Eagle-Master child climbs to a frost eagle eyrie at twelve and comes down with a chick or not at all. Their eagles carry messages between the tribes, the Frost Fair and the fortress, spot raiders a hundred li off and can be trained to take a man's eyes. Beast tamers buy their surplus chicks for a mid-grade spirit stone each. Both claimants want their eagles, and the chief is auctioning the alliance in all but name.
entries.truth: They do read the messages, and they have sold copies to the Eternal Night Palace for thirty years.

entries.name: Yin Fire Sect
entries.summary: A demonic refining sect, sworn vassal of the Eternal Night Palace, that forges with cold blue fire drawn from deep vents and quenches its blades in blood.
entries.lore: Yin fire burns blue, gives almost no heat and melts black iron in a breath; the sect draws it from vents too deep for mortals to survive. It makes the Palace's blood blades and armor and sells the seconds in Dawnless City. It recruits by buying slave children who can stand near a vent without fainting, and teaches the Fire Dao, artifact refining and the blood quench. It hates the Hearth Clan, who sit on the best vents, and wants the Earth Heart Fire said to be waking under the Spine. Bring it a fire salamander core and you get a month at its forges.
entries.truth: The sect's master forged the cages the Palace keeps thawed demons in, and kept a sliver of demon flesh for himself. He has been eating it a crumb at a time.

entries.name: Beast-Tamer Stockade
entries.summary: A school of beast tamers in the taiga that breaks frost eagles, ice wolves, spirit elk and white bears to the saddle, and buys stolen mammoth calves without asking.
entries.lore: The Stockade sells mounts to the Frost Fair, the Floating Peak Continent and the Myriad Sands Continent, trains tamers for a fee or seven years' labor, and takes children whom animals follow home. Its masters teach beast taming, beast medicine and the patience to wait a week beside a den. Its most profitable line is mammoth calves stolen from the tableland and raised in the forest, where the herds cannot follow. The Old Mammoth clan knows where the Stockade is and has not come yet; its master thinks that is because she pays the Cliff-Climb khan.

entries.name: Ice-Guard Fortress
entries.summary: The Seal Watch's northern fortress on the southern edge of the Demon-Sealing Glacier. Elders of every great power serve here in rotation and watch a hundred thousand frozen demons.
entries.lore: From its north wall you can see the Frozen Host through a hundred li of blue ice. The glacier pushes the wall south every decade, so the Watch builds a new one and leaves the old inside the ice. Formation masters keep the cold-seal arrays charged with spirit stones the great powers pay for, and geomancers measure the ice every month. Orthodox and demonic elders share a mess hall and do not speak. The fortress hires porters, cooks and ice-cutters on three-year contracts, and nobody is let go early.
entries.truth: This rotation's Palace elders keep volunteering for the night watch on the west wall. From there, nobody else can see the steam rising from the glacier's underside.

entries.name: Steaming Fjords
entries.summary: The western coast, cut by deep fjords where the Burning Spine's hot springs keep the water open through the polar night. Whalers, spirit rice terraces and the Eternal Night Palace's western port.
entries.lore: Hot springs pour into the heads of the fjords, so the inner harbors stay open while the outer sea freezes. Whalers and sealers sail from here into the Shoreless Sea and pay toll to the sea clans' northern court, or do not come back. The Eternal Night Palace ships slaves and black iron out of Chain-Gate Harbor; the fjord lords keep small fleets of their own and feud over fishing grounds and wrecks. Spirit farmers grow rice on terraces above the steam. This winter a Whale Tooth ship killed a jiao calf, and the sea clans want the killer's whole line.
entries.truth: The Palace paid the Whale Tooth captain to make that kill. It wants the sea clans to burn the fjord kingdoms so it can take their harbors.

entries.name: Heavy Stone Tribe
entries.summary: The small tribe that keeps the ancestor stones at the foot of Ancestor Mountain. They judge the stone-lifting, read mammoth shoulder blades for omens and take no side.
entries.lore: Every tribe's ancestor stone rests in Heavy Stone keeping between gatherings, and to steal one is to declare war on every tribe at once. Their children carry stones before they can talk. Their shamans crack mammoth shoulder blades in the fire and read the cracks, and chiefs pay in cattle for a reading before a raid. Foreign diviners may learn bone reading for a price paid in labor: a year of hauling stones.
entries.truth: The stones grow a little heavier every year, and the keepers have been shaving them to hide it. They are running out of stone to shave.

entries.name: Ancestor Mountain
entries.summary: A lone black peak in the middle of the Irongrass Steppe, sacred to every Iron Bone tribe. Chiefs lift the ancestor stones at its foot, and lately the mountain has begun to shake.
entries.lore: Tribal law forbids bloodshed within a day's ride of the mountain, and it is the one law every tribe keeps. The gathering at its foot every third midsummer decides chiefs by stone-lifting and, every few generations, raises a Great Khan. In the last ten years the mountain has shaken a dozen times, its springs have run hot and then cold, and herders swear they have heard breathing from the cracks on the north face. The stone-keepers forbid anyone to climb above the snow line.
entries.truth: The Bone Ancestor, a Deity Transformation body cultivator of the Dim Age, sleeps in a chamber at the mountain's heart and is waking. The shaking is his heartbeat.

entries.name: Realm of Ancestral Beasts
entries.summary: A shard world of Ascent Age beasts whose gate opens on the tableland's rim every twenty-four years for three months. Anyone below Nascent Soul can enter.
entries.lore: When the shard passes close, a dark basalt arch opens on the tableland's rim and breathes warm air. Inside is a world of beasts that died out in Severed Heaven sixty thousand years ago: giant elk, saber-tusked cats, mammoths twice the size of today's. Their cores are prized above anything living, and their young can be tamed by someone patient and lucky. The next opening is next winter, and beast tamers from four continents are already arriving at Harbor of Distant Peaks.

entries.name: Armillary Pavilion
entries.summary: The world's masters of formations and star reckoning. They run every transfer array between continents and tax every crossing.
entries.lore: From the Star Dial on the highest floating peak of the Floating Peak Continent, Armillary Pavilion astronomers chart the Mirror and the Shard Worlds and publish the calendar of secret realm openings every sect depends on. They rebuilt the transfer arrays eight thousand years ago and have never let anyone else learn how they work. They are strictly neutral, and will move an army for anyone who pays.
entries.truth: The Armillary Pavilion is rebuilding the Heaven Ladder. Every array toll for the last thousand years has gone into it. The Pavilion Master is a Body Integration formation master, and two Star Lords at Void Refinement keep the inter-continent arrays running.

ties.why: We pay the Abbey every year to keep its logs of the Stump's rising hum off the market.
The Tide-Watching Pavilion undersells our charts and calls our prices theft.

entries.name: Black Frost Continent
entries.summary: Ice, steppe and black volcanic ranges under a long polar night. Demonic sects, body-cultivating tribes and a frozen outer demon army.
entries.lore: For half the year the sun never rises over the Black Frost Continent. Its southern steppes feed the Iron Bone Tribes, who temper their bodies in blizzards and despise qi cultivators as soft. The Eternal Night Palace rules the black ranges, where fire runs under the ice. In the far north an entire outer demon army lies frozen in the Demon-Sealing Glacier, and the Seal Watch keeps a fortress on its edge.
entries.truth: The glacier is advancing south a few li every year. The tribes' shamans say the demons inside are dreaming.

top.note: the Night Sovereign, who never sleeps

entries.name: The Heavenly Circuit
entries.summary: The chain of transfer arrays linking each continent's great city, run by the Armillary Pavilion. One jump costs more spirit stones than a village earns in a lifetime.
entries.lore: Built eight thousand years ago in the Rekindling. Every great power pays the Armillary Pavilion's tolls and resents it. The arrays avoid the Shattered Sea: something about Heaven's Scar scrambles them.

ties.why: The Jing Capital's hall is our busiest jump and our best-paying toll.

entries.name: Nine Mouths River Sect
entries.summary: A water Dao sect with a Nascent Soul master that holds the nine mouths of the Imperial River, dredging its channels, keeping its flood-gates and piloting every barge and junk through the delta's bars.
entries.lore: The Nine Mouths River Sect has kept the Imperial River's delta open since before the Kingdom of the Setting Sun had a king. Its disciples dredge the channels, hold the spring floods behind sluice-halls built into the delta dikes, and pilot every barge and sea junk across the shifting bars for a toll in rice and stones. Its master, a Nascent Soul river cultivator, has never left the delta in his life, and the kingdom's rice and the city's trade both rest on his sluice-gates staying open. Evening Glow's harbor masters pay him for pilots; King Wen pays him for the floods.
entries.fromAbove: A chain of sluice-halls and dredging yards at the river's nine mouths, each under its own small ward dome, the delta's channels running clear between them.

ties.why: King Wen pays us a rice tithe to keep the nine mouths dredged and the flood-gates working.
The harbor masters pay us a toll in stones for pilots across the bars.

features.name: the sluice-halls at the river's nine mouths
the pilots' bar-stations
the master's flood-hall, where the spring floods are counted
